author: jonathanavis96
body:
Three changes from a live review of the new hero.

### The Master Suite leads on its view

Its photographs now open on what was the fifth frame — the bed with two walls of glass onto Camps Bay, the mountainside and the sea. It is the strongest of the eight and it is the room's whole argument; the old lead was a chandelier and a dressing area. The four frames it displaced shift down one, 6 to 8 are untouched, and **each caption moved with its own photograph rather than staying with its number** — the copy in `photoCatalog.ts` is keyed by slug, so a rename without that would have silently re-labelled four photographs.

Renames were made across all four derivative trees (`_webp`, `_thumb`, `_lead`, `_mid`) and the thumbnails regenerated. Verified by hashing every new filename against the blob it came from on `main`: all five renames and all three untouched files match.

### More shadow on the hero type

The regrade turned the pool from near-black to pale water directly behind the wordmark and the lede. The measured contrast still cleared AA but it was closer than it had been, and it read soft on screen. Each line now runs a tight dark halo near the glyph plus a wider soft one that darkens the plate behind the whole line.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| lede | 5.36:1 | 5.78:1 |
| label | 7.27:1 | 7.91:1 |
| wordmark | 15.17:1 | 15.37:1 |

Measured off the rendered page, not from the tokens. The scrim gradient was deliberately left alone, so the pool keeps its new brightness everywhere the type is not.

### The one Lighthouse item that was actually low-hanging

The review carousel's dots were **8x6 px tap targets** — the single accessibility failure on the mobile report. The bar still draws at 6 px tall; it now sits inside a 24x24 button, with the horizontal padding replacing the old flex gap so the dots sit the same distance apart. **Lighthouse mobile accessibility 97 to 100.**

Nothing else on the report is low-hanging, and it is worth saying why rather than leaving it looking unexamined:

- **SEO 66** is the deliberate `noindex` while the testimonials are placeholders. Real reviews, or cutting the section, is the only fix — and it is live on the site today.
- **Cache 1,958 KiB and document latency** are the local static server; GitHub Pages sets its own headers.
- **Total byte weight 8.4 MB** is the film, of which one encode loads.
- **The video poster** is 91 KB for 1600x900 and re-encoding it hard only reaches 74 KB. Not worth a quality risk on a frame the video replaces.
- **57 KB unused JS / 30 KB render-blocking CSS** are the app bundle and the stylesheet; neither is a small change.

Verification: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint src scripts` 0 errors with the one pre-existing `react-refresh` warning, build clean. Lighthouse mobile 85 / **100** / 100 / 66 with CLS 0; the desktop run scored 100 with LCP 0.1 s on a quiet machine and 87 under contention, which is the local measurement noise rather than the page.

- An MCP client starts `trg mcp proxy` without a TTY and discards its stderr, so a server that needs OAuth and has no cached credentials surfaces to the user as nothing but a closed connection.
- The error text is the only artifact that survives that path, so it should carry the recovery step and not just the diagnosis. Naming the server makes it a command the user can run as-is.

author: tphuc3519-coder
body:
Mode thứ ba, `tts`: thay vì file nguồn thì gõ chữ, nhận về bản đọc bằng giọng mẫu.

```
song:    input ──► separate ──► vocal ──► convert ──► mix ──► output.mp3
speech:  input ─────────────────────────► convert ──► encode ──► output.mp3
tts:     input.txt ──► synthesize ──────► convert ──► encode ──► output.mp3
```

Điểm chính của thiết kế: **không có model cloning thứ hai**. Bước đọc chữ chỉ tạo ra một bản thu bằng giọng tổng hợp; cái làm nó thành giọng của người dùng vẫn là Seed-VC ở nhánh `speech`, y nguyên code đang chạy. Nhờ vậy pitch auto-detect, chuẩn hoá độ ồn, watermark, consent gate, TTL 6 giờ đều là code cũ chứ không phải bản sao thứ hai. Một TTS zero-shot (XTTS, F5) sẽ làm lại đúng việc mà bước sau đã làm, bằng một bộ weight nữa, một GPU nữa, và phủ ngôn ngữ kém hơn Whisper-small mà Seed-VC đang dùng.

## Tiếng Nhật cần engine riêng — và đây là số đo

Thêm `"jpn"` vào danh sách sẽ ship ra một bản thu trôi chảy của thứ vô nghĩa. MMS đọc chữ ngoài Latin bằng cách romanise với `uroman` trước, và `uroman` đọc kanji bằng **âm Hán ngữ**:

```
今日はいい天気ですね。  ->  jinrihaiitianqidesune.       (đúng: kyou wa ii tenki desu ne)
私の名前は田中です。    ->  sinomingqianhatianzhongdesu.  (đúng: watashi no namae wa tanaka desu)
```

`lcode='jpn'` không đổi gì. Kana thì ổn, kanji thì không — mà văn xuôi tiếng Nhật khoảng một nửa là kanji, và đó cũng chính là văn bản `facebook/mms-tts-jpn` học từ đó. Đưa romaji đúng vào thì lệch phân phối training, đưa output uroman vào thì lệch ngôn ngữ. Không có input nào lấy được tiếng Nhật thật ra.

Nên tiếng Nhật đọc bằng **Kokoro** (`hexgrad/Kokoro-82M`, Apache-2.0, 82M tham số, CPU, một package pip), front end `misaki[ja]` là G2P có từ điển và phân tích hình thái thật:

```
今日はいい天気ですね。   ->  kʲoː βa iː teŋkʲi desɨ ne.
私の名前は田中です。     ->  βatakɯɕi no namae βa tanaka desɨ.
よろしくお願いします。   ->  joɾoɕikɯ oneɡai ɕi masɨ.
```

`tts.synthesize(language, ...)` là chỗ duy nhất biết có hai engine; `pipeline.py` chỉ biết ngôn ngữ.

**Romaji cũng đọc được**, vì không phải máy nào cũng có IME. Kokoro cho chữ Latin đi thẳng qua không đổi, nên `to_kana` chuyển sang kana trước khi cắt câu: `kyou wa ii tenki desu ne.` ra đúng bộ phoneme mà bản kanji cho. Bẫy nhỏ: wapuro romaji viết ん trước nguyên âm là `nn`, mà `jaconv` chỉ đọc dạng `n'` — `konnichiwa` ra こん**い**ちわ, thiếu một mora và thành từ khác; `_ROMAJI_DOUBLE_N` sửa chỗ đó.

## Ba thứ ngôn ngữ này làm vỡ, không liên quan gì tới model

- **Cắt câu** đòi khoảng trắng sau dấu chấm — tiếng Nhật không bao giờ có: 「です。」rồi vào câu kế, cả đoạn thành một "câu" 700 ký tự. `_SENTENCE_END` có thêm nhánh khớp rỗng cho `。！？`, `、` là chỗ ngắt mệnh đề.
- **Giới hạn ký tự** thực ra là giới hạn thời lượng đội sai đơn vị: 2000 ký tự tiếng Việt ~2–3 phút, 2000 ký tự tiếng Nhật hơn 10 phút. Giờ nó nằm trong `Language` (jpn: 700 ký tự, 80 mỗi segment so với mốc cắt cụt 510 phoneme của Kokoro), frontend theo đúng số đó — kể cả ca đổi ngôn ngữ làm đoạn đang gõ vượt giới hạn mới.
- **Bẫy `unidic`**: `misaki[ja]` phụ thuộc `unidic`, package *không* chứa từ điển mà chỉ tải về, và `fugashi` ưu tiên nó hơn `unidic-lite` khi có cả hai → container chết trong `Tagger()` trước khi đọc chữ nào. Image gỡ nó ra.

## Số và ký hiệu không được đọc

Tokenizer làm việc trên ký tự, bảng từ vựng chỉ có chữ cái và dấu câu — chữ số bị bỏ đi không kêu một tiếng, "25 tuổi" đọc thành "tuổi". `check_text` từ chối đoạn không có lấy một chữ cái (nếu không sẽ ra job chạy thành công mà file im lặng), và ô nhập nói thẳng điều đó. Cố ý **không** tự đọc số hộ: "25" là "hai mươi lăm" chứ không phải "hai năm", ngữ pháp số theo từng ngôn ngữ là việc lớn hơn nó trông.

## Riêng tư

Văn bản nằm trên Volume (`input.txt`) chứ không nằm trong job record, để cron 6 giờ xoá nó cùng lúc với audio. Audit log ghi độ dài và ngôn ngữ, không bao giờ ghi nội dung. Trang điều khoản cập nhật mục 1, 4, 6 — đây là chế độ dễ đặt lời vào miệng người khác nhất nên nó được nói rõ, và consent gate áp dụng đầy đủ.

## Kiểm tra

`ruff` + **315 test** (thêm 47), web thì eslint + prettier + tsc + build đều sạch.

Những thứ sau đã **chạy thật** lúc viết code (PyPI tới được từ môi trường này): `uroman` trên tiếng Nhật, G2P của `misaki[ja]` trên chính các segment mà `split_text` sinh ra, `jaconv` cho romaji, lỗi `unidic` và cách sửa, và việc resolve được `kokoro` cùng `torch==2.4.0` + `transformers==4.46.3` + `numpy<2` (numpy giữ nguyên 1.26.4).

`huggingface.co` bị chặn ở môi trường viết code, nên **checkpoint là phần duy nhất chưa từng được nạp**. Danh sách phải nghe bằng tai nằm cuối README mục "Phase 8", quan trọng nhất là:

```bash
modal run -m modal_app.tts --language jpn --text "今日はいい天気ですね。"
modal run -m modal_app.tts --language jpn --text "kyou wa ii tenki desu ne."   # phải nghe giống hệt
```

author: yaoharry
body:
## Related issue

Closes #

## Summary

A skill whose `description:` contains an unquoted colon was silently dropped from every Omnigent menu — even though **Claude Code, which the file was written for, loads it fine**.

Skill authors write `description:` as prose, and prose contains colons. YAML reads `": "` inside a plain scalar as a nested mapping and rejects the whole frontmatter:

```
Skipping skill with bad frontmatter: .../xxx-skill/1.23.5/skills/simplify/SKILL.md:
  SKILL.md has invalid YAML frontmatter: mapping values are not allowed here
  in "<unicode string>", line 2, column 255:
     ... , not code that was just written: finishing an implementation, b ...
                                         ^
```

The user's symptom is an installed skill that just isn't in the `/` menu, with only a runner log line to explain it.

- `_parse_skill` now retries once with colon-bearing plain scalars quoted before giving up.
- **Recovery is deliberately narrow.** A value opening a flow collection, block scalar, anchor/alias/tag, or quote is left alone, as is one carrying a ` #` comment — quoting either would change what the frontmatter *says* rather than recover it. Valid YAML never goes through the rewrite at all (it only runs after `yaml.safe_load` raises), so existing semantics are untouched, and any other malformed frontmatter still raises with the **original** YAML error so the message names the real complaint.
- Continuation lines fold with single spaces, matching YAML plain-scalar semantics, so a wrapped description recovers too.

```
frontmatter ── yaml.safe_load ──✔──▶ spec                    (unchanged path)
                    │
                   ✘ YAMLError
                    │
                    ├─ value opens [ { | > & * ! ' " , or has " #"  ──▶ raise (original error)
                    │
                    └─ value has ": " ──▶ quote it, fold continuations
                                            └─ safe_load ──✔──▶ spec
                                                          ──✘──▶ raise (original error)
```

## Test Plan

Prove-it-fails, then fix:

```bash
# 1. On main, the real upstream description reproduces the production failure:
.venv/bin/pytest tests/spec/test_parser.py -k colon -p no:randomly -q
# OmnigentError: SKILL.md has invalid YAML frontmatter: ...:
#   mapping values are not allowed here

# 2. With the fix — recovery + the still-loud case both pass:
.venv/bin/pytest tests/spec/test_parser.py -p no:randomly -q
# 240 passed

# 3. Whole spec suite, nothing else moved:
.venv/bin/pytest tests/spec/ -p no:randomly -q
# 589 passed
```

Verified against the real production shapes and the edge cases the narrowness depends on:

| frontmatter value | result |
|---|---|
| `description: ... just written: finishing ...` (real `simplify`) | recovered verbatim |
| colon on line 1 + indented continuation line | folded with a space, `user-invocable: false` still parses as bool |
| `metadata:` with nested `type: user`, `tags: [a, b]` | untouched, still a nested mapping |
| `description: a: b # note` | left alone → still raises (comment semantics preserved) |
| `argument-hint: [industry] [--rows N]` | left alone → still raises |
| `description: he said "hi": then left` | recovered, inner quotes escaped |

Manual check for a reviewer: drop a `SKILL.md` into `~/.claude/skills/colon-test/` whose description contains `something: like this`, then run `omnigent --harness codex` (or open the new-session composer's `/` menu). Before: the skill is absent and the runner logs `Skipping skill with bad frontmatter`. After: it appears, description intact.

## Demo

- [ ] Visual demo attached below
- [x] Non-visual evidence provided below or in Test Plan
- [ ] Not applicable — no behavioral change

The production log line is quoted in the Summary; the failing-before / passing-after runs and the edge-case matrix are in the Test Plan.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] UI / frontend change
- [ ] Refactor / chore
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Test / CI
- [ ] Breaking change

## Test coverage

- [x] Unit tests added / updated
- [ ] Integration tests added / updated
- [ ] E2E tests added / updated
- [x] Manual verification completed
- [ ] Existing tests cover this change
- [ ] Not applicable

## Coverage notes

Two new tests: `test_parse_skill_accepts_unquoted_colon_in_description` uses the literal upstream `simplify` description and fails on `main` with the same error as production; `test_parse_skill_colon_recovery_keeps_other_yaml_errors_loud` pins that the flow-sequence case still raises, so recovery can't quietly widen.

`test_discover_host_skills_skips_yaml_syntax_error` had used an unquoted colon to reach the tolerant-skip path — that input is now recovered, so it switches to `_UPSTREAM_BAD_ARGUMENT_HINT` (the flow-sequence case already canonical in this file), which is still genuinely unrecoverable. The strict-bundle test and the multi-bad-skill test are unchanged.

Manual verification covers the edge-case matrix in the Test Plan, which was run against the real parser rather than only through pytest.

## Changelog

Skills whose description contains a colon now load instead of being silently skipped.

author: ea-mitsuoka
body:
## What & why

Closes the ADR-0019 follow-up that asked to re-evaluate the `secure-ai-controls` `paused`
lifecycle. Its reason — "owner-level company account access is unavailable" — predates
the account move and no longer describes reality.

Since the move, all from the company account:

- secure-ai-controls PR #114 caught the repository up from lock `169c17a` (2026-08-02) to
  the parent's `main` at `150a493`, 31 first-parent commits, with all 162 inherited paths
  byte-identical and `finalize-sync` reporting `pending_sync: []`.
- Its scheduled Template Sync runs on its own; the ported single-flight preflight has been
  observed deferring a duplicate dispatch.
- PR #117 hardened its sync boundary; `make doctor` is green on its `main`.

The repository is maintained and synchronized from the account the fleet describes.
`paused` is wrong on both counts, so the entry returns to `active` with a reason that
states what it is rather than why it was once stopped.

Refs: #21

## What `active` changes

`fleet-audit` skips paused entries and only reports them. An active entry is **audited**:
its worktree must exist under `FLEET_WORKSPACE_ROOT`, its contract must validate, and its
manifest parent must match the fleet's `parent_repository`. `propagation-impact` also
starts treating it as a direct child of `terraform-gcp-template`. Both are the intended
effect.

## Change classification (ARC-020)

- [x] Local (inside one module, contract unchanged)
- [ ] Contract (MODULE.md public API / event changed — consumers updated in this PR)
- [ ] Architectural (ADR required — link: )

No new decision — this executes a follow-up ADR-0019 already recorded.

## Breaking change?

- [x] No
- [ ] Yes

## Testing (GR-021 / TST-002)

The pinned fleet tuple in `scripts/tests/test_template_inheritance_plan.py` moves from
`paused` to `active` in the same commit.

- `make fleet-audit FLEET_WORKSPACE_ROOT=/Users/yukihide.mitsuoka/Project`, before → after:
  - `summary`: `active: 3, paused: 1` → `active: 4, paused: 0`
  - `secure-ai-controls`: reported only → **audited**: `pending_sync: 0`,
    `pending_manual_port: 0`, `protected_review: []`,
    `locked_commit == target_commit == 150a493`, parent `ea-Mitsuoka/terraform-gcp-template`
    matches its manifest
- `make doctor` — `doctor: OK — template invariants hold`, `Ran 247 tests ... OK`,
  `context budget: mode=enforced`, `guard-bash.test.sh: 71 passed, 0 failed`
- `make test` — `Ran 247 tests ... OK`

Not verified / read carefully (GR-042):

- **The overall fleet status is still `attention` after this change.** Before, `attention`
  was forced by the paused entry. Now it comes from two *other* active children —
  `terraform-gcp-template` and `nextjs-saas-template` each show `pending_sync: 13`,
  because foundation `main` has moved past the source (`fe57278`) of their currently open
  sync PRs (#9 and #7). That is genuine pending work, correctly surfaced, and outside this
  PR.
- CI has not run yet on this branch.
- This clone had no `.git/hooks/pre-commit` installed, so hooks did not run at commit
  time; `--no-verify` was not used. `mdformat` was run directly on the decision log and
  converged.

## Documentation (DOC-030)

- [x] Doc-update matrix checked; updated: `docs/foundation/inheritance-fleet.json`,
      `.ai/decision-log.md` (LOG-0049)

The decision-log diff is ~83 changed lines for one added row: `mdformat` repads the whole
table when a new row changes a column width. That is the hook's own output, verified to
converge on a second run.

## AI disclosure

- [x] Authored by AI agent: Claude Code (claude-fable-5-1) — self-review against
      `.ai/review-checklist.md` completed
- [ ] Authored by human

## Self-review checklist (WF-090)

- [x] `make format && make lint && make test` green — output reported above
      (`format`/`lint` are template no-ops in this repository)
- [x] Diff within size limits (GR-020) — 3 files; 86/85 lines, of which ~82 are the
      mdformat repad
- [x] Diff contains no unrelated changes
- [x] No guardrail violated (`.ai/guardrails.md`)

author: damont14
body:
## Summary
- Adds the peer-reviewed planning/design packet for **NIS skill catalog resolution** (fixes Codex `/` skill-picker discoverability and the description-budget warning for `nis-close-ss-handoff-intentional`).
- Docs-only in this PR's diff: problem/evidence, requirements, design, architecture, ADR-001, implementation plan, and test/validation/rollback spec, plus the full peer-review packet (request, round-1 receipt: **YES-WITH-FIXES**, placement-correction receipt, blocker-recovery decision/receipt, local catalog reconciliation receipt).
- Adds `AGENTS.md` documenting the repository artifact placement conventions (`docs/superpowers/specs/`, `docs/superpowers/plans/`, `docs/work/reviews/<work-item>/`) that this packet itself follows.
- **Implementation-authorization status is disputed within the packet itself** — see below. Not asserting either side.

## ⚠️ Authorization status contradiction (found by Copilot review, unresolved)
The packet's own documents disagree:
- Round-1 receipt / README (`docs/work/reviews/NIS-SKILL-CATALOG-RESOLUTION-20260824/README.md`, dated 2026-08-24): `implementation_authorized: false`.
- Implementation plan frontmatter (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-24-nis-skill-catalog-resolution-implementation.md`, `last_updated: 2026-08-25`, one day later): `implementation_authorized: true`, `status: IMPLEMENTED_VERIFIED`, under authority `DC-CMD-E000071` / `CMD-E000071`.

This repo has no way to verify which is current — that authority lives in the external Work Control system, not here. Added a reconciliation note to the README surfacing both claims rather than picking one (commit `721bca5`). **A maintainer should confirm the live `CMD-E000071` status before merging.**

## Why this wasn't opened as a PR already
Per the packet's own README, commit/push/PR were deliberately held at the time because three unrelated source-authority hash assertions were red in the full repository test suite — not an issue with this doc set.

## CI fix
Original push failed all 3 checks (`boundary`, `candidate`, `lifecycle-contract`) on `SOURCE_BOUNDARY_FAIL: AGENTS.md unclassified` — `config/source-state-exclusions.json` didn't recognize the new root `AGENTS.md` file. Fixed by registering it in `managed_root_files` (commit `6b45d73`), validated locally against the exact CI commands before pushing. All 3 checks green as of that commit.

## Source
Recovered from branch `codex/nis-skill-catalog-docs-placement-20260824` (originally a single commit, 2026-08-25), which had never had a PR opened against it. Opened as draft — stays draft given the unresolved authorization contradiction above.

author: cesarferreira
body:
## Summary

After merged bottom-of-stack PRs get pruned locally, `stax refresh`/`sync --restack` can hit a rebase conflict for a descendant whose recorded parent branch no longer exists. Resolving that conflict via `stax continue` (or a manual `git rebase --continue` followed by `stax restack --continue`) trusted the on-disk `parentBranchName` verbatim when looking up the fresh parent tip. Since that branch was already deleted, the lookup failed, the metadata write was skipped entirely, and the branch stayed flagged as needing a restack with a stale recorded parent — only self-healing on some later, unrelated sync that happened to succeed cleanly, by which point trunk had already moved on. That's what produced the observed "parentBranchName correct, parentBranchRevision stale/inherited-from-further-up-the-chain" symptom, and the stale boundary made subsequent restacks replay already-merged patches and conflict.

- Added `effective_parent_branch` in `src/commands/continue_cmd.rs`, mirroring the orphan-to-trunk fallback `Stack::load` already applies in memory.
- Used it in both `continue_rebase_and_update_metadata` (the `stax continue` path) and the manual-`git rebase --continue` receipt-recovery path in `src/commands/restack.rs` (`stax restack --continue`), since both trusted the stale on-disk parent name the same way.

## Repro chain (confirmed empirically before the fix)

Stack `main <- json-output <- conflict-report <- dual-role-keys`; `json-output` and `conflict-report` squash-merged into `main` and locally deleted; `stax refresh` hits a real conflict restacking `dual-role-keys`; `stax continue` previously errored with `Branch 'conflict-report' not found` and left metadata stuck at the deleted branch, despite the underlying rebase having already succeeded.

## Test plan

- [x] Added `continue_after_conflict_reparents_orphaned_branch_onto_trunk` (`tests/continue_tests.rs`) — confirmed it fails on pre-fix code with the exact error above, passes after the fix.
- [x] Added `restack_continue_after_manual_rebase_continue_reparents_orphaned_branch_onto_trunk` (`tests/continue_tests.rs`) — covers the parallel `stax restack --continue` recovery path found during review; confirmed it fails on pre-fix code, passes after.
- [x] `cargo check && cargo clippy -- -D warnings` — clean.
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` — clean.
- [x] `make test` — full suite, 2676/2676 passed.

author: qwts-claude-agent[bot]
body:
Closes #171.

## Problem

`publishBootstrapConfig` accepted only a deep-equal config or a roster-scope narrowing (#167). Any evolution of the published organization profile (identities added or retired, harness defaults moved) therefore made every already-bootstrapped machine and dedicated account fail with `profile-config-conflict` on the next bootstrap, with a hand move-aside of `~/.config/agent-bot/config.json` as the only remedy. Seen on MacStudioM2 today: a config projected by 0.2.0 from the 2026-08-24 profile (15 identities, `vscode` default) against the current 29-identity profile.

## Change

- `isProjectedRuntimeConfig(config)` (organization-profile.mjs): true when the config carries the profile snapshot and round-trips through `organizationProfileToConfig(profileFromRuntimeConfig(...))`, scope aside. Such a config is profile-owned.
- `publishBootstrapConfig` rewrites a profile-owned config from the newly published profile in place, keeping its scope (or narrowing from none, as before). Scope removal or change stays a conflict; a scoped App the new profile retired or dropped still fails `profile-app-retired` / `profile-app-unknown` before anything is written; a config without a snapshot, or one that drifted from its snapshot, is never overwritten.
- README: the roster-scope section documents profile evolution and what still fails closed.

## Tests

`tests/bootstrap.test.mjs`: unscoped advance (roster grows, retires, defaults move; mode 600; idempotent afterwards), scoped advance keeps the scope, narrowing and advancing at once, retired and unknown scoped App leave the file untouched, scope change or removal across profiles conflicts, drifted config is not a projection and is left untouched, hand-written config is not a projection. Full suite: 692 pass, 0 fail.

author: enzo-azevedo
body:
Relato de uso real: com `inclusionai/ling-3.0-flash-fin:free`, o pedido "leia o repositório e me faça um resumo" leu 9 arquivos em 3 rodadas e **parou**. Sem resumo, sem erro, sem nada na tela.

## Descartei a hipótese óbvia antes de mexer

Meu primeiro palpite foi estouro de contexto. Medi:

- janela do modelo: **262.144 tokens** (catálogo do OpenRouter)
- os 9 arquivos lidos: **~20.000 tokens**

Não era contexto. Bom ter medido em vez de "consertar" a coisa errada.

## Defeito 1: o raciocínio do modelo era jogado fora

O parser lia apenas `delta.content` e `delta.tool_calls`. Modelos de raciocínio mandam a saída em `delta.reasoning`, `reasoning_content` ou `reasoning_text` — o nome varia por provedor, e nenhum dos três era lido.

Um modelo que coloque a saída no raciocínio produzia **texto vazio** aqui. É um buraco conhecido em parsers OpenAI-compatible: [rig#1440](https://github.com/0xplaygrounds/rig/issues/1440), [koog#2148](https://github.com/jetbrains/koog/issues/2148).

Os três campos agora são acumulados, separados do conteúdo, e não vazam para o streaming da interface (raciocínio não deve aparecer como se fosse a resposta).

## Defeito 2: turno vazio sumia da tela

Quando um turno não produz texto nem chamada de ferramenta, o laço encerrava e a UI não tinha o que renderizar. A conversa parava sem resposta e sem erro — parecendo travamento. **É o pior tipo de falha:** o usuário não sabe se espera, se tenta de novo, ou se algo quebrou.

Agora:

- turno vazio é dito explicitamente, com sugestão do que fazer;
- se houver raciocínio, ele é exibido com um aviso — melhor que nada, e serve de diagnóstico.

O aviso é no laço do agente, não no provedor, então vale para qualquer um — cobre também o caso de o Claude encerrar só com bloco de pensamento.

## Honestidade sobre o diagnóstico

Não posso afirmar com certeza que foi o raciocínio descartado: não tenho o stream original, e o modelo pode simplesmente ter parado. O que posso afirmar é que **as duas condições existiam no código** e que qualquer uma produziria exatamente o sintoma relatado.

A diferença prática: na próxima vez, a extensão vai *dizer* o que aconteceu. Se for raciocínio, você vai vê-lo. Se for parada seca do modelo, vai aparecer o aviso. Nos dois casos, você deixa de olhar para uma tela parada sem explicação.

## Testes

5 testes novos (**148 no total**), incluindo `runAgent` com provedor falso devolvendo resposta vazia — a regressão direta do que você relatou.

```
npm run build   # typecheck + dist/ (v0.3.4)
npm test        # 148 passed
```

## Nota de processo

O primeiro push deste PR saiu de um `origin/main` desatualizado (anterior ao merge do #9), o que fez o bump de versão falhar silenciosamente. Rebaseei sobre a main atual e reescrevi o commit — a branch tinha só esse commit e nenhum PR aberto, então nada foi perdido.

author: victortrinh
body:
## Summary

Adds a full-page cloud background rendered with WebGL2 (via `ogl`, lazy-loaded after idle) that the pointer/finger cuts a fine contrail through, which the deck then closes back over.

Two commits carry the bulk of it:

1. **`style: invert page palette to a near-white ground`** — the site moves from near-black to a near-white ground (daylight sky instead of night sky). `--color-ink`/`--color-paper` keep their names and swap roles. The bright accent fails AA as text on the new background (3.57:1), so a darker sibling token (`--color-accent-ink`, 5.35:1) takes over every text/focus use. Same fix for `text-red-400` → `-700` and `text-amber-400` → `-700`. Dead `prose-invert` classes removed from the four legal pages.
2. **`feat: interactive cloud sky background with mouse/touch wake`** — the effect itself.

The commits after those are visual iteration; the notes below describe where it landed, not the route.

## How it works

**`Sky.astro`** paints a static CSS gradient synchronously — the permanent fallback, and the only thing that exists before JS runs — plus a canvas that fades in once the engine mounts. The wrapper is `pointer-events-none` and `z-[-10]`: it never intercepts clicks and never shifts layout.

**`sky/prefs.ts`** gates loading on `prefers-reduced-motion`, `prefers-contrast`, `forced-colors`, Save-Data, a device heuristic (`deviceMemory`/`hardwareConcurrency`), WebGL2 support, and the visitor's own toggle. Any of these being true means the engine module is **never imported** — not loaded-then-paused.

**`sky/noise.ts`** builds three tiling textures at runtime from one seeded PRNG, each shaped for a different job:

| texture | build | used for |
| - | - | - |
| `placement` | unblurred | the coverage mask — needs full 0..1 range to separate thick deck from thin |
| `detail` | 2 box-blur passes | the shape's warp offset, and the erosion noise |
| `shape` | 4 passes, then contrast-stretched | the cloud masses themselves |

The stretch matters: repeated blurring is repeated local averaging, which compresses a channel's range toward its mean (four passes left one spanning only ~70-190 of 0-255). Without stretching it back, no cloud core can reach a solid tone.

**`sky/engine.ts`** runs three passes per frame:

- **fluid step** into a ping-ponged low-res buffer — advect, dissipate, and splat a disturbance along the segment the pointer travelled, with a counter-rotating vortex pair either side so the wake curls rather than smears. No pressure projection; a decorative wisp field doesn't need Jacobi iterations.
- **cloud pass** at 0.55 of display size. Big smooth masses come from one `shape` read, softly warped; those are cut by the coverage mask, then **eroded** at the edges by fine 3-octave noise. Erosion is the step that makes it read as cloud: because the fine noise is used as the *floor* of a remap, it bites only where the shape is already thin — edges fray into billowy wisps while cores stay solid and perfectly smooth. Blending that detail *into* the body instead is what produced grain in earlier attempts.
- **blit** to the display canvas, which also cuts the wake's clearing line. That cut lives here rather than in the cloud pass for a resolution reason: at 0.55 scale a hairline wake is thinner than one texel and dissolves (measured, a 4px line survived with a peak of 7/255). The soft velocity warp stays in the cloud pass, where something low-frequency belongs.

Every pixel keeps a floor of cloud and the mask's cut is capped, so the deck never opens to bare white — a swipe parts it to haze and stops there.

A rolling frame-time average steps quality down (cloud + fluid resolution → sim rate → give up entirely, fading back to the static gradient for the rest of the session) rather than deliver a janky effect on weak hardware.

A visible toggle sits in the header next to the locale switch, persisted to `localStorage`. It only overrides the *soft* JS-level preferences — an OS-level motion/contrast signal hides the toggle rather than exposing a control that would fight it. Two new `Dict` keys (`skyPause`/`skyResume`) in both locales, per the exhaustive-`Dict` rule in `CLAUDE.md`.

### Two bugs worth flagging for review

- **Fluid buffers were never initialised.** Velocity is stored as `v * 0.5 + 0.5`, so standstill encodes to 0.5 — but a fresh render target is zero-filled, and 0.0 decodes back to **-1.0**. Every buffer began life claiming a full-magnitude `(-1,-1)` velocity, which the cloud pass read as a position warp of roughly a quarter of the screen, sliding back to true as it dissipated. That was the diagonal sweep the sky performed on every page load. Both buffers are now seeded through `FLUID_SEED` on allocation.
- **Wake decay was per sim step, not per second.** The sim runs at 60Hz normally, 30Hz on coarse pointers and as low as 15Hz after the degrade path steps in, so a fixed per-step factor made the wake linger two to four times longer on exactly the devices least able to carry it. It is now a per-second rate raised to the step's duration.

## Verified (Chromium via Playwright, against `npm run dev`)

- `npm run check` and `npm run build` pass; `dist/client/index.html` has `<html lang="fr-CA">` and the three hreflang links.
- Under emulated `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, the engine chunk is requested **0 times** and the canvas stays at opacity 0.
- The engine chunk (`ogl` + our code) is its own async chunk, ~20KB gzip; the `Sky.astro` loader that ships on every page load is ~1.4KB gzip and contains zero `ogl` code.
- **Contrast against the ink foreground**, sampled from real pixels: lightest haze 242/255 → **17.7:1**; typical cloud 217/255 → **14.0:1**; darkest pixel anywhere on the canvas 191/255 → **10.8:1**. All past the 7:1 AAA floor, let alone 4.5:1 AA.
- **No bare sky:** zero pixels at the flat-white ceiling across four aspect ratios.
- **No load animation:** best-shift matching consecutive frames through page load gives 0.0px of apparent travel. Re-introducing the zero-fill bug deliberately gives 5.0px on the same measure, so the test does catch it.
- **Wake:** peak 46/255 against the surrounding deck, ~85% healed 0.7s after the pointer moves on. Measured against a drift-only control band — comparing to a pre-swipe frame alone makes the wake appear to grow back, because ambient drift swamps the signal within half a second.
- `pointer-events: none` confirmed not to block the signup form — filled the email field with the canvas mounted.
- The pause toggle freezes the simulation and its label swaps per locale (`Figer le ciel` / `Pause the sky`).
- All 20 existing vitest tests still pass.

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm run dev`, load `/` and `/en/`, confirm the sky renders and the pointer wake feels right
- [ ] Confirm nothing animates on load beyond the canvas fading in — no drift or sweep
- [ ] Toggle "Figer le ciel" / "Pause the sky" in the header and confirm it freezes/resumes
- [ ] Emulate `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` in devtools and confirm only the static gradient shows, with no WebGL request in the network tab
- [ ] Try on an actual phone/tablet: touch-drag should cut the sky the same way the mouse does
- [ ] Confirm the signup form and footer links are still fully clickable with the sky mounted

author: jadewisemann
body:
The landing that scored 2.8/9 on visual impact is gone. `/` now renders a dark diorama: screenshot frames arranged in depth with the name across them, a corridor the visitor scrolls through, and a footer. Nineteen candidate routes and the entire seam page are deleted.

## What the owner settled, and what it changed

> 포트폴리오는 내 프로젝트를 설명하는 게 아니야. 그냥 뭘 했는지 미적으로 보여주는 거지. 키워드랑 프로젝트 설명이랑 스크린샷 같은 것만 두고, 거기서 별도 페이지에서 아키텍처나 코드 리딩을 보고 하는 구조야.

The landing shows; project pages explain. Six rounds were built and rejected on the way here, and each is on disk under `review/rejected/` with the reason recorded in `DECISIONS.md`. The most expensive detour was rendering the engineering mechanisms — the coverage ratchet, the payment FSM, the two-tier cache — as operating machines, which followed from the ledger having zero images and stopped making sense once the owner said they would supply screenshots. `CLAUDE.md` now records both failure modes with the shape of each, because the second one reads as ambitious and will otherwise be restarted.

## The page

- First viewport is the name and nothing else — `firstScreenChars` is 12 at every breakpoint and the capture pipeline measures it.
- Strong ink 2.00% at 1920 against the rejected slice's 2.42%, and empty bands **0% against 58.3%**. Nearly the same amount of ink; the old page put all of it in a left-hand column and left the right 58% dead.
- 320 is a different composition rather than a reflow.
- Image slots are frames, not placeholders — outer border, mat, panel — so the page reads finished while they hold a plain field. Screenshots will replace the panel and change nothing structural.

Two defects are fixed by geometry rather than by eye. The camera could fly inside a plane and fill the frame with flat interior, so every plane's near edge is held outside a channel around the axis and the camera travels straight down it; intersection is impossible and `layout.test.ts` asserts it. Cutting a fixed tail off the travel to stop it overrunning the field then made scroll progress 100% land on the second project, leaving the third unreachable — the stop point is now the last project's own target.

## Dark is canonical, and there is no second theme

Chosen on what the frames will hold rather than on how they look empty. A screenshot is a bright rectangle: it separates completely on the dark ground and not at all on the kept-paper treatment, which looks best today and is the only one that collapses when real images arrive.

The light branch is deleted rather than kept. Nothing queried `prefers-color-scheme`, no light design existed against the new canon, and a half-maintained theme is worse than none in a repo that has already shipped one invisible-contrast failure. Every ratio recomputed: ink 16.53:1, labels 10.88:1, notes 5.25:1, the frame's panel 15.26:1 and mat 12.27:1, and the rule at **1.92:1** where the old one sat at 1.18:1 — under a floor the same document had set at 1.6:1.

## 3D, with its conditions met rather than promised

`CLAUDE.md` allowed Three.js for explicit scenes while `MOTION_LANGUAGE.md` §1.4 forbade it outright and nothing decided which won. §1.4, §6 and §8 are revised: flat stays the default for page layout, geometry may carry depth inside a declared scene, and the test is whether the depth encodes a fact or decorates a surface.

The hero is the scene, which collides with keeping 3D off the first-paint path, so first paint is a CSS poster whose geometry comes from the same `projectToScreen()` the scene uses — 201 of 1,296,000 pixels differ across the swap. First load for `/` is ~130 KB gzip with no three.js in it; the 234 KB scene chunk stays behind `next/dynamic` and an observer. Idle rAF measured zero. No-JS, no-WebGL and reduced-motion each get a designed static layout, not a hidden scene.

## Harness

The evidence pipeline could not run at all without a Chrome desktop install, and `capture.mjs` killed its server with the Windows-only `taskkill`, so on POSIX a stale server held the port and the next run photographed a page that no longer existed in the source — `HANDOFF.md`'s stale-screenshot trap, mechanised.

The ink metric summed bounding boxes and counted every `svg` whole, scoring ~100% for a full-bleed SVG that painted nothing. It now counts painted pixels from the screenshot, split by contrast, and reproduces the independent critic's hand measurements of the rejected slice: 2.42% strong ink against their 2.48%, 58.3% empty bands against their 58.3%.

`STRUCTURAL_BRANCH` gated on one string in `DECISIONS.md` — the node you reach *because the concept was wrong* let you pick the replacement on paper. It now requires nine rendered PNGs, three at 320px, all newer than `src/`, with three tests locking it shut.

## Deploying

Not connected yet. `docs/portfolio/DEPLOY.md` is the import runbook; the short version is to leave Vercel's build settings empty. There is deliberately no `vercel.json` — for a Next.js project that file exists only to override defaults, and an empty one invites a later reader to treat it as the source of truth.

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs lint, typecheck, unit tests, e2e and `graph doctor` on push and pull request. It does not deploy: Vercel's own integration does that, and a second path would mean a deploy token in repository secrets and no way to tell which path shipped a build.

## Still open

Screenshots. The ledger has none, this container's egress blocks both live demos, and the project repositories carry only badges. `scripts/capture-shots.mjs` and `docs/portfolio/CAPTURE_SHOTS.md` let a local agent with network access capture them; YORR has no deployed URL at all, so it needs the mirror run locally or an honest "not captured".

The corridor's last stretch is thinner than its middle. It clears the floor and is not as good, and the honest fix is more shots per project — so it waits for the images rather than being tuned around now.

Verified: lint, typecheck, 112 unit tests, production build, and 4 e2e specs. One e2e false positive was fixed rather than silenced — the hero deliberately scatters frames past the edges of a container that clips them, and the per-element overflow check counted those while `documentElement.scrollWidth` never exceeded `clientWidth`.

## Summary

Adds PDF → Markdown conversion to the `parser` package, replacing the hand-rolled PyMuPDF pipeline for Markdown generation. Built on `opendataloader-pdf` (benchmark #1 PDF parser), which recovers tables and reading order better than the previous approach.

## What changed

- **`parser/markdown_converter.py`** — new module with two modes:
  - **Hybrid (default)**: simple pages stay on the Java side; complex pages (tables, scanned content, formulas) are routed to a locally running Docling backend (`opendataloader-pdf-hybrid --port 5002`). Free and local — no API keys.
  - **Local**: pure Java processing via `hybrid="off"`; used automatically when the backend is unreachable.
- **Image deduplication** — the hybrid converter can emit the same figure twice (once at the document head without caption context, once inline). The converter now keeps only the last occurrence, so the generated Markdown no longer starts with a cluster of misplaced images.
- **`parser/pyproject.toml`** — adds `opendataloader-pdf>=2.5.0`.
- **Sample output** — generated Markdown + extracted images for one real paper under `claimtrace/generated_markdown/`.

## Tests

- 12 tests in `parser/tests/test_markdown_converter.py`:
  - input validation (missing file, wrong suffix, unreachable backend)
  - local-mode conversion (requires Java 11+)
  - hybrid-mode conversion (auto-skipped when the backend is not running)
  - image deduplication (6 cases)
- Full suite passes with the hybrid backend running; without it: `11 passed, 1 skipped`.
- Tests no longer clear the repository's `generated_markdown` sample output (the default output dir is redirected to a temp dir in tests).

## How to test

```bash
cd claimtrace/parser
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest tests/test_markdown_converter.py -v

# Manual conversion
python -c "from parser.markdown_converter import convert_pdf; print(convert_pdf(r'path/to/paper.pdf'))"

# Optional: start the hybrid backend first (better formulas/OCR/tables)
# Windows (Chinese locale): set PYTHONUTF8=1 first
opendataloader-pdf-hybrid --port 5002
```

## Notes

- Requires **Java 11+** at runtime (the CLI is a JVM app).
- `convert_pdf` clears `generated_markdown` before each default conversion (keeps `.gitkeep`).
- The hybrid backend downloads its models on first start (a few GB, local only, no API key).

author: obrien-k
body:
Closes nothing outright — this is the "21 hand-copied request bodies" task from the session handoff, taken ahead of the next `ui#277` service by Kai's call.

## Why this one, and why now

`src/lib/openapi.ts` described **21 of its 121 request bodies with an inline `z.object({...})` transcribed by hand**, while the other 100 referenced the real `*Schema`. So this is a deviation from the established pattern, not a missing one.

**It is also the only part of the contract problem that can be fixed structurally rather than watched.** A response shape has no artifact to check against — that is why registry errors keep surfacing only when a consumer binds to them. A request body already has one: the Zod validator the route passes to `validate()`, which is what the server actually enforces. Referencing it does not add a gate; it **deletes the drift class**.

## Nine of the twenty were already wrong

| endpoint | was | is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PUT /settings` | **omitted `dismissedLaunchChecklist`** | accepted and written by the route — it was unsendable per the contract |
| `POST /reports` | one flat object, `targetType` an open string, **both** category fields optional | `anyOf` of the two variants `fileReportSchema` actually discriminates |
| `POST /reports/{id}/resolve` | `resolutionAction: string` | the 7-value enum |
| `POST /downloads/{grantId}/reverse` | `reason` **required** | optional, `maxLength 500` |
| `POST /communities/{cid}/dnc` | `comment` **required** | optional, `default: ""` |
| `POST .../releases/{id}/tags` | `name: string` | `minLength 1` / `maxLength 50` |
| `POST /contributions/{id}/access` | — | `idempotencyKey` `maxLength 128` |
| `POST /reports/{id}/notes` | — | `body` `minLength 1` |
| `POST /donations` | `currency`/`source` required-ish | defaults, `format: email`, `format: date-time` |

The `POST /reports` one is the substantial change: the spec permitted a Release report with **no category** and an arbitrary `targetType`, neither of which the server accepts.

**stellar-ui's hand-written `downloadApi` already had `reason?: string`** — so for the **seventh time**, the UI's type was the accurate one and the contract was wrong.

## What did *not* move

The other eleven were faithful transcriptions and emit **byte-identical JSON**. Referenced request schemas are *inlined* by `zod-to-openapi` rather than registered as components, so `components.schemas` stays at **169** and `paths` at **268**. Verified by diffing the whole emitted document with the 21 request bodies removed: **identical**.

## Two exceptions, both deliberate

- **`POST /top10/snapshot` stays hand-written**, and now says why in the source: *there is no schema to reference*. `routes/api/top10.ts` reads `req.body?.type` directly and coerces anything not exactly `'Weekly'` into `'Daily'`, so it accepts any body at all — a live exception to AGENTS.md's "always run `validate(schema)` before the handler". Adding a validator is a behaviour change; tracked separately.
- **`PUT /artists/{id}/vanity-house`** is now referenced, but the route still hand-rolls `.safeParse` instead of `validate()`, so it answers `{ msg }` on a bad body where every other validated route answers `{ errors }`. Changing that is a response-shape change, so it is recorded rather than fixed.

## The schema moves (first commit)

Eight schemas were module-local consts inside route files and could not be referenced at all: **nothing in `lib/` may import from `routes/`** — `routes/api/docs.ts` imports `lib/openapi.ts`, so the dependency would have inverted the layering. They move into `src/schemas/` on the documented one-file-per-domain convention, three into new files, qualified where a route-local name would be ambiguous in a shared namespace (`reportSchema` → `contributionReportSchema`, `commentSchema` → `friendCommentSchema`, `overrideSchema` → `ratioPolicyOverrideSchema`).

**Each is moved verbatim** — no constraint added, removed or rewritten, `z.nativeEnum` kept where the route used it — so validation behaviour is unchanged.

## Downstream: stellar-ui needs a follow-up

`reportsApi.ts` is already spec-typed, so both report changes land on its types.

- `FileReportBody` becomes a discriminated union. `ReportForm.tsx` **already branches Release / non-Release exactly as the union does**, so it should type-check as-is.
- `ResolveBody.resolutionAction` narrows to the enum, and `ReportDetailPage.tsx:60` is `useState('Dismissed')` — inferred `string`. **This will fail `tsc` there**, which is the gate doing its job. One-line fix in a follow-up PR after this merges.
- `downloadApi.ts` already declares `reason?: string` — no break.

## Verification

- `npm run openapi:completeness` — `361 routes served, 361 operations registered, 0 unregistered` (unchanged)
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run typecheck:test`, `npm run lint` — clean
- `npm run test` — **121 suites, 2161 tests, all passing**
- `npm run openapi:export && git diff --exit-code openapi.json` post-commit — **idempotent**
- `npm run changelog:check` — entry present, all 19 base entries preserved
- **Integration is CI-verified** — not run locally (~25–35 min here vs ~1m 30s on CI)

body:
## Scope

Bounded theorem, self-contained (`upstream_dependencies: []`), exact sympy, `PASS=37 FAIL=0`. It documents the composition gap that every matter route since May has ended on, and records two candidate composition clauses as a science-level decision for the owner per `AXIOM_MINIMALITY_POLICY.md` section 4. It amends no axiom, sets no status, and edits no registry.

## Result

- **Same one-site data, two compositions.** On three sites the ungraded tensor product and the graded parity product of the one-site algebras `M_2(C)` both embed every site faithfully, both generate `M_8(C)`, both agree on every one-site even element, and differ exactly in the cross-site relation. Every axiom sentence names one-site data or lattice adjacency, so the composition rule is "a choice not fixed by the supplied structure" in the Qualification's own words.
- **The ungraded product admits no site-local anticommuting family**; a cross-site anticommuting family there is nonlocal and needs a total order and a per-site axis.
- **Every complex grading of the site algebra is an unoriented axis**, no axis survives the 24 proper cubic rotations, and the only rotation-equivariant unital real automorphisms of `M_2(C)` are the identity and the antilinear Clifford involution.
- **Under the graded product with the mode's own parity**: exact CAR with no string; the site order is a representation artifact (one-dimensional even unitary intertwiner space); the ladder fixes its parity axis; every parity-diagonal state annihilates every odd element; the readable one-site content is `span{1, n_x}` with spectrum `{0,1}`.
- **The rotation-covariant real alternative is `Cl(6,0)`**: real dimension 64 against 32, site generators odd, one-site even Hermitian content scalar; its three-Majorana bilinears form a commuting Hermitian spin-1/2 lattice in the even sector.
- **Coexistence.** Both local structures share the same even and odd subspaces of `M_8(C)`; on the `2x2x2` cube at most 7 of 12 nearest-neighbour bonds are string-free under any total order.
- **Selects no state and no Hamiltonian.**

## Decision recorded, not made

Candidate Q (parity composition; author's recommendation) and Candidate C (Clifford composition) are stated verbatim in the note. Neither is adopted here.

## Boundaries

Three sites (two for `Cl(6,0)`). No claim that no derivation of the composition rule exists; no no-go typed; no dynamics, action, mass, generation count, chirality, or gauge content supplied.

author: jat255
body:
Completes `data_source()` with its two remaining forms, over a SQLAlchemy engine and over a pins board. Closes the data-source issue for M2.

## Engine sources

`from_engine()` queries a caller's database directly and copies nothing. With `tables` unset the backend's own listing is taken as given, since it reports what exists. Named tables are checked, because a typo there should fail construction rather than a conversation, and the check is one `UNION ALL` probe rather than a round trip per table, which dominates startup against a remote warehouse.

Absence is asked of the backend through SQLAlchemy inspection rather than inferred from a failed query, so a permissions or connectivity failure surfaces as itself instead of being reported as a missing table. If inspection also fails the answer is inconclusive, and the original probe error propagates.

## Board sources

Pin names are validated in one listing call at construction. Reads are deferred: a table reflects its pin's value at first use and is not refreshed afterwards. A pin leaves the pending set only after its write succeeds, so a network failure surfaces to the caller and is retried on the next touch instead of caching an empty table.

Loading is driven off DuckDB's own catalog error rather than by parsing SQL, so a genuine error such as a bad column surfaces unchanged and each pass either loads a table or stops.

## Specific identifier handling

Handling identifiers surfaced a number of issues during implementation that the agent struggled with, so calling them out here for posterity. Matching a pending label against an error message is fiddly, and five defects came out of review, each reproduced against a live board before fixing:

- **Scanning the message for labels was too broad.** DuckDB echoes the failing statement, so a label appearing only in a string literal triggered a read. Matching is anchored to the head of the message now.
- **Parsing the label out of the phrase needed a delimiter that labels may contain.** A pending `sales does not exist archive` was read as `sales`, so its pin never loaded. Each label is tested against the complete phrase instead, which removes the ambiguity and drops the regex.
- **That in turn let one label match another's error**, since `sales` is a prefix of the longer label up to the trailer. DuckDB names one relation per error, so the longest match is the one it named.
- **Case collisions were unhandled.** DuckDB folds identifiers even when quoted, so `sales` and `SALES` are one table. Board labels differing only by case selected each other, and the frames path failed with a raw DuckDB error rather than a named one. Both paths reject the collision at construction.
- **Folding is ASCII-only, matching DuckDB rather than Python.** `casefold()` maps `ß` to `ss` and merged `straße` with `STRASSE`, which DuckDB keeps apart, as it does `Ä` and `ä`.

`tables` is also no longer an explicit parameter. As one it reserved a frame name, so `data_source(sales=df, tables=df2)` silently dropped `df2`. It is read out of the keywords only when a positional source was supplied.

## Deliberate divergence from `pkg-r`

`pkg-r` has the equivalent built-in-relation check, but no case-collision check, and its pending-table matching searches the whole error unanchored with locale-aware case folding. Treating that as implementation detail rather than aligning the two or pinning it in `tests/shared/`: both differences need a contrived input, and both fail in the safe direction, with Python refusing at construction where R raises a raw DuckDB error later.

## Verification

246 tests, ruff and pyrefly clean. `pins` is a dev-only dependency, since a caller passing a board already has it.

author: mrandreyisachenko
body:
A failing gate is cheap: it names the thing and stops. The expensive kind passes while checking less than its name claims. Three of those were found here within two days — green the whole time — and each is now a rule.

## 1. A skip must be about the environment, not the fixture

A test that skips because this machine cannot run it is honest: nothing was checked and nothing could be. A test that skips because the fixture *it built itself* did not produce the input checked nothing and reads identically.

The eleven environmental reasons in the tree are recorded (Postgres DSNs, the continuous clock, sing-box, group/privilege capability). A new one has to be written down, which is the moment the question gets asked.

Verified against the real case: restoring `t.Skip("no watermarks in this fixture")` fails the guard.

## 2. A shell check that `set -e` reaches first

`cmd` on its own line followed by `status=$?` never reaches the second line when `cmd` fails — errexit ends the script first, so the check is unreachable in the only case it exists for. I wrote exactly that in the archive review test in [#44](https://github.com/mrAndreyIsachenko/hexroute/pull/44).

**The guard tracks errexit state rather than reading the previous line.** My first version looked one line back and flagged six legitimate uses in `operational_acceptance_drill_test.sh`, where `set +e` sits above a command spanning several lines. That was a false positive in my own rule, found by checking it before shipping it rather than after.

Verified: restoring the bare-capture form fails the guard.

## 3. A package where every test can skip still prints `ok`

The same line a package that ran everything prints. `internal/retention` and `internal/databasemigrate` are integration-only by design; each names the gate that does run it, and the guard checks that gate exists in the Makefile.

Verified: making `connectivitytrace` skip throughout fails the guard.

## What none of this can mechanize

The first shape — a test named for surviving a process that never restarts one — needs someone to read the name against the body. No rule catches that.

So the Definition Of Done gains something else instead: **a change records the hypotheses it disproved and what disproved them.** The code keeps the answer that survived and nothing keeps the two that did not, so the next person to meet the same symptom pays for the same measurement again.

Journal eviction did not explain the diverged links. The wake explained one of seventeen. Neither is recoverable from the code today, and both cost hours.

`dod-gate` gains a step and a line in its report. An empty paragraph written to satisfy a checklist is explicitly worse than its absence — it reads as "nothing was ruled out" when the truth is "nobody looked".

## Ruled out

That gate verdicts should be recorded over time, so a model could notice patterns across them. Checked against this week's findings and dropped: all four were **green**, so a verdict log would have recorded nothing. The pattern was in the shape of the tests, not in the outcomes — which is why this is three static rules and not a trend.

author: steipete
body:
## Summary

Restore the staged executable's `0755` permissions after stripping and signing, before strict signature verification. Keep the caller's umask and all signing options unchanged.

During AXorcist 0.1.9 qualification, a fresh-copy Xcode 27 worker diagnostic reproduced `install -m 0755` → `strip` producing `0700` → the ZIP recording `0100700` under `umask 077`. Successful signing alone therefore did not establish the intended distribution permissions. An owner-only executable is unsuitable for a shared installation.

The fix belongs in the universal binary builder, which owns the output-file contract. Four source-only regression cases simulate permission narrowing by strip or signing in both signing modes. They are wired into `make check`; the release documentation explains the distinction between these tests and native artifact verification.

## Validation

- All four regression cases fail on the previous builder with successful commands but output mode `0700`, then pass after the fix with `0755` and the original private umask retained.
- The unchanged offline Commander dependency-policy suite passed on the qualified Xcode 27 worker in 38.55 seconds, including shared/no-cache matrices, repeated resolution, workspace edits and root path overrides.
- The source-only native-AX policy fixture, ShellCheck, shell syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.
- Scoped P0 Codex autoreview completed with no findings.

Two additional local dependency-policy attempts timed out at 180 and 900 seconds. They are retained as failed local observations; the worker result does not explain or erase them. An extra local `make native-only` invocation was stopped after it started an unnecessary debug build; the source-only policy fixture was then run explicitly. No result is claimed for that cancelled build.

The original `0700` archive remains unchanged and is not promoted. A fresh archive must pass the existing permission, signature, architecture and release checks before publication. No release or notarization is performed by this PR.

author: panyaasanee
body:
`COO-DECISION 20260902_0648` ordered **H1** (stop resolving MSVCP90 with `GetModuleHandleW(L"msvcp90.dll")`) and **H2** (`PF_GM_SLOT0_TOUCH_PLUS4` default `0`), and moved `patches/gm_plugin/` into LANE-GM's write zone. `NOW.md` P-3 blocks the owner from building the plug-in until both land on `main`.

Both are done, plus the three-cell build order and stop rule in the README, the `plugin_image_check` step 0 in the build script, and a **GT-P3 draft** for chief to file.

**What changed after that.** pf-adversary refuted the first version of the fix, so what is committed here is **revision 4**; revision 3 never left the working tree:

- **CRITICAL** — searching the client's import table by *symbol alone* returns the first descriptor that imports the name. `??3@YAXPAX@Z` is also imported by MFC90 and by injected modules; the wstring ctor's decorated name is byte-identical across MSVCP80/90/100. So H1 was **not achieved** and the cross-heap free it targets was still reachable, with a green `located` line printed over it. Both lookups now filter on the descriptor's DLL name as well, and the descriptor-name mode verifies the candidate actually exports what we need.
- **HIGH** — all resolution moved out of `DllMain`: `GetProcAddress` on a forwarded export re-enters the loader, and that failure looks exactly like "the DLL was never loaded" on screen — a state the three-cell stop rule can enter and cannot leave. `loaded` is now the first thing `DllMain` prints; the CRT/MSVCP90 lines print at the first `CreateGameMaster` call instead.
- **HIGH** — "the sha256 changed, so the flag reached the compiler" is false for every build (the DLL embeds `__DATE__`/`__TIME__`). The build script now prints the `EXTRA_DEFS` it actually received, and the README/GT ticket name the `[GM_PLUGIN] key=` line as the real control.
- **HIGH** — `PLUS4=0` is written up honestly as a *deliberate divergence* from `GM-IMG-012`'s fallback (which initialises `+4`) on a slot that has a pinned call route, not as "only what the row states". Triage updated accordingly.
- **HIGH** — slot `+0x08` returns the destination, not `NULL`: with `possible_hidden_sret` the caller destroys its own buffer either way, so `NULL` adds a dereference without preventing anything.
- Plus one-call `Announce` (the token the whole test order greps for could be split across DebugView rows), single space in `loaded build=`, checked self-pin, per-reason walk failures, and two documentation defects.

Second, independent piece of the round: consuming ka1-B's letter `20260901_2215` — the missing string tag byte in three of this lane's server codecs (`pirate-force-server` PR, same round).

**ผู้เทสจะทำอะไรได้ที่เมื่อวานทำไม่ได้:** เดิน build สามช่องตามลำดับที่มีกติกาหยุดเขียนไว้ · แยก "DLL ไม่เคยถูกโหลด" ออกจาก "DLL โหลดแล้วแต่ปุ่มไม่เคยเรียกมัน" ได้จากบรรทัด log · และอ่านได้ว่าเราผูกกับ CRT/MSVCP90 instance ตัวไหน แทนที่จะกดหนึ่งครั้งแล้วเงียบพร้อมสาเหตุที่เป็นไปได้ห้าตัว

**nonclaim:** ไม่มีการ compile ด้วย MSVC ไม่มีการโหลด ไม่มีการบูตเกมในรอบนี้ — ABI ตรวจซ้ำด้วย clang กับ `windows.h` ปลอมที่เขียนเองเท่านั้น ตัวที่นับยังเป็น `build_vs2008.bat` check 3/3 บนบริดจ์ · **GM ข้ามขั้นไหน:** ไม่ให้สถานะ GM กับบัญชีใด ไม่มีไมล์สโตนใดขยับ ปุ่ม GM ยังไม่มีหลักฐานใหม่ว่าเปิดได้

author: nstanford5
body:
## Summary

Publishes this repository as a browsable static site on GitHub Pages, closing #28.

Uses **Jekyll** — the de-facto standard for improvement-proposal repos (EIPs, BIPs, and the Cardano CIPs example cited in the issue all use it) — with the **just-the-docs** theme for sidebar navigation and built-in full-text search. Proposal Markdown is rendered **in place**; the repo structure is unchanged (no moving files into `_mips/` collection folders), so the repo remains the canonical source.

Once merged, enable Pages via **Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions**. The site publishes at `https://midnightntwrk.github.io/midnight-improvement-proposals/`.

## What's included

- **`_config.yml`** — theme, `baseurl`, path-based layout defaults, and `jekyll-relative-links` so in-document `.md` links resolve to real page URLs.
- **`Gemfile`** — pins `jekyll`, `just-the-docs`, and `jekyll-relative-links`.
- **`_layouts/proposal.html`** — renders a metadata header (number, Status, Category, Authors, Created, Requires/Replaces) for each proposal. Handles both author formats present in the corpus (YAML list *and* plain string).
- **`index.md`** — landing page.
- **`mips/index.md`, `mps/index.md`** — index tables auto-generated from the proposal front matter (#, Title, Status, Category), sorted by number.
- **`.github/workflows/pages.yml`** — official Jekyll-via-Actions build + deploy on push to `main`.
- **`_sass/custom/custom.scss`** — small theme override so the wrapping sidebar title isn't clipped.
- **`.gitignore`** — ignores build artifacts (`_site/`, `vendor/`, caches).

## Content fixes needed to render

Building the site surfaced front matter that Jekyll couldn't use. Minimal, targeted fixes:

- **Front matter added/relocated (7 proposals):** `mip-0013` and `mps-0032` had valid front matter placed *after* the license comment (Jekyll requires it at the top) — relocated, and quoted a `Requires:` value with a colon. Five legacy MPSs (`mps-0005/0008/0009/0010/0011`) had a plain-text note instead of key/value front matter — replaced with proper front matter, preserving the original note as a body blockquote.
- **Number normalization (14 files):** unquoted values like `MIP: 0005` were parsed as integers, dropping the leading zeros (they displayed as `1`–`7`). Quoted them as 4-digit strings (`mip-0001`–`0009`, `mps-0002/0003/0004/0006/0007`).
- **Category rendering (2 files):** `mps-0018` and `mps-0027` had a `|` in the Category value, which spawned a stray column in the index table — removed the pipe.

Line endings were preserved throughout (`mip-0008` is CRLF).

## Preview locally

```bash
bundle install
bundle exec jekyll serve --baseurl "/midnight-improvement-proposals"
# → http://localhost:4000/midnight-improvement-proposals/
```

## Notes / possible follow-ups

- **`deployments/`** records have no front matter and are excluded from the site for now (they'd otherwise ship as raw Markdown). Adding front matter would let them render.
- **Templates** are excluded from the site and linked to GitHub instead.
- For the five legacy MPSs, `Authors`/`Created` were left out (unknown in source) and **Category values are best-guess** — worth a maintainer sanity-check.

Closes #28

author: sboyce80-lang
body:
Three customer-facing onboarding gaps.

## 1. Welcome email said "Knight Shift"

Subject, opening and signature now say **KnightShiftAI**, and the email lists the two support contacts. New env-overridable constants `SUPPORT_CONTACT_EMAIL` (admin@) and `FOUNDER_CONTACT_EMAIL` (steve@).

## 2. Waitlisted signups got a one-line note

Free-email-domain signups don't auto-approve, so they got nothing at signup and only a terse "your access is approved" when an admin confirmed them. `admin_orgs_approve` now sends the real welcome.

That path deliberately sets `plan="beta"` (no quota), so `notify_welcome` takes `bid_limit=None` and swaps in unlimited wording rather than promising 5 free bids it wouldn't honor. `notify_freemium_welcome` is kept as an alias for the signup path; `notify_user_of_approval` is now unused by web_app but left defined.

## 3. Both forms advertised the wrong upload limits

`index.html` and `mobile.html` hardcoded "600 MB each / 25 files" — the paid limits — while freemium orgs are enforced at 5 files / 100 MB. A free user was told one limit and rejected under another.

The plan branch moved out of `_freemium_upload_caps` into a pure `_upload_caps(is_freemium)`, so rendered copy and the API gate read the same numbers. `/mobile` had no template context at all and now resolves the signed-in snapshot.

## Plus

- New public `/guide` page (first-bid walkthrough, what each of the six tabs does, free-plan rules), linked from the welcome email. Un-gated deliberately — auth is per-route here, and a new user may open the link before signing in.
- The welcome now sends **multipart**. Gmail rewrites bare URLs in `text/plain` into `google.com/url?q=` redirects and shows that redirect as the visible link text, so the old email led with two lines of tracking cruft. `_send` takes an optional `html_body`; the HTML part uses labelled anchors. `font-family` is declared on every text node — clients don't inherit it, and unset renders serif.

## Verification

- `/`, `/mobile`, `/guide` all render 200
- `_upload_caps` returns `(25, 600)` paid, `(5, 100)` freemium
- Both welcome variants render clean and go out multipart
- HTML part rendered in a browser before sending
- `test_plg_freemium.py` has 3 failures (`no such table: organizations`) that reproduce on the pristine baseline — a test-harness DB gap, not this change

Rebased onto `main` at 3672376; the `notifications.py` line from #61 survives intact.

# O que mudou?

Este PR refatora as imagens Docker do backend e frontend do APAE Geral, padronizando o processo de build e os runtimes conforme a estratégia adotada nos demais produtos APAE.

As alterações têm como objetivo reduzir a superfície de ataque, melhorar o tempo de build, diminuir o tamanho das imagens, tornar os builds mais reproduzíveis e preparar os serviços para publicação no GHCR e execução em Kubernetes/K3s.

## Tarefas Relacionadas

* Issue: IFPBEsp/APAE-INFRA#25
* Outras dependências: N/A

* Refatoração do Dockerfile do backend:
  * remoção de `dependency:go-offline`;
  * adoção de cache Maven com BuildKit em `/root/.m2`;
  * remoção de `clean` no build;

* Mantida compatibilidade com o estado atual do frontend, que não possui `package-lock.json` versionado:

author: byeongsu-hong
body:
## What changes

Two more steps on the compiler-inserted component memo from #807, plus the docs for them.

**A row component is a boundary now.** A use whose argument was a `for` or keyed row, or a `match` payload, was refused ("reads a row local"). The row is a function of the list its view iterates, and the payload of the value its match takes it from, so the memo fold now keys on that expression's revisions — chasing an outer row's list on up when the list is itself a row. This is the compiler's key only: `lazy` over a row still hashes the row, so a prepend rebuilds one row rather than the list. On trading every row component (`OrderRow`, `PositionRow`, `AlertRow`, `BookRow`, `Stat`, `VenueTab`, …) became a boundary; the only refusals left are inside `lazy` bodies and a clock-driven flash.

**A held key skips the diff below it.** `rev_memo` skipped its layout while the key held but still let iced diff every node below it on every pass, and on a dense screen that walk is a large share of the build. With the same site and the same revisions the element below is the one the tree was last walked against, so `diff` now returns at the memo. A body holding a `lazy` is refused, since a lazy hands its cached element to each new instance in `diff` and is its own boundary anyway.

**A memoized use keys on what its inputs bind.** CI caught a hole the diff skip exposed: an `input`'s `<->` binding is a read the widget makes outside any expression, and the fold walked expressions only, so a component showing its own `draft` through a binding was keyed on everything but `draft`. Showcase's `component_state` render contract froze the accessibility value at the first keystroke. The fold now adds the bound place's revisions (`memo_keys_a_use_on_what_its_two_way_binding_reads`, Red → Green); a secret binding refuses the memo.

User-visible effect: an idle or lightly changing frame on a screen built from components does less work per frame; nothing changes in what is drawn.

## Measured (release, private target dir, `Driver::redraw_phases().layout` = `UserInterface::build`)

Trading dense terminal, idle frame diff + layout:

| step | diff + layout | memo hits |
|---|---|---|
| main (#808) | 1202us | 68 component / 57 lazy |
| row components keyed on their list | 1202us | 113 / 57 |
| held key skips the diff below | 1074us | 113 / 57 |

The row memos hit without moving the number because the layout under a trading row is small; the diff skip is what paid.

## Evidence

Codegen (`memo_*` tests, Red before / Green after): `memo_keys_a_for_row_on_the_list_it_iterates`, `memo_keys_a_keyed_row_on_the_list_it_iterates`, `memo_keys_a_match_payload_on_what_it_matches`, `memo_keys_a_row_of_a_nested_for_on_both_lists`, `memo_skips_a_body_that_holds_a_lazy`; `memo_skips_a_use_whose_argument_is_a_lazy_alias` keeps the lazy alias refused. The `lazy-component-context` compile fixture now expects the memo wrapper around the use under `for`.

Runtime: `a_held_key_skips_the_diff_below_and_a_moved_one_walks_it` — Red against the previous `diff` (`a held key must not diff the child: left: 2, right: 1`), Green after.

## Commands run

```
cargo test -p ui-lang-core
cargo test -p ui-lang-core performance_contract -- --ignored --test-threads=1
cargo test -p ui-lang-runtime --lib
cargo test --release -p trading-example -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1 frame_probe::frame_cost frame_probe::frame_panels
cargo clippy -p ui-lang-core -p ui-lang-runtime --all-targets --no-deps
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```
