author: shieldrj
body:
Turning the overlay off meant leaving the map, opening the app and finding the switch — while driving, which is the one situation the card exists for and the worst one to ask that in.

A **✕** in the card's top-right corner now dismisses it. Drawn in `HudContent`, hit in `OverlayHost.DragHandler`, because this window has a single touch listener that already owns drag, tap and long-press — a `clickable` inside the composition would never see the event. `CLOSE_TARGET_DP` keeps the drawn glyph and the hit region in agreement.

Three details that decide whether it works in a moving car:

- The target is **44dp**, not the size of the glyph. The glyph has to be small (the card is 128dp wide, over a map being navigated by); the thing being aimed at is a dashboard in a moving car.
- Whether a gesture started on the cross is decided **on the way down**, so sliding off before lifting can't turn a miss into a dismissal.
- It's tested **before** the long-press branch, so resting a thumb there dismisses the card rather than cycling its theme.

Dismissing writes the preference as well as the flow — the same pair the in-app switch writes — because a card that returns on the next drive hasn't been dismissed.

417 tests pass, 0 failures.

author: mark-torres10
body: # Switch preprocess to skip then collapse ## Summary Preprocess loads ids from every prior preprocessed run before it creates the new run directory, drops those ids with pandas, then collapses remaining ids so the later raw row wins. The printed skip count is prior-run ids only. It does not include rows removed by collapse. ## Purpose Skip and collapse used to share one helper, and the skip set was loaded by passing the preprocessed stage root as if it were a run directory. Callers now load all prior preprocessed ids first, drop known ids on the table, then collapse remaining ids in a named helper on the preprocess runner. Ingest, warmup deletion, and the stimuli runbook stay out of this PR. Plan: `docs/plans/2026-09-02_switch_preprocess_to_skip_then_collapse_d2084b/` ## Architecture Components: - `preprocess_records` — loads the all-runs skip set, drops known ids, collapses remaining ids, then transform, filter, and save. - `collapse_candidates_by_id` — one row per id on the preprocess runner, later row wins. Not a skip-set session method. - `Skip-set session` — `load_seen_ids_from_all_runs` only. Preprocess does not call exclude or extend. - `save_preprocessed` — still creates the new run directory. The skip set is loaded before that call. Existing flow: ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph before [Before] Warm["Load skip set with warmup"] Combined["Skip and collapse in one helper"] Save["Save"] Warm --> Combined --> Save end ``` New flow: ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph after [After] Load["Load all prior preprocessed ids"] Drop["Drop known ids with pandas"] Collapse["Collapse remaining ids, later row wins"] Save2["Save"] Load --> Drop --> Collapse --> Save2 end ``` ## Interfaces ### Skip then collapse After the raw-run gate, preprocess constructs a skip-set session with the id column only, then calls all-runs load on preprocessed storage. It never passes the stage root as a run directory, and it never passes the prior-runs flag. Known ids are dropped with pandas membership on the id column. Remaining ids collapse with `keep="last"`. `row_counts.input` is still the length after skip and collapse, and before filters. Print shape: ```text preprocess_records: kept {n} of {m} {noun} (skipped {skipped} already in a prior preprocessed run) -> {output_dir} ``` ## How to run ```bash PYTHONPATH=. uv run pytest tests/data_platform/preprocessing tests/data_platform/utils/test_deduplication.py -q ``` Expected: exit 0. ```bash rg -n "_drop_already_preprocessed" data_platform tests ``` Expected: no matches. ```bash rg -n "include_prior_runs|\\.warm\\(" data_platform/preprocessing ``` Expected: no matches. Fixes #70 Part of #67

author: urbicon
body:
Closes #346.

The issue reported four measured-wrong statements in the two documents a library developer reads first, plus one wrong JSDoc. It predates #343, #353, #360 and #367 — all of which rebuilt this exact layer — so the first work was measuring, not repairing.

### The measurement, before anything was touched

| claim | verdict |
| --- | --- |
| `class` is not the last rung of the cascade | **already fixed** by #353 — `override-precedence.test.ts` now pins the opposite |
| `class` attributed to the `resolveSlotClasses` call | **still stood** — the signature takes no `class` |
| "every component family resolves through the shared resolver" | **still false, different set** — the ten the issue listed are not today's exceptions |
| "entries match active prop values, not the internal variant structure" | **already fixed** by #343 — the phrase matches nowhere any more |
| "exactly two components carry a hand-maintained slot union" | **count fixed, enumeration incomplete** — Calendar's 66-member union became an alias; `Guide` and `SidebarLayout` were never named |
| `PaginationItem.class` "on the button element" | **still false** — measured by mounting both branches |

Two of five would have been fixes for defects that no longer existed. Three more statements had gone wrong *since* the report, all from #360 and #367, and are corrected here — same defect, younger.

### Two counts are gone rather than updated

"Every component family resolves through the shared resolver" is now the three **shapes** that do not: a wrapper (which resolves indirectly), `CalendarHeader`/`FormField` (which declare a `slotClasses` prop and read it from elsewhere, so a provider entry type-checks, narrows, and arrives nowhere), and `PaginationItem` (no provider name at all). "Exactly two hand-maintained unions" is now the two shapes that produce a hand-written slot name.

A count goes stale on the next component; a condition does not. And the authoritative half is derived in `provider/component-slots.ts` since #367, so listing it here would be a second copy.

### Two code changes

`PaginationItemProps.class` said "on the button element". With `href` no button in the tree gets it — the class is on the wrapping `<a>`.

`SidebarLayout` maps five `sidebar*` keys onto the embedded Sidebar's own slot names and nothing checked the target half: renaming `panel` to `panelTYPO` compiled and landed nowhere. An annotation on the binding does **not** close it — measured: the object is an argument to `$derived`, so no contextual type reaches the literal, and it arrives at the child as a variable, where excess-property checking no longer applies. `satisfies` on the literal does; the typo is now a compile error.

### Not done

`PaginationItemProps.unstyled` ("so only `class` remains") is arguable rather than false in the `href` branch, and `CopyButton` conforms — its root *is* the Button.

Gates: `lint`, `imports:lint`, `build:ts`, `types:guard`, `check` (0 errors, all packages), blocks 6987 tests, `docs:gen:all`, `summary:lint`, docs-app 241 tests, `size --check` — all green.

author: bwsalmon
body:
ask_question and comment_on_issue did nothing on a real run. The agent
called them, the mcpserver recorded them, and then the question was
never asked and the closing comment never posted: the run was written
off as no_action instead.

Both frameworks drive a CLI that namespaces an MCP server's tools by the
key it loaded the server under, so a call comes back reported as
"mcp__grain-sandbox__ask_question" -- a prefix grain itself writes onto
--allowedTools. Each transcript parser recorded that name verbatim into
agent.ToolCall.Name, while ProcessResult decides what a run asked for by
comparing that field against "ask_question", "comment_on_issue" and
"propose_task" exactly. It matched none of them, on every real dispatch,
silently: a run that stopped to ask a human ended with no comment
relayed and no PendingQuestionCommentID parked, so nobody was asked and
nothing said why.

Every test of the path scripted the bare name -- the e2e harness, the
orchestrator's own finish tests, and both parsers' -- which is why the
suite stayed green over a path that had never once worked outside it.
v1 had no equivalent bug because it never matched on a reported name at
all: the tool wrote a file and core.py read it back.

Put both halves of the convention in pkg/mcp, where the tools it names
are registered, and have each framework take the prefix back off before
recording a call -- agent.ToolCall.Name is the tool's identity, not one
CLI's spelling of it, which is now what its doc comment says. The
transcript narrative loses the prefix with it, so a reader sees the tool
the agent called.

Tests use the prefixed name a real CLI actually emits, in both parsers,
and assert on the exact names ProcessResult matches; all four fail
without the fix.

body:
> **[foreman-lite · Worker]** task: fix-trait-call-site-pol-mtjo91sy

## Summary
- add the exact recursive `JV` repro plus a focused matrix covering non-recursive mixed instances, repeated same-instance calls, the existing match-arm boundary, and ordinary let-polymorphism
- stop concrete constrained results such as `Bool given a implements Eq` from resolving the unrelated trait input variable to `Bool` during unification
- preserve independent call-site substitutions without special-casing `Eq` or touching higher-kinded trait slot handling

## Root cause
`typeVariableExpr` already instantiated each trait identifier occurrence independently; the suspected metadata re-fetch was not the failing mechanism. The corruption happened later when `&&` unified each call result (`Bool given <input> implements Eq`) with concrete `Bool`: `unifyConstrainedWithConcrete` treated the result type as if it were the constrained input and wrote `<input> := Bool`. In the surrounding list callback, later tuple inference then collided with those overwritten String/JV/Float substitutions. Concrete constrained result bases now unify directly, so their unrelated input constraints cannot rewrite lambda substitutions.

## Validation
- `AGENT=1 bun test src/typer/__tests__/trait-call-site-polymorphism.test.ts` — 5 pass
- `AGENT=1 bun test` — 1471 pass, 8 skip, 0 fail

## Deliberate scope choices

Acquisition recovery creates a reviewed authoritative successor via `fork --resume-through discover` while reusing verified discovery and artifact bytes. It does not edit a frozen generation or inherit scientific approval. Large files that exceed the explicit ceiling receive an early stop/provider-subsetting path; this change does not add unlimited streaming or unverified external references. Metadata-only and unparsed binary sources cannot count as potential atom-based role coverage. An incomplete acquisition audit may still be retained with an honest inference stop.

## Validation

- regressions observed RED then GREEN in independently created clean Docker runtimes; intermediate test and fix commits retained
- final integrated CLI 0.0.58 cold container: 590/590 tests pass, no skips; lint, typecheck, build, and coverage pass
- independent review found and drove additional RED/GREEN tests for receipt replay, unknown usage, wall reservation, Policy Markdown, atomic recovered submission, smoke readiness, and same-dimension metadata-only forecast eligibility

No default token budget is increased; byte ceilings remain generous and finite. author: macanderson
body:
## What & Why

#2602 declared `ONTOLOGY_READ_CAPABILITIES` and added the `toolPolicy.ontology` flag, then merged with one definition-of-done item unmet: no document described either. `dod-close-guard` reopened #2601 eleven seconds after that merge, and an [earlier sweep](https://github.com/macanderson/oxagen/issues/2601#issuecomment-5493574858) verified three of the four reopening items and confirmed this one is real:

```
$ grep -rn "toolPolicy.ontology\|ONTOLOGY_READ_CAPABILITIES\|withOntologyReads" docs/ apps/docs/ README.md
(no matches)
```

That sweep deferred writing it because documenting `toolPolicy.ontology` means deciding where the section lives. Per SCR-002 that is a call to make, not a question to ask, so this PR makes it:

- **`docs/capabilities/_ontology-read-set.md`** (new) — the set gets one page rather than eight near-identical paragraphs: the membership table, why traversal and lookup travel together, how a narrowed run opts in, what keeps the set read-only, and what the flag deliberately does not do.
- **The eight capability pages** point at it from `## Related`. `graph.node_label.get.md` gains that section, which it did not have.
- **`docs/specs/agent-engine-v2/spec.md` §4.4 "Tool plane details"** — the doc describing how tools reach a turn, so the set is named there beside the tool-plane bullets it belongs with.
- **`docs/capabilities/_index.md`** points at the new page from its intro.

Closes #2601

## Vision Alignment

Neutral-to-advancing. No product surface changes — but the subject is **graph grounding**, and the reason the set was declared at all is that an agent's access to the business graph should be a stated guarantee rather than a side effect of which contracts happen to carry the `agent` surface. Documenting it is what makes that guarantee legible to the enqueuer who has to opt into it.

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm gate` passes locally — **not run, stated plainly.** This container has no `node_modules`. The diff is Markdown only and touches no package the gate compiles, lints, or tests; CI on this PR is the authoritative gate.
- [x] New/changed logic has unit tests; coverage ratchets hold — N/A, no logic changed.
- [x] New capability ships the full parity stack — N/A. No capability is added, renamed, or removed. All eight already have `docs/capabilities/` pages, and the [earlier sweep](https://github.com/macanderson/oxagen/issues/2601#issuecomment-5493574858) confirmed `check:manifest` reports no gap for any of them.
- [x] User-facing changes have E2E tests with screenshots — N/A, docs only.
- [x] LLM calls / DB access conventions — N/A, no code touched.
- [x] Dep changes — none.
- [x] Env var changes — none.
- [x] Migrations — none.

## Verification

**Every claim in the new page was read out of the source, not inferred from another document.**

| Claim | Checked against |
|---|---|
| The eight members and their order | `ONTOLOGY_READ_CAPABILITIES` in `packages/agent/src/runtime/ontology-tools.ts` |
| `"version": 1` in the run-spec example | `LEGACY_RUN_SPEC_VERSION = 1`, `packages/agent-runner/src/run-spec-v1-legacy.ts` |
| `toolPolicy.ontology` is a real, optional, defaults-off field | `legacyToolPolicySchema` — `ontology: z.boolean().optional()` |
| The driver reads it | `turn-driver.ts` — `withOntologyReads(…, spec.toolPolicy?.ontology === true)` |
| Inert when no allowlist is declared | `withOntologyReads` returns `undefined` for an `undefined` allowlist |
| The read-only admission rules | `ontologyReadViolation` / `assertOntologyReadOnly` |
| Traversal needs a start node the lookup half supplies | `ONTOLOGY_READ_CAPABILITIES`' own doc comment, and `startNodeId` being required in `ontology.query.md`'s input table |

**Links resolve.** All eight table links, the spec's `../../capabilities/_ontology-read-set.md`, and the index link were each resolved against the filesystem — 10 of 10 exist.

**Prose.** The page carries no count of the set in running text (the table is the count), and cites code by symbol rather than by line number, so neither drifts when the set or the file changes.

### One thing deliberately left out, and why

`toolPolicySchema` in `run-spec-v2.ts` is `.strict()` and carries `allowlist` + `risk_ceiling` with **no `ontology` key**, while the v1 legacy schema the turn driver actually reads does carry it. That is either a deliberate v2 scoping decision or a gap in the v2 spec, and I could not tell which from the code alone. This PR documents the shipped v1 path and makes no claim about v2. Flagging it rather than guessing — if it is a gap it wants its own issue, and I did not file one on a judgement I could not settle.

author: davidhouweling
body:
## Context

`/stats player` and `/stats compare` were reported as noticeably slow. Both compute a per-metric leaderboard rank for every displayed stat (~16 metrics for the default aggregation), and `/stats compare` does this for two players.

## This PR

Investigated using `wrangler d1 execute --remote` (read-only) against `prod-db-guilty-spark` to measure real query cost rather than guessing.

**Root cause:** `getLeaderboardPlayerMetricRank` ran one full-population aggregate-and-rank query **per requested metric, per player**. For `/stats compare` that's ~32 independent full scans per interaction. Measured directly: one such query for a single metric took **501ms and read 233,894 rows**, of which a correlated per-row Gamertag identity subquery (re-executed once per distinct player in scope, on every single metric query) accounted for ~60% of that cost — removing it alone dropped the same query to 200ms / 93,243 rows.

**Fix:**
- Replaced `getLeaderboardPlayerMetricRank` (one metric) with `getLeaderboardPlayerMetricRanks` (a full metric list), splitting requested metrics into stat-family (game-fact based, e.g. Kills, DamageDealt, objective metrics) and outcome-family (series/game win-loss based) subsets and issuing **at most one query per subset** instead of one query per metric. Each query computes every requested metric's value once in a shared `agg` CTE, then ranks each metric independently via its own `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY <per-metric eligibility>)` / `SUM(<eligibility>) OVER ()` pair — preserving the exact existing per-metric eligibility rules (objective-category-specific games-played thresholds, etc.), just computed from one population scan instead of N.
- Removed the correlated Gamertag identity subquery entirely from both rank queries. `LeaderboardPlayerMetricRank` is only `{rank, total}` and never exposed gamertag — callers already have each player's real gamertag from `getLeaderboardPlayerStats`.
- `LeaderboardService.getLeaderboardPlayerMetricRanks` now delegates straight to the batched DB method instead of its own per-metric `Promise.all` loop.
- Investigated a suspected `LeaderboardGames` index mismatch (queries filter `EndedAt`, only index is on `StartedAt`) as a third fix, but `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` showed this access pattern is driven by the `LeaderboardGamePlayers` index with `LeaderboardGames` joined by primary key, so that index would not be used here — no schema change made.

**Verified against production**, correctness and performance:
- New single-metric query for Kills returned the *exact same* Rank/Total as the old query (10/173), now reading ~94k rows instead of ~234k.
- A 4-metric batch (Kills/Deaths/PersonalScore/MedalPoints) in **one query read 96,168 rows total** — essentially the same cost as ranking a single metric alone, versus ~936k rows for the old per-metric approach on the same 4 metrics. This ratio only improves as more metrics are requested (the full ~16-metric case per player).
- The outcome-metric batch (SeriesWinRate/GamesWinRate) was verified separately, returning correct, plausible ranks in one query.

Out of scope / unaffected (confirmed via `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`): `getLeaderboardPlayerPairRelationship` (compare's "Head to head" page) and `getLeaderboardPlayerRelationships` (`/stats player`'s top-10 relationship views) are already narrow, indexed point-lookups, not part of this problem.

Full test suite passes: 124 files, 2438 tests, 1 pre-existing skip. `npm run done` clean (one pre-existing Astro hint unrelated to this change).

## Subsequent work

- None identified; the head-to-head and relationship-view query paths were already efficient.

body:
This repository has no workflows. Nothing has ever been checked automatically,
and the release that fixes two use-after-free windows has been sitting on
master unpublished while `worktable 1.0.0-beta.16` resolves the unsound 0.1.0.

Four jobs, modelled on `WorkTable/.github/workflows/rust.yml` so the two read
the same way: build and test, format and clippy, Miri, and publish.

## Doctests are a separate step

`--all-targets` silently skips doctests, and the `compile_fail` doctest on
`Guard` is the entire enforcement of `!Send`. A green build that never ran it
would look exactly like a green build that did, which is precisely how the auto
trait applied unnoticed in 0.1.0.

## Miri runs with strict provenance

A native test run cannot observe the reorderings this crate's correctness rests
on. Strict provenance specifically is what rejected the integer round trip the
packed guard was first written with, so a pass without that flag proves less
than it looks like it does.

## Publish

On a push to master, if the version in `Cargo.toml` is not already on the
index, publish it. Same shape as WorkTable's job, minus the codegen twin.

`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` is **not set on this repository**, and the job exits
successfully when it is unset, so merging this publishes nothing today. Once
the secret is added, master carrying a new version is the release, and merging
this then makes 0.1.1 live.

## Verified locally

`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
`cargo test` (8 contract tests plus the compile_fail doctest), and
`MIRIFLAGS=-Zmiri-strict-provenance cargo +nightly miri test`, all clean at
`d207d06`. Opening this PR is the first time any of it runs off a laptop.

author: mediaconceptllc
body:
Аудитын №1 ба №2. Хоёулаа нэг хэвшинжтэй: арифметикийн хувьд боломжтой утга, алдаа өгөхгүй, ба системийг **хэн ч мэдээлдэггүй** төлөвт үлдээдэг.

---

## №1 — Тэг урттай segment (`backend/app/models.py`)

Танигчийн буцаасан үгийн эхлэл, төгсгөл нь ижил агшин байвал segment нь **тэг секундийн** үнэтэй болно. SRT бичигч `00:00:12,340 --> 00:00:12,340` гэж гаргах ба ямар ч плеер түүнийг харуулахгүй; cut төлөвлөгч нь огтолж боломгүй нэгж авна.

**ХЭМЖИГДСЭН:** production дээрх 9 минутын нэг транскрипт өөрийн 54 огтлох нэгжийн дунд `shortest 0.0s` гэж бүртгэсэн.

Шалгалт нь builder бүрд биш **`Transcript` дээр**:

| Segment үүсгэдэг зам | Хамрагдав уу |
|---|:--:|
| `segments_from_words` (танигчийн үгийн цаг) | ✅ |
| `synthesize_segments_from_text` (тэмдэгтийн эзлэх хувиар) | ✅ |
| `merge_transcripts` (chunk тутмын үр дүн offset-той нийлүүлэх) | ✅ |
| дараа нь нэмэгдэх дөрөв дэх нь | ✅ |

Транскрипт **УГСРАГДДАГ** цэгт засвал дээрх бүгд, ба дараагийнх нь, хэн нэгэн санахгүйгээр хамрагдана.

**Үг хэзээ ч хаягдахгүй.** Хэн нэгэн тэдгээрийг хэлсэн — транскриптыг арифметикт алдах нь богино cue-гээс дор. Төгсгөл нь зөвхөн УРАГШ түлхэгдэнэ, дараагийн segment эхэлсэн газраас хэзээ ч цааш биш — тиймээс юу ч давхцахгүй, юу ч эрэмбээ алдахгүй. Огт зай байхгүй segment (дараагийнх нь ЯГ тэр агшинд эхэлсэн) хэвээр үлдэнэ: **байхгүй цагийг зохиохоос үнэнээр нь хэлэх** нь дээр.

## №2 — Хөдлөхгүй forced cut (`stt/chunking.py`, `audio/vad_chunking.py`, `config.py`)

Хоёр chunker хоёулаа завсар цагтаа ирэхгүй бол cursor-оо `max_chunk_sec - FORCED_CUT_OVERLAP_SEC`-ээр урагшлуулна. Давхцал нь тогтмол; таазыг `DUUDLAGA_MAX_AUDIO_SEC` шийднэ. Түүнийг 0.4с ба түүнээс доош тавибал **cursor зогсоно, атал давталт `append` хийсээр байна**: төгсгөлгүй давталт бөгөөд санах ойг ч иднэ.

Хамгийн муу нь — тэр нь worker thread дотор эргэлддэг тул:

- ажлын heartbeat **цохилсоор** байна → reaper түүнд хүрэхгүй
- алдаа алга · унасан ажил алга · логт юу ч алга

Яг #29-ийн `split_span` гацалттай ижил дохиогүй байдал.

**Хоёр хамгаалалт**, учир нь нэг env var нь бичгийн алдаа ба гацсан worker хоёрын хооронд байх ЦОРЫН ГАНЦ зүйл байх ёсгүй:

1. **Гадна тал** — тохиргоо процесст ОРОХ цэгтээ хязгаарлагдана (`ge=5, le=600`). 5-ын доод хязгаар нь chunk-ыг `TARGET_CHUNK_MIN_SEC`-ээс дээгүүр ч барина.
2. **Дотор тал** — `forced_cut_step()` нь таазыг шууд дамжуулсан хэнд ч зогсонги байдлыг **татгалзана**.

Алдаа өгөх нь зорилго. Ямар ч мэдэгдэлгүйгээр worker-ыг зогсоодог буруу тохиргоо бол боломжит хамгийн муу үр дүн; хувьсагчийн нэрийг хэлээд унасан ажил бол энд байгаа хамгийн сайн нь.

---

## Тест

**22 шинэ тест**, тус бүрийг засваргүй код руу БУЦААЖ шалгасан:

- `test_models.py` (9) — 9-өөс **6** нь буцаахад унана; үлдсэн 3 нь «засвар хор хөнөөл учруулаагүй» гэдгийг барьдаг (үг хаягдаагүй · зайгүй тохиолдол хөндөгдөөгүй · энгийн segment хэвээр).
- `test_forced_cut.py` (13) — 13-аас **7** нь буцаахад унана. Гацсаныг ХЭМЖСЭН: `compute_pause_boundaries did not return within 2s — it is looping`, мөн VAD-ынх нь ижилхэн.

Гацалтын сэрүүлэг `test_utils_text.py`-аас **`conftest.py`** руу шилжив: одоо хоёр дахь гэмтэл түүнийг шаардаж байгаа ба нэг signal handler-ыг зөв сэргээх нь хоёроос амархан.

author: fw-bot
body:
Steps to reproduce:
- Install `l10n_fr_pdp` and `l10n_be` module
- Activate `French e-invoicing` (you need to put your DB in test mode)
  (i.e: `account_peppol.edi.mode = 'test'` in system parameter) Refer this Documentation https://www.odoo.com/documentation/19.0/applications/finance/fiscal_localizations/france.html?highlight=e%20invoicing#localizations-france-e-invoicing-fac-elec-config
- Create a Invoice and Sent with `E-invoicing`
- Run `PEPPOL: retrieve new documents` Cron
- In Invoice Other Info >  `E-Invoicing Status` should be in `Done` state
- Now Vendor Bill is created for that invoice > Cancel that bill with reason >  Check `E-Invoicing Status` response for bill(one response will be without UUID)
- Go to schedule actions > `PEPPOL: update message status`
- Run it and get the traceback: `KeyError: 'false'`

Issue:
When sending a lifecycle response to the French PDP, `_pdp_send_response` calls the `/api/pdp/1/send_response` endpoint and expects IAP to return a `message_uuid` for each response.

However, IAP return a response without a message UUID, for example: ` {'messages': [{'message_uuid': False}]}` `_pdp_send_response` currently assumes that every returned message has a valid UUID and creates an `account.peppol.response` with:
```
    'peppol_message_uuid': False
    'peppol_state': 'processing'
```
This leaves an `account.peppol.response` in `processing` state without a UUID that can be used to track it.

During the next execution of `_cron_peppol_get_message_status`, `_peppol_get_message_status` retrieves this response through `_peppol_get_documents_for_status` and builds `uuid_to_record` using `peppol_message_uuid` as the key. The resulting mapping contains the Python value `False` as a key.

The cron then calls the PDP `1/get_document` endpoint with this invalid UUID. IAP returns it as the string `'false'`, which is passed to `_peppol_process_messages_status`. The French PDP implementation tries to retrieve the corresponding record with: `uuid_to_record[uid]`

Since the mapping contains `False` while `uid` is `'false'`, this raises: `KeyError: 'false'`

This failure prevents the status cron from completing the processing of the messages.

Solution:
Avoid creating the `account.peppol.response` when IAP does not return a `message_uuid`. A response without a UUID cannot be tracked through the PDP status flow, so creating it in `processing` state only leaves an
invalid record that will later cause the status processing to fail.

Refs #6586

## Summary
Live verification failed: `tm doctor` reported `skill_project_tier` green while this checkout's `.claude/skills` held 51 bundled copies, because the check intersected against `list_project_custom_stems`, which drops every stem the project manifest marks managed — the exact shape a pre-#6602 deploy leaves behind. The check now reads the tier from disk (`bundled_skill_dirs`, manifest-blind) and also counts bundled-named entries that are not skill directories, so check and repair agree.

`tm doctor --fix-skills --yes` gains a sweep: each ledger-recorded stray whose whole subtree passes `skill_removal_verdict` is backed up under `~/.trusty-mpm/backup-doctor-remediation-<ts>/project/<stem>/`, removed, confirmed gone, and dropped from the manifest (stem and `<stem>/…` keys) under the tier's ledger lock. Refused: unrecorded copies, any operator edit or extra file anywhere in the subtree, symlinked entries or symlinks inside a stray, a symlinked or unlistable tier, and a tier that canonicalises onto the managed deploy dir. A bare `--fix-skills` previews the sweep and defers those stems from the redeploy half, so it writes nothing at the project tier; the redeploy half keeps its existing apply-on-flag contract. `--fix` never sweeps. The sweep runs before the redeploy on one shared backup root.

author: voces
body:
A generic struct holding both a `T` field and a closure capturing the `T` value: the second ref instantiation emitted `type mismatch: expected i32, found (ref $type)`. The disassembly named it in one line — both `mk` instances built their env with `struct.new $10`, and `$10` is `(struct (field i32))`, minted from the **first** instantiation. One lifted slot means one env struct, because `fnEnvIdx` is parallel to `fnStmts`.

**Three things were missing, and two of them look like progress while changing nothing.**

1. **The clone gate read the written signature, not the captures.** `monoLamNodeIsTemplate` asks whether a parameter or the return names a type parameter; `show: () => string` names none and only *captures* a `T`. Asked as "does it capture at all" — captures are recorded by name, and being broad is safe in the direction that matters: an extra clone is a correct clone.

2. **The walker never reached this lambda.** `monoPinBodyLambdas` documented its own bound — "only a `LetDecl` INITIALIZER is rewritten" — and this lambda is a field value in an object literal returned from the generic. That is exactly the shape a generic *builder* has, so the stated bound excluded the main case rather than an edge of it.

3. **The clone inherited the template's frame.** `fnParent` cannot be set at clone time: the instance's `FuncDecl` does not exist yet, because its body is what the walk is producing. So `captureValKind` resolved `value` to `value: T` on the template and both instances minted the same layout — a clone that existed and bought nothing.

Fixes 1 and 2 each produce a build that compiles, mints a second env struct, and prints the identical error. "The clone now happens" is not "the clone is typed at the instance".

The fixture also reads `b.actual` / `b2.actual` back at both instantiations — the env fix must not cost the struct field its own per-instance layout.

Zero `runs` lost · mono-tyaram-grid and native fixpoint green · gate 11/11 · 380 filed witnesses as filed.

body:
## Summary

- add a testable attachment-store health contract and use a bounded, prefix-scoped `ListObjectsV2` read to validate S3 without requiring bucket-wide permissions
- add bounded background probes with cached, disclosure-safe readiness state and recovery
- keep `/healthz` and `/api/v1/health` as liveness; add public `/readyz` and `/api/v1/ready`
- add opt-in strict startup validation while preserving non-strict startup by default
- document the new flags, probe semantics, operational guidance, and compatibility behavior

## Configuration

| Flag | Environment | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-s3-startup-check` | `OWLMAIL_S3_STARTUP_CHECK` | `false` |
| `-s3-health-check-interval` | `OWLMAIL_S3_HEALTH_CHECK_INTERVAL` | `30s` |
| `-s3-health-check-timeout` | `OWLMAIL_S3_HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT` | `3s` |

The default remains compatible: an unavailable S3 service does not terminate OwlMail. It makes readiness fail until a later cached probe succeeds. Strict startup is explicitly opt-in.

## Safety and least privilege

Readiness responses expose only a state and allow-listed category. They do not include provider error messages, endpoint configuration, access keys, secret keys, or session tokens.

The probe carries the configured attachment prefix and requests at most one key, so policies that grant `s3:ListBucket` only for that prefix are supported.

## Tests

Added fake-S3 coverage for success, missing bucket, insufficient permission, network failure, timeout, recovery, prefix scoping, and monitor shutdown, plus API, authentication, configuration, and strict/non-strict startup regression tests.

Repository CI runs the full Go 1.27 race/coverage, vet, formatting, lint, build, CodeQL, and Bun browser/documentation suites.

💡 What: Wrapped the setStaticPos React state update in the mousemove event listener with requestAnimationFrame. Also properly handles cleanup on unmount.
🎯 Why: The mousemove event fires at a very high frequency. Updating React state directly in this listener causes excessive re-renders (thrashing the main thread). Throttling with rAF limits updates to the browser's refresh rate.
📊 Impact: Reduces re-renders significantly (e.g., from ~1000/sec to ~60/sec on high polling rate mice) during mouse movement when prefers-reduced-motion is enabled, lowering CPU usage and preventing dropped frames.
🔬 Measurement: Profile the application with Chrome DevTools performance tab while moving the mouse rapidly. Observe fewer React commit phases and reduced JS execution time per frame.

author: thagale
body:
## Summary

Implements MAN-12 — `manta-server` (ARCHITECTURE.md §7-§8), the last remaining M3 sub-project besides the RBN parity benchmark.

- **Telnet DX-cluster server** (`:7300`): standard login handshake, RBN-format `DX de` lines, and real command grammar — `sh/dx[/n]` replays recent spot history, `set dx filter unique > n` suppresses a callsign until it's been seen more than `n` times (both slash- and space-separated forms; the occurrence count is captured atomically at publish time, not queried later, so back-to-back publications can't race the filter). Any other command is accepted without disconnecting the client.
- **JSON Lines spot stream + WebSocket, sharing one port** (`:7301`, per ARCHITECTURE §7's documented "tcp/ws :7301"): a connection is classified by peeking its first bytes for an HTTP `GET` upgrade before either side has sent anything. Message shape mirrors dispensa's `contracts/spots/spots.v1.schema.json` (ADR-0011) — `source: "skimmer"`, the three proposed optional decoder-quality fields, and real `dxContinent`/`dxCqZone`/`dxLat`/`dxLon` (and `de*`) resolved from the already-vendored `cty.dat` (including the west→east longitude-sign fix and per-alias CQ-zone overrides). `dxDxcc`/`deDxcc` (ADIF entity numbers) are serialized as `null`, not a fabricated placeholder — no ADIF entity-number table is vendored in this repo. Spot ids include the station callsign + session epoch so two stations (or a restart) can't collide.
- **Prometheus text metrics endpoint** (`:7302`): spot count, a lag-drop counter, per-protocol connected-client gauges, plus `set_active_tracks`/`set_source_health` injection points — the daemon layer now wires a real (if coarse) per-source health signal in.
- Both spot-emitting servers are thin fan-out consumers of one `tokio::sync::broadcast` channel (`SpotBus`) — a lagging client is disconnected and counted (`spots_dropped_lagged_total`), never back-pressuring the decode pipeline. All three server loops (telnet, TCP JSON, WebSocket) detect a client closing the connection during a quiet period, not just on the next failed write.
- `[server]` TOML config (station callsign + ports) nested under a real `[server]` table (`DaemonConfigFile`), matching ARCHITECTURE §8's single-config-file design.
- Wired into `manta listen --server-config <path> --dial-freq-hz <hz>`: starts all servers on their own tokio runtime, drains in-flight writes on exit (`Runtime::shutdown_timeout`), and uses a fixed epoch for file replay so two runs of the same fixture stay byte-identical.
- Publicly-bound-server hardening: bounded + timed-out line reads (telnet, metrics HTTP), write timeouts (all three servers), a WebSocket handshake timeout, and WebSocket control-frame polling (Ping/Close), so an unauthenticated client can't grow a buffer, hold a task open, or leak a connected-client count.

## Test plan

- [x] TDD throughout (red→green, verified failing for the right reason before implementing each unit)
- [x] The three MAN-12 Gherkin acceptance scenarios are covered as integration tests using real sockets (`crates/manta-server/tests/{telnet,json_stream,metrics}_acceptance.rs`), plus regression tests for each review finding (publish-time filter ordering, closed-client detection, port sharing, portable-call RBN formatting, cty.dat longitude/zone-override, spot-id uniqueness, etc.)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test --workspace` (all green, including pre-existing suites — no regressions)
- [x] `cargo clippy`/`cargo test` with `--features soapy` (CI's second job)
- [x] Manual smoke test: ran the built `manta listen --server-config ... --dial-freq-hz ...` binary end-to-end against a synthetic WAV — clean bind of all ports, no panics, clean exit
- [x] Two rounds of Codex review, all 19 findings addressed (fixed inline, or replied-to as a verified disagreement — `deCqZone` isn't in the dispensa schema; `active_tracks` needs a manta-engine API that doesn't exist yet, flagged below)

## Known follow-ups (out of scope here)

- `dxDxcc`/`deDxcc` need a real ADIF DXCC entity-number table to stop being `null` — not vendored in this repo yet.
- `active_tracks` stays 0 — needs a live track-count API from manta-engine that doesn't exist yet (`listen()`'s callbacks have no such hook).
- Telnet command grammar covers `sh/dx` and `unique` filtering; other cluster filter types (band/mode/spotter/frequency-range) aren't implemented.

author: siddharth705
body:
## Why

Follow-up to #743, which fixed the wrong half of a problem it created.

#743 detects UPI/NEFT/IMPS narrations naming an individual and files them as **Transfer**. But in India a large share of everyday **spending** settles to what looks like an individual, because small merchants and service providers take payment on a PSP *business account* rather than a storefront merchant ID. The canonical case is paying an Uber/Ola driver directly instead of in-app — but it generalises to vegetable vendors, snack counters, tea stalls and kirana shops.

#743 read all of those as "sent money to a person." A confidently wrong category is worse than an honest unknown, by this codebase's own stated principle.

**Yes — we can tell merchant from personal.** The rail leaves a fingerprint even when the payee's *name* doesn't.

## What changes

**1. `MERCHANT_ACQUIRER_MARKER`** — a payment settling over a merchant-acquiring rail is a business payment whatever the payee line says:

| Marker | Real corpus rows |
|---|---|
| PhonePe merchant Q-VPA (`Q…@ybl`) | 96 |
| Merchant-UPI pseudo-branch IFSCs | 64 |
| Paytm `PAYTM.S` / `PAYTM.D` | 58 |
| Google Pay for Business (`@okbiz`) | 23 |
| BharatPe | 20 |
| Vyapar | 4 |

Deliberately **excludes** PhonePe's general `YBLUPI` branch and the bare PSP brand names — those appear on ordinary personal transfers too and carry no merchant/person distinction. There's a test pinning that.

**2. Small-shop trade words re-added** to `BUSINESS_SUFFIX_TOKENS` — `SNACKS`, `DHABA`, `PROVISION(S)`, `WINES`, `FILLING`, `AUTO`, `FRESH`, `SUPER`, `DIGITAL`, plus a tier that structurally cannot be a payer's remark (`XEROX`, `TAILORS`, `TYRES`, `SPARES`, `NURSERY`, `PHOTOGRAPHY`, `PARLOUR`/`PARLOR`).

## The correction that matters more than the words

#743 **removed** this vocabulary based on an A/B over **constructed** narrations, which claimed free-text remarks like `"-Fresh veggies money"` would veto genuine transfers wholesale — 12 of 18 lost.

Re-measured on the real corpus, that was wrong in both magnitude and direction:

- Real remarks carry a purpose word only **1.8%** of the time, and are dominated by one bank's generated `PAYMENT FROM PHONE` boilerplate — not payer-written text at all.
- These words flip **12 of 673** real rows, and **all 12 are genuine businesses** (`BALAJI SNACKS`, `BANSI VAISHND DHABA`, `NATRAJ PROVISION`, `REGAL WINES`, `SNEHA FRESH CHI`, `DEEP FILLING`, `RAVI AUTO CENTR`…), most independently corroborated by an acquirer marker in the same narration.

The risk was overstated ~37× **and its sign was inverted**. The class doc now carries a warning to measure this component against the real corpus, because invented narrations mislead here.

`FURNITURE` is deliberately left **out** — it's the one word with real negative evidence (its single corpus occurrence is a remark on a genuine person transfer). The remaining everyday nouns (`SALES`, `BOOKS`, `TOYS`, `COLLECTION`, `PUMP`, `TRADING`, `ENERGY`, `CEMENT`, `PAINTS`) stay out for want of evidence either way.

## Measured effect

Like-for-like on the real 29-statement corpus — only rows the keyword table leaves as `Other` ever reach the detector, so both sides are gated identically:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Classified person-to-person | 673 | **450** |
| Correctly reclassified | — | **223** |
| **Newly misread as transfers** | — | **0** |

Reclassified rows fall through to `Other` with their review flag — the honest answer, since knowing money reached a business is not knowing *which* business.

## Known residual — stated, not papered over

~32 rows (~5%) are a bare truncated trade name and an RRN, with no VPA and no rail marker at all (`UPI-HANUMAN TEA`, `UPI/NEW AMOGHA VEG/<rrn>/UPI`). Name *shape* cannot substitute, and the corpus proves it: **`MANAS CHAT`** appears 18 times, reads exactly like a chaat stall, and is a **person** (recurring credits remarked RENT/SAVINGS) — while `SUPER BA` and `DEEP FILLING` are shops. Separating those needs a merchant directory or a user confirmation, not more vocabulary.

Also worth knowing for sequencing: **52.7%** of person-to-person rows are a payee seen exactly once, so per-user merchant learning can never fix them — though recurring payees carry **76% of rupee value**, so a value-weighted target is far more reachable than a count-weighted one.

## Testing

- `PersonToPersonTransferDetectorTest`: 19 tests, including pins for the acquirer families, the general-`YBLUPI` counterweight, the shop words, and an explicit test recording the accepted cost of re-adding `FRESH`/`AUTO`.
- Corpus measurement run by compiling the detector standalone against the 1,875-row real dataset; the 673 baseline reproduces the independent measurement exactly.
- Full backend suite green. One earlier local run showed 11 `com.finora.architecture.*` failures — all `failed to check any classes`, an ArchUnit cold-worktree race before compilation finished; they pass in isolation and are unrelated to this diff.

author: abdallah01
body:
Closes #136.

## What

Every dynamic-reflow number rested on one synthetic seed and one repetition. This PR regenerates the Tesseract half of the corpus — the seven step streams, `rewrap`, and the three tesseract-matrix controls — at three further seeds, each with a fresh-noise repetition, plus a fresh-noise repetition of the published seed: **7 new configurations, 77 streams**, committed as `.jsonl` only under `doc/replay/validation/2026-08-dynamic-reflow/variants/<config>/` and replayed live (no `.ab.json`, so the alias and byte-identity guards are untouched).

New section in the corpus's `EXPERIMENT.md`: **"Variance across seeds and repetitions (#136, 2026-09-02)"** — four tables (controls, steps, the floor window per configuration, min/median/max across configurations), a reading, a boundary statement, and a reproduce block.

## Findings

- **Controls hold under every lever:** 0 step events on all 32 control replays under `coherentShift`, the 390 px floor and the adopt lever.
- **`coherentShift`'s 4/7 is stable:** the same four steps pass and the same three fail on all 8 configurations.
- **The adopt lever's 150 px result is one configuration in eight.** On the same page under fresh noise and on all six configurations of the other three pages, no matched pair clears its own 3×-height gate, so no plan forms and the lever is byte-identical to plain `coherentShift`. The default stays (never worse anywhere); the README's 2.4.0 note is qualified.
- **The floor window is page-specific and often empty.** (377, 406] is the published page's; (335, 392] under fresh noise; (220, 340] / (< 200, 346] on the s07 page; empty on s21 (no floor-qualified mover survives) and s42 (the scroll control's mover exceeds the slab's). No single floor is inside every page's window; 390 is a safe no-op on three of four pages. The README calibration recipe is qualified accordingly.
- **Correction:** the #116 entry's "this environment does not reproduce the committed streams" note was a line-ending artefact (CRLF working tree vs the generator's LF). Against the index bytes, Tesseract 5.4.0 + `chi_sim` + Microsoft YaHei + Pillow 12.2 regenerate all five committed Tesseract streams byte for byte.

## Tooling

- `gen_corpus.py` (both generators): `--perturb-seed` seeds the per-frame capture noise separately from the page text; the tesseract-matrix generator gained `--seed`. Default output is byte-identical to the committed streams (verified against `git show HEAD:` bytes; the matrix generator's meta-line key order was the only drift and is restored).
- `variants/gen_seed_suite.py`: one configuration = the 11 streams; keeps `rewrap` only from reflow-at-7 runs and checks the five agree.
- `variants/variance_report.py`: prints the section's four tables from CLI replays; floor bounds by integer bisection over [200, 700]. On the published seed it reproduces the #119 entry exactly (window (377, 406], every lag triple, tallies 4 / 5 / 4 of 7).
- `test/replay/experiment_doc_support.dart`: the #128 helpers moved out of `experiment_doc_tables_test.dart` verbatim (private names made public) so a second pin test can share them; the #128 test is unchanged in behaviour (14/14 green).
- `test/replay/experiment_doc_variance_tables_test.dart`: pins every cell of the new tables against live replays; each floor bound as a boundary (fires at N, not at N+1); the summary table against the per-row tables. Mutation-verified: a slab bound 406→405, a lag cell 0.1→0.2 and a summary median 343→344 each turn it red.

## Gates

`dart analyze --fatal-infos` clean; `dart format --set-exit-if-changed lib/` clean (no change under `lib/`); `dart test` 868/868; `dart pub publish --dry-run` archive 475 KB → 828 KB compressed.

CHANGELOG 2.5.1 gains an "Added" entry. No code change under `lib/`.

author: breken-ai
body:
> Built by breken, your AI support engineer - breken.ai - this one's on us.

## The problem in plain words

Add or delete an auth hook in the dashboard (for example a Send Email hook) and your custom SMTP settings silently disappear: host, port, username, password, sender name, admin email, plus your email rate limit (one reporter watched it drop from 25 back to 2).

While the hook is on, nothing looks wrong, because the hook sends email without SMTP. The damage shows up later: turn the hook off and every auth email stops - password resets, magic links, confirmations - with no warning anywhere in the dashboard.

Reported in #49873 and reproduced twice there: once on hook create, once on hook delete.

## Root cause

The dashboard's hook forms send only hook fields to `PATCH /platform/auth/{ref}/config/hooks`:

- `CreateHookSheet.tsx` `onSubmit` sends `{ [enabledKey], [uriKey], [secretsKey] }`
- `DeleteHookConfirmationDialog.tsx` sends the same three keys set to `false`/`null`

That is all the endpoint's own type (`UpdateGoTrueConfigHooksBody`) allows - no SMTP fields exist on it. The API behaves like a replace of the surrounding GoTrue config, so everything not in the request - every `SMTP_*` field and `RATE_LIMIT_EMAIL_SENT` - comes back reset.

## The fix

`apps/studio/data/auth/auth-hooks-update-mutation.ts` now wraps every hooks update:

1. Snapshot the current SMTP + email rate-limit config before the hooks PATCH.
2. Re-read it after the PATCH.
3. Restore only the fields the hooks update reset, through the regular auth config PATCH (`skipInvalidation: true`, since the hooks mutation already invalidates the config query).

If nothing was reset, no extra write happens - so this also goes quiet automatically if the API stops resetting these fields later. A failed snapshot never blocks the hook change itself, and a failed restore logs to the console rather than masking the hook change's success.

## Behavior change

Before: create or delete a hook, custom SMTP config is gone and the rate limit is back to the default, with no warning.
After: SMTP config and rate limit survive hook changes.

## Evidence and testing

- Verified in source: the exact request bodies both hook forms send, the hooks endpoint schema (hook fields only), and that `GoTrueConfigResponse` / `UpdateGoTrueConfigBody` expose `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASS`, `SMTP_ADMIN_EMAIL`, `SMTP_SENDER_NAME`, `SMTP_MAX_FREQUENCY` and `RATE_LIMIT_EMAIL_SENT` for read and write via `/platform/auth/{ref}/config`.
- Field names in the fix are checked against the published platform API types in `packages/api-types`.
- NOT done: I could not run this against a live hosted project with custom SMTP configured. The restore only writes when a reset actually happened and restores exactly what was there before, but it deserves one staging pass on your side.
- Worth saying out loud: the deeper fix belongs in the API - a hooks update should never touch unrelated config. This PR makes the dashboard resilient in the meantime, and it no-ops once the API is fixed.

Happy to iterate. If you would rather merge the current config into the hooks request, or gate the restore behind a user-facing warning, I can rework it.

author: leifhansen
body:
## What broke

The app runs on one Fly machine and every deploy replaces it. A bulk batch that was **drafting** when that happened ended with:

> The server restarted while identifying item 1 of 6, so this batch stopped early. The items it had already finished are saved in Drafts — please run the rest again.

Six deploys landed between 04:29 and 05:30 UTC today (#233, #235, #236, #234, #238, #237), and every batch running under them died exactly that way — while #233's research pass was also making each item take a minute or more (fixed separately by #237). The photo phases could already be picked back up after a restart (`_resume_interrupted_batches`); drafting could not, because each finished item was already saved and billed and nothing recorded which.

## What this does

The batch now writes its plan down as it goes, in the job mirror it already keeps on the volume:

- the grouping and the photo order the moment grouping finishes (`_names`, `_groups`);
- every finished item as it lands (`_done` — ids and titles only, never the drafts);
- the item in flight, named **before** its AI is charged for (`_inflight`).

A restart reads that back (`_drafting_plan`) and continues from the first item without a draft:

- nothing already saved is drafted or billed twice;
- the item that was charged and never finished is finished in the session that already holds its photos, **without a second charge** — the first charge bought nothing and its receipt died with the process;
- an item whose draft landed just before the process died counts as finished, because its `listing.json` is on disk.

The queue's poller also stops giving up on a batch it cannot reach after eighteen seconds. A deploy takes the server away for a minute or two; the watch now rides that out (four minutes) and finds the batch picked back up on the other side, instead of telling the seller the connection was lost while the batch went on without them.

## What stays the same

A mirror from before the plan existed, a swept pile, a batch the seller stopped (#239), or one that has died `BULK_MAX_RESUMES` times all keep the honest "run the rest again" message exactly as before. Seller notes (#240) are copied onto each new item as before; an item picked back up already has its copy from the first attempt.

## Also

The resume tests (this file and `test_bulk_resume.py`) now keep their job mirrors in a per-test data root and finish every job they leave running. A job registered with a stubbed worker was otherwise left "running" in its mirror file in the shared test data root, and the next `TestClient` in the process adopted it at startup and ran the real worker in the background of an unrelated test — which is how `test_the_pile_is_grouped_with_the_sellers_inventory` (#240) failed one run in three on main.

## Tests

`backend/tests/test_a_batch_survives_a_restart_mid_draft.py` — the decision (picked up; an item that finished just before the restart is not drafted twice; a swept pile, a plan-less mirror and a batch that keeps dying are left alone), the worker (drafts only what is left, bills once, purges the pile), a fresh batch writing its plan down, and the round trip through the mirror file on disk.

Verified locally: `ruff check backend`, the full backend suite, the smoke job's API test list twice (655 passed each), `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, and `npm run smoke` against a Postgres-backed server (all checks clean).

author: bestian
body:
Fixes #3

## 問題

iOS 上接 CarPlay（或藍牙裝置）後無法切換音訊來源。原因有三層：

1. 麥克風晶片（向下小箭頭）在錄音中被 `.disabled`，點了沒反應。
2. 來源清單來自 `AVCaptureDevice.DiscoverySession`，而 CarPlay／藍牙麥克風是 `AVAudioSession` 的路由埠，結構上不可能出現在該清單——通常只剩內建麥克風一項，無從切換。
3. audio session category 未帶 `.allowBluetoothHFP`，藍牙免持麥克風連 `availableInputs` 都不會出現；全 App 也沒有任何 `setPreferredInput` 或 `routeChangeNotification` 處理。

## 修正（iOS）

- **`SourceCatalogService`**：iOS 改列舉 `AVAudioSession.availableInputs`（CarPlay、藍牙、內建都會出現），目前路由中的輸入排最前；列舉為空時退回原本的 device discovery（模擬器相容）。
- **`LiveTranscriptionSession` / `ConversationAudioTap`**：統一用 `.record` + `.measurement` + `.allowBluetoothHFP` 設定 category；停用 `automaticallyConfiguresApplicationAudioSession` 改為手動管理，避免 capture session 啟動時蓋掉 category options 與 preferred input；擷取啟動前套用 `setPreferredInput`，必要的 category 設定或 activation 失敗時不再帶著無效狀態繼續啟動。
- **`AppModel` + glue**：同時監聽 `routeChangeNotification` 與 `availableInputsChangeNotification`；新接上 CarPlay／耳機時清除舊的 preferred input，讓新裝置照系統預設接手；所有來源刷新入口都會同步實際路由，且只有系統接受 `setPreferredInput` 後才更新選取狀態。對話模式啟動時也會重新套用同一來源。
- **`ControlBar`**：移除錄音中停用選單的限制，錄音中也能即時切換。
- **`SettingsSheet`**：新增「輸入來源」設定卡，與小箭頭選單同一份來源清單。
- 新增 `iosAudioInputHint` 在地化（en / zh-Hans / zh-Hant，其餘語言沿用英文 fallback 慣例）。

### 行為語意

- 預設**跟隨系統路由**：接上 CarPlay／藍牙自動切換過去，斷開自動切回。
- 手動選擇立即生效（含錄音中），效力維持到該裝置斷開；之後新接上的裝置回到系統預設。

## Android（獨立 commits，best effort）

Android spike 原本沒有音訊來源 UI。新增 AUDIO INPUT 下拉選單，列出 `AudioManager.availableCommunicationDevices` 提供的通訊路由；選取後透過 `setCommunicationDevice` 交由系統配對相應麥克風，並以 `AudioDeviceCallback` 處理熱插拔。更新清單時會保留仍有效的手動選擇，路由遭拒或裝置移除時回到系統預設。由於實際擷取屬於系統 `SpeechRecognizer`，部分裝置可能忽略此設定，因此 UI 明確標示為 best effort。所有 Android 變更都位於 Android-only commits，可一起捨棄而不影響 iOS 修正。

## 驗證

- ✅ iOS 模擬器建置（Xcode / SDK 26.5）
- ✅ macOS `swift build` + `swift test`（新增 `SourceCatalogServiceTests` 3 項全過；`OverlayWindowControllerTests`／`AudienceDisplayWindowControllerTests` 在乾淨 `main` 全套執行時同樣失敗，為既有的視窗類 flaky，與本 PR 無關）
- ⚠️ Android 原始版本曾通過 `compileDebugKotlin`；最後的 communication-device 修正尚未重新編譯（本機缺少已接受授權的 Android SDK 35，且 PR 目前沒有 CI checks）。
- ⚠️ **尚未在實機 + CarPlay／藍牙驗證**（無硬體）。建議手動測試清單：
  1. 接上 CarPlay → 麥克風晶片自動顯示 CarPlay 麥克風
  2. 錄音中點小箭頭改選「iPhone 麥克風」→ 收音立即切換
  3. 斷開再接上 CarPlay → 自動回到 CarPlay（不被先前手動選擇釘住）
  4. 設定頁「輸入來源」選單與晶片顯示一致
  5. 在設定頁選擇外接麥克風後啟動「對話模式」→ 仍使用同一輸入來源

author: linuxexpert-org
body:
The header checkbox selected the loaded page. On a folder of ten thousand that is fifty of them, and the only way to act on the rest was to scroll until they loaded and tick again.

This is the case that makes archive-by-month (#198) actually useful: "archive everything from 2024 by month" is unusable at fifty at a time.

## The interaction

Ticking the box still takes the loaded rows. A line then appears offering the rest **by name and count** — "Select all 9,950 in Inbox" — and taking it is a separate press. A checkbox that silently meant ten thousand when the screen shows fifty would be the worst of both, so each option says what it actually covers. Once taken, the line says so and offers a way back, and the toolbar count tells the truth.

## The selection model

**It is a query, not a list of ids.** What it reaches is resolved from the server when an action runs, walked a page at a time — a folder holds far more than one call returns, and `Email/set` refuses more ids than `maxObjectsInSet` in one go (which `setEmails` already chunks for).

**It resolves uncollapsed, unlike the list.** "Everything in this folder" means every message rather than one per thread. Expanding threads the way a click does is impossible here anyway: that walks loaded `Email` objects, and these are precisely the ones that were never loaded.

**It only applies to actions aimed at the selection.** A right-click or a swipe on one row still means that row, whatever is ticked.

## Two bugs this exposed

**Undo would have destroyed data.** `move()` builds its undo from `emails[id]?.mailboxIds ?? {}` — the folders each message was in, taken from what the browser holds. For an unloaded message that is `{}`, so undoing would have written an *empty* `mailboxIds` and left the message in no folder at all, which is worse than the move it was undoing. `move()` and `archiveByDate()` both did this. Both now withhold the Undo offer when any target is not loaded, rather than restoring something wrong.

**An action did not consume the wider selection.** The optimistic paths cleared the selected ids but not the flag, so the next action would have silently reached the whole folder again.

Both are covered by tests.

## Testing

12 new store tests against a simulated server: the two-step selection, paging behaviour and the short-page stop, the uncollapsed query (asserted against the list being collapsed), Undo offered when everything is loaded and withheld when it is not, the move still happening either way, and the flag not outliving its action.

Suite green: web 729 across 80 files, server 116, typecheck clean.

## Not verified

Not exercised in a browser — automation stopped cooperating for me partway through this session. The store behaviour is well covered; the banner itself and the toolbar count have not been seen rendered.

Worth a look before merge, and worth trying one large-folder action against a real mailbox: the paging is tested against a fake server with a page size of 3, not against Stalwart with a page size of 500 and a folder that actually needs several round trips.

## 概要

`docs/development/worker-discipline-template.md` の「Node バージョン / worktree の `npm ci`」節に、直前のウェーブで実測した教訓を 4 文追記する。

## 背景（実測）

- dependabot PR #1994 で `gh api --method PUT .../update-branch` が 422 `merge conflict between base and head` を返した。
- CLAUDE.md「Strict-mode batch merge」は 422 を lock-file 競合として手順化しているが、実際に競合したのは `runners/github-action/dist/index.mjs.map` だけで、`package-lock.json` は auto-merge された。
- 原因は先行マージした PR #1992（`@anthropic-ai/sdk` 0.120.0 → 0.121.0 のランタイム依存 bump）が main の bundled dist を動かしたこと。#1992 の変更ファイルに `runners/github-action/dist/index.mjs.map` が含まれることを `gh pr view 1992 --json files` で確認済み。
- したがって手順を選ぶ前に `git merge origin/main` → `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` で競合実体を測り、dist なら手で解かず再生成する。

- `npx textlint --no-cache docs/development/worker-discipline-template.md` → exit 0
- `npm run fix:dashes` 相当（`scripts/fix-dashes.mjs`）→ exit 0（差分なし）
- `npm run meta:validate` 相当（4 スクリプト）→ exit 0

author: justingallivan
body:
Supersedes Dependabot #141, which is red on Jest as-is.

## What
- **sanitize-html 2.17.5 → 2.17.7** (GHSA-g8qq-57p8-ggw5 / CVE-2026-84371, moderate). The bypass requires allowing SVG animation tags; all three sanitizer configs (`lib/external/sanitize-review-html.js`, `shared/utils/policy-markdown-server.js`, `shared/utils/grantee-markdown.js`) use tight allowlists without `svg`/`math`/`animate`/`textarea`/`xmp`, so the app was not exposed. Bumped for hygiene.
- **postcss-selector-parser 6.1.2 → 6.1.4** via lockfile refresh (GHSA-w9m9-85wc-3x92 / CVE-2026-9358, low). Build-time Tailwind dependency; never sees user input.
- **jest.config.js**: sanitize-html 2.17.7 depends on htmlparser2 12, which is ESM-only along with its `dom*`/`entities` tree. next/jest ignores node_modules for transformation and only lets custom `transformIgnorePatterns` append, so the config widens its exemption group post-hoc. Test-only; `next.config.js` untouched. This is why #141 fails CI (`SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module` in htmlparser2).
- **CI Node 20 → 22** in `test.yml` and `e2e.yml`. Next externalizes sanitize-html in the server build (`require("sanitize-html")` in the chunks), so Node's own `require()` loads ESM htmlparser2 at runtime and sanitize-html now declares `node >= 22.12`. Vercel's project runtime is already 22.x; CI was behind it.

## Lockfile scope
Only: sanitize-html, htmlparser2, domhandler, domutils, dom-serializer, domelementtype, entities, escape-string-regexp (nested), postcss-selector-parser.

body:
### 💡 What
Enhanced the search input keyboard shortcut hint (`/`) in `index.html` by:
1. Adding `aria-describedby="kbd-hint"` to the `#search` input.
2. Adding `aria-label="Keyboard shortcut: /"` to the `#kbd-hint` badge.
3. Adding `visibility` transition to `.kbd-hint` CSS and dynamically setting `hint.style.visibility = (v || f) ? 'hidden' : 'visible'` in `ui()` when search is active or focused.

### 🎯 Why
When keyboard shortcut hints are visually hidden on input focus or text entry, setting only `opacity: 0` leaves them in the screen reader accessibility tree. Updating `visibility: hidden` removes them from screen readers while preserving smooth CSS transitions. Linking `#search` with `aria-describedby` provides assistive technology users with context about available shortcuts upon focusing the field.

### ♿ Accessibility
- Screen readers announce the shortcut hint context when focusing the search input.
- Hidden shortcut hint is removed from the accessibility tree when input is focused or query is typed.

author: oharboe
body:
Every `orfs_flow()` that runs synthesis grows two targets:

- **`<name>[_variant]_estimate`** — a deterministic, one-to-two-minute estimate of what the design can achieve at its configured floorplan parameters, built **from the synthesis output**: floorplan initialized in-script from the same variables the production stage reads (both init modes), macros placed by the production placer when present, then a non-timing-driven global placement early-stopped at overflow 0.6.
- **`<name>[_variant]_estimate_run`** — the same script as a `bazelisk run` executable with run-time `KEY=VALUE` parameter overrides: **one point in floorplan-parameter space per invocation** (smoke: `CORE_UTILIZATION=10 PLACE_DENSITY=0.6` — floorplan rebuilt at the new point, echo reflects the override).

```sh
bazelisk run //test/smoketest:lb_32x128_asap7_estimate_run -- \
  CORE_UTILIZATION=10 PLACE_DENSITY=0.6 OUTPUT=$PWD/point.json LOG_DIR=$PWD/logs
```

**Division of labor**: this is the *oracle* half of floorplan-parameter automation. bazel-orfs computes points and recommendations — the JSON's `params` object carries the parameters in force under their **exact ORFS variable names**, so a chosen point is directly consumable by ORFS's config.mk pin machinery (`pinAutoFloorplan.py`, OpenROAD-flow-scripts#4487). bazel-orfs never writes config.mk. Constraints imported from that PR's measured negative results: utilization is constraint satisfaction, never blended into a period objective (ρ = −1.0 on gcd for the blend), and "did not resolve" keeps the incumbent.

**Properties**: parallel to the entire physical flow by DAG construction; cannot perturb flow artifacts; deterministic (an estimate delta between commits has no sampling noise of its own); content-addressed (the merge-base baseline for a PR diff is a cache hit; nightly builds are a trend line at ~1% of flow cost); pre-route optimistic **by design, for differential use** where the uniform bias cancels.

**Macro designs**: the JSON carries the macro-path channel (`macro_paths_mean/worst/sampled` — the KPI macro placement actually controls) and `macros_pinned`: unpinned estimate deltas on macro designs carry placement-draw variance; with `MACRO_PLACEMENT_TCL` set (stock ORFS) the draw is held constant and deltas are clean. Racing the pin is #868's business.

**Cadence — estimate always, audit as you can afford, pin occasionally**: the estimate is *purposely* sweep-free (it has no sampling noise to sweep away; the chaos lives in the macro draw and the stages it doesn't run). Pin machinery stores the estimate JSON at pin time — a **receipt** — and the always-on estimate's drift against the receipt is the measured re-pin signal (deltas reported, policy the consumer's, zero new code). And the honest audit economics: an explicit k-seed sweep of a large design is an adorable aspiration — the nightly build over evolving commits *is* the seed sweep, smeared across time; each point confounds improvement with a fresh draw, the trend averages over draws, large effects stand out regardless, and detrended residuals estimate the draw-noise floor for free. When audit compute is starved, the deterministic estimate delta is the only noise-free per-commit measurement in the system.

**`docs/estimate.md` is the thesis**: a flow result is a draw (Kahng & Mantik, ISQED 2002); honest comparison needs seed sweeps; the guided-random-walk model shows a fast imperfect gate plus an overnight seed-sweep audit reaches the PPA goal with orders of magnitude less gate compute; calibration provenance (measured vs pending — E14 backtest named); own-your-scoring-function guidance; stated limits (a speedometer, not a map).

This PR consolidates the *lessons* of the exploratory campaign work into one thesis; the doc's "Why the estimator is shaped this way" section gives the design rationale without the number-dump, and its "Provenance, trust, and breadcrumbs" section says plainly what a thesis owes and doesn't: the numbers were observed once on one machine with evolving instruments — **do not trust them, or the archived data, without re-measuring** — with pointers to where the evidence and its flaws live, so a proper follow-up study can be done right.

Tests: `lb_32x128_estimate_test` asserts the JSON contract; smokes on the smoketest designs. Pending before ready: capstone period-fidelity numbers into the calibration section, one macro-design smoke on the freed campaign machine.

nb = json.loads(open('MyIA.AI.Notebooks/SymbolicAI/Tweety/Tweety-7a-Extended-Frameworks.ipynb', encoding='utf-8').read())

author: dierks27
body:
Everything from the Homestead field report on v0.1.0, plus a persistent memory.

Released as [v0.2.0](https://github.com/Dierks27/Lumen/releases/tag/v0.2.0) — the jar is attached there.

## What changed

**World awareness.** `WorldSnapshot` writes what Lumen can actually see into every prompt: biome, time, weather, light, **what it is standing on and looking at**, nearby players, hostiles, animals, ground items, and the blocks in range. Blocks that glow or hold a block entity are always called out, which surfaces modded ores and machines without needing to know the mod. The system prompt now states that anything absent from that list is not visible — the lever against invented detail. This is the "stood on the bed, then asked where it was" case.

**Conversation memory.** Chat that wasn't addressed to Lumen, and chat arriving while a request is in flight, is now remembered instead of dropped — silently discarding those is what made replies feel disconnected. The addressed line is recorded when the request *starts*, so history keeps its order and survives a failed request.

**Location memory, persisted.** `config/lumen/memory.json` records the container an item actually came out of. The next request for it walks straight there, out to a wider radius than a cold search. Memories that turn out wrong are forgotten as they're ruled out, and an empty container triggers a retry elsewhere — capped at three, so a bad query can't send Lumen on a tour of the base.

**Navigation.** Wooden doors are pathable and get opened. `LumenPathNodeMaker` treats a block as open when the pathfinder calls it BLOCKED but it has no collision box — the common modded case. Stuck detection re-paths and, as a last resort, warps.

**Inventory, chests, combat.** A 27-slot pack, right-click handover, ground pickup, auto-equip, drops on death. `find me some iron` searches nearby containers via the `Inventory` interface, so modded crates work too. Defends itself and whoever it follows.

## Note on Baritone

It was the #1 request and it can't be done. Standard Baritone is a **client** mod — it drives `Minecraft.getInstance().player` through client tick and input hooks, and the 1.20.1 build is a Forge jar. It won't load on a Fabric server and has no client to attach to. That stays true for the Phase 3 fake-player route, since a fake `ServerPlayerEntity` is still server-side. Automatone is the fork that *does* drive server-side mobs — and it's the one that blew the stack on modded blocks.

So this attacks the symptom in the pathfinder instead, and adds `/lumen why`, which names the blocks around Lumen that vanilla refuses to route through. In a 375-mod pack that output is the fastest route from "he's stuck" to the mod at fault.

## Verification

CI compiles and runs the tests on every push; all green. The parser and memory-matching tests cover the pure logic — the memory test caught a real bug on the way in: matching against the full item id meant `create` matched every item from `createaddition`, and `minecraft` matched everything.

**Not runtime-tested.** No Minecraft server in the build environment, so entity behaviour, pathfinding, chest access and combat are unexercised until this runs on Homestead.

## Still outstanding

- The repo's default branch is still `claude/lumen-ai-companion-mod-aza44q` — flipping it to `main` needs repo admin (Settings → General → Default branch); I don't have that access.
- The v0.2.0 release page's Notes section was generated before this commit and describes two v0.1.0 defaults. Fixed for future releases; the README is authoritative.

## **User description** # feat(release): replace upstream macos-signing with reusable fleet-ops workflow ## Summary `helios-cli/.github/scripts/macos-signing/{sign_macos_code.sh,notarize_macos_binary_with_rcodesign.sh,codex.entitlements.plist}` are inherited from the upstream OpenAI Codex CLI fork. They reference `OAI_CODESIGN_BACKEND=akv-pkcs11` (Azure Key Vault) — which is the Windows EV cert path in our org, not the Apple path. The current pipeline has never been executed on kooshapari. This PR replaces the upstream pipeline with the reusable `phenotype-fleet-ops` workflow that uses Infisical. ## Notes Replace upstream AKV-pkcs11 pipeline; CLI binary, no .app bundle ## What this PR does 1. Adds `Entitlements.plist` at `apps/helios-cli/src-tauri/Entitlements.plist` (minimal sandbox-safe defaults: network client, JIT where needed; repo-specific extras inlined) 2. Adds `.github/workflows/release-macos.yml` that calls the reusable workflow `kooshapari/phenotype-fleet-ops/.github/workflows/macos-release.yml@main` 3. The reusable workflow pulls Apple Developer secrets from Infisical (project `8efe392e-56a6-4c3c-89f9-8141183dd7e8` → `/apple/helios-cli`), runs `codesign` + `xcrun notarytool` + `xcrun stapler`, attaches the signed + notarized DMG to the GitHub Release ## Why now - Upstream sign script: `helios-cli/.github/scripts/macos-signing/sign_macos_code.sh` references `OAI_CODESIGN_BACKEND=akv-pkcs11` — wrong path for Apple signing - Upstream entitlements: `helios-cli/.github/scripts/macos-signing/codex.entitlements.plist:1` (carried from upstream, minimal) - No tracked `apps/helios-cli/src-tauri/Entitlements.plist` exists - Local ForgeCode session evidence: 12 sessions referenced helios-cli + Apple tokens; "MLX backend" / "Apple Silicon support" / "aarch64-apple-darwin" ## Constraints honored - **Zero billed runners** — every job targets self-hosted runners only (`[self-hosted, macos, arm64, mac-signing]`) - **Infisical is the only secret store** — no GitHub Actions secrets for Apple Developer creds; only `INFISICAL_TOKEN` (service identity, not Apple-specific) is in repo secrets - **No `.p12` ever committed** — cert + `.p8` API key are base64-encoded secrets in Infisical, decoded to `runner.disk/.apple-keys/` per build only, mode 600 - **Single source of truth** — the signing/notarization pipeline lives in `phenotype-fleet-ops`; this repo just calls it. Any future repo adopting Apple signing gets the same pipeline by changing `app-name` and `build-cmd` ## Verification plan 1. Tag `v0.2.0-macsigtest` → `release-macos.yml` triggers 2. Download `helios-cli-macos-signed` artifact (DMG) 3. `codesign -dvvv helios` → Developer ID 4. `xcrun stapler validate helios-dmg` → valid 5. Run `helios --version` on a clean Mac → no Gatekeeper dialog ## Pre-merge checklist (run by Koosha) - [ ] Provision Infisical secret `/apple/helios-cli` with these keys (if missing, default to `/apple` org-level path): - `APPLE_TEAM_ID` - `APPLE_DEVELOPER_ID_P12_BASE64` - `APPLE_DEVELOPER_ID_P12_PASSWORD` - `APPLE_NOTARIZATION_ISSUER_ID` - `APPLE_NOTARIZATION_KEY_ID` - `APPLE_NOTARIZATION_KEY_P8_BASE64` - `APPLE_BUNDLE_ID = app.phenotype.helios` - [ ] Provision repo secret `INFISICAL_TOKEN` (machine identity, scoped to project `8efe392e-56a6-4c3c-89f9-8141183dd7e8`) - [ ] Confirm the org-level self-hosted Mac runner `KooshaPari` is online with labels `[self-hosted, macos, arm64, mac-signing]` - [ ] Confirm `kooshapari/phenotype-fleet-ops@main` contains the new `.github/workflows/macos-release.yml` (already shipped at commit `fd8373f`) - [ ] Tag a `v*.*.*-macsigtest` to dry-run - [ ] After green, remove `-macsigtest` and re-tag for real release ___ ## **CodeAnt-AI Description** Sign, notarize, and publish helios-cli for macOS ### What Changed - macOS releases now build the Apple Silicon helios-cli binary when a version tag is pushed or a release is started manually - Release binaries are signed, notarized, wrapped in a DMG, and attached to the GitHub Release - Apple signing credentials are retrieved from Infisical instead of being stored in the repository - Adds macOS entitlements needed for network access and hardened-runtime notarization ### Impact `✅ Installable macOS releases` `✅ Notarized binaries trusted by macOS` `✅ No signing certificates committed to the repository`

author: hl-support
body:
## Warum

Am 01.09.2026 starben 19 `mysql_initial_rank`-Auftraege und loesten **neun** Health-Alarmmails aus (`outbox_dead_jobs`). Kein einziger echter Lead war betroffen: Alle stammten aus E2E-Laeufen mit `e2e-scroll@example.com`.

Der Mechanismus: Das E2E-Geschirr stubt den Bridge-Submit ab, `/api/lead-track` laeuft aber echt weiter und reihte den Rang-Rueckschrieb ein. Der schreibt `update ... where hash = <lead_hash>` in die MySQL-Kartei — eine Zeile, die es fuer Testverkehr nie gibt. n8n antwortet mit HTTP 200 und `matchedRows: 0`, der Worker wertet das als Fehler, fuenf Versuche ueber ~1,5 h, dann `dead`.

**Zweite, unbemerkte Haelfte desselben Fehlers:** Ohne Testmarke war der Lead fuer den Nurture-Sender (`RqKSRTgFv8mv04H2`) von einem echten nicht zu unterscheiden — der schliesst ausschliesslich ueber `test_lead_marked` aus. Zwoelf Stunden nach dem Opt-in waere eine Erinnerung an `e2e-scroll@example.com` gegangen, eine reservierte Domain und damit ein sicherer Hard Bounce auf dem Postmark-Konto. Gemessen: Die Auswahlabfrage des Senders lieferte alle 19, ein Mautic-Kontakt ist nicht noetig (die Adresse allein genuegt).

## Was sich aendert

- **`api/lead-track.js`** — beim `form_submitted` wird `is_internal_traffic` ausgewertet: kein Rang-Auftrag mehr, stattdessen ein `test_lead_marked`-Ereignis. Das ist derselbe Marker, den der Sender ohnehin liest, deckt auch manuelles `?test=1`-Surfen ab (nicht nur die E2E-Suite) und laesst den n8n-Workflow unangetastet.
- **`api/lead-outbox-worker.js`** — `matchedRows: 0` bei einem test-markierten Lead ist "uebersprungen", nicht "gescheitert". Fuer echte Leads bleibt es ein lauter Fehlschlag; dort ist die fehlende Kartei-Zeile genau der stille Verlust, den der Alarm melden soll. Ist die Marke nicht lesbar, gilt der Lead als echt. Die Zusatzabfrage laeuft nur nach einem Fehlschlag, kostet im Normalfall also nichts.
- **`scripts/e2e/lib.js`, `scripts/e2e/scroll-reset.e2e.js`** — der Kommentar "kein Lead im Backend" war falsch und hat den Fehler mit verdeckt. Gestubt ist nur der Bridge-Submit.
- **`LEAD_SYSTEM_RUNBOOK.md`** — `matchedRows: 0` nicht mehr blind zuruecksetzen; Abfrage, um echten Lead und Testlead zu unterscheiden.
- **Neue Tests** — `interner-testverkehr.test.js` (5) und `outbox-rang-kein-treffer.test.js` (4).

## Bereits erledigt in der Produktion

Die 23 Altauftraege (19 vom 01.09. plus 4 vom 02.09.) stehen auf `done` mit `response_data.reason = internal_traffic_no_kartei_row` — derselbe Ausgang, den der reparierte Worker jetzt selbst erzeugt. Die betroffenen Leads sind als Testleads markiert, es ging keine Nurture-Mail an eine Testadresse. `/api/lead-system-health` meldet wieder `ok`.

🔴 **Bis das hier auf `main` ist, erzeugt jeder E2E-Lauf den Fehler neu** — am 02.09. um 05:48 UTC ist das mit `e2e-matrix@example.com` aus `etappe/e0b-beweisgeschirr` bereits ein zweites Mal passiert.

## Pruefung

- `node --test scripts/tests/*.test.js` — 349 Tests gruen
- `pnpm run lint` — sauber
- `node scripts/verify.js` — bestanden
