author: saikiranreddy18
body:
## The behavioural signal — collect now, score later

Adds `user_tool_interactions`: an append-only log of what people actually do with the tools we recommend.

### The gap

Toolnaut asks nine questions once and answers forever. It knows what someone **said** they wanted; it has never known what they **did next**. Saves and dismissals reach GA4 for a human to read in a dashboard, and nothing about them reaches the ranking — so a tool that every user rejects keeps being recommended.

### What this is not

**Not a scoring table.** Ranking off behaviour needs a volume of users this product does not have yet, and precomputing `tool_recommendation_scores` while `matchScore()` runs in milliseconds would be inventing a cache for a problem nobody has. The data only accrues if collection starts before it is needed.

**Not a widening of `tool_refs`.** That table answers *what is in your stack right now* — current state, one row per tool, rewritten as it changes. This answers *what happened, and when* — history, many rows, never rewritten. Collapsing them would destroy the history the moment someone unsaves a tool.

**Not four new tables.** `user_preferences` is already `profiles.quiz_answers`; `user_tool_stacks` is already `tool_refs` where `kind='stack'`; `learning_paths` is already `roadmap_progress`; `user_skill_profiles` is derivable from the quiz answers. Adding them would recreate the duplicate-schema problem #32 just fixed.

### Design

| Decision | Why |
|---|---|
| Closed action vocabulary in a CHECK | An open text column becomes six spellings of the same event within a month, and then nothing can be counted |
| A `context` column | Saving from a personalised kit is a far stronger signal than saving while browsing the catalogue. Only this column can tell them apart later |
| `metadata jsonb`, unindexed | Room for signal we have not thought of yet without a migration per idea. Nothing queries it, and an unused GIN index is pure write cost |
| Logging in the **stores**, not call sites | Three pages already save tools and a fourth will exist. At the store, a new call site cannot forget |
| Fire-and-forget writes | Saving a tool must feel instant whether or not the network is there. Nothing awaits it, nothing it does can reject |
| No-op for guests | Guests are most of the traffic and have no user id. The product behaves identically; there is simply nothing to record |
| **No UPDATE policy** | Append-only even for its owner. A history that can be rewritten is worthless as evidence |
| DELETE stays open | A person can erase their own behavioural record without filing a support request |
| Two indexes | `(user_id, created_at desc)` matches the RLS predicate; `(tool_slug, action)` is the saves-vs-dismissals aggregate that will eventually feed ranking |

### Tests — 11 new

RLS matrix for the new table: A reads own rows; **B cannot read A even asking for everything**; **B cannot file a row under A**; **nobody can rewrite history**; a user can delete their own; anonymous sees nothing.

Plus a **drift guard**: the `INTERACTIONS` vocabulary in the store must equal the database CHECK exactly. These live in two files, and a silent divergence would fail every insert *inside a fire-and-forget write* — events would just quietly stop arriving with nothing in the logs.

### One incidental fix

`src/utils/supabase.js` now reads `import.meta.env` defensively. It only exists under Vite, so a plain read threw on import and **no `src` module touching it could be unit-tested at all**. Undefined simply means "not configured", which was already a supported state.

### Verification

```
npm run test:app     209/209 pass  (11 new)
npm run test:radar   102/102 pass
npm run build        clean
npm run smoke        all routes render, 0 console errors
```

Note: one smoke run failed a single route transiently, then passed three consecutive times. Worth watching, but it did not reproduce and the failure was not in a route this PR touches.

### To apply

`0007` in Supabase → SQL Editor after merge. Until then `logInteraction` writes to a table that does not exist, the insert fails, and the fire-and-forget path swallows it — the product is unaffected either way.

body:
## Summary

A third account type, alongside Spending and Asset: **Credit**, for credit cards.

- A purchase on a Credit account increases what's owed instead of decreasing a cash balance. Paying it off works through the existing Transfer feature — transferring from a spending account to a credit account reduces what's owed, rather than adding to a positive balance.
- Every place that mutates an account's balance for a transaction (New Log, Quick Add's one-line parser, friend-paid settlement, delete, edit, CSV import, transfer) now goes through a shared `acctDelta()` helper, so a charge and its reversal always net out correctly no matter the account type.
- Credit card spending still counts toward the expense pie chart, payment breakdown, weekly bar chart, and envelope totals — it's real spending, just not immediate cash out — the same way those already excluded only Asset accounts.
- The Bank Accounts & Wallets grid gets a third "Credit" section, subtotaled and shown in red as "owed". Account dropdowns show "owed" next to a credit account's balance, and the Add/Edit Account modal's balance field relabels itself ("Starting amount owed" / "Amount owed") based on the selected type.

author: bigsimmo
body:
## Summary

- **A hardcoded topic denylist was refusing in-corpus psychiatric queries with zero retrieval, and caching the refusal.** `clearlyOutsideCorpusMedicalPattern` short-circuits a query before any content is looked at. Its entries had been transcribed from the four medical false-positive controls' own question text, including the bare tokens `ssri`, `antibiotic`, `pneumonia` and `dka`. So *"Which SSRI is first line for generalised anxiety disorder?"* was refused content-blind, and the empty result was written to `rag_response_cache` under both `cache_kind = "search"` (60 s) and `"answer"` (300 s). This is a live clinician-facing fault, reproduced against the real `analyzeClinicalQuery` before anything was changed.
- **`ssri` is demonstrably in corpus.** It is an `expectedContentTerms` entry of the golden case `vector-gad-worry`, which expects a Generalised Anxiety document at rank 1.
- **The pattern is narrowed to disease-specific phrases**, dropping the bare tokens. All four controls in `rag-eval-cases.ts` still refuse; the in-corpus queries now reach retrieval and are judged on what comes back.
- **The two divergent copies are folded into one constant.** `clinical-search.ts` carried `ketamine sedation` and `rag-query-guard.ts` did not, so the same query could be classified `unsupported_or_general` in one place and still reach retrieval in the other. That is the divergence in its most consequential form: the class selects the composition menu and second-stage rerank engagement, and is a search cache key component.
- **The regex was an unpinned literal.** It is now a stated contract in `tests/corpus-grounding.test.ts`, in both directions, with the genuinely red-provable cases separated from the forward pins rather than presented as one undifferentiated block.

### What this deliberately does not do

`#000GN4`'s recorded fix was "delete the denylist, let `classifyCorpusGrounding` decide". That does not work, and would regress. `classifyCorpusGrounding` is consulted only for soft-tail-eligible analyses, and `unsupportedSoftTailEligible` requires `reasons` to be exactly `["no_specific_rag_class_terms"]`. Three of the four controls carry `reasons: ["medication_dose_or_risk_terms"]` because they contain the word "dose", so deleting the guard hands the decision not to corpus grounding but to the weak-support route gate — the mechanism `docs/process-hardening.md` records as measured at `unsupported_correct_rate` 0.79 on 2026-07-03.

The cache-write behaviour is also left alone, and that is a change from the plan for this work. Skipping the cache write was justified only by the pattern being over-broad; once it matches genuine out-of-corpus phrases, `rag-query-guard.ts`'s own stated rule applies — a deterministic corpus-derived true negative stays cacheable — and adding an exclusion would have contradicted the module's design for no clinical gain.

One deliberate, separate loss to name: dropping bare `dka` means *"What is the DKA protocol?"* no longer refuses by pattern and falls to the weak-support route gate. The control spells the disease out, so no eval gate depends on the abbreviation.

## Verification

- [x] `npm run verify:pr-local` — full risk-routed gate: `check:runtime`, `check:installed-lock-parity`, `format:changed`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `test`, `check:repo-awareness-snapshot`, `build`, `eval:rag:offline`, `eval:rag:adversarial:offline`, `check:medication-interactions`, `check:medication-lexicon-report`. Summary line: `- failed: (none)`.
- [x] Full offline unit suite: `Test Files 947 passed (947)` / `Tests 12067 passed | 1 skipped (12068)`.
- [x] `npm run eval:rag:offline` — offline contract fixtures, `Test Files 26 passed (26)` / `Tests 630 passed (630)`.
- [x] `npm run eval:rag:adversarial:offline` — `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 25 passed (25)`.
- [x] Targeted: `tests/corpus-grounding.test.ts` `Tests 31 passed (31)`, plus `clinical-search`, `rag-query-guard-soft-tail-cache`, `rag-unsupported-short-circuit-cache`, `retrieval-query-variants`, `rag-routing`, `rag-classifier-memo` all green.
- [x] `npm run format` — run, and the result is committed.
- [x] Reviewed by the `rag-retrieval-reviewer` subagent on this exact diff before push, against `docs/rag-behaviour/` (README, behaviour-map, refuted-approaches, safeguards). It confirmed by execution that all four eval controls still refuse and that nothing here contradicts Refutations 1–6. Three of its findings were applied before this push: a false claim about why the golden set cannot see this bug (corrected — see below), the untested `ketamine sedation` class flip (now pinned), and four assertions presented as defect proofs that were in fact forward pins (relabelled).

**Two claims corrected during review, recorded because the first version of this PR would have shipped them:**

1. The reason the golden set cannot catch this is **not** that its cases set `forceEmbedding: true` — only 10 of 36 do, and `eval:retrieval:quality` does not pass `--force-embedding`. The correct reason is stronger: **not one of the 36 golden queries matches this pattern in either its old or its narrowed form.** `ssri` appears only in a case's expected content terms, never in a question. So the guard never fires during that eval, and `eval:retrieval:compare` cannot move in either direction from this diff.
2. Consequently, **a green canary here would be green by construction and must not be read as evidence this change was safe.** The eval that actually discriminates is `eval:quality --rag-only`'s `unsupported_correct_rate`, which pins the four controls through `scripts/eval-utils.ts`.

Not run, provider-backed, named rather than skipped silently:

- `npm run eval:retrieval:quality` — needs live Supabase and OpenAI. As established above it structurally cannot observe this code path, so it is named for completeness rather than as the gate that matters.
- `npm run eval:quality -- --rag-only` — **this is the one that matters**, and it needs live keys and provider spend.
- The `eval-canary` repository dispatch pair — provider-backed, ~US$1–2 per run.

## Risk and rollout

- Risk: medium. This is a protected RAG surface, and the change alters which queries reach retrieval at all. It is bounded in the safe direction — the change only lets MORE queries through to be judged on retrieved content, and never suppresses a query that previously retrieved — but "more queries reach retrieval" is a real behaviour change on a live clinician-facing path, and offline-green was proven insufficient for this surface on 2026-07-20.
- Rollback: revert the single commit. No state is written and no schema changes, so a revert fully restores prior behaviour; existing cached refusals expire within 60 s (search) and 300 s (answer) on their own TTLs, and no cache version bump is needed.
- Provider or production effects: None from this diff. The evals and canary named above are separate, explicitly-approved actions.
- RAG impact: behaviour change — canary pair 32111839806 (last green scheduled canary on `main`, 2026-08-18) -> planned post-merge.

**On that canary baseline, honestly:** `docs/rag-behaviour/safeguards.md` sanctions `planned post-merge` for the second half, because the workflow has no `workflow_dispatch` and no `ref` input and can therefore only ever measure `main`. The baseline half needs a caveat the gate itself cannot express: **the canary has been red on `main` for two weeks.** Runs 90 through 93 (2026-08-22, 08-23, 08-30, and 09-02 — today) all concluded `failure`. Run `32111839806` is simply the last green one. That standing red is unrelated to this diff and predates it, but it means the pair is not currently meaningful evidence, and re-establishing a green baseline is a precondition for reading the post run, not a formality.

## Clinical Governance Preflight

- [x] Source-backed claims still require linked source verification before clinical use
- [x] No patient-identifiable document workflow was introduced or expanded

author: bjmeetsfo
body:
Follow-up to #618, on a fresh branch — #618 auto-merged before this landed on it.

The new accessor guard asks what each accessor returns for an **unconfigured** tenant, which means unsetting that knob's env var. `unittest discover` runs the whole suite in one process, so unsetting without restoring reconfigures every test that runs after it.

Nothing has been observed failing from it. I initially suspected it caused the 35 red tests on that run and checked rather than assumed: main's own ratchet reports the identical `failing now: 156 baseline: 121`, the two NEW-failure name sets differ by zero in both directions, and stripping these vars by hand does not reproduce the failures. So this is a hazard being removed, not a regression being fixed.

It is worth removing anyway: a test that takes process environment and does not put it back is the Python form of the defect behind the "flaky" Rust suite, and it has no business being introduced by a test whose entire purpose is catching quiet disagreements.

Verified: with the cleanup in place, the process environment before and after the guard runs differs by no keys.

**Separately, and more important than this PR:** the ratchet baseline is stale. main is at 156 failing against a recorded baseline of 121, so the gate is currently red on every branch and gates nothing. Worth re-recording from a main run.

author: claude[bot]
body:
## Le defaut

`naming._audio_track_sort_key` lisait le rang du codec par un lookup **EXACT** sur le `codec` **BRUT** du probe (`AUDIO_CODEC_RANK.get(codec, 0)`). Or aucun backend ne rend la forme canonique :

- **ffprobe** range le codec de BASE dans `codec` (`dts`, `truehd`) et la VARIANTE dans des champs SEPARES (`profile`, `is_atmos`, `is_dts_x`) — cf. `infra/probe/_normalize_ffprobe.py:209-215` ;
- **ffprobe** ne rend jamais « pcm » nu, mais `pcm_s16le`, `pcm_s24le`, `pcm_bluray` ;
- **MediaInfo** rend son `Format` : `AC-3`, `E-AC-3`, `PCM` — cf. `_normalize_mediainfo.py:97`.

Aucune de ces formes n'est une cle de `AUDIO_CODEC_RANK`, donc toutes tombaient au rang **0**, c'est-a-dire **SOUS l'AAC et le MP3 (1)** :

| forme reellement produite | rang lu | rang canonique |
|---|---|---|
| `pcm_s16le` / `pcm_s24le` / `pcm_bluray` | **0** | 3 |
| `ac-3` / `e-ac-3` (MediaInfo) | **0** | 2 |
| `mlp` | **0** | — |
| `dts` + `profile: DTS-HD MA` | 2 | 4 |

`_best_audio_track` prend le `max` de cette cle. Sur un **remux PCM 5.1 double d'une piste AAC 2.0 de commentaires**, c'est l'AAC qui etait elue « meilleure piste ». Et cette piste alimente `{audio_codec}` et `{channels}` (`naming.py:339-341`), deux variables reconnues du template (`_KNOWN_VARS`) — donc le **NOM DU DOSSIER**, la seule chose que ce produit renomme, portait « aac » et « 2.0 ».

## Quatrieme site d'un defaut deja corrige trois fois

C'est R8-039 / ultra-audit 2026-08-03, referme dans `quality_score._best_audio_track`, `duplicate_compare._best_audio`, puis `audio_perceptual.select_best_audio_track` le 2026-08-31. Celui-ci est reste en arriere pour une raison **datable** : il est ne « self-contained » en **PR #758** (juillet 2026), AVANT que `_canonical_audio_codec` n'existe. Son argument d'alors — « `codec_ranks` est un module feuille deja importe -> aucun cycle » — etait exact au moment ou il a ete ecrit.

**Et le depot affirmait deja que ce site etait bon.** La docstring de `audio_perceptual._track_codec_rank` (`audio_perceptual.py:117-118`) cite `naming._best_audio_track` parmi les trois implementations qui « passent toutes par `_canonical_audio_codec` ». C'etait faux. Ce correctif rend l'affirmation vraie plutot que de la corriger.

## Le remede

Delegation a `quality_score._audio_codec_rank`, qui porte deja la derivation canonique **et** la table d'alias — le meme chemin que `duplicate_compare` et `audio_perceptual`. **Aucun rang n'est invente** (donner une place a `mlp` reste un arbitrage produit, hors sujet ici) et **aucune valeur ne peut baisser** : `_canonical_audio_codec` est idempotente et laisse passer les etiquettes deja canoniques.

## Verifications faites avant d'ecrire

- **Pas de cycle** : dans `cinesort/domain/`, seul `duplicate_support` importe `naming` ; `quality_score` ne l'importe pas, ni aucun des modules de sa chaine transitive (`codec_ranks`, `confidence_thresholds`, `conversions`, `custom_rules`, `explain_score`, `genre_rules`, `release_name_parser`, `resolution_class`, `tiers_helpers`).
- **Cliquets** : l'import est TOP-LEVEL, donc sans effet sur `test_lazy_imports_bounded` (`MAX_LAZY_IMPORTS_BY_LAYER`) ; `_audio_track_sort_key` reste tres en dessous de `MAX_LINES = 100` (`test_function_size_budget.py`) ; `domain -> domain` ne touche aucun contrat d'`.importlinter`.
- **`_AUDIO_CODEC_RANK` retire de `naming`** : son unique usage etait cette ligne, et aucun test ne l'importe depuis ce module (`naming` n'est pas un module de re-export, contrairement a `plan_support` / `probe_models`).
- **Portee** : `_audio_track_sort_key` n'a qu'un appelant (`_best_audio_track`), lui-meme appele au seul `build_naming_context:338`.

## Tests

`tests/test_naming_piste_audio_canonique.py` — les formes reellement produites par les backends, plus un contre-test que le correctif **ne redistribue aucun rang deja etabli** (truehd, aac seule, departage par canaux a rang egal), plus le **cablage** via `build_naming_context`. L'assertion du cablage porte sur `channels` (« 5.1 ») : c'est la seule valeur que SEULE la piste elue peut produire — le libelle du codec, lui, pourrait etre satisfait par une autre source du contexte.

Sans le correctif, six de ces assertions sont rouges (l'AAC 2.0 gagne, `channels` vaut « 2.0 »).

---

> **Correctif NON verifie localement** (le runner d'audit n'installe et n'execute rien : ni ruff, ni pytest, ni l'application) — **verification deleguee a la CI de cette PR**.

Audit automatique du 2026-09-02, couche `all`. Rapport : `docs/internal/audits/claude/2026-09-02-all.md`.

author: unchidev
body:
Adds ChordPro (`.cho`, `.chordpro`, `.chopro`) — a plain-text lead-sheet
format where `[Am]`-style chord annotations are interleaved with lyrics,
`{directive}` lines carry metadata, and `{start_of_tab}` /
`{end_of_tab}`-style blocks wrap a foreign notation (tab, ABC, LilyPond)
that is carried verbatim.

## What's in here

- `[[language]]` / `[[grammar]]` entries in `languages.toml`, pinned to a
  commit of the grammar in `packages/tree-sitter-chordpro`
- `chordsketch-lsp` as the default language server (`cargo install
  chordsketch-lsp`); it speaks LSP over stdio and needs no arguments
- `runtime/queries/chordpro/highlights.scm`
- a highlight test corpus under `tests/query/highlights/chordpro/`

Only `highlights.scm` is shipped: ChordPro is flat and line-oriented, so
no construct opens an indent level, and there is no function/class-like
node for textobjects to hang off.

`block_content` is captured as `@markup.raw.block` rather than
`@embedded` — the body of a delegate block is a raw block of another
notation, not an interpolated expression inside a string.

## Verification

```
$ cargo xtask query-check chordpro
Query check succeeded

$ cargo xtask highlight-check chordpro
Highlight check succeeded (33 assertions)

$ cargo xtask theme-check
Theme check successful!
```

author: avifenesh
body:
/v1/embeddings with N inputs and /v1/rerank with N documents run one admitted, priced
worker request per item, and every one of them opened its receipt under the parent
envelope id. The budget ledger keys debits by request id as a replay guard: a second
debit under an already-debited id is swallowed when the amount matches and refused
("conflicting budget debits") when it does not. So N items billed as ONE item whenever
their costs rounded to the same micro-USD, and the whole request answered HTTP 500
request_ledger_unavailable, after item 0 was billed, whenever they did not.

Surfaced 2026-09-02 on the Texas retrieval stack right after the rerank re-price to
$0.05/1M: documents of 80 and 81 prompt tokens cost 4.0 -> 4 and 4.05 -> 5 micro-USD.
Ledger receipts (darklanes research/fleet-consolidation-tx-20260902/
INCIDENT-rerank-ledger-conflict.md): rerank [79, 79, 79] -> one debit of 4; rerank
[80, 81] -> 500 after a debit of 4; embeddings [2, 40] -> one debit of 1.

Fix: run_capture derives Envelope::capture_child(index) = "<parent id>.<index>" and
opens the receipt, admission, meter line and rate-limit slot under it. Each capture
debits exactly once; the HTTP response and x-request-id keep the parent id; children
nest under it by prefix for reconciliation and log attribution. Unit test pins the
derivation. The ledger-side contract (children each debit; a shared id stays a replay
guard) is pinned in darklanes serving/darklanes-metering, and the darklanes retrieval
deploy gate now reranks documents of different lengths and asserts one journal debit
per item (red on this binary's predecessor by construction).

Darklanes side (same incident): the ledger contract test, the retrieval deploy gate arms and the incident note land in darklanes `lane/retrieval-rerank-ledger-20260902`; the engine pin bump follows this merge.

author: jaeyoon-choi
body:
Add FreeBSD support, backed by DPDK's contigmem kernel module, plus a few
Linux fixes found along the way.

## Why contigmem and not superpages

This tool exists to reserve memory that a user space driver can hand to a
device for DMA. That needs three things: the memory must be physically
contiguous, it must be wired so the kernel cannot move or page it out, and
its physical address must be readable from user space.

Linux hugetlb gives all three. FreeBSD has no equivalent pool. Its
superpages are a transparent mapping optimization: the VM promotes 512
aligned, contiguous 4 KiB pages into one 2 MiB PDE when it happens to be
able to, and demotes them again when it needs to. Nothing is reserved,
nothing is pinned, and no physical address is exported. Superpages solve TLB
pressure, not DMA.

Physically contiguous DMA memory on FreeBSD comes from the contigmem kernel
module that ships with DPDK. It allocates with `contigmalloc(9)`, so the
memory is contiguous and wired, and it publishes each buffer's physical
address as a sysctl. The buffers are consumed by `mmap`ing `/dev/contigmem`.

So the real counterpart of Linux hugetlb here is contigmem, not superpages.

## What the FreeBSD backend does

| Command | Linux | FreeBSD |
| ------- | ----- | ------- |
| `info` | totals/free/reserved per size from sysfs | contigmem load state, buffer count and size, physical addresses |
| `setup --count N` | writes `nr_hugepages` | sets the `hw.contigmem` tunables with `kenv`, then `kldload` |
| `setup --count 0` | releases the pool | `kldunload` |
| `mount` | mounts hugetlbfs | informational, there is no filesystem to mount |

Details that shaped the code:

- contigmem reads its tunables only at load time, so a resize unloads and
  reloads the module. `kldunload` returns EBUSY while a process still has a
  buffer mapped, so a live reservation cannot be taken away.
- `--count` and `--size` are validated before any command runs. A rejected
  size must not cost the user a working reservation.
- `--size` means different things per platform. On Linux it is an MMU page
  size and argparse restricts it to what sysfs reports. contigmem takes any
  power-of-2 size, so there is no list to enumerate: `supported_sizes()`
  returns `[]` and the backend validates the size itself.
- `info` reports which large page size each buffer is aligned to, read from
  `hw.pagesizes` rather than hardcoded, and warns when a buffer is smaller
  than the smallest large page.
- Error paths name the next step: non-root exits with EPERM and asks for
  sudo, a missing module points at the DPDK package, a busy unload names
  `fstat /dev/contigmem`, and a failed reload says the previous reservation
  is already gone.

Linux behavior is unchanged.

## Also included

Four commits that stand on their own, ordered before the FreeBSD work:

- `802bc1f` drops an unused constant and adds `--version` to the bash
  completion.
- `a60aebc` runs commands as argument lists instead of shell strings. A
  mountpoint with shell metacharacters used to run as a command, as root.
- `3d5af05` stops reporting `setup --count 0` as a failed reservation.
- `344db24` moves the Linux implementation behind a backend class so a
  second platform has somewhere to go.

## Testing

Unit tests fake every external command, so they cover the logic, the command
ordering, and the error paths on any host: 32 tests, all passing.

Those tests cannot say what the real commands do, and one gap already
mattered. FreeBSD `kenv(1)` prints no errno text when it fails, so a root
check that matched on stderr never fired and a plain user got a generic
error instead of the sudo hint. The check now reads the euid before running
anything.

That is why this PR also adds `tests/freebsd-smoke.sh`, which drives the
real kenv, kldload, kldunload, and sysctl path. It needs root, refuses to
run anywhere but FreeBSD, and restores the contigmem state it found.

Verified on FreeBSD 15.1-RELEASE with contigmem from `dpdk25.11`:

- 27 smoke assertions, all passing, from both an unloaded and a loaded
  starting state
- manual runs covering a missing module, a plain user, load, resize,
  a rejected size, EBUSY while mapped, release, and a reboot with the
  tunables in `/boot/loader.conf`

Measured alignment, which is what `info` now reports:

| Requested | Physical address | Reported |
| --------- | ---------------- | -------- |
| 512 MiB x 1 | `0x280000000` | `(1 GiB aligned)` |
| 4 MiB x 2 | `0x26e400000`, `0x1bb000000` | `(2 MiB aligned)` |
| 1 MiB x 1 | `0x1b2500000` | none, with a warning |

## Note for reviewers

contigmem is not part of the FreeBSD base system. It ships with DPDK, and
the package name carries the DPDK version, so `pkg install dpdk25.11` rather
than `pkg install dpdk`. The tool detects the missing module and says so.

author: kamira
body:
Three defects on `main`, found by the **defect seat** reviewing the **third** draft of CHG-20260901-15. One root, three surfaces: **the grade a panel decides reached nothing that names it.**

| | the declaration | what it reached |
|---|---|---|
| D-1 | `_Process.risk` — *"Derived from **the grade in force**"* | the plan's proposal, bound once |
| D-2 | `Node.settles_risk` | only a node with >1 model configured |
| D-3 | `SCHEMAS.md`'s `closed` turn — `… · risk · change_class` | no `risk` key at all |

## D-1 — bounded at the plan's proposal, told it is at the grade in force

`can_write` is a property of the role and was wired per ask, with a test written because an earlier version looked at the seat name and *"the table was right and the promise was still not kept."* `risk` was bound **once**, from `cfg.risk` — which `cmd_run` documents as *"the plan's proposal"*.

```
cfg.risk (the plan's proposal)  : low
report.risk_agreed              : high
_Process(role='engineer').risk  : 'low'  -> {'write': 'workspace', 'network': True}
```

**The same ask carried `policy_verdict.risk = "high"` in its work order while running in a `low` sandbox.** All three shipped example plans declare `risk: low`.

The fix needed **no new parameter**: the order already carries the grade, because `workorder.render` puts the resolved verdict in `policy_verdict` and that verdict was resolved at `_grade_in_force`. `_ask` reads it off the order it is already holding. Zero changed call sites. Measured over a full walk: **0 asks** where the two disagree.

## D-2 — the ratifier only ratified when it was a panel

`report.risk_settled` was written at one line, inside `if node.mode == MODEL_PANEL and len(configured) > 1`. `pm_signoff` is the only `settles_risk` node; a default install has `node_models = {}`.

```
default install, risk=low    risk_settled = None      <- before
                             risk_settled = 'low'     <- after
```

`_grade_in_force`'s per-workstream branch is guarded on `if not settled`, so **CHG-20260827-18 was dead code by default.** Two tests assign `risk_settled` on a hand-built report; none drove a walk to it.

Moved to where the three answer paths meet, keyed on the answer rather than the mode.

**One thing this nearly got wrong**, recorded because it is the same defect class: the first version compared `choice == policy.PASS`. `pm_signoff` offers `yes`/`no`; `pass` is what a *panel* answers. A literal `"yes"` would be a branch name standing in for a constraint, so the ratifying branch is read off the node's own `panel_branches`.

## D-3 — the durable record dropped the grade

`conversations.close` drops falsy values, so with D-2 the closing turn carried no `risk` on any default install — with `change_class` right beside it, which is what made it read as *"this run had no grade"* rather than *"this field is unwired"*.

## Test-the-test — three fixes, four reverts

| | revert | result |
|---|---|---|
| D-1 engine seam | stop `_open` passing the grade | **1 failed** |
| D-1 `cli` seam | `risk=risk` | **1 failed**, a *different* test |
| D-2 | settling back inside the panel branch | **1 failed** |

**The second row is the point.** Reverting the `cli` side alone left the engine-side test **green** — it drives a stub factory and measures the engine, not `cli.session_factory`. Two seams, two tests. Stopping at one revert would have shipped a test that could not see the defect it was written for, which is what CHG-20260901-17 M-3 was about.

## Disclosed

- **This tightens sandboxes on runs that were passing.** A raised grade now dispatches at `{'write': 'none', 'network': False}`. It will read as a regression before it reads as a fix.
- **`_grade_in_force`'s per-workstream branch runs on a default install for the first time.** Its tests built the report by hand.
- **The examples mutation anchor moved for the third time** and is re-anchored; `mutation_check --only examples` still reports **CAUGHT**.
- **Not fixed, named:** `--worktree` is silently inert for a module built by a `node_models` model; `plan.FIELDS`' drift guard is one-directional.

Fifteen defects across four design reviews now, all the same shape, none found by the suite.

Suite: **1944 passed, 4 skipped**. README 1944 → 1948.

M5-V1's third bullet (#177), on top of #247 and #248.

The fidelity invariant has been a rule about the *engine*. The claim a
person actually cares about is about their seam — that turning it on and
not using it changes nothing — and no synthetic program can make it.

So a seam PR now owes two recordings: one `identical <baseline>` and one
`contrast <baseline>`. Both are checked on the files with no disk, so CI
checks them on every push. The second is not politeness: a seam can be
on, armed and reporting itself while doing nothing at all, which
happened twice to the cheats (#129, #130) with a green suite throughout.

And it says what to do when a seam genuinely cannot carry the first,
because one cannot — a seam that draws the moment it is on changes the
machine on any run that reaches the thing it draws on. Say so in the
descriptor and pair it with a `contrast`;
`tests/sessions/quiet-journal.session` is the worked example. What is
not acceptable is loosening what `identical` means so that it fits.

pairs as they stand.

author: linusnorton
body:
### Jira link

See [HDPI-8713](https://tools.hmcts.net/jira/browse/HDPI-8713)

### Change description

**MEASUREMENT PR — DO NOT MERGE.** Control arm for an A/B experiment on pcs-api PR build duration. Comment-only change so a PR can exist; build behaviour is identical to `origin/master`.

Needed because **master builds #1996–#1999 are all `FAILURE`** (7.2min, 8.4min, 67.4min, 24.5min), so there is no reliable baseline to compare optimisation branches against.

### Context: where pcs-api build time actually goes

Verified via the Jenkins MCP on PR-2523 #9 (22.7min total). The critical path is the **`Static checks / Container build` stage at 10m23s**, which is `./gradlew --no-daemon --init-script init.gradle check`:

| Task | Duration |
|---|---|
| `writeManifest*` ×9 + `createManifestApplication` | ~40s |
| `composeUp` (wiremock) | ~18s |
| **`cftlibTest`** | **2m40s** |
| `composeDown` | ~6s |
| **`integration`** | **3m14s** |
| `test` (4360 unit tests) | ~15s |

Two corrections to earlier assumptions, both verified:

- **Docker Build is NOT the constraint here.** It is ~1m50s with ~9min of slack. From ACR's own run records the split is pack+upload 32–37s, **ACR queue wait 0.14–0.20s**, remote exec 54–64s. The `Waiting for an agent...` line is printed speculatively by the CLI and is not evidence of queueing — measured queue wait across the 300 most recent `hmctsprod` runs was ≤10s. **No ACR capacity problem.**
- **The 639 MiB Docker context is real but nearly free.** `pcs-api` has no `.dockerignore`, and the image needs only `lib/applicationinsights.json` (417 B) and `build/libs/pcs-api.jar` (141 MB). The bulk is four unused `build/distributions/` archives (~513 MB) generated by the `application` plugin and consumed by nothing. Worth fixing for egress hygiene, but it saves ~40–50s of *branch* time and ~0s of build duration.

So the real target is the `check` stage: roughly 7 of those 10 minutes is Spring/cftlib context startup for **71 test annotations**, with `check.dependsOn cftlibTest` (`build.gradle:643`) booting 8 CFT services in-process for just **11 assertions**.

### Testing done

No code changed. This PR exists to be built and timed, 3 times, with the median reported.

### Security Vulnerability Assessment

**CVE Suppression:** Are there any CVEs present in the codebase (either newly introduced or pre-existing) that are being intentionally suppressed or ignored by this commit?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

### Checklist

- [x] commit messages are meaningful and follow good commit message guidelines
- [ ] README and other documentation has been updated / added (if needed)
- [ ] tests have been updated / new tests has been added (if needed)
- [ ] Does this PR introduce a breaking change

author: urbicon
body:
Implements **S12** from the auth probe's blind-redesign divergences — the last of the three (S2 and P9 shipped with #327).

`authError(code, status, opts?)` took the status per call. 103 call sites repeated it, and nothing checked that one code answers under one status.

### The census, and what it found

A regex would have been the obvious instrument and the wrong one: it cannot see double quotes, templates, a code held in a variable, or a multi-line call. An AST pass over the whole tree found **103 call sites, 30 distinct codes, and exactly one ambiguity** — `invalid_code` at 400 (2FA enrolment) and 401 (sign-in). Cross-checked at runtime by instrumenting `authError` to record what it emitted during the suite: 30 of 31 codes are reached through a real handler under test, each with the status the static census found.

### Both statuses were right

Enrolment refuses a wrong code from a user who **is** signed in; sign-in refuses one from a user who is **not**. Forcing either onto the other's status would be a regression that reads as a unification. The defect is a name doing two jobs, so the name is split — along the vocabulary the family already had (`two_factor_setup_required`, `two_factor_challenge_expired` name the two flows):

| flow | code | status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sign-in, second factor | `invalid_code` (unchanged) | 401 |
| enrolment, verifying to enable | `two_factor_setup_code_invalid` (new) | 400 |

The generic name stays on **sign-in** because that is the arm every 2FA consumer necessarily has, and the only one a shipped component branches on (`LoginPage.svelte:127`). `<TwoFactorManager>` branches on no code at all — it renders through `errorTextFromBody` and picks up the new string with no change.

Rejected: the mirror cut (breaks our own login handling and every consumer's, to spare a path no shipped component branches on). Also rejected, and this one is the closer call — retiring `invalid_code` for two flow-named codes. It would make the break loud, but `errors.ts` and `AUTH.md` both state the set is append-only, "never repurposed, only extended"; narrowing a name to the flow it already dominates keeps that, retiring a live member does not.

### The table is total, and that is load-bearing

`AUTH_ERROR_STATUS: Record<AuthErrorCode, number>` — a code without a status does not compile (`TS2741`, reproduced). `Partial<Record<…>>` was measured rather than dismissed: the error disappears, and the value it would have produced is `json(body, { status: undefined })` → **200 OK for a failure**. Exactly the silent fallback this repo forbids.

### No status changed anywhere

The codemod refused to drop an argument that disagreed with the table. **103 of 103 agreed** — that is the proof the table reproduces current behaviour rather than restating it. The one behavioural change is the `code` field of one response body.

### Verification, each instrument seen red first

- **Table totality** — `TS2741` on a code added without a status; and the `Partial` counterfactual measured to 200 OK.
- **i18n binding** — the new code failed to compile before its key existed (`TS1360`, fired for real). Worth recording: `bun run i18n:check` does **not** scan `packages/auth`, so it is not the oracle here despite being in the gate list — `translations.parity.test.ts` is, confirmed by removing the German string.
- **Status assertions bite** — flipping `not_authenticated` 401→403 fails 63 tests; collapsing `invalid_code` to 400 fails 4.
- **The split is tested** — neither wrong-code test asserted `body.code` before, only the status, so the split would have been untested. Both do now; reverting the enrolment site fails with `expected 401 to be 400`, which is the original defect, visible.
- **Argument-slot shift** — the compiler catches a leftover status (`TS2559`) but is **blind** to a dropped `opts`: removing `{ headers: NO_STORE }` from a call type-checks and passes its suite. Covered for the migration by diffing every call's `opts` source text before and after — 38 of 95 carry opts, all byte-identical, none moved slot.

### Found, not fixed

A dropped `{ headers: NO_STORE }` is caught by nothing standing — not the compiler, not the suite. That is pre-existing (equally invisible on the old 3-argument calls) and orthogonal to status-per-code, so it is reported rather than folded in.

`email_unverified` is the one code with no call site anywhere, so its `403` is a judgement rather than a reproduction. Marked as such in the code.

Gates: `lint`, `build:ts`, `types:guard`, `check` (0 errors, all packages), auth 95 files / 1584 tests, `docs:fences:lint`, `examples:lint`, `variants:lint`, `imports:lint`, `icons:lint`, `livery:check`, `a2ui:axes:check`, `consumer-css:check` — all green.

author: k0heik
body:
# 概要

[sparkcast-rename-runbook.md](infra/docs/sparkcast-rename-runbook.md) の **Stage 1〜6 を dev に適用**します。prod の tfvars は変更していないため **prod は無変更**です。

| Stage | 対象 | 変更 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | provider の `default_labels` | dev の `system` を `sparkcast` へ |
| 2〜6 | automator 系の実リソース名 | `automator_name_prefix = "sparkcast-automator"` |

改名される dev リソース:

| 種別 | 変更前 | 変更後 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GCS 入力バケット | `podcast-automator-audio-input-dev` | `sparkcast-automator-audio-input-dev` |
| GCS バックアップ | `podcast-automator-db-backup-dev` | `sparkcast-automator-db-backup-dev` |
| Cloud Run Job | `podcast-automator-{app,agenda,db-backup}-dev` | `sparkcast-automator-…-dev` |
| Cloud Scheduler | 同上 | 同上 |
| Workflows | `podcast-automator-dev` | `sparkcast-automator-dev` |
| Eventarc | `podcast-automator-gcs-finalize-dev` | `sparkcast-automator-gcs-finalize-dev` |
| Artifact Registry | `podcast-automator-dev` | `sparkcast-automator-dev` |

## あわせて修正した 2 点

### 1. `cloud_sql.tf` の名前をリテラル固定（重要）

Stage 1 で `var.system` をラベル用に `sparkcast` へ変えたところ、**Cloud SQL インスタンス名が `podcast-automator-postgres-dev` → `sparkcast-postgres-dev` になり、再作成＝データ喪失の計画**になっていました。#124 では「接頭辞の切替に巻き込まれないよう `var.system` 直参照のままにする」としていましたが、ラベル側から同じ変数を踏む経路が残っていました。

Cloud SQL は #90 Stage 5 で撤去予定であり、かつ **#90 のロールバック先**でもあるため、インスタンス名と DB パスワード secret 名を現行値でリテラル固定しました。これで prod の live サービスが参照する `podcast-automator-database-password-prod` も守られます。

### 2. バックアップバケットの `force_destroy` を変数化

`force_destroy = false` のままだとバケット改名時の destroy が「中身がある」で失敗します。既定 false のまま `backup_bucket_force_destroy` 変数を追加し、**dev のみ true**にしました。dev のダンプは開発データのため破棄可、**prod は false のままで、rsync でダンプを移送してから改名**します（手順書 Stage 6）。

## 検証（terraform console）

| 式 | dev | prod |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `local.automator_name_prefix` | `sparkcast-automator` | `podcast-automator`（不変） |
| `var.system` | `sparkcast` | `podcast-automator`（不変） |
| `var.backup_bucket_force_destroy` | `true` | `false`（不変） |
| Cloud SQL インスタンス名 | `podcast-automator-postgres-dev`（不変） | `podcast-automator-postgres-prod`（不変） |
| DB パスワード secret | `podcast-automator-database-password-dev`（不変） | `podcast-automator-database-password-prod`（不変） |

`terraform fmt` / `validate` も通っています。

## 適用時に想定される影響（dev）

- **パイプラインが数分停止します。** Job / Workflows / Eventarc トリガが順に再作成されるため、その間の GCS アップロードは処理が起動しません。収録の無い時間帯に流してください。
- **入力バケットのデータ移行は不要**です。`gcs_retention_days = 3` の一時領域で、DB の `source_audio_path` はバケット名を持ちません。ただし**切替時点で `processing` のエピソードは入力を見失う**ため、処理中が無いことを確認してください。
- **dev のバックアップダンプは破棄されます**（上記のとおり意図的）。
- ⚠️ TF が UI サービスの `GCS_UPLOAD_BUCKET` env を新バケットに更新するため、**新しいリビジョンが作られます**。cd.yml はトラフィックを特定リビジョンにピン留めする運用なので、**配信中のリビジョンが古いバケットを指したままになる可能性**があります（#90 Stage 2 で実際に踏んだ罠）。本 PR は `infra/**` のみの変更で `ui` ジョブがスキップされるため、apply 後に UI のアップロードが通るかを必ず確認し、必要なら `gcloud run services update-traffic` で新リビジョンへ寄せてください。続く ui 側の PR（Stage 7）で `cd.yml` を変更するので、そこで CD が新リビジョンを作り直してトラフィックを寄せ直します。

## 検証観点（apply 後）

- [ ] 新しい名前の Job / Scheduler / Workflow / Eventarc / バケットが存在する
- [ ] UI から音声をアップロードし、**新バケット**にオブジェクトが置かれる
- [ ] Eventarc → Workflows → Job が起動し、エピソードが `completed` になる
- [ ] db-backup ジョブを手動実行し、新バケットにダンプが出力される
- [ ] Cloud SQL インスタンスが**削除されていない**

## 関連issue

#72（Stage 1〜6 の dev 適用。prod と ui 側 Stage 7〜8 が残るため close しません）

author: devmattg
body:
## Summary

Reworks how topic/sequence metadata and time-window statistics travel over
Arrow Flight, fixing schema metadata clobbering and moving row-count/interval
computation off the DO_GET data path and onto GetFlightInfo.

- Client schema/field metadata (e.g. set via pyarrow's `Schema/Field.with_metadata`
  at `do_put` time) was being overwritten by platform metadata flattened into the
  Arrow schema's key-value metadata. Platform metadata (ontology info,
  timestamp range, message count, etc.) now travels on `FlightEndpoint::app_metadata`
  for `get_flight_info` instead of being merged into the schema.
- `TimeseriesEngine::count_and_timestamp_range()` computes row count + timestamp
  interval for a requested time window directly, so this no longer requires
  streaming the data through DO_GET first.
- `TopicAppMetadata` now separates whole-topic stats (`data_info`) from
  optional per-request time-window stats (`time_window_info`), which are
  populated when a client requests `get_flight_info` with a timestamp range
  — including topics/sequences with no data in the requested window.
- Added docs: new "API Specs" section describing the `GetFlightInfo` response
  shape (`docs/daemon/api_specs/get_flight_info.md`).

## Breaking changes

- `FlightInfo`/`do_get` responses no longer carry `mosaico:properties` /
  `mosaico:user_metadata` / `mosaico:context` as Arrow schema metadata;
  consumers must read `app_metadata` instead.
- `TopicAppMetadata`'s JSON shape changes: `info` is replaced by `data_info`
  (whole-topic stats, always present) and `time_window_info` (present only
  when a timestamp range was requested). `TopicDataInfo.chunks_number` is
  renamed to `total_chunks`, with `total_row_count` added.
- `DO_GET` no longer carries `app_metadata` on the first message
  (`TopicDoGetAppMetadata` removed).

## Testing

- Updated/added coverage in `tests/tests/{do_get,topic,sequence,concurrent,schema,unsorted_data}.rs`
  for the new `TopicAppMetadata` shape, including `get_flight_info` with a
  time window on a sequence and on a topic with no data.
- Updated `mosaico-sdk-py` integration tests (`test_endpoints.py`) for the
  new metadata shape.

Closes #732

author: neoemptor
body:
## Summary

Cleanup pass over `src/lib/server`. Every scraper in there had at least one defect that made it unable to do the thing it was named for — two of the three ignored the sites they were passed and scraped a hardcoded URL instead.

| Commit | Change |
|---|---|
| `cc6ac27` | Fix shell command injection in `FileHandler.save`; delete stale compiled output |
| `1c7c832` | Remove unused `express`, `openai`, `@types/express` |
| `1b033fa` | Fix `Keyword.extract` scraping `example.com` instead of the given sites |
| `6d846f6` | Match keywords that start or end with punctuation |
| `1edf2dc` | Resolve Chrome and SEO Quake paths instead of hardcoding them |
| `f47ade8` | Take the sites to scrape as a parameter in `SEOQData.extractData` |

## Shell injection

`FileHandler.save` built a command string with the site URL interpolated into it and handed that to `exec()`, which spawns a shell:

```ts
const command: string = `lighthouse ${site} --output=json ...`;
exec(command, ...)
```

Any shell metacharacter in a site value would have been executed. The site list is hardcoded today, so this is not currently reachable — but user-entered URLs are the whole point of the app, so it would have become reachable as soon as the UI was wired up.

**Fix:** `execFile()` with an argv array and `shell: false`, so arguments reach the process verbatim. `execFile` alone still leaves a gap — a value beginning with `--` is read by Lighthouse as an *option* rather than a target — so `isSafeUrl` rejects anything that is not a parseable `http:`/`https:` URL.

## Scrapers ignoring their input

`Keyword.extract` defined its scrape function inside the `forEach` body and then called it with a literal `'https://example.com'`, so the `site` parameter was never used. ESLint had been reporting this as `'site' is defined but never used`. `SEOQData.extractData` took no arguments at all and always navigated to `robinsonswelding.com.au`.

Both now take `websites: string[]`, consistent with `LHData.extract`. `SEOQData` launches one browser and reuses it across the list rather than one per site — it runs headed with a ten second settle per page.

## Keyword counting

Two bugs in the same expression:

- Keywords went unescaped into `new RegExp`. Verified in Node: `"c++"` threw `Invalid regular expression: /\bc++\b/gi: Nothing to repeat`, `"a[b"` threw `Unterminated character class`. Either rejected the whole scrape.
- `\b` only matches where a word character meets a non-word character, so a keyword whose first or last character is punctuation could never match at all.

Both boundaries are now `(?<!\w)` / `(?!\w)`. Checked against the previous behaviour:

| keyword | expected | new | old |
|---|---|---|---|
| `c++` | 2 | 2 | **0** |
| `$99` | 1 | 1 | **0** |
| `(perth)` | 1 | 1 | **0** |
| `garage doors` | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| `doors` in `"Doorstop indoors doors"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `c++` in `"abcc++nope"` | 0 | 0 | 0 |

Counts for ordinary keywords are unchanged, which was the constraint — a fix that shifted existing counts would be a regression. The last row confirms the lookarounds still reject a match embedded in a surrounding word, which is the property `\b` was there for.

## Hardcoded machine paths

`SEOQData` hardcoded both the Chrome binary and the SEO Quake extension. Neither resolves any more, checked on the machine they were written for:

```
missing  /Program Files (x86)/Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe
missing  /Users/infil/AppData/Local/.../Extensions/<id>/3.10.3_0
```

The Chrome path had no drive letter, so it could never resolve on Windows regardless of install location. The extension path embedded a username and pinned version `3.10.3_0`, which Chrome has since replaced with `3.13.5_0`.

Both are now resolved from `CHROME_PATH` / `SEOQUAKE_EXTENSION_PATH`, falling back to the usual per-platform locations. On Windows both `ProgramFiles` and `ProgramFiles(x86)` are checked. The extension version is read from disk rather than hardcoded. Failures name what was searched and which variable to set, instead of failing later inside `puppeteer.launch`.

## Resource leaks and swallowed errors

Surfaced while making the above changes, and fixed alongside them:

- `browser.close()` in both scrapers sat on the success path, so any throw leaked a Chromium process — a visible window in `SEOQData`'s case, which runs headed. Moved into `finally`, along with `page.close()`.
- `SEOQData`'s handler was `.catch(() => console.log('error'))`, discarding the error object. It now logs the real error; without this, every diagnostic added above would have been invisible.
- Each site in `SEOQData` is wrapped individually, so one unreachable site no longer abandons the rest of the list.
- `FileHandler`'s `Audit completed` log ran synchronously before the audit finished, reporting success unconditionally including on failure. Moved into the callback.

## Unused dependencies

Removed `express`, `openai`, and `@types/express` — no references anywhere in `src/`, `src-tauri/src/`, or the root config files. `express` in particular does not fit the architecture: the app builds to a static bundle via `adapter-static` and ships in a Tauri shell, so there is no Node server for it to run in.

Removed with `npm uninstall` so `package-lock.json` stays in sync — **−915 lockfile lines**. `npm audit` drops from 49 to 43 reported vulnerabilities as a side effect; the remaining 43 are pre-existing and untouched here.

## Testing

After `npm install`, at the tip of the branch:

- `npm run check` — `svelte-check found 0 errors and 0 warnings`
- `npx eslint src/lib/server/ src/hooks.server.ts` — clean

Regex counting and path resolution were both verified by running them in Node; those results are the tables above. **No scraper was run end to end.** `FileHandler` needs the `lighthouse` CLI on PATH, which this project does not declare as a dependency; `SEOQData` needs Chrome with the SEO Quake extension actually loading.

## Not addressed

- `hooks.server.ts` runs all of this as a module side-effect at dev-server boot. With `ssr = false` and `adapter-static` there is no server in a production build, so none of this code ships anywhere yet. That is a design decision — Tauri commands versus `adapter-node` — rather than a fix.
- `WBMData` is not imported by anything, and `Competitor` is an empty class. Left as-is.

> Note: the `cc6ac27` commit message carries an earlier "not verified by compiler" caveat. That was accurate when written (`node_modules` was not installed at the time); the checks above have since been run and pass.

author: captainurist
body:
`OverlayDesc` is a row of the `doverlay.bin` table, so it becomes `OverlayData` in `Engine/Data`, and `OverlayList` follows it as `OverlayTable` in `Engine/Tables`. That is the pairing every other data table already uses. `Engine/Graphics` keeps `ActiveOverlay` and `ActiveOverlayList`, which are the runtime and savegame half, so that header no longer mixes the two. Names come along for the ride, `InitializeSprites` is now `initializeSprites` and the row vector is `overlays`, which no longer collides with `ActiveOverlayList::pOverlays`.

The snapshot type becomes `OverlayData_MM7` to match `TileData_MM7` and friends. Its layout is untouched and `MM_DECLARE_MEMCOPY_SERIALIZABLE` keys off the type rather than its name, so no data file or save is affected.

The last two bytes of the row are gone from the runtime struct. They were called `spriteFramesetGroup`, but nothing supports that name, and digging into MM6.exe and MMExtension turned up what the other fields really are. `uOverlayType` is a placement mode that `overlay.txt` spelled as a keyword, and MM6 branches on it, while `uSpriteFramesetID` is populated in MM6 alone. Details are in a comment below.

author: frauschi
body:
## Description

Three related defects in the PKCS#7 RecipientInfo walk. None involve post-quantum algorithms - the reproduction throughout is two plain RSA recipients. The commit messages carry the detailed rationale.

**AuthEnvelopedData with more than one recipient has never worked.** The decoder stops at the RecipientInfo that matches and, unlike the EnvelopedData decoder, never steps over the ones after it, so the `EncryptedContentInfo` that follows the set is parsed from the wrong offset. `wc_PKCS7_DecodeAuthEnvelopedData()` has behaved this way since `bc94cdc11`, first released in v3.15.5-stable. The equivalent fix landed for EnvelopedData alone in `6987304f4` (v5.8.4-stable), which introduced `PKCS7State.recipientSz` and the step-over; AuthEnvelopedData was not covered by it.

**The recipient search was not bounded by the RecipientInfo set.** After exhausting the recipients the walk read the `EncryptedContentInfo` that follows as though it were another RecipientInfo, so a message carrying no recipient for the reader came back as a parse error rather than as "no recipient found". `wc_PKCS7_ParseToRecipientInfoSet()` already returns the size of the set, so it is passed down as a new `setEnd` argument and the walk stops at the end of the set.

**The stream accounting was left inconsistent after a rejected RecipientInfo.** A rejected handler stops counting the moment it decides the recipient is not the reader's, but the index has already stepped over the whole structure, so the next handler's bookkeeping compounded the difference and the decode asked for input it had already consumed. The two stream modes need opposite handling, hence the new `wc_PKCS7_StreamResyncRecipient()` helper.

## Behaviour change

`wc_PKCS7_DecodeEnvelopedData()` returns **`PKCS7_RECIP_E` instead of `ASN_PARSE_E`** when no recipient in the set is the reader's. The old value was a symptom of the unbounded search rather than an answer; the one expectation in `tests/api/test_pkcs7.c` that asserted it is updated in the commit that makes it wrong.

`wc_PKCS7_DecryptRecipientInfos()` takes an eighth argument. It is `static` to `pkcs7.c`, so no public or internal API changes; the only other callers are the MC/DC white-box programs under `tests/unit-mcdc/`, which `#include` the source directly and are updated here.

## Testing

New `test_wc_PKCS7_MultipleRecipients` encodes one message to two `KeyTransRecipientInfo` recipients and opens it as each of them in turn, for EnvelopedData and AuthEnvelopedData, whole and fed in 128-byte chunks. The second recipient is the interesting one - decoding as the first passes even with the search unbounded.

## Out of scope

The chunked leg is scoped to EnvelopedData and the second recipient. Two gaps in the partial-input path predate this change and are untouched: matching on the *first* recipient in chunks fails with `ASN_PARSE_E` on the merge-base and still does, and AuthEnvelopedData fed in chunks has never opened for a recipient other than the first. A `NOTE` on the EnvelopedData step-over marks the arithmetic that is only right while the whole set is read in one piece; the AuthEnvelopedData step-over refers back to it.

author: asadullah5593
body:
…d to

An order taker asked a regular where they live every single time, and a call centre agent takes nothing but delivery orders, so it was the most repeated keystroke on the phone. The addresses were already there — 19 of the 25 on record were typed by customers into the app themselves — just never offered back.

customer_addresses is its own table rather than a query over order history. An order records where THAT order went and must never change; an address book is current state, something a customer can move away from, correct a typo in, or ask to have forgotten. Reading one off the other makes none of that expressible without rewriting past orders. orders.delivery_address stays as its own snapshot, the same way order items keep name_snapshot. Hiding an address now leaves every order that went there intact, which was the point.

Keyed on the phone number because that is what the till holds before a customer record exists — guest orders never make one. address_key collapses the spellings of one doorstep, so "House #5, Street 2" and "house 5 street-2" are one entry instead of two; the SQL in the migration and normalizeAddressKey() must agree exactly or the backfilled rows stop matching later writes, which is what address-key.spec.ts is for.

Picking an address restores its COORDINATES with the text. A delivery order is refused without a point, the fee is priced by distance from it and the rider navigates to it, so filling in the words alone would look like it worked and quietly misprice the order. Typing over a picked address drops the point, which would otherwise outlive the words on screen.

Recording happens after the order commits and is never awaited: an address book is a convenience and no failure in it may cost a customer their order.

`orders:customer-addresses:view` gates the lookup, granted to no role — a complete number is all it takes to learn where somebody lives, so who carries it is the client's decision. A partial number is refused, so the till cannot be walked through the customer book a prefix at a time. Brand-locked users see only what their own brand delivered; branch is deliberately not a filter.

## Summary

- add an expand-safe idempotent async admission endpoint for the Flaky Test Hunter, backed by a bounded current/previous UTC-day key and Temporal `REJECT_DUPLICATE`
- preserve the legacy backend route for rollback, while the new Admin BFF calls only the additive route and never falls back during mixed-version rollout
- make 202 mean admission only, preserve ambiguous recovery across reload, midnight and reauthentication, validate the exact workflow handle, and keep unknown outcomes visibly non-final
- remove the duplicate trigger from the generic agent page and retire the old synchronous Admin BFF as a non-mutating 410 tombstone
- update OpenAPI 1.4.0 to 1.5.0, regenerate the Pact, and replay it against the provider on PRs

## Migration and rollback

1. The backend expands with `/check/trigger-async-idempotent`; the legacy async and synchronous endpoints remain available to an older Admin UI image.
2. If a new Admin UI replica reaches an old backend replica, that backend returns 404 before Temporal admission. The BFF returns a bounded 503 and does not fall back to the unsafe legacy trigger.
3. A retry reuses the same persisted UTC key. A completed or running Temporal execution therefore returns the same workflow ID instead of starting another sweep.
4. Rolling the Admin UI back remains safe because the legacy backend route is retained. No backend contraction is part of this PR.

- `./gradlew --no-daemon :openbank-flaky-test-hunter:build` — success, including service tests, Kover, ktlint, detekt, Pact provider replay and Quarkus build

body:
Completes the path. cloudflared points at the internet-facing Gateway and the
canary is published as `canary.techyon.dev`.

## Verified against the live cluster before writing this

```
Gateway homelab-tunnel        Programmed=True, 192.168.32.11
Certificate wildcard-techyon  Ready=True  (Let's Encrypt, DNS-01)
SecurityPolicy tunnel-gate    Accepted=True
authentik authorize:  canary.lab.techyon.dev  → 302   (was 400 — the bug from #80)
                      canary.techyon.dev      → 302
```

The Service name was **looked up, not guessed**, per the rule in the file:
`envoy-gateway-envoy-homelab-tunnel-6cc00307`, port 443 only — the Gateway has
no HTTP listener because nothing but cloudflared reaches it.

## Why the target had to change

Not tidiness. The gated Gateway serves `*.lab.techyon.dev`, for which Cloudflare
has **no edge certificate**, so the previous config published a hostname whose
TLS handshake died at the edge before this config was ever consulted. Pointing
at the tunnel Gateway is what makes the name certifiable.

## No annotations on the route

`canary-public.lab.techyon.dev` is replaced by `canary.techyon.dev`, which
carries no external-dns annotations at all. `homelab-tunnel` holds the `target`,
so attaching a route to it is enough to publish a proxied CNAME reconciled from
git. That is the entire reason it is a third Gateway rather than a listener.

`canary.lab.techyon.dev` is untouched and stays the **control** — when the
public path misbehaves it answers "is the app broken, or is the exposure
broken?".

## Cleanup owed

⚠️ external-dns is `upsert-only` and never deletes. Removing the old route
leaves `canary-public.lab.techyon.dev` in Cloudflare, still pointing at the
tunnel. Delete it by hand.

## Verification after merge

- cloudflared reloads (reloader watches the ConfigMap) and re-registers
- external-dns creates `canary.techyon.dev` CNAME → `69f49aa0-….cfargotunnel.com`, proxied
- `https://canary.techyon.dev` gets a **valid edge certificate**, redirects to
  Authentik, and after login returns the whoami dump showing `CF-Connecting-IP`
  and `Cf-Ray` — proof the request came through Cloudflare and not the LAN
- `canary.lab.techyon.dev` still answers on the LAN
- the negative: cloudflared still cannot reach anything but DNS, Cloudflare and
  gateway-envoy — checked with Hubble, not from inside a container with no shell

author: bisingha-xilinx
body:
#### Problem solved by the commit

`rmmod zocl` oopses after an AIE partition request fails. `zocl_create_aie()`
stores the `ERR_PTR` from a failed `aie_partition_request()` into
`slot->aie->aie_dev`. Every other user tests that field with a plain NULL
check, which an `ERR_PTR` passes, so the bad handle reaches the AIE driver.

#### Bug / issue (if any) fixed, which PR introduced the bug, how it was discovered

Pre-existing in `zocl_create_aie()`, not from a recent PR. Found on VEK385
revB: a PL+AIE test failed because partition 2058 was already in use, and a
later `rmmod zocl` crashed in `aie_partition_release()` with
`x0 = fffffffffffffff0`, i.e. `ERR_PTR(-EBUSY)`.

#### How problem was solved, alternative solutions (if any) and why they were rejected

Request into a local and publish it only once valid, so `aie_dev` is always
NULL or a real device.

Two teardown paths needed fixing too, otherwise the crash is only traded for
a leaked `aie-workq` kthread: `zocl_destroy_aie()` returned early on
`!aie_information` (set on the success path only, after the workqueue is
created), and `zocl_cleanup_aie()` aborted on the `-ENODEV` the reset now
correctly returns.

#### Risks (if any) associated the changes in the commit

Low.

#### What has been tested and how, request additional testing if necessary

Reproduced on VE2 revB with partition 2058 held by another client. After
the fix the test fails cleanly with the same `ENODEV`, dmesg reports
`No available AIE partition`, and `rmmod zocl` unloads with no oops.


#### Documentation impact (if any)

None.

body:
Two UI follow-ups on top of #155, reported after using the shipped screens.

## 1. Chips sit under the editor, not halfway to the input

The playground card is a `gap-8` column, so the placeholder chips floated equidistant between the System Instructions editor and the input block and read as their own section. `TextEditor` and `PlaceholderChips` are now wrapped in a `gap-3` column inside that `gap-8` layout, so the chips attach to the editor they describe. Spacing to the input block is unchanged.

## 2. Placeholders tab is a two-level menu

The tab stacked every value of the selected placeholder as a card, and both create actions lived outside the lists they created into. It is now three panes:

1. **Placeholders** — search and `New placeholder` inside the block.
2. **Values** — the selected placeholder's values, with `New value` inside the block.
3. **Editor** — one selected value, taking the remaining width.

The selected value is derived, not stored raw: a value id that does not belong to the current placeholder resolves to nothing rather than showing another placeholder's content, and nothing is auto-selected while the values are still loading. So the highlighted row and the editor cannot disagree.

**Behaviour change:** the full-page "No data" empty state is gone. At zero placeholders the first pane still renders, so `New placeholder` stays reachable — previously the only way in was the red chip in the playground.

## Verification

`pnpm --filter web build` clean (this is web's type-check). No backend change, no schema change, no new dependency. Not smoke-tested in a browser.

author: dsova06
body:
## Summary
- Add an optional Headroom-based prompt compression module (`sova/llm/compression.py`) that gracefully degrades to an identity passthrough, establishing the foundation for token-cost reduction without any behavior change on systems that do not opt in.
- Introduce the `compression` optional dependency (`headroom-ai>=0.3.0`) plus a `[compression]` config section, so compression is fully off by default and only activates when explicitly installed and enabled.
- Scaffolding only: the module is not yet wired into the live LLM path.

## Changes

### LLM module (`sova/llm/compression.py`)
New module wrapping the optional `headroom-ai` package behind an import guard. `compress()` returns the input unchanged (exact identity passthrough) when the package is missing, `[compression] enabled = false`, the payload is below `min_chars`, or Headroom raises during compression.

### Optional dependency (`pyproject.toml`)
Adds `compression = ["headroom-ai>=0.3.0"]` to the optional dependency groups, alongside the existing `anthropic`, `litellm`, `vertex`, and `batch` extras.

### Configuration (`sova/config/models.py`, `sova/config/loader.py`, `sova/dashboard/settings_meta.py`)
- `HeadroomConfig` Pydantic settings model with `enabled` (default `False`) and `min_chars` (default `500`, `ge=0`), env prefix `SOVA_COMPRESSION_`.
- Wired into `ProjectConfig` as the `compression` field.
- Registered in `_NESTED_SECTIONS` in the loader so `[compression]` in `sova.toml` is parsed rather than silently ignored.
- Added `SettingMeta` entries so the fields appear in the dashboard settings UI.

### Docs (`.claude/rules/architecture.md`)
Updated the `sova/llm/` module description to document `compression.py` and its passthrough semantics.

### Tests (`tests/test_compression.py`)
New test suite (203 lines) covering the compression module's fallback and passthrough behavior.

## Review guidance
- Confirm the identity-passthrough guarantee: `compress()` must return input bytes/text unchanged across all four fallback paths (package missing, disabled, below `min_chars`, Headroom raises). This is the key correctness property since the module can be present but inert on any install.
- Note the triple-registration requirement for new config sections was followed: model class, `_NESTED_SECTIONS` entry, and `settings_meta` entry are all present.
- Trade-off/scope: this is intentionally scaffolding. The module is not called from the actual LLM invocation path yet, so there is no runtime effect from this PR beyond config surface area. Reviewers should verify nothing inadvertently activates it.

## Test plan
- `tests/test_compression.py` added, exercising the passthrough and fallback branches of `compress()`.
- Verified via the standard suite (`make check` / `make test-py`).
- Pre-push hook violations addressed in commit `df1e6b80`.

Closes #895

Thank you for contributing to Ruff/ty! To help us out with reviewing, please consider the following:

## Summary

<!-- What's the purpose of the change? What does it do, and why? -->

`unix::symlink_inside_project` already documents that the file watcher may emit the change for the original path (`patched/bar/baz.py`) or the symlink path (`bar/baz.py`). Applying a change event for `bar/baz.py` adds that path to the project index. inotify reports the symlink path on some hosts, including riscv64, so the strict "original path only" check fails there.

Keep the original path indexed and allow the symlink path as the only extra entry.

<!-- How was it tested? -->

`cargo clippy -p ty --test file_watching --locked -- -D warnings` and `prek` on `crates/ty/tests/file_watching.rs`.

author: kielek
body:
## Why

When `TMPDIR` was set, the shell installer downloaded the archive to a
predictable filename directly inside that directory. In a shared temporary
directory, a local attacker could pre-create a symbolic link and redirect a
privileged installer's download to another file.

Found by Splunk/Cisco internal Codex scan

## What

- Create a unique private download directory beneath `TMPDIR` using `mktemp -d`.
- Preserve the existing behavior when `DOWNLOAD_DIR` is explicitly supplied,
  including reuse of an existing archive.
- Update the installer documentation and changelog.

## Tests

- Ran an offline installer test with stubbed download and extraction commands.
- Verified that a preset `TMPDIR` produces a unique nested download directory.
- Verified that an existing archive in an explicit `DOWNLOAD_DIR` is reused.

author: turquet78
body:
Capture du 6.7 (v283) : ✗ « la propriété au rang n+1 n'est écrite nulle part » sur une copie qui la portait bel et bien, et un retour du modèle qui exigeait les calculs de f(0) et f(8). La sonde sur vrai MathLive a montré que ni le juge ni le modèle ne lisaient la copie de l'élève : l'APLATISSEUR la mutilait.

## Le défaut, nommé dans `toPlain()`

- **Un U stylé disparaissait** : l'élève avait écrit ses U par une variante du clavier virtuel (`\mathbf{U}` — le U en gras de la capture). `toPlain` retirait les accolades (`\mathbfU`) et le nettoyage aval effaçait ce faux nom de commande AVEC son U → le juge cherchait un « u » qui n'existait plus, d'où le ✗ sur une propriété parfaitement écrite.
- **`\le` devant une lettre mourait avec elle** : la suppression des espaces recollait `\le` au `f` suivant (`\lef`), effacé comme un faux nom de commande → les trois écritures du ≤ (`\le`, `\leq`, `\leqslant`) perdaient le ≤ ET le f. Le modèle citait « f(0)(Uₙ)(8) » — il disait vrai sur ce qu'il recevait, c'est l'aplatissement qui mentait sur la copie.

## Le correctif (v284 / v129 / v195)

- Dans `toPlain`, AVANT la suppression des espaces : les relations sont converties (≤, ≥ sous leurs trois écritures) et les habillages de style (`mathbf`, `mathrm`, `mathbb`, `text`…) sont retirés en gardant leur argument — dans **les trois fichiers à l'identique**, ce qui guérit d'un coup tous les juges et tous les envois au modèle qui lisent une feuille.
- L'aplatisseur gagne son **contrôle d'identité** (`readArg`/`struct`/`toPlain`, comparés au caractère près entre les trois fichiers) : il était identique par discipline seule.
- La **règle du modèle** porte la décision du professeur : une chaîne d'encadrements (« 0 ≤ 2 ≤ U(n+1) ≤ 8 ») écrit les images et conclut d'un coup — le modèle n'exige jamais que f(m) et f(M) soient posées sur une ligne à part.

## Contrôles

- La capture est épinglée en LATEX à travers la vraie chaîne `toPlain → rrClair → rrJuge` (verdict attendu : accepté) ; le banc jsdom éprouve le `toPlain` de la SOURCE (le double du harnais pose un `mlDexp` passe-plat qui mesurerait autre chose) ; bords opposés tenus (`\left(x\right)` reste `(x)`, `\ln` reste `ln`).
- Le banc navigateur fait le trajet réel `setValue → lecture` sur du vrai MathLive.
- `npm test` : Première 242 ✓, Seconde 227 ✓, Terminale 208 ✓ · `npm run test:navigateur` (les trois pages) : 198 / 183 / 166 ✓
- Trois sabotages, chacun rouge en nommant son défaut ; restauration au caractère près. Marge de la règle : 3867 / 4000, affichée à chaque exécution.

body:
## Summary / Podsumowanie

**EN:** Minimum-diff conversion of Quarkus employee/department/organization microservices from MicroProfile REST Client to Graftcode. `EmployeeFacade` and `DepartmentFacade` wrap the original in-process repositories and run as two separate `gg` nodes (`ws://localhost:19780/ws`, `ws://localhost:19790/ws`). Callers keep `EmployeeClient` / `DepartmentClient` names; internals use `RuntimeBridge.webSocket` + `com.graftcode:hypertube-java-sdk:3.1.8`. No `.cursor/` committed; original modules, Docker, and tests kept (legacy REST pact verifies disabled).

**PL:** Minimalna konwersja mikroserwisów Quarkus (employee/department/organization) z MicroProfile REST Client na Graftcode. `EmployeeFacade` i `DepartmentFacade` owijają oryginalne repozytoria w procesie i działają jako dwa osobne węzły `gg` (`19780`, `19790`). Klienci zachowują nazwy `EmployeeClient` / `DepartmentClient`; wnętrze to Hypertube WS. Bez `.cursor/`; oryginalne moduły, Docker i testy zachowane.

## Topology / Topologia

- employee gg: `:19780` / http `:19781` — `EmployeeFacade` + `EmployeeRepository`
- department gg: `:19790` / http `:19791` — `DepartmentFacade` + `DepartmentRepository`
- organization/department clients call remote facades over WS — never in-memory stubs in callers

```text
SMOKE TEST PASSED
```

Scripts: `scripts/start-graft-nodes.sh`, `scripts/smoke-graft-min.sh`

La freccia del riavvolgimento (`#btnIndietro`) stava fissa al 62% dell'altezza dello schermo — il bordo alto *teorico* massimo del box del dialogo (cinque righe più eventuali risposte). Ho misurato dal vivo (browser reale, 390×844) il caso più alto che il gioco produce davvero — una scelta a 5 opzioni in registrazione — e non supera il 79% (top ~664px su 844px). Ho spostato la freccia al 77%, che tiene un margine sopra quel caso e sta molto più vicina al box nei casi normali.

author: boserh
body:
## Why

A morning report narrated the day wrongly: a 2-hour kite session went unmentioned while two auto-detected evening walks were reported as *"два коротких вело-виїзди"*. The request dump (`scripts/dump_prompt.py`, #303/#304) settled where each half came from.

**The word "вело" came from the previous day's report.** `daily[01.09].extra.auto_activities` read `"20:24 walking 24хв; 21:01 walking 30хв"`; `previous_report` read *"Вчора зафіксовано лише два коротких вело-виїзди (по 12-13 хв)"* — correct the day before, when the auto-detections really were cycling. The model kept the sentence and swapped in the new durations. The carry-over rule covered relative DATE words only, so it did not apply.

**The kite was in the payload and was ignored.** `recent_activities[0]`, `day: "вчора (вт)"`. The prompt described `auto_activities` as the day's real cardio load but never said what wins when the same day also has a real activity.

**And the payload was diluted.** `activity_limit` is a *count*, so a 3-day morning report was handed 20 activities spanning 24 days — nine Alpine hikes and two set-by-set strength dumps around the one session that mattered — each row carrying `zones`, coordinates and gear the prompt documents nothing about, plus per-day duplicates of `race_*`/`endurance_*` that `fitness` already carries.

## What

- `_as_dict` (`app/analysis/cache.py`) becomes the one place the analyst's view is narrowed: drop-lists for `daily[].extra` and activity rows, and an activity window derived from the payload's own `window_days` (floor `ACTIVITY_CONTEXT_MIN_DAYS` = 10, so morning and `/report` get 10 days and `/deep` keeps 14), with `ACTIVITY_CONTEXT_MIN_KEEP` = 3 newest rows kept whatever their date so an idle athlete still sees what they last did.
- Prompt: the `previous_report` carry-over ban now covers *content* — activity types, durations, phrasing — not only date words. And `auto_activities` gains a priority rule (a `recent_activities` entry for that date IS the day) plus "take the type literally: `walking` is walking, even if yesterday's line said `cycling`".

Measured on the real payload:

| | `data` before | after | activities |
|---|---|---|---|
| morning (`window_days=3`) | 11 496 B | 4 938 B (−58%) | 20 → 9 |
| `/deep` (`window_days=14`) | 25 456 B | 14 333 B (−44%) | 20 → 13 |

## Safety

This is an attention budget, not a cost one, and two invariants keep it safe — both pinned by tests:

- **Nothing computes from the trimmed fields.** `baselines`, `intensity`, `records`, `health`, the weather location and gear mileage all read them from the DB, never from the payload. Only what the model reads changes.
- **Prompt and cache key are trimmed identically.** `run_analysis` keys the dedup cache off the same `_as_dict` output — trim one side only and an invisible field (a jittering `spo2_low`) buys a fresh paid call every morning. There is also a test that a *kept* field still busts the key.

The drop-lists were derived by grepping every `daily[].extra` / activity key produced by `app/garmin/service.py` against `prompts.py`, then keeping anything with real coaching value even when unnamed (`sleep_start`/`sleep_end`, `skin_temp_dev_c`, the Garmin verdict strings) and dropping only duplicates, undocumented counters, and values `fitness` carries.

Verified with `ruff check .` and `pytest tests/test_payload_trim.py tests/test_prompt_dump.py` (17 passed). No existing test asserts on the daily-report prompt contents.

## Deploy note

The cache key changes, so the first report per user after this is a real (paid) call rather than a hit — one Sonnet call each, not a re-run of anything.

## Still open

Whether the 01.09 kite was in the 07:15 payload at all, or arrived later — the dump at 10:08 has it. `PROMPT_DUMP_DIR` answers that tomorrow. If it turns out activities arrive after the report, there is a second gap: `_activity_watch_for_user` filters on `"run" in type`, so a late non-run activity produces no DM and the morning guard blocks a re-run.
