Milestone 1 delivers the full student-facing UI shell as real Next.js App Router routes, rendered from the synthetic seed through the existing app-services plus an in-memory repository. `pnpm dev` works with zero setup — no database, no migrations.

## What's here

**Design system & component kit**
- `globals.css` — Tailwind v4 `@theme` tokens ("focused high-contrast": paper `#FDFCFA`, ink `#17140F`, accent `#1E5BFF`), Space Grotesk / IBM Plex Sans / IBM Plex Mono via `next/font`.
- `components/ui.tsx` — `AppFrame`, `PageHeader`, `Card`, `Bar`, `Chip`, `StatTile`, `RowLink`, `PrimaryButton`, `GhostButton`, `SectionLabel`, `SyntheticNote`.
- `components/` — `icons.tsx`, `bottom-nav.tsx`, `phase-strip.tsx`, `trajectory-chart.tsx` (pure-SVG projection chart).

**View-model services (no new persistence)**
- `app-services/demo.ts` — lazily-seeded in-memory `DemoContext`.
- `app-services/overview.ts` — `getStudentOverview`: phase, overall/subject readiness, key dates, needs-attention with reasons.
- `app-services/chapter-view.ts` — `getChapterView`: progress, readiness snapshot, weights, recent sessions.

**18 screens**
dashboard · today · study-now · session · subjects · subjects/[subjectKey] · subjects/[subjectKey]/[chapterKey] · revision · tests · tests/new · tests/result · review · plan · parent · reminders · trajectory · course-correction · more

Dashboard, subjects (list + detail + chapter), today, plan, parent, review, trajectory and tests are **wired to real data** (curriculum → progress → readiness snapshots → study sessions → resolved phases → capacity). The remaining screens render representative synthetic content, clearly marked.

**Other**
- Fixtures imported as JSON (`spec.ts`, `curriculum-fixture.ts`) so they bundle under Next rather than being read from disk at runtime.
- `tests/e2e/shell.spec.ts` — tab navigation, the daily loop (today → chapter detail → study-now), and the more-menu paths.

author: nitishagar
body:
## Summary

Range-mode review (`--from … --to …`) requires every commit between merge-base and head to exist locally. Shallow checkouts — GitLab CI commonly sets `GIT_DEPTH: "1"` to reduce server load — therefore fail before any review starts: target-branch refs do not resolve and `git merge-base` comes back empty. This lets the diff layer fetch exactly what is missing from `origin`, on demand, so shallow clones work without raising `GIT_DEPTH` or switching to a full checkout.

Fixes #634.

## How it works

The behavior is strictly conditional on **repo is shallow AND a ref/merge-base is actually missing AND an `origin` remote exists** — non-shallow repositories issue no new git commands on success paths, and repositories without a usable remote keep today's exact errors.

- **Destination-bearing refspecs everywhere.** Wants are always `+<ref>:<destination>` forms: SHA → `refs/remotes/ocr-fetch/<short>`, `origin/<name>` → `refs/remotes/origin/<name>`, bare name → `refs/remotes/origin/<name>`. This is the only form that both creates the ref a later `rev-parse` can find in a `--single-branch` clone and extends the shallow boundary when deepening — a bare SHA or branch name on the fetch line is a silent no-op once the object is present, and `+HEAD:…` fetches the remote's *default* branch, so `HEAD` is mapped to the current branch (`symbolic-ref --short HEAD`; detached HEAD falls back to its SHA).
- **Fallback resolution + SHA substitution.** After the fetch, refs resolve as `<ref>` → `origin/<ref>` → the ocr-fetch destination. Spellings that only resolve through the fallback are substituted with their resolved SHAs so downstream `git diff`/`git show` call sites (which are not fallback-aware) keep working.
- **Bounded deepen for merge-base.** A missing merge-base triggers one `--depth` doubling loop (2→1024, both endpoints as destination-bearing wants, merge-base recomputed each round) inside `computeMergeBase`. If it still fails, the existing error gains a shallow-aware hint — only on the path where the loop actually ran.
- A package-level mutex serializes fetch/deepen within one process (several `Provider` instances share a clone per run).

## What does not change

- Non-shallow repos: zero new git invocations on success paths (pinned by an argv-recording test).
- No remote / unreachable remote / fetch failure: today's error messages with the underlying git failure surfaced.
- No full `--unshallow`, no new user-facing flags; the trigger is automatic and scoped to the shallow case.

## Testing

New integration suite builds real upstream fixtures (`main` + `feature`, tags) and `git clone --depth 1 --single-branch --branch feature file://…` clones, then exercises the actual code paths: the canonical GitLab spelling `--from origin/<target> --to $CI_COMMIT_SHA`, bare branch names, `--to HEAD`, tag auto-follow, deep history requiring the deepen loop, depth-cap exhaustion with the hint, no-remote negatives with no fetch attempted (argv recording), unreachable-origin error surfacing, and the `validateReviewRefs` recovery branch. `make check` and `make test` (race) green; coverage for the new/changed functions ≥ 90% (package `internal/diff` 93.8%).

author: lyfne123
body:
## Summary

`LowerAutoVectorSplit` rebuilds and tracks a `ForStmt`'s loop-carried state so a halved carry stays lane-local, but did the same for **no** `IfStmt`. Both branch bodies were lowered and their `Yield` values substituted, while `IfStmt::return_vars_` kept its original full-width type, was never added to `tile_vars`, and got no old→new replacement.

Two things went wrong at once:

```python
v: pl.Tile[[64, 128], ...] = pl.tile.load(data, [0 + subblock_idx * 64, 0], ...)
if flag > 0:
    merged: pl.Tile[[128, 128], ...] = pl.yield_(doubled)   # branches are halved
else:
    merged: pl.Tile[[128, 128], ...] = pl.yield_(v)
out_store = pl.tile.store(merged, [0, 0], out_0)            # BOTH lanes write row 0
```

- the merge variable contradicts both `Yield` values — the same declared-type-versus-operand defect as #2203, on the merge path;
- because it stays untracked, the following `tile.store` gets **no lane offset**, so the two AIV lanes overlap their writes instead of taking a half each.

Behavior change: a branch-merged tile inside an automatically split region is now halved and lane-offset correctly; a merge whose branches disagree is rejected at compile time with a `ValueError`. No in-contract program changes behavior. No interface or migration step.

## Changes

- `src/ir/transforms/utils/split_axis_utils.{h,cpp}`: add `RepairIfReturnVars`, mirroring what `RepairIterArgs` / `RepairReturnVars` do for loop carries — retype the merge to the per-lane extent, register it in `tile_vars`, record the replacement. A `Yield` value still references the pre-halving var, and the halving path registers *both* the old and the new var in `tile_vars`, so looking the yielded value up there is what tells a lane-local branch value from a shared one.
- `src/ir/transforms/utils/split_axis_utils.cpp`: call it from `ProcessStmt`'s `IfStmt` branch.
- `src/ir/transforms/lower_auto_vector_split_pass.cpp`: call it from the AUTO affinity-gated arm too — that arm recurses through its own walk and cannot reach `ProcessStmt`'s `IfStmt` branch, the same reason the loop carries needed two call sites.
- `docs/{en,zh}/dev/passes/21-lower_auto_vector_split.md`: the "Carries and dropped axes" section becomes "Carries, merges and dropped axes" and documents the merge rule.
- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_lower_auto_vector_split.py`: three cases (below).

### The two rules the merge needs

**Branches must agree.** One yielding a halved value while the other yields a full-width one has no single merge type: halving is wrong for the else path, not halving is wrong for the then path, and picking either silently gives one AIV lane the wrong extent. Rejected, with the merge variable named.

**An `if` with no `else` is not a disagreement.** `return_vars_` is a `DefField`, so an else-less `if` defines the merge name on the taken path only — its one branch is the sole constraint on the type, and following it is what makes that path well-typed. (Verified that shape parses and reaches the pass; it does.)

## Verification

Run at the pushed commit, in a worktree-local build:

- `pytest tests/ut/ir/transforms/ tests/ut/ir/operators/ tests/ut/codegen/ -q -n 16 -p no:randomly`: 6050 passed, 2 skipped.
- 12 `tests/lint/` checks: all passed.
- `clang-format --dry-run --Werror`, `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` on the changed sources: passed.

Two pre-existing failures on this machine, both reproduced with **every change in this PR reverted** and therefore unrelated:

- `tests/ut/language/test_unified_ops.py::...::test_symlinked_import_path_still_names_the_caller` — the editable install's meta-path finder hijacks the subprocess's symlinked `import pypto`.
- `tests/ut/codegen/test_orchestration_codegen_graph.py::test_generated_orchestration_compiles_against_the_pinned_runtime` — the local `runtime` submodule is checked out at `dbdd041e` while the branch pins `15f5cbd9`, so the generated file is type-checked against the wrong headers (`static assertion failed: all arguments must be simpler::hbg::Tensor`). The submodule is deliberately left unstaged.

### Tests added

- `test_if_merge_variable_is_retyped_and_tracked` — both branches yield a halved value; asserts the merge is `[64, 128]` and the store carries `+ subblock_idx * 64`. Fails on `main` with the merge left at `[128, 128]` and the store at `[0, 0]`.
- `test_if_branches_disagreeing_on_the_merge_are_rejected` — one halved branch, one full-width parameter; asserts the diagnostic names `merged`.
- `test_if_without_else_takes_the_merge_type_from_its_only_branch` — pins the else-less rule.

No system tests were run locally; CI covers them.

Closes #2608

body:
## FRESCO-395 — A4-L4 + A4-L5 (audit-4 ola-3, eje Seguridad, ambos BAJO)

### A4-L4 — brute-force oracle in `reassign-guest-data`

ADR-0004's ownership proof ran a **server-side `signInWithPassword`** on
credentials the caller put in the request body. Anyone can open an anonymous
session for free (ADR-0003), so that endpoint was an unauthenticated password
brute-force oracle — no rate limit, outside the protections Supabase Auth
applies to its own login (per-IP/username limits, leaked-password protection,
CAPTCHA).

**Fix:** the caller authenticates to the target account through native
Supabase Auth and passes the resulting **session token**; the function only
verifies it (`getUser()`), never a password. Plus a **5/h per-guest rate
limit** via the shared `enforceRateLimit` helper.

- Contract: `ReassignGuestDataRequest { email, password }` → `{ targetAccessToken }`
- `handleReassign` runs the proof sign-in on a throwaway in-memory client
  (`persistSession: false`) so the guest session stays live until the data
  move completes — **ADR-0004's ordering guarantee is preserved**
- No SQL change (`reassign_guest_data(uuid, uuid)` untouched)
- **ADR-0022** (Proposed): partial supersession of ADR-0004 — verification
  step only; the service-role RPC, its grant boundary and the orphan-anon
  cleanup all still stand

### A4-L5 — `/qa` public + indexable

The testability guide rendered the Supabase project ref, the Studio dashboard
URL and the Functions base URL verbatim, and `robots.txt` allowed indexing.

**Fix (option A — no auth/flag gate, keeps the external-evaluator use case):**
- `robots: { index: false, follow: false }` in the page metadata
- `Disallow: /qa` in `robots.txt`
- project ref → `<PROJECT_REF>` placeholder across the DB + API sections,
  with a note it comes from `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`

author: ekalinin
body:
P10's fourth cut: the policy and permission families and `import`. Everything
was measured against a live Keycloak 26.7.1 on 2026-09-02, container `kc-policy`
on port 8156, removed when the cut finished.

**Seven of the last nine operations land** - `GET`/`POST .../policy`,
`GET .../policy/search`, `GET`/`POST .../permission`,
`GET .../permission/search` and `POST .../import` - taking
`admin/authz-resource-server` from 22 to **29 of 31**. The two `evaluate`
operations do not; see the last section.

Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-02-p10-authz-policies.md`.
Handover: `docs/superpowers/handover/p10-authz-policies.md`.

## The measurement that sized it

The roadmap and the previous handover both guess "nine providers, nine typed
representations". One probe settles it: send **one config carrying every
provider's keys at once** to **all nine types**.

The generic view came back **byte-identical on all nine**; the typed view
projected exactly the keys the type owns. That is **eight distinct field sets
over nine types** - `resource` and `scope` share one - produced by a nine-row
table over one stored map rather than by eight structures. `resourceType` is not
a shared base field on the read: a `role` policy carrying `defaultResourceType`
serves it generically and does not project it.

## What else the sweep found

- **A policy needs a name *and* a type.** AGENTS.md and F129 both say `type` is
  the gate, from a probe set that never left the name out. `{"type":"role"}`
  with no name is the same `409 Duplicate resource error`.
- **The create's 201 is the request echoed and the read is not.** A `role`
  create's config comes back verbatim where its own read has role names resolved
  to uuids; `owner` and `resourceType` are echoed and no read serves either.
- **Three providers resolve a reference and all three answer an unknown one
  differently** - a role is dropped, a group path is dropped, a clientId is a
  500.
- **`GET .../settings` and `GET .../permission` partition the same rows
  differently.** The listing counts `uma` as a permission; the export leaves it
  among the policies and moves `resource` and `scope` to the end.
- **The export denormalises**: ids back to names, paths back to paths, and the
  three association sets synthesised back into the config by name - and it
  **filters** a role, client or group policy's config to the provider's own keys.
- **A null enum is a third state**: `{"logic":null}` is a 201 and the row reads
  back with no `logic` key at all.
- **`CONSENSUS` is a 201 here and a 500 on `PUT .../authz/resource-server`.**
- **`POST .../import` is strict where `POST .../policy` beside it is not**, it
  deletes nothing, it resets the three settings to the representation's own
  initialisers, and a name it already holds it merges into.
- **A policy's config is placed by `javamap.SizedKeyOrder` and its size argument
  is the count of what is *stored*** - the opposite of what AGENTS.md's protocol
  mapper bullet says about its own family, and pinned by a vector that fell out
  of a failing test.

`GET .../settings` was already counted as served and was already wrong: its
`policies` was `[]struct{}` because no fixture could create a policy. That is
the second time this one struct has held an always-empty key for that reason,
one cut after `resources`. It is fixed here, which is why the diff touches
`authz.go`.

## F147

The brief asked for two probes; both were sent and both hold. A third family
reproduces the split on five requests, and `POST .../policy` with no type and
`PUT .../authz/resource-server` with no decisionStrategy answer the **identical
67-byte body** one verb apart with opposite header sets.

**But the sweep that went with them refutes the entry's own lead.** Fourteen
409s were measured on both verbs, and two `PUT`s answering byte-identical
67-byte `Duplicate resource error` bodies disagree about the five:
`default-default-client-scopes/{id}` sends all five and `roles/{name}` sends
none. The request `Content-Type` was varied over four spellings on the first and
never moved it. So after the status, the body, the length, emptiness and the
request's `Content-Type`, **the verb is out too**. No rule is written; "the
endpoint decides" is what survives.

## What is left undone

`POST .../policy/evaluate` and `POST .../permission/evaluate`. Their 200 runs
the whole authorization engine and mints an **RPT** - an access token's claim
set, which lives in `internal/token`, a package this branch may not modify, and
reproducing it in `internal/admin` would be the second truth the boundary table
exists to prevent. They are in the catalogue as `Recorded` with a `Reason` and
measured in full in §1.9 of the handover, which is what this repository's
convention says to do with an operation that is measured and not served.

## Discipline

- **Forty mutations**, one per claim, each naming the test it had to break.
  **Five survived**: four were holes in a test and one was a claim no test made
  at all. All five are killed now, three tests were repaired and one was added.
- Both store drivers implement the five new methods and the Postgres suite was
  run with `-v` with the new subtest confirmed executing.
- `make lint`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./...` and `make oracle` are green.
- Twenty-four goldens recorded; **no existing golden moved**.

author: claude[bot]
body:
> **Title note:** the dispatch brief specified "…with the six regression clusters
> repaired". They were root-caused, not repaired — the decision below is the
> brief's option (b), so the title states what actually landed.

## What

Re-lands the `#3523` R4 **gap-6a** slice (module-scope closure pre-lift +
`discovery-static` pass-1 skip) that PR #5474 landed and PR #5477 reverted —
**with the pass-1 skip OFF by default**. The pre-lift, the fail-closed gate, the
census counters and the suite all ship; the route they drive is opt-in behind
`JS2WASM_ENABLE_MODULE_INIT_DISCOVERY_STATIC=1`. A default build takes exactly
the two-pass path `main` takes today, so this PR is byte-neutral by default.

## Why

#5474's merge group measured **76 pass→other test262 regressions (net −71)**,
`compile_error` 500→542, trap ratchet `oob` 14→29 and `null_deref` 70→74, and
its merge commit reached `main` anyway through a queue defect. All 76 were
reproduced locally on the runner-faithful harness (`runTest262File`: compile +
instantiate + run + strict rerun) before anything was changed, and every one of
them is on a population the gate **admits** (census: 87/87 of the cited files).

A discriminating matrix settles what is and is not to blame:

| route | 5 files, one per cluster |
| --- | --- |
| base (`main` − gap-6a) | 5 pass |
| base + `JS2WASM_TEST_FORCE_MODULE_INIT_PASS2=1` | **5 pass** |
| candidate (gap-6a as landed) | 5 fail |
| candidate + `JS2WASM_TEST_DISABLE_MODULE_INIT_PRELIFT=1` | 5 fail |
| candidate + `FORCE_MODULE_INIT_PASS2=1` (kill switch) | 5 pass |

Row 2 shows that compiling the initializer in the pass-2 slot is fine; row 4
shows the closure inventory is not the variable. What breaks is compiling it
there with **no pass 1 having run at all**.

**Correction carried forward: compile "success" is not instantiation.** Nine of
the 76 are `WebAssembly.instantiate()` compile errors on modules the compiler
reported as successful — invisible to the 325 + 163 compile samples that were
#5474's evidence, because nothing in that lane validates the binary.

## Root causes per cluster

**Family A — a captured module-global index goes stale across a global-shifting
compile.** Clusters 1 (16 `decodeURI`/`decodeURIComponent` OOB traps), part of
cluster 2 (ill-typed modules), the `do-while` single. Reduced to 4 lines inside
the runner's harness:

```js
var a = [1, 2];
var n = 0;
for (var j = a[0]; j <= 2; j++) { n = n + 1; }   // n === 4, expected 2
```

`compileForStatement` reads `ctx.moduleGlobals.get(name)` into a local, compiles
the initializer expression, and only then pushes `global.set`. Compiling `a[0]`
adds the bounds-check error string, `fixupModuleGlobalIndices` shifts
`ctx.moduleGlobals`, every reachable emitted instruction and ~20 cached maps —
but it cannot shift a number held on a caller's stack. Emitted WAT: the for-head
writes `global.set 107` where every other reference to the same variable reads
`global.get 108`. **Pre-existing latent bug**; pass 1 masks it by pre-creating
those imports. Not fixed here on purpose — see "Not touched".

**Family B — bodies specialize against types the INITIALIZER mints.** Cluster 3,
all 33 array-pattern parameter rows. Two lines:

```js
function f([w]) { return w; }
var r = f([7]);   // r === undefined
```

The two-pass build's `$f` opens with `ref.test (ref 12)` against the tuple struct
that `f([7])`'s argument literal mints, because pass 1 compiled the call first.
With pass 1 gone the body is compiled first, the arm never exists, and the
remaining arms mis-handle what the initializer later hands them. **No AST-level
inventory can publish this family — producing it *is* compiling the
initializer.** The gap-6 census filed `structMap`/`anonTypeMap`/`mod.types` as
"on-demand caches (order drift only)", which is true for the init and false for
any body compiled before it.

**Cluster 4 (`with` / `@@unscopables`, 8 rows)** reproduces with the
registrations off and surfaces as `null is not a function [in
__module_init_chunk_0()]` / `count` 2 vs 6. Its lowering reaches
`reserveMemberSetDispatch`, one of the `addStringConstantGlobal` callers the
fixup instrumentation caught inserting globals mid-init — i.e. family A's
signature. **Classified, not reduced.** **Cluster 5's remaining singles**
(`S13.2.2_A13`, the two `scope-*-param-rest-elem-var-close`, `unary-{minus,plus}
S11.4.x_A3_T5`) were **not reduced** either — recorded, not explained away.
**Cluster 6 (32 Temporal fail→compile_error, 4 `Array/prototype/find*`
compile_error→fail) did not reproduce locally**: the 3 Temporal and 4 find rows
sampled are at parity on both trees, so those transitions are most likely
shard-level provider/timeout effects, and they are named rather than counted.

The 5 improvements are the same mechanism running the other way — a different
arm wins when the init's type is absent. A family that moves rows in both
directions is an ordering accident, not a fix.

**Why the first sample said zero:** 76 regressions against ~35,400 passes is a
**0.21 %** rate. A 90-file sample (71 passes) expects **0.15** hits and shows
zero with probability ≈ **86 %**.

## Decision

**Option (b): flip the default off; keep the inventory and gate as an opt-in
seam.** A narrowed admission rule was rejected on measurement, not taste:

- every regressing population is already admitted (87/87), so narrowing means
  adding refusals, not tightening existing ones;
- family B's only fail-closed marker is "the population contains a top-level
  function declaration compiled between the passes and called from the
  initializer" — the runner-faithful harness prelude puts `Test262Error`,
  `$DONE` and the `assert` family in **325/325** sampled populations, so that
  rule admits **0** of the corpus the slice exists to serve;
- enumerating the six observed clusters' syntactic markers is fitting the gate to
  the failures we happened to find, which is exactly what produced this incident.

## Evidence

- **Runtime parity, instantiation counted.** All 87 cited files, default route vs
  base tree (`runTest262File`, host lane): **87/87 at status parity, 0 divergences** — every one of the 76
  pass→fail rows is back at `pass`.
- **Byte neutrality of the default route.** **341/341 identical** on the host lane (328 successful compiles sha256-identical, 13 compile-failure rows identical by sorted diagnostic set) and **120/120 identical** on the standalone lane over the first 120 files of the same sample.
- **Under the seam the route still does what it claimed.** The
  `issue-3523-module-init-discovery-static` suite runs all 12 existing cases with
  the seam ON and gains two: `(g)` pins the default off (every admitted shape
  reads `pre-lift = 0, pass1 = 1` on all four lanes and still reads its value),
  and `(g) WHY it is off` flips two runner-faithful files — one per family — from
  `pass` to not-`pass` by setting the seam, so the reason the default moved is a
  mutation, not a paragraph.
- **`tests/issue-3523-module-init-single-pass.test.ts` restored byte-for-byte**
  to its pre-slice state: with the route off, gap-1b's `1/0` and `1/1` censuses
  are the truth again.
- **Suites** `--pool=forks --poolOptions.forks.singleFork --no-file-parallelism`, **9 files / 139 tests / 0 failures**: `issue-3523-module-init-discovery-static` 13, `issue-3523-module-init-single-pass` 15, `issue-3523-ir-module-init-compile-once` 20, `issue-3765-numeric-locals` 18, `issue-4376-module-init-chunking` 19, `issue-3872` 28, `issue-2965` 11, `issue-4182-annexb-global-blockfn` 9, `issue-4195-eval-refusal-message-and-dedupe` 6. `tests/issue-3518-multi-prepared-string-leaf-planner.test.ts` was **skipped** — it OOMs on this 4-core box, as the dispatch brief notes.
- **Gates** `pnpm run -s typecheck` clean. The five ratchets (`check-loc-budget`, `check-func-budget`, `check-coercion-sites`, `check:oracle-ratchet`, `check:dead-exports`) exit 0 bare and again under `LOC_GATE_BASE=$(git rev-parse origin/main)`. Note which run

author: dhsorens
body:
Closes the **opcode half of obligation 4** — and, with #13224's gas debit in the middle, the **whole sixteen-instruction dispatch step**.

## Outcome: tier 1, and the premise of tier 3 turned out to be wrong

The brief expected the expensive part to be *bridging `OpcodeTables`' `execBlock`/SAsm table-load facts to the CPS engine*. Two measurements changed the plan:

1. **A general `execBlock` → CPS bridge already exists** and did not need building: `SAsm/BlockSound.lean`'s `execBlock_sound`, its PC-threaded sibling `SAsm/GlobalData.lean`'s `execBlockAt_sound` (the one that can step an `AUIPC` — `blockOk` rejects `AUIPC`, `blockOkAt` accepts it), and `SAsm/BlockAtBridge.lean`'s `blockAt_flat_spec`.
2. ⛔ **None of them can carry this block, for a reason of register scope.** Their register currency is `regFileIs rf` / `regAtoms rf exposedRegs`, and `SAsm/RegFile.lean`'s `exposedRegs` is `[x5..x7, x28..x31, x10..x17]` — neither `x1` nor `x20`. The dispatch body writes `x1` (the `jalr` link register) and reads `x20` (the environment pointer), so no `execBlock`-side statement can even *mention* the two registers that make this block a dispatch. `regs_not_exposed_here` states that as a theorem rather than as prose.

So the block is built from the `↦ᵣ`-atom one-step specs, which have no such restriction, and the only bridging that was actually needed is **four lines**: `tableRegion_dword_at`, which splits a `bytesRegion` pinned to `OpcodeTables.tableBytes entries` into the `op`-th `↦ₘ` dword atom plus a frame. `bytesRegion_dword_at` (dependency) and `tableBytes_slice` (`OpcodeTables`) already existed and meet exactly.

## A computed exit PC needs no new rule

`cpsTripleWithin n entry exit cr P Q` takes `exit` as a **term**, and `jalr_spec_within`'s exit is already `(v1 + signExtend12 offset) &&& ~~~1` over `rs1`'s value. Naming the loaded handler in the precondition is therefore enough to name it in the exit. No CPS rule was added, and none is needed. `halign` (`h &&& ~~~1 = h`) is the standard `jalr` side-condition — the same one `Fn.jalr_ret_spec` carries — discharged by `decide` at any concrete table.

## The theorems

`EvmAsm/Codegen/Proofs/DispatchStepOpcode.lean`

| decl | prog idx | shape |
|---|---|---|
| `dispatchStep_fetch_within` | 0..5 | `cpsTripleWithin 6 B (B+24)` — `lbu` out of the code region, `slli`, `la opcode_gas_costs`, index, load. Leaves `x5 = 8*op`, `x6 = gasCosts[op]` |
| *(#13224)* `dispatchStep_gasDebit_within` | 6..10 | `cpsBranchWithin 5 (B+24)` |
| `dispatchStep_opcode_within` | 11..15 | `cpsTripleWithin 5 (B+44) entries[op]` — the handler `la`, index, load, and the indirect `jalr` |
| **`dispatchStep_body_within`** | **0..15** | **`cpsBranchWithin 16 B`**, exits `handlers[op]` / `GuestAddrs.exit_outofgas` |

plus `dispatchStep_opcode_image` / `dispatchStep_body_image`, the same statements inside `guestImageCodeReq` through `dispatchLoopBody_block_sub`.

**Which opcodes it covers: all 256.** `op` is not a parameter — it is `(code[i]).toNat`, a projection of the EVM code region the loop's `x10` points into. The gas charged and the handler reached are read out of the two tables *by that index*. `x5` survives the gas debit untouched, which is what lets indices 11..15 reuse the scaling computed at index 1.

`dispatch_ra_is_resume`: the `jalr`'s link value `B + 64` is `GuestAddrs.dispatch_resume`, so this is a CALL back into the loop, not a tail jump.

`opcode_tables_adjacent`: `opcode_handlers − opcode_gas_costs = 8 * 256`, both dword-aligned, `decide`d off `GuestAddrs`. That is the table analogue of the `prog.length * 4 == hi − lo` extent cross-check; no index or extent in this PR was eyeballed.

## The one thing that is *not* proven, stated as a theorem

⚠️ **Nothing in Lean ties the shipped image's `.data` to `opcodeGasCostEntries` / `opcodeHandlerEntries`.** `guestScratch` (`Proofs/GuestImage.lean`) owns the writable `.data` tile as `regionScratch`, i.e. `anyBytes` — ownership with contents *forgotten*. `opcode_table_contents_not_scratch_determined` proves that gap rather than describing it: two distinct table images of equal length, plus the havoc weakening that maps either onto the same `anyBytes`. So no `↦ₘ` about the table follows from the image assertion, and the tables' contents enter as premises here exactly as they do in `OpcodeTables`. `scripts/check-opcode-tables.sh` checks the bytes offline; the missing piece is a `.data` counterpart of `guestImageCodeReq`.

What *is* unconditional is the control flow and the indexing: whatever the tables hold, this body charges the `op`-th gas entry and jumps to the `op`-th handler.

## Non-vacuity + controls (by name)

- `dispatchStep_opcode_instance` — the whole opcode-half statement at the real `opcodeHandlerEntries` mirror of the SHIPPED `callFrameGuestRegistry` for `0x01` (ADD) under `demoResolver`, plus: the table is 256 entries, the indexed cell is an addressable aligned dword, and the entry is 2-aligned so the exit really is the loaded value.
- `dispatchStep_body_premises_satisfiable` — all seven side conditions of the whole-body theorem hold simultaneously at one concrete point (aligned in-range one-byte code region holding `0x01`, both 256-entry mirrors), so the hypothesis family is not contradictory.
- `dispatchStep_opcode_premises_refutable` — three conjuncts provably FALSE: the `la` really is at `+44` and not `+40`; `halign` fails at an odd handler address (so the `jalr` exit would *not* be the loaded value); a 256-entry table refuses `op = 256`.
- `dispatchStep_body_premises_refutable` — a misaligned code base, and a code pointer in the gap between the model's legacy zone and its RAM zone. `bytesRegion_lbu_within` is unusable without both.
- `regs_not_exposed_here` carries its own control: `x5`/`x6`/`x7` **are** exposed, so the point is scope, not a broken predicate.

## `CodeReq` shape

`CodeReq.ofProg (BitVec.ofNat 64 GuestAddrs.dispatch_loop_body) dispatchLoopBody_prog` — the whole 16-instruction body, reused from #13224, so no #13191 too-small-`cr` hazard. Instruction-indexed at a 4-byte stride. The `la` pairs reconcile `Codegen.laHi/laLo` (Nat symbol, Nat pc) with `Rv64.laHi/laLo` (Word pc, Word target) by `decide`, the established `CallFrameBaseSAsm` idiom, then go through `la_materialize_within` — the address is PROVEN, not assumed.

## Obligation 4's cell

`Progress/Obligations.lean` said *"What remains is the OPCODE half — the fetch, the two `.data` table loads and the indirect `jalr`"*. That is now false, so it is retired and replaced with what actually remains: the tables' contents, and the handler-side seam. `DRIFT.md` regenerated (`drift-report.sh --write`). Per the standing warning in that file, **no new guest symbol was spelled in the cell** — `transcription_queue.py --write-doc` produces a byte-identical doc and `--check-doc` is green before and after, so the queue did not move.

## Registry rows: deferred

⚠️ `routineRegistry_all_witnessed` is at its measured 244-row elaboration ceiling (noted on the #13224 row). **This PR adds no registry row and no `AxiomWitnesses` entry** — the rows for `dispatchStep_body_within` and `dispatchStep_opcode_within` are deferred pending the ceiling fix, which is in flight separately. Census figures are unchanged.

## Axioms

`#print axioms` on all sixteen new declarations: `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` or a subset (`dispatch_ra_is_resume`, `opcode_tables_adjacent` and `dispatchStep_body_premises_refutable` depend on none). No `sorry`, no `native_decide`, no `bv_decide`. The proofs use `xperm_hyp` at eleven seams, so given #13207 this was checked explicitly rather than assumed: `check-axioms.sh` is green over all 810 witnesses.

## Gates run

Green: `lake build` (6243 jobs), `check-axioms.sh` (810 witnesses), `check-forbidden-tactics.sh`, `check-layout-literals.sh`, `check-naming.sh`, `check-unimported.sh`, `check-no-warnings.sh`, `check-file-size.sh`, `check-embedded-counts.sh`, `check-heartbeats-approved.sh

author: velvetmonkey
body:
A top-level JSON-RPC array reached `child.stdin.write` undecided. A guarded tool call wrapped in an array was forwarded verbatim with zero decisions and zero receipts, while the same call alone was gated.

The proxy now refuses the array as one frame. It mints one receipt carrying `tool: "<batch>"` and the kernel's own verdict reason, and it answers the client with a JSON-RPC error.

Ben ruled the behaviour (hard refuse, no unpacking), the carrier (`<batch>`), and the sentence. MCP revision 2025-06-18 removed JSON-RPC batching, so naming the caller non-conformant is accurate rather than rude. JSON-RPC 2.0 prescribes `id: null` and `-32600` for a request whose id cannot be determined.

Client capture from a real `createProxy` drive:

```
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"error":{"code":-32600,"message":"MCP 2025-06-18 does not permit JSON-RPC batches; send each call as its own message."}}
```

Round 1 of this branch shipped the gate but delivered the sentence nowhere, and its test asserted zero client frames, which encoded that silence. Round 2 replaced that assertion with a `deepEqual` on the error frame.

Verified independently on disk before merge:

- `node --test test/spine-retry.test.cjs` on the branch: 17 tests, 17 pass.
- Removing only the client delivery line: 16 pass, 1 fail, `not ok 5 - a top-level batch is refused as one frame and never reaches the child`. The test measures the behaviour rather than passing either way.

Cold frisk on grok-4.6, cross-family from the gpt-5.6-luna builder: verdict MERGE. It independently ruled that `docs/assurance/evaluator-start.md:97` stays true, because that cell describes what the Lean model theorems state, not what the Node proxy does. I had recorded the same reading before its report landed.

Known and queued, not fixed here: the `!frame || typeof frame !== "object" || Array.isArray(frame)` branch also catches `null`, numbers and strings, and gives them the batch sentence.

body:
## Summary
Restored background session tabs now show their real title after launch instead of reading "New session" until they are clicked.

Root cause: a restored tile has no `runtimeId` and its pane does not mount until first activation, so the by-id resolution effect inside `SessionTilePane` never runs. When the session row is also outside the recents page and project tree, `tileTitle()` has nothing to resolve from and falls back to the placeholder.

Closes #94167. Supersedes #94212 — salvaged only the one-shot by-id backfill from @686f6c61's PR (co-authored on the commit). The title-persistence half (`knownSessionTabTitle`, `$sessions.listen` writer, `setSessionTileWorkspaceScope` change) was dropped: `workspaceTabTitle` stays the canonical Bot Chat marker and no new state is written to disk.

## Changes
- `session-tile.tsx`: `startUnrestoredTileTitleBackfill()` — once the gateway is open, look each tile with no `runtimeId`, no `workspaceTabTitle`, and no `tileStoredRow()` up via `resolveStoredSession(id, tile.ownerRoute)`. That call already upserts the row into `$sessions`, which the tab strip mirror watches (`also: [$sessions, …]`), so the tab re-labels itself. One shot per launch; owner route preferred so cross-profile tiles never probe the ambient gateway.
- `controller.tsx`: wire it next to `watchSessionTiles()` (same non-browser / non-HUD gate).
- `session-tile.test.ts`: one test — unlisted unrestored tiles are looked up by id with their `ownerRoute` once the gateway opens; listed, live, and explicitly titled tiles are skipped; a later reconnect does not re-probe.

## Validation
| | Before (main) | After |
|---|---|---|
| Electron e2e: target pushed off the 50-row recents page by 60 newer sessions, restored as a stacked background tab, no click | tab strip `["*sessions","Bots","*New session","New session","New session","terminal"]` — target reads "New session", pane unmounted | `[…,"E2E tile title target",…]` — real title, pane still unmounted; the nonexistent second tile correctly stays "New session" |
| New unit test | fails (`startUnrestoredTileTitleBackfill is not a function`) | passes (4/4 in file) |
| `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint` on touched files | — | clean |

**Live repro:** Electron e2e (built `dist/`, real backend, `RealSessionBuilder` seeded target + 60 filler rows via `SessionDB`, tiles restored from `hermes.desktop.sessionTiles.v2`, reload) — before: target tab labeled "New session" after boot with the transcript unmounted; after: labeled with its stored title, still unmounted. Repro spec was temporary and is not committed.

## Infographic

![Restored tabs keep their names](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aa8ce0c/lzVirtzYsJ3FD2fRmVnP2_hO91YZS4.png)

author: brianjfox
body:
Fixes #64.

## What

`deriveKrakenLots` (pure twin of the Coinbase builder) over `/0/private/Ledgers`:
- trade legs pair by `refid` — all-dollar-like siblings → basis = Σ|amount| + fees; crypto-to-crypto and `staking` → real date, unknown basis (spot-lookup default covers them); fees are charged in the entry's own asset (lot = amount − fee; withdrawal consumes |amount| + fee);
- internal spot↔staking transfers skipped (same normalized symbol; consuming them would churn real lots into unknowns); deposits/external transfers → `transferred_in`;
- `normalizeKrakenAsset` aggregation matches balances.

Adapter: paced paginated walk (1.2 s, rate-limit backoff, page cap), per-symbol reconciliation guard (net must equal balance exactly) with notes in the raw snapshot, best-effort — a funds-only key leaves positions lot-less and manual lots (#62) still apply. Docs: CONNECTORS.md.

## Verified live on the operator's account (12.4 s)

All four symbols reconcile exactly (BCH, BTC, DOT 3,490.57…, ETH 17.78…): DOT 198 lots (193 staking rewards, 5 USD-quoted buys with basis), ETH 15 lots, BCH/BTC dust dated 2017/2019.

## Tests

`kraken-lots.test.ts`: fiat-trade pairing + fees, crypto-crypto/staking/deposit handling net of asset-side fees, internal-transfer skipping, withdrawal consumption with unit-cost scaling. Full suite 338 pass; typecheck clean.

body:
## Cosa c'è

La build dal sorgente `778573f` (PR #8 fusa in `sorgente`): tabella di qualità unica per tutti i dispositivi, il telefono parte con tutto acceso come il desktop, la scala non scende da sola (`?scala=auto` per vederla lavorare). Etichetta: `778573f.3b4f5c33`.

## Perché

author: pericles-luz
body:
O extrato nunca funcionou em produção. Descoberto ao tentar identificar o crédito das vendas no cartão que caiu na conta hoje.

## O que estava errado

O adaptador lia um "contrato interno limpo" — `id`, `date`, `amount_cents`, `kind` — que a Camada A usava como dublê e que a Camada B ia traduzir contra homologação. **A tradução nunca chegou à produção.**

Nenhum nome batia, exceto `entries` e `description`:

| lia | o C6 manda |
|---|---|
| `id` | `external_id` |
| `date` | `entry_date` (data civil, não instante) |
| `amount_cents` (int) | `amount` (**texto** em reais: `"37.29"`) |
| `kind` | `operation_type` (`INCOMING` / `OUTGOING`) |

O resultado era pior do que a rota não existir: todo campo caía zerado, o `kind` vazio reprovava na revalidação de domínio, e `GET /v1/statement` devolvia **400 em qualquer janela de datas** — como se o pedido do cliente estivesse errado.

## Como foi medido

Em produção, mesmo tenant e mesma chave:

```
GET /v1/bank-capabilities  →  200  {"configured":true,"pix":true,"card":true}
GET /v1/statement          →  400  {"error":"invalid request"}
```

Não era autenticação nem período. Chamando o C6 **direto**, com a sonda:

```
GET /v1/statement?start_date=2026-09-01&end_date=2026-09-02  →  200
{"entries":[{"external_id":"2256146244…","entry_date":"2026-09-02","amount":"37.29",
  "title":"CRED LOJ C CREDITO","description":"CART. CREDIT - PAYGO ADMINISTR - Elo Cré",
  "operation_type":"INCOMING","reference":"202609010000499095671", …}]}
```

O banco responde. O 400 era nosso.

## Três decisões no mapeamento

**`amount` passa por `brlDecimal`**, a mesma disciplina sem float do resto do adaptador. Um centavo perdido num extrato é um centavo que ninguém consegue explicar depois.

**Tipo de operação desconhecido vira string vazia, de propósito**, para o domínio recusar o extrato inteiro. Num extrato, errar o sinal é errar o saldo — melhor a leitura falhar visivelmente do que classificar como entrada algo que talvez seja saída. É o oposto de adivinhar.

**`title` e `description` são juntados**, não escolhidos. São duas metades do histórico — natureza (`CRED LOJ C CREDITO`) e origem (`PAYGO ADMINISTR - Elo Cré`) —, e quem concilia precisa das duas.

## Sobre o teste que existia

Ele fixava a forma inventada:

```go
{"id":"e1","date":"2026-06-05T00:00:00Z","amount_cents":1000,"kind":"credit",…}
```

Passava, e era **pior do que não ter teste**: dava confiança num caminho que nunca funcionou. Foi substituído pela resposta real capturada no fio em 02/09/2026, com uma entrada de débito acrescentada no mesmo formato para cobrir o outro sentido. Mais dois testes: tipo desconhecido não vira crédito, e histórico com uma metade só não deixa separador órfão.

## Verificação

`go build ./...`, `go test ./...` (46 pacotes, zero falhas) e `gofmt -l` limpos.

Uma ressalva honesta: **não rodei `staticcheck`** — ele não está instalado nesta máquina. Descrições de PR anteriores minhas de hoje o citaram porque eu usava `which staticcheck && staticcheck ./...`, que falha em silêncio. Os outros três comandos sempre rodaram de verdade.

Também não consegui exercitar a rota completa contra produção, porque isso depende deste merge. O que está provado é o mapeamento, contra o corpo real; o que falta é uma chamada a `/v1/statement` pela nossa API depois do deploy.

## Junto vai um modo de sonda

`c6-webhook-probe <tenant> --extrato [inicio] [fim]`, somente leitura. O modo padrão da sonda não servia: ele segue para um PUT de webhook com ref descartável e, com a varredura de renovação desligada, isso não se cura sozinho — sobrescreveria a inscrição viva do tenant.

author: profhepta
body:
## Summary

- Adds one protected-`main` GitHub Actions lane that runs the complete desktop transaction: exact source commit → Android build → target-files/APK verification → allowlisted APK install → AiShell launcher smoke on the approved handset.
- The job requires runner group `trillionnium-real-devices` and the exact labels `self-hosted`, `linux`, `x64`, `desktop`; it cannot be routed to the ROG or macOS runners.
- It clones the exact `GITHUB_SHA` itself (no `actions/checkout`) and keeps the control checkout, Android tree, `OUT_DIR`, persistent bounded ccache, temporary files, extracted APKs, receipts, and logs under `/data/toshiba-dev/TrillionniumOS`.
- The desktop runner `_work`/`_temp`/`_tool` paths resolve to the same external filesystem. The tracked systemd drop-in adds mount dependencies and stops the listener/workers if the removable disk disappears.

## Build and device contract

- The helper verifies the pinned 1,172-project manifest identity and the five declared overlay project heads/content digests. The remaining pre-provisioned base projects are explicitly treated as trusted inputs; this lane does not claim a fresh all-project revision attestation.
- The transaction is serialized, checks for an active Android build, performs a read-only device preflight before materializing the overlay, uses recoverable backups, and fails closed on path/mount/symlink/space mismatches.
- The fixed build is `trillionnium_fogos-bp4a-userdebug` with the four Trillionnium APKs plus the checked-in security-contract host targets and `target-files-package`.
- Device mutations are limited to `adb install -r -d --no-streaming` for those four APKs, package readback, and the fixed AiShell force-stop/start. No root, push, remount, reboot, fastboot, flash, OTA, or arbitrary shell command is allowed.

## Validation and current host state

- Latest commit: `372aed9b708239e4b412ff3ffc6973754eef5a22`.
- 13 targeted Android CI unit tests, Python compile, `git diff --check`, and actionlint 1.7.7 with ShellCheck 0.10.0 pass.
- Live ADB preflight passed read-only for `ZY32JLVHGN` (`fogos`, `userdebug`, SDK 36); no mutating ADB command was issued during validation.
- The external disk currently has about 210 GiB free, while the workflow gate is 400 GiB (and the existing checkout plus `out` is roughly 724 GiB). Therefore the first real run intentionally fails before cloning/building/installing until space is reclaimed or the disk is replaced. No automatic deletion is performed.
- The device preflight runs before overlay materialization, and bounded build-log writes/timeout cleanup fail closed if the removable disk fills during compilation.
- A full clean build → APK install has not been claimed or run yet; merge to protected `main`, satisfy the storage gate, and approve the `android-real-device` environment before dispatching.

The launcher smoke is not an instrumentation suite and does not prove a new system image/OTA. Framework, kernel, APEX, init, SELinux, vendor, or other system-image changes need a separately reviewed image lane.

author: kuroi17
body:
## Description Summary
This PR implements a full 20-point codebase audit and refinement across platform configuration manifests (Android and iOS), data integrity algorithms, optical QR resilience, and UI/UX usability heuristics.

All changes have been validated against the Flutter test suite (`30/30 unit and benchmark tests passing`) and Flutter analyzer (`0 issues`).

---

## Changes Breakdown by Phase

### Phase 1: Critical Platform & Functional Fixes (P1)
- **Asset Path Casing Normalization (`home_screen.dart`, `pubspec.yaml`):**
  - Updated `Image.asset` references from `assets/Qiwii_logo.png` to `assets/qiwii_logo.png` and configured `- assets/` wildcard directory packaging in `pubspec.yaml`.
  - Added graceful fallback `errorBuilder` containers to prevent unhandled asset runtime exceptions and overflow banners.
- **iOS Photo Library Access (`ios/Runner/Info.plist`):**
  - Added `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription` to resolve crashes and App Store compliance issues when users select QR codes from the photo gallery.
  - Configured `CFBundleDisplayName` to `Qiwii`.
- **iOS Custom URL Scheme Registration (`ios/Runner/Info.plist`):**
  - Added `CFBundleURLTypes` registering `qiwii` and `contactqr` custom schemes to handle deep links opened outside the application.
- **Android App Links (`android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`):**
  - Added intent-filter `<data>` entries for `kuroi17.github.io` (`/Qiwii` and `/Qiwii-Easy-Contact-Share-QR`) to ensure web transfer links intercept cleanly into the native app.
- **Web Transfer Base URL Correction (`qr_codec.dart`):**
  - Updated `webBaseUrl` from the deprecated repository path to `https://kuroi17.github.io/Qiwii/#`, resolving HTTP 404 errors when opening transfer links in messaging platforms.
- **Search Multi-Select State Preservation (`sender_provider.dart`, `receiver_provider.dart`, `send_screen.dart`, `received_screen.dart`):**
  - Updated `selectAll()` and `clearAll()` methods to use Set Union (`selectedIds.union(filteredIds)`) and Set Difference when search filters are active.
  - Updated UI selection counter and toggle buttons to display dynamic labels (`Select all matches` vs `Deselect matches`).
- **Scanner Re-Scan Debounce (`scanner_screen.dart`):**
  - Introduced a 3-second cooldown window (`_lastScannedPayload` and `_lastScannedTime`) to prevent infinite PIN modal re-trigger loops when canceling modal dialogs while pointing the camera at a QR code.
- **Deep Link Root Navigation (`result_screen.dart`):**
  - Replaced `Navigator.popUntil` with `Navigator.pushAndRemoveUntil(context, MaterialPageRoute(builder: (_) => const HomeScreen()), (route) => false)` to avoid blank screen traps on cold-boot link opens.

---

### Phase 2: Data Integrity & UI/UX Heuristics Polish (P2)
- **Address Book Name Splitting (`contact_repository.dart`):**
  - Split multi-word full names into `firstName` and `lastName` fields when writing to the native device address book, preserving alphabetical sorting by surname.
- **10-Digit Mobile Number Duplicate Precision (`phone_normalizer.dart`):**
  - Updated phone normalization and duplicate matching algorithms to evaluate 10 national significant digits for standard mobile formats, eliminating false-positive duplicate collisions across different telco prefixes.
- **ReviewScreen Token Alignment (`review_screen.dart`):**
  - Aligned color palette and icon tokens with the unified Warm Almond and Orange Ember design system (`AppColors.accent`, `AppColors.accentTint`, `AppColors.ink`, `AppColors.ink2`, `Icons.verified_rounded`).
- **Menu Capitalization (`home_screen.dart`):**
  - Standardized popup menu item text from `LICENSES` to Title Case `Licenses`.
- **Duplicate Banner Touch Target (`received_screen.dart`):**
  - Replaced text link with an accessible, styled button container for `Skip All` duplicates to satisfy mobile touch target guidelines (Fitts's Law).
- **Soft Keyboard Dismiss on Scroll (`send_screen.dart`, `received_screen.dart`):**
  - Added `keyboardDismissBehavior: ScrollViewKeyboardDismissBehavior.onDrag` to contact list views for automatic keyboard dismissal when scrolling.
- **PIN Peek Toggle & Minimalist Layout (`enter_pin_modal.dart`, `set_pin_modal.dart`):**
  - Added an interactive visibility eye toggle to switch between masked dots and readable digit boxes.
  - Removed redundant step badges to maintain a clean, compact layout across mobile and desktop browser viewports.
- **Landscape & Accessibility Scale Protection (`enter_pin_modal.dart`, `set_pin_modal.dart`):**
  - Wrapped modal contents in `SingleChildScrollView` to prevent `RenderFlex` overflow errors in landscape orientation or high system text scale factors.

---

### Phase 3: Optical QR & Network Advisory (P3)
- **QR Error Correction Level Upgrade (`qr_screen.dart`):**
  - Upgraded QR rendering error correction from `QrErrorCorrectLevel.L` (7% recovery) to `QrErrorCorrectLevel.M` (15% recovery) to enhance camera scanning tolerance against screen reflections, smudges, and low lighting.
- **Tier 2 Local Network Transfer Advisory (`qr_screen.dart`):**
  - Added a contextual connectivity helper badge for bulk transfers (>30 contacts) advising users to maintain sender and receiver devices on the same Wi-Fi network or Personal Hotspot.

---

## Testing & Verification

- **Static Analysis:**
  ```powershell
  flutter analyze
  # Result: No issues found! (0 errors, 0 warnings)
  ```
- **Automated Test Suite:**
  ```powershell
  flutter test
  # Result: All 30 tests passed! (100%)
  ```
- **Tested Modules:**
  - `crypto_utils_test.dart` (Key derivation, payload encryption, tampering rejection)
  - `phone_normalizer_test.dart` (Phone normalization, 10-digit matching, email comparison, duplicate flagging)
  - `qr_codec_test.dart` (Direct QR encoding, minified format, PIN encryption, URL generation)
  - `receiver_import_test.dart` (Duplicate counting, selection metrics, batch imports)
  - `scalability_benchmark_test.dart` (Tier 1 instant direct encoding, Tier 2 local network transfer benchmarks)
  - `session_resilience_test.dart` (Server lifecycle, memory wipe, authentication validation, error recovery)
  - `widget_test.dart` (Home screen rendering, contact model initials, state filters)

---

## Related Documentation
- `CODEBASE_AUDIT.md` (Full 20-point audit matrix and resolution tracking)

# What does this PR do?

`get_repetition_penalty_reward` currently accepts non-positive `ngram_size` values. These values produce an empty n-gram list and result in a `ZeroDivisionError` only when the returned reward function is called.

This PR:

- validates `ngram_size` when constructing the reward function and raises an actionable `ValueError`;
- documents that `ngram_size` must be greater than zero;
- adds regression coverage for zero and negative values.

Fixes #7015

body: ## What Changed When the server loads persisted history for a session it has no live process for, it now neutralizes what the dead process left on before the new shell starts: - Appends `CSI ? n l` or `CSI ? n h` for every tracked DEC private mode the history leaves away from its power-on default: mouse tracking and encodings (9, 1000, 1002, 1003, 1005, 1006, 1015), focus reporting (1004), alternate screen (47, 1047, 1049), cursor visibility (25), cursor keys (1), origin (6), autowrap (7), bracketed paste (2004). The alternate screen is left first so its cursor restore cannot undo a cursor-show. - Replays the Kitty keyboard stack (push, pop, set, RIS) and appends `CSI = 0 ; 1 u` when the stack ends with flags set. - RIS clears the tracking. DECSTR is ignored, because libghostty-vt leaves all of these modes alone on DECSTR (measured against the vendored wasm). About 95 lines in `apps/server/src/terminal/Manager.ts`. Tests: five Manager cases (Codex Kitty push, Claude mouse and focus, alternate screen with hidden cursor and a DECSTR that must not count, a clean exit that must be left alone, idempotency across two restarts) and one ABI assertion that `CSI = 0 ; 1 u` silences key releases in the vendored libghostty-vt. ## Why Fixes #9219. Fixes #8574. A server restart while Codex CLI or Claude Code is running leaves their modes in the persisted history with no teardown. The fresh shell inherits that history, the client replays it, and key releases or mouse reports reach zsh as junk until the terminal is recreated. The reset sits at the one boundary where the server knows a new process is inheriting a dead one's history. Restart-in-place, exit-then-reopen, and UI close already wipe history, so no other path needs it. Resetting on the server means web, desktop, and mobile clients all get a clean replay from the same snapshot. The Kitty sequence was chosen from measurement: `CSI = 0 ; 1 u` zeroes the active flags without a full reset, whereas RIS would also drop scrollback. The mode table matches the one in #9027 so that PR can absorb this on rebase. Verified in a T3 Code (Dev) build against the real broken histories: the logs gained the resets after the dangling sequences, and the fresh shells took typing and scrolling cleanly. ## Checklist - [x] This PR is small and focused - [x] I explained what changed and why - [x] No UI changes, so no screenshots or video Fable 5.1 via Claude Code. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes terminal replay semantics on session open and relies on regex-based CSI parsing; incorrect neutralization could append wrong resets or miss dangling modes, but scope is limited to persisted-history reopen and is heavily tested. > > **Overview** > When a terminal session is **created** with no in-memory session but persisted history exists, the server now runs that history through **`neutralizeInheritedHistory`** before the new shell starts. The helper replays ESC/CSI traffic to infer lingering DEC private modes (mouse, focus, alternate screen, cursor visibility, bracketed paste, etc.) and Kitty keyboard stack state, then **appends** the sequences needed to return to power-on defaults—**leaving the alternate screen first** so cursor restore does not fight a show-cursor reset, and appending **`CSI = 0;1u`** when the active main-screen Kitty stack is non-zero. RIS in the history clears tracked state; DECSTR is intentionally not treated as a full reset. > > This only affects the **first open** path in `openLocked` (not restart or reopen-after-exit, which already wipe history). Clients replay the normalized snapshot instead of re-enabling modes a crashed TUIs left behind (Codex CLI, Claude Code, nvim). Tests cover Kitty/mouse/focus/alternate-screen edge cases, clean exits, idempotency across two opens, and vendored ghostty ABI behavior for the Kitty clear sequence. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit caf3d46d2bcc8cc8f37f4cbc65c2f9427e788509. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. author: mbeka02
body:
# Slice 2 — Summary of Changes & Capabilities

Here is a breakdown of everything delivered in **Slice 2: Candidate Preview & Transactional Assignment**.

---

## 1. Pure Constraint Engine (`server/scheduling/constraints.ts`)

A pure TypeScript rule engine (`evaluateAssignment`) with **zero database or framework dependencies**. It computes structured scheduling blockers, warnings, and projected labor impacts:

* **Qualification & Certification:** Validates required skills and location certifications against shift dates.
* **Timezone-Aware Availability:** Evaluates availability rules inside each rule’s specified IANA timezone (resolves cross-timezone shifts correctly).
* **Shift Overlap:** Detects overlapping active assignments using half-open `[)` intervals.
* **10-Hour Minimum Rest:** Enforces a mandatory 10-hour rest gap before and after candidate shifts across all locations.
* **Daily Labor Limits:** Computes daily totals in the staff member's primary timezone ($>8\text{h}$ warning, $>12\text{h}$ hard block).
* **Weekly Labor & Overtime:** Tracks weekly hours starting Monday 00:00 local time ($\ge 35\text{h}$ warning, $\ge 40\text{h}$ overtime projection).
* **Consecutive Workdays:** Counts contiguous worked calendar dates ($6\text{th}$ day warning, $7\text{th}$ day block requiring manager override).
* **Headcount Enforcement:** Blocks assignment when active shift headcount is full.
* **Structured Errors:** Returns structured violations containing `{ code, severity, message, details }`.

---

## 2. Transactional Assignment Service (`server/scheduling/assignment.ts`)

Concurrently-safe database operations that guarantee data integrity:

* **Server-Side RBAC:** Enforces manager location scoping against `manager_locations` valid windows.
* **Deterministic Lock Hierarchy:** Locks the shift row (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`), then staff profile row before re-evaluating state—preventing deadlocks and check-then-insert races.
* **Authoritative Revalidation:** Re-reads current assignments and headcount inside the transaction; rolls back completely if blockers are detected.
* **Atomic Commit:** Persists `assignments` row, `assignment_periods` range row, and increments `schedule_weeks` optimistic version atomically.
* **Structured Race Error Translation:** Traps PostgreSQL GiST exclusion (`23P01`) and unique index (`23505`) violations into structured `CONCURRENT_ASSIGNMENT_CONFLICT` errors.
* **Dry-Run Preview (`previewAssignment`):** Computes exact constraint outcomes and projected labor impact without modifying database state.

---

## 3. Database Schema & Migration Additions

Added tables, constraints, and backfills in Drizzle ORM and PostgreSQL migrations:

* `staff_skills` — Qualifications with `valid_from` / `valid_to` dates.
* `staff_location_certifications` — Location access with validity dates and statuses (`active`, `suspended`, `revoked`).
* `availability_rules` — Recurring weekly rules with day-of-week, local wall-clock times, and IANA timezone.
* `availability_exceptions` — Specific date overrides (`unavailable` or `override`).
* `assignment_periods` & **GiST Exclusion Constraint:**
  * Enabled PostgreSQL `btree_gist` extension.
  * Stores `work_period` as `tstzrange` in `[start, end)` half-open format.
  * Added `EXCLUDE USING gist (staff_id WITH =, work_period WITH &&)` constraint to prevent double-booking at the database layer.
  * Backfilled active historical assignments into `assignment_periods`.

---

## 4. Manager Schedule Board & Candidate Drawer UI

User-facing manager assignment workflow:

* **Candidate Drawer (`components/shift-sync/candidate-drawer.tsx`):** Sliding sheet opened by clicking any shift on the schedule board (`/schedule`).
* **Candidate Ranking:** Ranks staff members by constraint status (Clear $\rightarrow$ Warning $\rightarrow$ Blocked).
* **Impact Ledger:** Displays real-time projected daily hours, weekly hours, consecutive days, and overtime warnings per candidate.
* **Inline Conflict Details:** Displays exact violation codes, human-readable explanations, and specific metric details.
* **Interactive Controls:** Blocked candidates disable assignment actions; warnings require explicit confirmation. Successful assignment closes the drawer and refreshes the schedule board state.

---

## 5. Test Suite & Verification

Added **17 new unit and integration tests** (27 total passing across 7 test files):

* **`tests/constraint-engine.test.ts` (11 tests):** Pure logic verification for skills, certifications, availability timezones, overlaps, 10h rest, 12h daily limits, 40h overtime, 7th-day overrides, headcount limits, and clean assignments.
* **`tests/assignment-transaction.test.ts` (6 tests):** Integration tests for non-persisting previews, atomic assignment commits, constraint rollbacks, and concurrent race conditions (competing staff for overlapping shifts & final headcount slots).

---

author: sattyamjjain
body:
Closes the measurement half of issue #11. The enforcement switch that issue asked for now exists, but it cannot be turned on by an environment variable alone — it needs a published false-positive rate under a named threshold.

## What this measures

The coherence-divergence monitor is a lexical matcher over the run trajectory. Its false-positive rate is therefore a property of the vocabulary it meets, and until now that number did not exist. It does now:

**10.42% (25 of 240 benign trajectories), Wilson 95% CI [7.16%, 14.92%]**, at the shipped defaults (lookahead 8, min_confidence 0.5) — not at a tuned setting.

Roughly one correct run in ten would be parked at an approval gate. That is a bad number and it is published as one. `README.md` and `docs/runbooks/coherence-divergence.md` both state it.

Split by provenance, never pooled silently:

| Provenance | Flagged | n | Rate | 95% CI |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `synthetic_grounded` | 13 | 192 | 6.77% | [4.00%, 11.24%] |
| `synthetic_authored` | 12 | 48 | 25.00% | [14.92%, 38.78%] |

**Trajectories captured from a real agent run: 0.** No committed artifact in this repository carries agent trajectory text — 0 of 35 reports have output-like fields — so the corpus is generated and the manifest says `real: 0` rather than letting "grounded in real text" drift into "real". What is real is the vocabulary: statement and action strings come from this repo's own `git log` subjects and the safe-pr-agent tool allowlist.

The worst shapes are `vocabulary_trap_statement` (50%, e.g. `error: 0 errors, 0 warnings`) and `handoff_then_unrelated_closure` (33%). `boring_success`, `multi_step_tool_sequence`, `partial_failure_disclaimed` and `commit_message_names_fixed_bug` are all 0%.

## The corpus

`evals/datasets/coherence-negatives/` — 240 committed traces across 8 shapes, seed 20260902, each carrying `provenance`, `why_benign` and `sources` so any flag can be argued with rather than taken on faith. The manifest separates generated from captured.

An earlier draft of this corpus read 16.67% because every trace ended in a commit inside the lookahead window — inflated by construction, not by the monitor. Varying the tail (0–6 extra steps) brought it to the honest 10.42%.

## The gate

`rust/services/gateway/src/coherence_evidence.rs`:

```rust
pub const MAX_FP_RATE_FOR_ENFORCE: f64 = 0.15;
pub const MAX_EVIDENCE_AGE_DAYS: i64 = 14;
```

0.15 is not a tolerance anyone derived from an operational requirement, and the comment says so. It is the Wilson upper bound (14.92%) rounded up — the honest reading of "the rate could plausibly be this bad". Setting `FERRUMDECK_COHERENCE_MODE=enforce` now only *requests* enforce; it is granted when the series file carries a `coherence_fp` measurement that is present, fresh, and under the threshold. Otherwise the gateway logs at `error!` and stays in shadow. `/ready` reports `{requested, active, reason}` so the refusal is visible rather than silent.

Fail-closed was mutation-tested: inverting `EnforceDecision::allowed()` fails 3 tests.

## Series row

One row appended to `docs/eval-health-series.jsonl`, matching the existing schema, with the harness version stamped and the numbers under the canonical Wilson keys (`ProportionCI.to_dict()` — the same serializer `asb` and `injection_defense` already use). The report carries no timestamp, which is what keeps it byte-identical local vs CI; a test pins that.

## Not in this PR

Issue #9 is untouched. The narrowing-only auto-apply guard writes to a policy plane and deserves its own PR.

## Test plan

- `cargo test --workspace` — 802 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo fmt --check` — clean
- `pytest` — 662 passed
- `ruff check` + `pyright` — clean
- Honesty gates: `gen_eval_health.py --check --release`, `--check-series` ("1 row(s) added since HEAD"), claims integrity, route backing, `bump_version.py --check` — all green
- `make eval-coherence-fp` reproduces the report byte-for-byte

Workspace bumped to 0.8.17 across all four published crates.

author: dosteeve2-hash
body:
## État initial

| | avant | après |
|---|---|---|
| Limite de débit IA | **aucune** | 20 req/h/appelant sur `/api/chat` |
| CI | 2 workflows, **cassés** | réparés |
| `npm run lint` | 4 erreurs, 60 warnings | **0 erreur**, 56 warnings |
| `npm test` | 41 ✅ | **50** ✅ |
| `tsc --noEmit` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `npm run build` | ✅ | ✅ |

---

## 🔴 Aucune limite de débit sur l'endpoint qui coûte de l'argent

`CLAUDE.md` est explicite :

> Rate limit sur tous les endpoints AI : 20 req/user/heure

Or :

```
$ grep -rln "rateLimit\|rate-limit\|ratelimit" src/
(rien)
```

`/api/chat` appelle l'API Anthropic. Sans limite, une boucle depuis une seule machine vide le crédit d'API — et l'endpoint est public.

### Ce que j'ai implémenté

`src/lib/rate-limit.ts` : compteur à fenêtre fixe, dans **Redis quand il répond**, **en mémoire sinon**.

Ce repli n'est pas un détail. Redis est optionnel partout dans ce projet — `initializeRedis()` renvoie `false` et l'application continue. Une limite qui n'existerait que côté Redis se contournerait donc en rendant Redis indisponible. Le compteur mémoire est par instance, ce que le résultat signale honnêtement :

```ts
export interface RateLimitResult {
  allowed: boolean;
  limit: number;
  remaining: number;
  retryAfter: number;
  /** `false` quand Redis est indisponible : le compteur n'est alors pas partagé. */
  shared: boolean;
}
```

**Identification de l'appelant.** L'application n'a pas d'authentification : l'IP transmise par le proxy (`x-forwarded-for`, puis `x-real-ip`) est le meilleur identifiant disponible. C'est usurpable, et je préfère le dire que le sous-entendre — mais cela borne l'abus le plus courant. Le jour où l'authentification arrive, remplacer `clientIdentifier` par l'id utilisateur suffit.

Un refus renvoie **429** avec `Retry-After`, `RateLimit-Limit` et `RateLimit-Remaining`.

**13 tests** couvrent le passage sous quota, le blocage, l'isolation entre appelants, la réouverture après la fenêtre (avec `Date.now` figé) et le cas sans Redis.

## 🔴 Les deux workflows CI ne pouvaient pas passer

| problème | conséquence |
|---|---|
| `node-version: '18'` dans les deux | Next 16 exige Node ≥ 20 |
| `actions/upload-artifact@v3` | **désactivée par GitHub depuis janvier 2025** — l'étape échoue systématiquement |
| `npm install` au lieu de `npm ci` | un lockfile divergent passe inaperçu |
| lint seulement dans `build.yml`, déclenché sur push vers `main` | **aucune PR n'était lintée** |
| pas de typecheck | — |

Et le job `deploy` :

```yaml
- name: Deploy to production
  run: |
    echo "🚀 Deploying to production..."
    # Add your deployment steps here (Vercel, Railway, etc.)
```

Un `echo` derrière un commentaire. Il passait au vert à chaque push sur `main` sans rien déployer — un badge vert qui ne signifie rien. Je l'ai retiré plutôt que de laisser le faux signal ; le déploiement se fait via l'intégration Vercel.

L'étape `generate-embeddings` est **conservée** : j'ai vérifié le script, c'est du TF-IDF local sans appel d'API, il tourne donc sans secret. `codecov-action` passe de v3 à v5.

## 🟠 Lint

**Le tableau de bord de monitoring se vidait toutes les 30 secondes.** `fetchData` commençait par `setLoading(true)`, et l'intervalle le rappelait :

```tsx
const fetchData = useCallback(async () => {
  setLoading(true);          // ← à chaque rafraîchissement
  // …
}, []);

useEffect(() => {
  void fetchData();
  const timer = setInterval(fetchData, 30_000);
  // …
});
```

`loading` démarre déjà à `true`. Il n'a aucune raison d'y revenir : les setState vivent maintenant dans les callbacks de la promesse, le premier chargement affiche l'indicateur, et les rafraîchissements suivants remplacent les données sans faire clignoter l'écran. La règle `set-state-in-effect` était satisfaite au passage, pas contournée.

Le reste : `require()` réautorisé dans `scripts/**/*.js` (scripts Node lancés à la main, hors bundle), et deux apostrophes en typographie française. La troisième occurrence méritait un traitement différent — c'est une commande shell affichée à l'utilisateur :

```tsx
export ADMIN_API_KEY="your-secret-key-here"
```

Ses guillemets doivent rester des guillemets droits. Elle devient une expression JS plutôt que du texte JSX, ce qui règle le lint sans altérer la commande.

## ⚠️ Ce que je n'ai pas fait

**Les 41 `any` restent en warning.** Ils sont concentrés dans les couches RAG et agent, et les typer correctement demande de comprendre les formes de données du corpus — c'est un travail à part entière, pas un passage de lint. La règle est laissée en `warn` avec un commentaire qui le dit, pour que la CI bloque déjà sur tout le reste. Dis-moi si tu veux que je m'y attaque.

- **~30 fichiers Markdown de statut à la racine** (`CODEX_*.md`, `STATUS_FINAL.md`, `WORK_COMPLETED.md`, `FINAL_STATUS.md`, `CONTINUATION_SUMMARY.md`…). Ils noient `README.md` et `ARCHITECTURE.md`, les deux qu'on veut vraiment trouver. Un dossier `docs/archive/` les rangerait.

## `!restart` did not restart

It set exit code 221 and stopped, and nothing started it again

A level change takes effect at once, so the `say` and the `InitGame` landed in the same second -

author: posthog[bot]
body:
## Problem

- Self-service checkout is blocked for active users: the billing checkout route returns an auth rate-limit error before it can mint a Dodo Payments URL.
- The route preflights `GET /auth/me` to resolve the active workspace. That read shares the generic **per-user 100/60s** request budget, so once a user's normal activity — or a checkout that fires several requests at once — crosses the budget, the *session lookup itself* returns `429 RATE_LIMITED` and the checkout route surfaces it as a failure.
- Observed as an active `ApiCallError` issue: 9 occurrences across 3 users inside one second, all `GET /auth/me -> 429 RATE_LIMITED`, all from the checkout route. The events for one user landed within ~2 ms of each other — parallel requests, not spaced retries.
- The same latent bug hits every other `/auth/me` caller (dashboard shell, billing status banner, many client pages); checkout is only where the throw was captured.

## Change

- Mark `GET /auth/me` with `@SkipRateLimit()`. The identity read is a session bootstrap that every authenticated surface hits on load; the limiter runs *after* `InternalAuthGuard` has already resolved `req.user`, so the handler only echoes fields already in hand yet still spends a rate-limit token.
- Scope stays tight: the paired `POST /auth/me/welcome-email` and every workspace mutation keep their limits. Expensive paths (agent generation, the checkout `POST`) have their own guards.
- Two source-level test pins: the exemption is on the `@Get('me')` handler and **not** on the welcome-email POST.

## Why

Rate-limiting the session-identity endpoint turns normal activity into broken sessions and blocked checkout. Session resolution should not be a limited resource; it is nearly free here because the auth guard already did the work.

## Verification

- `apps/api` rate-limit guard suite: 19 passed (incl. 2 new pins).
- `apps/api` auth suite: 27 passed.
- `pnpm typecheck` clean; `eslint` clean on changed files.

## Agent context

- Considered in-request backoff/retry on the preflight, but the limiter window is the full 60 s, so a short retry cannot clear it.
- Considered client-side dedup of parallel checkout requests; it reduces the fan-out but does not stop a user near the budget from 429-ing on the identity read, and would not fix the same failure on the dashboard/banner. Exempting the read fixes the root cause for all callers.

---
*Created with [PostHog Desktop](https://posthog.com/desktop?ref=pr) from [this inbox report](https://us.posthog.com/project/548081/inbox/reports/01a061e9-e0bc-710a-b074-346b1c5d86fd).*
