author: zigzagcai
body:
## Summary

This PR shards the replicated GLM-5.3-Flash sparse-indexer prefill work across
tensor-parallel (TP) ranks for long MQA prefills. Each rank computes a
cost-balanced contiguous query-row slice, runs MQA logits/top-k locally, and
exchanges only the final int32 index rows with one layout-preserving
`all_gatherv` per indexer layer.

## Scope and safety

- The row planner uses compressed causal MQA key length as its cost, avoiding
  an imbalanced “equal rows” split for ragged/long contexts.
- GLM kpool expansion and incomplete-pool tail semantics are preserved; the
  gathered width includes `topk_tokens + index_kpool - 1` tail columns.
- The feature is gated to CUDA, TP > 1, long MQA prefills with at least 1,024
  rows per rank. DCP/PCP, ROCm, disabled PyNCCL/symmetric-memory,
  batch-invariant, and FULL CUDA-graph modes retain the old path.
- Decode, short-prefill, KV-cache, sampling, model-weight, and excluded
  execution paths are unchanged. No padded/fixed-shape collective is used by
  the upstream treatment path.

The branch head is `d66da5c4a6b9dd309e35d576f26b48d3dd034924`, and its parent
is the latest #53906 head `4500c80c080328dfe62435d083f4063e00d987df`
(`refs/pull/53906/head`). `git merge-base --is-ancestor` passes. The
optimization commits are `9bef8be552` and `a30eb3e734`; the kpool correctness
follow-up is `e4185bbd90`; long-context coverage is `d66da5c4a6`.

## Matched 1K–1M performance A/B

Configuration: 4x NVIDIA H200 (CUDA devices 4–7), TP4, native FP8 weights,
BF16 KV cache, balanced profile, chunked prefill,
`max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, `max_model_len=1,048,576`, `max_num_seqs=8`,
MTP=0, prefix caching disabled, C1 sequential requests, 16 output tokens,
`temperature=0`, `top_p=1`, `top_k=1`, and `ignore_eos`. Each arm used a fresh
server, two warmups, and six measured requests per context with fixed seeds.
TTFT is p50 with per-request MAD in parentheses; TPOT is the benchmark p50 using
vLLM's standard `latency - TTFT` definition. With 16-token outputs, long-context
responses can bundle multiple tokens into one SSE chunk, so TPOT is included for
completeness but has higher transport variance than TTFT and aggregate
throughput. Throughput is aggregate input+output tokens/s. Positive latency
deltas mean lower latency.

Both arms used the same model/runtime/compiled CUDA extensions; treatment
overlaid only the row-sharding Python logic. All 66 requests in each arm
completed successfully, with no HTTP failures, CUDA errors, or illegal memory
accesses. The 1M point is exactly 1,000,000 input tokens (not 1,048,576), so
the 16-token completion remains within the server limit.

| Context | Baseline TTFT ms (MAD) | Optimized TTFT ms (MAD) | TTFT Δ | Baseline TPOT ms | Optimized TPOT ms | TPOT Δ | Baseline total tok/s | Optimized total tok/s | Throughput Δ |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1K | 135.24 (0.52) | 133.50 (0.37) | +1.31% | 5.702 | 5.723 | -0.37% | 4,676.6 | 4,728.3 | +1.11% |
| 2K | 139.24 (1.54) | 135.75 (1.04) | +2.57% | 5.697 | 5.769 | -1.24% | 9,109.1 | 9,283.6 | +1.92% |
| 4K | 174.04 (0.92) | 175.97 (1.66) | -1.10% | 5.634 | 5.644 | -0.19% | 15,886.4 | 15,782.3 | -0.66% |
| 8K | 317.52 (1.07) | 319.53 (2.35) | -0.63% | 5.493 | 5.534 | -0.76% | 20,536.4 | 20,425.8 | -0.54% |
| 16K | 635.51 (4.47) | 634.28 (4.46) | +0.19% | 5.270 | 5.223 | +0.91% | 22,967.0 | 22,993.4 | +0.11% |
| 32K | 1,315.38 (3.54) | 1,283.76 (3.03) | +2.46% | 4.564 | 4.505 | +1.31% | 23,724.6 | 24,273.9 | +2.32% |
| 64K | 2,679.43 (6.10) | 2,579.41 (4.27) | +3.88% | 3.045 | 3.391 | -10.19% | 24,036.6 | 24,938.1 | +3.75% |
| 128K | 5,416.63 (4.14) | 5,254.29 (2.97) | +3.09% | 0.640 | 0.418 | +52.89% | 24,167.1 | 24,915.3 | +3.10% |
| 256K | 11,462.02 (7.36) | 10,684.88 (9.45) | +7.27% | 0.175 | 0.178 | -1.99% | 22,876.4 | 24,499.6 | +7.10% |
| 512K | 25,608.19 (36.48) | 22,193.62 (12.19) | +15.39% | 0.315 | 0.333 | -5.41% | 20,470.3 | 23,611.6 | +15.35% |
| 1M (1,000,000) | 59,411.88 (10.93) | 45,449.92 (94.02) | +30.72% | 1.026 | 1.034 | -0.72% | 16,823.2 | 21,990.2 | +30.71% |

The small 4K/8K negatives are not a persistent regression: those sizes are
below the 1,024-row/rank gate and execute the existing replicated path. An
independent repeat with ten requests per point measured 4K TTFT/TPOT/throughput
changes of `+0.06%/-0.34%/+0.16%` and 8K changes of
`+1.10%/-1.54%/+0.65%`. No short-path code change was required. From 128K
upward, the long-prefill gain increases with context length.

## Correctness and accuracy

The operation is layout-preserving: every prefill row is scored and top-k
selected exactly once, then reassembled in original row order. The focused
suite passes **54 tests**, covering cost-balanced partitions, all gate
predicates, metadata construction, and exact gather/reassembly at 128K/256K/
512K/1M. The long-context serving gates completed 128K C1/C4 with matching
32/32 token IDs; 256K/512K/1M control and treatment each completed 2/2 with
32/32 tokens, no invalid IDs, and no CUDA errors.

Exact generated strings are not used as a bitwise quality criterion at
256K–1M: separate FP8/JIT server processes are not bitwise-repeatable even for
the unmodified baseline. The semantic correctness gate is exact row
partition/reassembly plus the 128K end-to-end parity case, and model-level
evaluation should be used for quality deltas. The dedicated long-context
accuracy artifacts (`accuracy-baseline-128k-1m.json` and
`accuracy-optimized-128k-1m.json`) exercised 128K/256K/512K/1M prompts with
two 32-token greedy completions per point and reported no invalid token IDs or
CUDA errors. A model-quality score is intentionally not claimed from those
two-request random-token probes. The previously reported GSM8K 0.925 vs
0.940 result belongs to a separate short-context indexer change and is not
attributed to this row-sharding PR.

The optimization is therefore confined to the long MQA-prefill critical path;
short requests and all other components retain their previous implementation.

author: claude[bot]
body:
## 真機第二輪（觀察中 43 分鐘）

```
記憶體：130 MB（起始 26・峰值 162 MB）・近期 -247 MB/小時・整體 +144 MB/小時（10 樣本／43 分）
```

**好消息是曲線的形狀**：閒置 30 MB → 觀察中衝到 162 MB → 回落到 130 MB，近期斜率是**負的**。
上去又回來 ＝ 大工作集 + 有在回收。無上限洩漏的曲線只會一路往上，不會掉。

**壞消息是那個「整體 +144 MB/小時」根本不是速率。** 它是把「閒置 30 MB 跳到觀察中 130 MB」
這個**階段落差**攤到 43 分鐘上算出來的。閒置與觀察中是兩個不同的工作集，把它們接成一條線
取斜率，得到的是「落差 ÷ 總時間」——一個沒有物理意義、但看起來很像成長率的數字。

這是同一類錯誤的**第二次**（第一次是一次性暖機被攤成 +4 MB/小時，PR #33）。

## 修法：斜率不跨越狀態邊界

`MemorySample` 帶 `regime`（閒置／觀察中／接手中），斜率與峰值都只看**目前這一段**，
狀態標在摘要最前面：

```
記憶體〔觀察中〕：130 MB（本階段起始 30・峰值 162 MB）・近期 -247 MB/小時・本階段 +140 MB/小時（7 樣本／43 分）
```

| 決定 | 為什麼 |
|---|---|
| `toggleObserving` **前後各取一次** | 只取一次的話新階段永遠要等下一次開選單才有第二個點，斜率會一直是「待累積」 |
| 同狀態一秒內的重複取樣**丟棄** | 切換路徑可能疊在一起（`toggleObserving` 內部又呼叫 `stopAll`），同一瞬間會冒出好幾筆一樣的點，讓「幾個樣本」這個數字騙人 |
| 狀態不同就一定留，**即使同一瞬間** | 那正是階段邊界，丟掉它新階段就沒有起點 |
| 峰值也改成**本階段** | 判斷「觀察中會不會漏」時，上一階段的峰值只是雜訊。全期峰值另由 `allTimePeakMB` 提供 |
| 切回原本的狀態算**新的一段** | 中間隔了另一個狀態，工作集早就不同了 |

回歸測試**直接用真機那六個點重演**，並釘住「上去又下來要看得出在回收」等四條性質。

## 兩輪的共同教訓（已寫進檔頭）

> **一個看起來像資料的猜測，比「不知道」更糟**——它會讓人停止繼續查，或往錯的方向查。

這正是這個診斷工具本來要避免的失敗，而它自己犯了兩次。

## 現階段結論

兩輪都**沒有重現**那個記憶體告警，而且兩條曲線的形狀都不像洩漏（閒置持平、觀察中上去又回來）。

**在拿到一張告警當下的 Activity Monitor 截圖之前，不應該再為這件事改任何程式碼**
——包括 `CaptureEngine` 那條無上限 `AsyncStream`。改了只會把線索蓋掉。

body:
## What this does

Replaces the `/ussd` stub with the real Africa's Talking browse flow, built as a stateless replay of AT's accumulated `text` field so no server-side session state exists to lose:

- **Home screen** — lists learning areas from the database (seeded Mathematics) and invites direct sub-strand code entry.
- **Strands screen** — the chosen learning area's strands, from the `substrands` table.
- **Sub-strands screen** — the chosen strand's sub-strands, ordered by code.
- **Selection (END)** — records a `teaching_sessions` row, creates/updates the `teachers` row (`last_substrand`), replies `END <code> <title>: your teaching pack is on its way by SMS.`, and sends the seeded `sms_pack` content through the `SmsClient` seam.
- **Direct code entry** — `M-ALG-02` (case-insensitive) at the home screen jumps straight to selection.
- **Invalid input** — re-prompts the same screen with `CON Invalid choice.` and the next input still lands where the caller expects; the session is never dropped.
- **Pack splitting** — new `app/sms_pack.py` splits the pack body on line/word boundaries into `i/n `-numbered parts that each fit one 160-char SMS, with the sub-strand code guaranteed in the final part.

New modules: `app/ussd_menu.py` (pure menu state machine, read-only against the DB), `app/sms_pack.py` (splitter). Side effects (teacher upsert, teaching session, SMS send) live in `routes/ussd.py`. No shared modules touched.

## Tests

`66 passed, 1 skipped` (up from 49 passed, 1 skipped). New coverage in `tests/test_ussd_browse.py` (multi-step sessions via AT's accumulated-text convention, DB side effects, `sms_outbox` assertions, a walk of every reachable screen asserting the 160-char limit) and `tests/test_sms_pack.py` (splitter unit tests). No live Africa's Talking calls; sandbox simulator verification of the end-to-end flow remains a manual step.

Closes #2

author: oxoxdev
body:
## Summary

After an operator **Approved** a parked blocker from the console, two things went wrong: (A) the stopped step did not auto-resume — the operator had to click a separate **Resume** button — and (B) the resumed run's output was never delivered back to the operator. This was the last live-failing residual of the #1860 "blockers are conversations" epic (park → ask → answer/approve → **resume** → **output lands back**).

Root cause — one shared missing wire: the console approvals-resolve path bypassed the blocker-resume tier from #1863. That machinery is complete but was only reachable from the DM-reply entrypoint (`apply_blocker_reply`), the only place that armed a `BlockerResolution`. The HTTP resolve entrypoint (`run_resolve` → `resolve_approval_spawned`) never armed one, so `spawn_follow_up`'s `take_blocker_resolution` returned `None`, the resume fork was skipped, and it fell to a plain `continue_turn` that never moved the card off `paused`. The blocker's origin thread (on the approval, not the card) also received only an ack, never the resumed output, and there was no settle-notification to mirror `notify_blocker_parked`.

Fix:
- **Arm on the console entrypoint** — when the resolved id is a blocker, translate the verdict, capture the step off the parked payload, and `record_blocker_resolution` + `arm_blocker_resolution` before `spawn_follow_up`, so the existing resume fork drives `resume_task_card` → the dispatch choke point. Console **Approve** now resumes identically to a DM answer, for every blocker kind. The #1861 never-execute guard is preserved (a resolving verdict routes to resume, never `perform_effect`).
- **Route resumed output + notify** — the blocker's origin thread becomes a first-class output target on resume, so the answer (not just the ack) relays into it, and a resumed-settle operator notification is raised.

## API Or Behavior Changes

- Approving a blocker from the console (Approvals card / approvals API) now auto-resumes the paused step and delivers the agent's answer back to the blocker's origin thread, plus raises a resume notification — matching the DM-reply behavior. Declining cancels the card.
- No change to the #1861 guarantee that a resolving blocker verdict never re-executes the underlying effect. DM-reply path unchanged except it now also delivers output, not just an ack.

## Tests

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo clippy --no-deps --features openhuman --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo check --all-features`
- [x] `cargo test --features openhuman --lib company::runtime::` (69 passed, 0 failed)

Added 4 tests in `company::runtime::tests::blocker_resume`: `console_approve_resumes_the_paused_card`, `console_approve_never_executes_the_blocker_effect` (regression pins the #1861 guard on the new path), `console_approve_routes_output_to_the_blocker_thread`, `console_deny_cancels_the_card`. The existing `a_resolved_blocker_never_executes_its_effect` and `a_blocker_parked_before_a_restart_still_resumes_after_it` stay green.

Live console verification on a staging tenant is pending (bearer-gated). No Playwright change: no existing e2e harness drives the approvals/blocker flow.

## Documentation

None — completes the #1860 resume contract already described in the blocker docs; no public API surface changed.

Closes #2008

  - Resumed activity is routed to the thread where the blocker was answered.
  - A durable notification is added to that thread when a blocked card resumes.

- **Bug Fixes**

body:
## 정정

v3.00에서 별지점·평단 매수에 LOC 주문가 상한을 넣으며 안내문에 이렇게 적었다:

> LOC는 '종가 ≤ 주문가'면 체결이라, 오늘 종가가 $129.71를 넘지 않는 한 **결과는 같습니다**.

**틀렸다.** 백테에 같은 상한을 넣어 재보니, 결정이 바뀌는 날은 6년에 열흘 남짓인데 무매가 경로의존이라 결과가 크게 갈렸다.

## 실측 (6년 · 10개 설정)

| 상한 | 중앙값 편차 | 최악 | 최선 | 바뀐 결정 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| +10% | 0.30% | −6.8% | +15.6% | 32일 |
| +12% | 0.21% | **−31.3%** | +106.7% | 20일 |
| **+15% (기존 기본값)** | 1.85% | **−28.2%** | +106.5% | 10일 |
| +18% | 0.35% | −2.2% | +5.9% | 4일 |
| **+20%** | 0.24% | **−3.1%** | +1.2% | 2일 |
| +25% | 0.24% | −0.0% | +1.5% | 1일 |

대표 사례 — SOXL 40분할 20%, 상한 +15%: 최종 **−28.25%**, MDD **51.0% → 68.1%**. 바뀐 결정은 25일뿐이다.

중앙값은 어디서나 작지만 **꼬리가 크다.** 상한이 높을수록 바뀌는 결정이 줄어 꼬리가 닫힌다. 기본값 15는 하필 가장 나쁜 구간이었다.

## 수정

- **큰수 % 기본값 15 → 20** (신규 세션 + `st.big` 미설정 세션). 설정 힌트도 실제 용도에 맞게 수정
- **안내문을 사실대로**: "결과가 같다" → "종가가 상한 위로 마감하면 **회차를 건너뜁니다**", 그리고 증권사가 받아주는 한 높게 두라고 안내 (20 권장 → 거부되면 18 → 15)
- 여러 건이 상한에 걸리면 **가장 많이 벗어난 주문가**를 안내에 표시

## 검토했지만 못 쓴 대안 — MOC

MOC(시장가 마감)는 지정가가 없어 가격 밴드에 걸리지 않는다. 실측해보니 훨씬 충실했다:

| 상한 +15% | 지정가 상한 | MOC |
|---|---|---|
| SOXL 30분할 20% | +14.20% | +0.26% |
| SOXL 40분할 20% | **−28.25%** (MDD 51→68%) | **+0.62%** (MDD 51.0→51.0) |
| TQQQ 20분할 15% | +0.77% | 0.00% |

MOC의 오차 집합이 상한 방식의 **부분집합**이라 구조적으로 더 정확하다. 그런데 국내 증권사는 **MOO/MOC를 매도만 지원**해서([삼성증권 공지](https://www.samsungpop.com/ux/kor/customer/notice/notice/noticeViewContent.do?MenuSeqNo=17529): "MOO/MOC 주문은 매도 주문만 가능합니다") 매수엔 쓸 수 없다. 근거를 주석에 남겼다.

## 재발 방지

회귀 `[13]`:
- 상한이 **공짜가 아님을 안내하는지** (건너뛴다는 설명 + 큰수 % 조정 안내)
- 큰수 % **기본값이 20**인지 (꼬리가 닫히는 구간)

회귀 **131 PASS / 0 FAIL** · 전략 SSOT **22/22 PASS**

author: yongjohnlee80
body:
Consumer items **(a)**, **(b)** and **(d)** of jarvis's seam handover, on `ecc381a`.

## What changed

- **(a)** `Authenticator` gains `OpenWireSessionWith`; the listener calls it with the accepted `application_name`. The old method stays — it is what the engine still exposes and what the fakes implement.
- **(b)** `synthesizedStatuses` forwards the target's own reported set **verbatim**, then the three overrides. Before the seam the front door could not know these, so a client asking for `DateStyle` was told nothing at all — that is why row 3.3's forwarded half was `awaiting`.
- **(d)** Row 3.3 and claim `3.1:application_name#session-audit` cited and promoted; the parent row follows by derivation, not by hand.

**Order is load-bearing and asserted.** A later `ParameterStatus` is the one a client keeps, so appending the overrides *after* the forwarded set is what makes them win for the same names. Filtering the set would have been the other way to do it, and is not what this does.

The `application_name` echo now comes from what the **engine accepted** rather than being re-read from the startup params, so it cannot disagree with what the session records and audits under.

## A fake that was modelling the engine wrong

`fakeAuth` ignored the request and returned a canned result, so the echo went empty and the 256-byte-truncation cell failed. The engine populates `ApplicationName` on the result (`core/exec/wire_session.go:281`) and on the session (`:245`) — so production was correct and the fake was not. Worse, it would have let a change that really *did* drop the label pass, since the echo would have been empty either way. It now round-trips the label as the engine does.

## Evidence

- The client's received set is proven equal to an **independent connection's** `SHOW` output, not to a list written in the cell — which would encode this build's parameters and pass while the relay forwarded something else.
- The overrides are proven to win over the target's own values.
- The accepted label is proven to reach the **engine**, not only the wire: an echo synthesized here would satisfy a wire-only cell while every audit row said `app ""`. The engine's half is #58's own `TestWireOpen_ApplicationNameIsOnTheSessionAndEveryAuditLine`.

Mutations: dropping the forwarding, and reversing the order, each redden their cell.

Gate: 31 covered, 0 uncited, 18 awaiting; claims 15/1. VM43: `go vet`, `GOARCH=386` build, full `-race` suite green across 9 packages.

Not in scope: the matrix criterion row and canary-set witness (blocked on #57, which owns `backendCanaries()`), and lector's non-blocking `runSession` `br`/peek comment, which goes with them.

author: mrizzi
body:
## Summary

Adds a CI job that automatically runs the Python test suite, and updates `CONVENTIONS.md` so the tests are documented and enforced — no more relying on contributor discipline.

The repo ships executable Python under `plugins/sdlc-workflow/scripts/` with a 95-test `pytest` suite, but nothing ran it in CI and `CONVENTIONS.md` still said "no runtime code" / "no unit test framework".

## Changes

- **New CI workflow `.github/workflows/python-tests.yml`** — installs `pytest` + `jsonschema` and runs `python3 -m pytest plugins/sdlc-workflow/scripts/ -q` on pushes and PRs to `main`, matching the trigger convention of the existing `skillsaw` / `validate-plugins` workflows.
- **`CONVENTIONS.md`** (docs):
  - Language and Framework / File Organization / Error Handling acknowledge the Python + shell helpers under `plugins/sdlc-workflow/scripts/` and their `test_*.py` suite.
  - Testing Conventions documents the pytest suite as a mandatory pre-commit/pre-merge gate.
  - CI Checks adds the pytest command to the pre-push list and a dedicated Python Unit Tests subsection referencing the new workflow.
  - Test-coverage wording corrected to name the covered core modules (`execute-actions.py`, `jira-client.py`, `pre_verify_pr.py`) and note that `strip_extra_properties.py` and the shell helpers are not yet unit-tested; the Dependencies section no longer claims the repo "contains only documentation and configuration files" (**TC-5974**).

## Verification

- `python3 -m pytest plugins/sdlc-workflow/scripts/ -q` → **95 passed**
- `claude plugin validate plugins/sdlc-workflow` → **passed**
- `uvx skillsaw` → **0 errors** (7 pre-existing warnings, none from this change)

> Note: like the other workflows in this repo, `python-tests.yml` triggers on `main` (push + PR), so it activates once this feature branch lands on `main`; it does not run on this feature-branch-based PR.

Jira: TC-5973 (relates to TC-5811); follow-up **TC-5974** corrects the CONVENTIONS.md coverage/dependency wording. Surfaced as a non-blocking advisory during verify-pr of PR #281.

author: d-morrison
body:
Closes #810.

A second assembly into a `NEWS.md` whose development block already held
category sections prepended another full set of headings under the top-level
heading, leaving duplicate sibling sections that a consumer's MD024 gate
rejects, plus an MD012 double blank at the seam (ucdavis/bcs#862).

## What changes

`assemble-news.sh` now pre-scans the first top-level section only, splices
new bullets under a heading already present there ahead of its existing
bullets and as one tight list with them, emits only the absent headings as a
fresh block, and separates spliced text from a following heading or
paragraph by exactly one blank line.
An older release block carrying the same heading is not a target; a `# `
line inside a fenced code block is not a heading in either pass; the
heading-to-bullets map crosses into awk as line pairs, so any single-line
heading survives; one `trap ... EXIT` removes every temp path.

## Tests

Tests 27 through 34: repeat merge (with the older release block diffed
before and after, and a tight-list adjacency check), older-release heading
untouched, tight layout keeps every bullet, tab-bearing heading, whitespace-
only line at each seam, empty fragment, fenced comment not a heading.
Confirmed red by mutation: the first-section bound, the `getline` seam,
the merge branch, the pair of awk-side release guards, both whitespace
seams, the merge-branch probe, and fence tracking.
Suite passes under BSD awk and mawk.

author: cinamoncandy
risingtides-dev
body:
## What a person can do that they could not before

Sign in at `ocean.agentsworld.org` and reach **whichever of their own machines they mean**, instead of the one machine their roster entry was pinned to. This PR is the proxy half: roster schema, per-session device selection, routing, ops. The picker UI lands on top of it in a follow-up PR (`cloud/surface-device-profiles-ui`).

## The premise, re-derived at `4ab7a71`

The proxy already had a multi-user roster — `ProxyUser` (`main.rs:215`), `users_file_path` (`:283`, `~/.config/ocean-surface/users.json`, 0600 enforced), `load_users` (`:293`), each `UserFileEntry` carrying `username`, `password`, an optional `daemon_url` falling back to `OCEAN_DAEMON_URL`, an optional `observer_token_path` and `operator_key_path`. So a **login decided whose Ocean you saw, but never which**: one profile, one daemon, and the operator's mini as everyone's default. The auth gate resolved one `ResolvedDaemon(String)` per request and every proxied `/v1` handler read it off the request extension — which turned out to be the whole leverage point.

## Schema

A user entry may now carry `devices`:

```json
{ "username": "…", "password": "…", "devices": [
  { "name": "mac mini", "daemon_url": "http://100.119.217.76:4780",
    "observer_token_path": "…", "operator_key_path": "…", "default": true },
  { "name": "studio", "daemon_url": "http://100.64.0.12:4780" }
]}
```

Validated on load: unique non-empty names without control characters, absolute `http(s)` URLs with a host, at most one `default` (roster order elects one when nobody marks it). The legacy single `daemon_url` still loads and normalizes into **one device named after its host**, so every existing deployment keeps working byte-for-byte. Setting both `daemon_url` and `devices` on one entry is refused rather than merged — guessing which machine somebody's turns execute on is not a thing to ship. A world-readable roster is still refused at startup.

`operator_key_path` is per-device alongside `observer_token_path` for the same reason the observer token is: without it, Room-authority mutations against a non-default device would fail closed and silently lose a capability that exists today.

## Selection, and why it is server-side

- `GET /api/devices` → `{ devices: [{ name, default, selected, health }], selected, selection_explicit }`. Health is probed live per device (`GET {daemon}/health`, 3s client, all devices concurrently so a roster of sleeping laptops costs one timeout): `ok` with `version`/`rev`, `unhealthy`, or `unreachable`. `selection_explicit` is false until somebody actually picks — that is what lets the surface offer the picker **once after a login** instead of nagging on every load, without any browser-side flag.
- `POST /api/devices/select {name}` → records the choice against a **SHA-256 digest of the session token** in a 0600 `device-selections.json`, written atomically (temp file in the same dir, then rename). Never in the cookie: a browser cannot re-point its own traffic, and the one piece of device state on disk is not a place bearer material accumulates. Since a session token is derived from one person's credentials, the map holds at most one row per roster user and cannot grow without bound.
- Neither payload contains a `daemon_url`. The browser addresses a machine **by name only**, so nobody types a URL and no page — one that renders untrusted model output — learns the operator's tailnet addresses.
- Both routes are login-gated like every other `/api/` route.

## Routing

`ResolvedDaemon` grew from a newtype into `{ device, url, observer_token_path, operator_key_path }`, and the auth gate resolves the session's **selected** device into it. Every proxied route — buffered JSON, the SSE tails (`/v1/agent/events`, `/v1/events`, room events, observatory events), and the voice relay — already read that one extension, so they all moved together; a switch cannot leave a transcript streaming from the machine you just left.

The credential now travels **with** the upstream it belongs to, so the two cannot drift apart. The custody rule is unchanged and now per-device: the process-wide observer token and operator key apply only to the device that is in fact the process default daemon; a machine naming no credential of its own gets none and the route fails closed.

**Typed failure.** A forward that cannot reach its machine, and a selection naming a device the roster no longer has, both answer one shape:

```json
503 {"ok":false,"error":"device_unavailable","reason":"unreachable"|"unknown_device","device":"studio"}
```

This replaces the opaque `502 daemon unreachable` on the proxied routes. `/api/config` and `/api/devices` deliberately keep answering under a stale selection — otherwise a removed device would be a locked door.

## Checks that pin it

`cargo test -p ocean-surface-proxy`: **78 passed, 0 failed** (was 64).

- **Schema** — legacy `daemon_url` → one host-named device; an entry with neither inherits the process default; a `devices` list keeps roster order with one default elected; five validation failures (both shapes at once, duplicate names, two defaults, empty name, non-http URL) each refused with an error naming the reason. Plus unit tests for `device_name_from_url` (port, path, IPv6 literal, userinfo) and `validate_daemon_url`.
- **Persistence** — a recorded selection survives a fresh `DeviceSelections::load` off the same file (a simulated restart), the file is 0600, a later choice replaces the earlier one, the session token never appears in the file, and a group-readable selections file is ignored rather than trusted.
- **Routing** — two users × two devices × four stub daemons, driven through the *production* router: each lands on their own default; Eric selects `studio` and his buffered JSON (`/v1/permissions`), SSE tail (`/v1/agent/events`) and voice relay (`/api/stt`) all move to it; the other user does not move.
- **Typed 503** — a stale selection answers `unknown_device` while `/api/config` and `/api/devices` still return 200; an unreachable **named** device answers with its name and never its address (the old opacity test, strengthened).
- **Device list** — health `ok` with `version`/`rev` from a live stub and `unreachable` from a closed port; `selection_explicit` flips false → true across a select; an unknown name is a 404, not a silent no-op; no `http://` anywhere in the payload.
- **Source guard** — `every_daemon_route_resolves_its_upstream_through_one_resolver` scans the production half of `main.rs`: every handler registered on a `/v1/` route must take its upstream from the request's resolved device, and nothing outside the resolver may read `state.daemon_url`. Both arms mutation-checked for real (a handler rewritten to build its URL from the process default reds the first; a stray `state.daemon_url` read inside `proxy_turns` reds the second), tree restored after each.

## Ops

`ops/README.md` gains the device recipe and states the boundary plainly: **the daemon has no auth of its own**, so binding it to a machine's tailnet address (`OCEAN_BIND=100.64.0.12:4780`, never `0.0.0.0`) trades loopback trust for the tailnet ACL — and that ACL is then the entire fence. This is one person reaching **their own** daemons; cross-person rooms still federate through Bedrock and no daemon accepts another person's connection (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-10-ocean-federated-rooms-design.md`).

`ops/add-device.sh` appends a device to a user's entry atomically with 0600 preserved, folds a legacy `daemon_url` into an explicit device on the way, refuses a duplicate name, and **refuses a non-tailnet `daemon_url`** (not `100.64/10`, `*.ts.net`, or loopback) unless `--allow-public` is passed in as many words. Exercised by hand across all of those paths.

`README.md` documents the two new `/api` routes next to `/api/config`, which is where `/api/config` is documented today.

## Gates

All seven frozen gates run on this exact tree:

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|

author: knockoutez
body:
Closes #148.

## What changed

The daemon's binding of the REST `events` port bound a replay page in **rows only** — a plain
`LIMIT ?`, every row `JSON.parse`d, synchronously, on the daemon's own event loop. At the route's
default page of 500 rows against payloads near `MAX_EVENT_PAYLOAD_CHARS` (64k) that is a ~32 MB read
in one uninterruptible block with the loop closed to every other request, and
`WIGOLO_STUDIO_RUN_REPLAY_PAGE` had no ceiling, so an operator could make that block the whole log.
The route already computed the same ~32 MB figure and used it to bound the socket **write**
(`DEFAULT_SSE_FLUSH_BYTES`) while the read that produced those bytes was bounded by nothing.

The broker sibling already had both clamps, with the argument written down ("a count alone bounds the
wrong thing") and the character bound measured with `LENGTH()` so the page is sized **before** it is
materialized. That argument applies verbatim to the daemon binding, which never got the clamp.

- `MAX_EVENTS_PAGE`, `MAX_EVENTS_PAGE_CHARS`, the envelope-character constant, the measure SQL and
  `pageRowsWithinChars` move to `src/studio/run-store.ts` as **`eventsSinceBounded`**, with the unit
  and value of each bound stated in its docstring. Both owners of the store now call it — one
  definition, both bindings. The broker re-exports both constants under their existing names and keeps
  its own positive-limit throw; its behaviour is unchanged and its 33 rows are green untouched.
- `replayPageSize()` is clamped to `MAX_EVENTS_PAGE`, so the env knob can no longer buy an ask the
  store will always cut.

The contract that makes this compatible is preserved and asserted: a **short** page is not end-of-log,
so every paged reader stops on an **EMPTY** page. New rows drive a replay whose pages split on the
character bound and assert no event is lost and no reader terminates early.

## Demo — one replay page, old tip vs fixed tip

Log of 1200 `decision.requested` events × 63,800-char prompts (the realistic producer: `pendingCardOf`
reads `prompt` uncapped below 64 KB). One page asked for 500 rows — the route's default.

```
OLD  eventsSince (rows only)       rows= 500  chars= 31915988 (31.92 MB)  loop blocked=22.5 ms
NEW  eventsSinceBounded            rows=  64  chars=  4029500 ( 4.03 MB)  loop blocked=14.8 ms

env knob WIGOLO_STUDIO_RUN_REPLAY_PAGE=1000000 (no ceiling before this issue):
OLD  eventsSince                   rows=1201  chars= 76752350 (76.75 MB)  loop blocked=50.4 ms
NEW  eventsSinceBounded            rows=  64  chars=  4029500 ( 4.03 MB)  loop blocked=28.9 ms

NEW  full drain: 20 pages, 1201 events recovered of 1201 in the log
     (first page 64 rows, reader stops on the EMPTY page)
```

## Tests, shown able to fail

`tests/unit/daemon/rest-runs-store-page-bounds.test.ts` — 6 rows against a **real** SQLite handle
through `sqliteRunsStore`, because the defect was that the port's two bindings disagreed and no
fixture store can show that: a fake honours whatever limit it is handed, which is exactly what the
daemon binding wrongly did.

Both mutations were run and restored:

- Lifting the store clamp (binding `eventsSince` directly again) → **4 red**, including
  `one page now exceeds the budget ...: expected 12081018 to be less than or equal to 4064000`. The
  row assertion beside it stays green at that size, which is the finding restated: a row count cannot
  see this.
- Lifting the `replayPageSize()` ceiling → **1 red**: `expected 2000000 to be less than or equal to 2000`.

## Verification

```
npm test              1006 files passed | 5 skipped   12793 passed | 20 skipped | 7 todo   341s
npx tsc --noEmit      exit 0
npm run gate:studio   exit 0  (no-electron, lint, typecheck:studio, typecheck-gate,
                               typecheck:debt held at baseline 363, typecheck:contract)
```

CI deferred — quota.

## Non-goals held

No SSE write-path change, no pagination-protocol change, same route shape and cursor semantics. The
one judgement call — moving the constants into `run-store.ts` and having the broker import them,
against the issue's "no broker-side changes" non-goal but as its acceptance criteria asked — is
recorded with its reversal condition as `A-148-1` in `DECISIONS-AUTO.md`.

author: daveboyd777
body:
## Summary
Exposes the stats module's results through a stable, versioned JSON schema (`freecell stats --json`), per ROADMAP.md's two-track visualization architecture: this is the hinge point in-app charts (issue #14) and the web dashboard (issue #20) will consume. All computation stays in Rust; a consumer of this output only ever renders it.

## Changes
- `src/stats.rs`: `Stats::history()` (the complete, unfiltered history), and a new `StatsExport` + `StreakExport` + `STATS_EXPORT_VERSION` (currently `1`) -- deliberately a **separate type** from `Stats`'s own `Serialize`/`Deserialize` impl. That internal format (used by `Stats::save`/`load` for on-disk persistence, issue #11) is free to evolve alongside the app itself, since only this app ever reads it back; `StatsExport` is the external contract, versioned so a future breaking change is explicit rather than silently changing what renderers see. `StreakExport` is internally tagged (`{"type": "winning", "length": 3}`) so the JSON reads naturally for a JS consumer.
- `src/main.rs`: `freecell stats --json` prints `StatsExport::from_stats(..).to_json()` and exits, alongside the existing plain-text `freecell stats`.

## Scope boundary worth flagging
Deliberately scoped to exactly what the `stats` module itself computes. Solver-derived per-game grading (issue #13's `analysis::grade`, e.g. "solver's best line was 52") is **not** included -- computing it for an entire history would mean re-running the solver once per historical game on every export, a materially different and potentially very slow feature, left to its own issue if wanted. Also CLI-only, matching the issue's/roadmap's explicit `freecell stats --json` naming -- no TUI/GUI raw-JSON UI, since that's inherently a scripting/pipe use case.

## Tests
`tests/stats_export_tests.rs` -- schema snapshot tests comparing the **full `serde_json::Value` shape** (not just individual fields) for an empty history and a populated one covering both streak directions, pinning down field names, types, and the version number so any accidental drift fails loudly. Plus a JSON round-trip test.

## Validation
- `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean).
- `cargo test --workspace` -- 136/136 passing.
- Confirmed `freecell-gui` still builds for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- Manually smoke-tested the real CLI binary: `stats --json` on an empty history, then again after recording a real loss, confirming correct JSON output both times.

Closes #19.

#159 removed the `execute` input on the wrong belief that pr-monitor v1 defaults execution on. The v1 `action.yml` declares `execute` with default `'false'`; the retired `owner/repo:job` spelling that #159 deleted was an accepted alias for `true`. So the removal turned execution off, and src-touching PRs lost dynamic-matrix resolution — #160's gate went red with 12 unresolvable "(dynamic matrix)" names (run 33624942065). This restores the pre-#159 behavior in the current boolean spelling.

Note: this PR only touches workflow YAML, so its own gate run may not exercise execution (paths filters keep src jobs out of the predicted set). That is expected; #160 or the next src-touching PR is where the fix shows.

author: loganathan-sekaran
body:
## Problem

Every request from `mosip-abis-client` (biochq-abis, our ABIS partner client) to datashare's `/get/{policyId}/{subscriberId}/{randomShareKey}` endpoint fails with:

```json
{"errorCode":"KER-ATH-401","message":"Authentication Failed"}
```

even with a correctly issued, valid internal token (issuer `.../auth/realms/mosip`, client `mosip-abis-client`) and correct roles.

## Root cause

`data-share-default.properties`'s `auth.server.admin.allowed.audience` is a hard client-ID allowlist gating datashare access. This fork's copy is missing `mosip-abis-client`:

```
# this repo (before fix):
auth.server.admin.allowed.audience=mosip-partner-client,...,mosip-pms-client

# MOSIP's own upstream default (mosip/mosip-config):
auth.server.admin.allowed.audience=mosip-partner-client,...,mosip-pms-client,mosip-abis-client
```

`mosip-abis-client` is present in MOSIP's own reference config (it's the standard ABIS-partner client, e.g. used by `mosip/mosip-mock-services`'s mock ABIS) — it was simply dropped from this fork at some point. No token, role, or deployment fix on the ABIS side can work around a client ID that isn't on this allowlist at all.

## Fix

One-line addition: append `mosip-abis-client` to `auth.server.admin.allowed.audience`, restoring parity with MOSIP's upstream default.

## Found while

Validating [ooru-digital/biochq-abis#292](https://github.com/ooru-digital/biochq-abis/pull/292) (a separate STOMP ClassCastException fix) against two real STP registrations (`10001100020000320260901115814`, `10001100020000420260901121316`), both stuck failing with "unable to fetch biometric details (using referenceURL)" at the `BIOGRAPHIC_VERIFICATION` stage.

Refs [ooru-digital/biochq-abis#283](https://github.com/ooru-digital/biochq-abis/issues/283), [ooru-digital/biochq-abis#285](https://github.com/ooru-digital/biochq-abis/issues/285)

author: ryouku
body:
Fixes the false alarm `blinkinglight` found in review of #171, **after** that PR had merged. One field, one stat, one message.

## The defect, reproduced before fixing

`registeredHookEvents` keys its map by `filepath.Base(path)` — right for matching a registration against scripts found by scanning the config dir. `uninstalledRegistrations` then asked whether `dir/<base>` existed.

So a hook installed in a **second config directory** and registered by its real absolute path — what `--config-dir` produces, and what any operator running more than one config has — looked identical to a registration with nothing behind it:

```
registered by absolute path in 002; file really exists: YES

  agentsmemory-recall-hook.sh  SessionStart  NOT-INSTALLED
    registered in 001 but no such file — the agent runs nothing for this event
exit=1
```

The agent runs it perfectly well. And the message is not merely noisy, it is **false**.

## Why the exit code makes this worse than noise

`doctor` exits **non-zero** on this one — deliberately, and I argued for that in #171: nothing registers a file it means to be absent. But a check that fails a red build on a healthy machine is exactly how a check earns being switched off, which is the reasoning `staleHooksIn`'s own comment already records about the absent-file case. The asymmetry I defended is only sound if the check is right.

## The fix

`hookRegistration` keeps the command's path whole; the absence check stats **that**; the report names it. First registration wins, for the same reason `env` does — a script registered twice with different paths is a hand edit this command must not silently average away.

The message now sends the operator where the registration points:

```
NOT-INSTALLED  registered as /…/002/agentsmemory-recall-hook.sh but no such file
```

## Verification

Both directions, live against the reproducer:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| hook in a second dir, present | `NOT-INSTALLED`, exit 1 | silent, **exit 0** |
| registration naming a file that exists nowhere | caught | **still caught**, exit 1, names the real path |

Two mutations, both caught by the new test:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| revert to stat'ing `dir/<base>` (the defect) | **red** |
| stop recording the path at all | **red** |

⚠ The first mutation initially appeared to *survive* — my `perl` assumed one tab of indentation where the block has two, so the edit silently did nothing. Verified `grep -c MUTANT` before believing the result, which is the only reason it was caught. Same trap this repo already records; it does not stop being easy.

`go test ./...` exit 0, 44 packages. `go vet` clean, `gofmt` clean.

author: lian662ryt5
body:
## Summary

You asked me to test every feature and take my time finding real problems, rather than re-confirming what was already known to work. I did a full pass: read through the remaining untouched source files with an eye for authorization/escaping bugs, drove the whole app end-to-end through every tab with a rich seeded dataset while capturing console/page errors, and cross-checked client-side assumptions against the actual live Supabase RLS policies. Found and fixed three real issues:

- **Restroom delete button shown to non-owners.** Every restroom card rendered a delete (`×`) button regardless of who saved it. The database's own RLS policy only allows the owner or an admin to actually delete a spot (`auth.uid() = user_id OR is_admin()`) — a click from anyone else would silently no-op server-side (no error) while the client optimistically removed it from the local list, making it look deleted until the next reload brought it back. Fixed the button to track that same rule.

- **Stored XSS via unescaped image URLs (5 places).** `food_image`, `restrooms.photo`, and `profiles.avatar_url` were all interpolated into ``'<img src="${value}">'`` with no escaping. The most serious: `food_image` comes straight from OpenFoodFacts, a public database anyone can edit — a poisoned barcode entry could plant a payload that executes in the browser of any user who scans it, with access to that user's live session. `restrooms.photo` is exploitable via a direct Supabase REST call bypassing the UI (RLS only checks ownership, not the field's shape) and would then run in *every* viewer's browser, since restrooms are a shared public table. All five spots now go through the app's existing `escapeHtml()` helper.

- **Test-coverage gap: hidden-restroom visibility was never actually tested.** The "hide a flagged spot from the public list" behavior is enforced entirely by server-side RLS — the client never filters it client-side. The fake Supabase test fixture didn't simulate that policy at all, so nothing in the suite would have caught a regression that started showing hidden/flagged spots to everyone. Added the simulation plus a regression test.

## Verification discipline

For each of the fixes above, I wrote the regression test first against the *old* code (via `git stash`) to confirm it genuinely fails, then restored the fix and confirmed it passes — not just written to look plausible. This PR adds comprehensive logging to the project

### LogRite coverage

_Two tables, two units. The app's "Log Coverage" figure counts **log statements** against the opportunities the analyzer found; the file table below counts **files**. They differ by construction and neither is wrong._

**Files.** A file counts once here, whether it gained one log or forty.

| Language | In repo | Cannot hold a log | Eligible | Instrumented | Coverage | Nothing to log | Recommended, none placed | Reverted by gate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| C# | 40 | 0 | 40 | 15 of 40 | 37.5% | 21 | 4 | 0 |
| **Total** | **40** | **0** | **40** | **15 of 40** | **37.5%** | **21** | **4** | **0** |

_Why those 21 file(s) had nothing to log:_ **NO_LOGS_GENERATED** 13, **NO_METHODS_FOUND** 7, **NO_RULE_MATCHED** 1.

_Of the **19** eligible file(s) the analyzer found something to log in, **15** gained a log — **78.9%**. The Coverage column counts every eligible file, including the 21 with nothing to instrument._

**Log statements.** What the analyzer asked for, and what the diff contains.

| Language | Recommended | Placed | Not placed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| C# | 107 | 86 | 21 |
| **Total** | **107** | **86** | **21** |

_**Recommended** already excludes statements recommended more than once for the same file: only one copy can be placed, so a duplicate is not an opportunity and is not counted as one._

> **21 recommended log(s) were not placed** (C#). Where they were lost, by stage:
> - **17** skipped before the write with no guard claiming it — the placement walk never visited the line. If this number is large it is the one worth reporting: nothing turned these statements down
> - **2** the key was reserved for another handler — an exit log deferred to the method's return site, or a statement drained by the consecutive-key chain. Expected, and a loss only if that handler had no room either
> - **2** the scope guard refused the position — a variable the statement reads is not in scope there yet, so placing it would not compile
> Files reverted by a syntax gate are counted separately, in the last column.

author: yi-luo-hua
body:
Runs the forensic comparison the evaluation in #30 left open, and the answer changes that document's conclusions.

## Method

Downloaded both released installers and listed their packaged contents with `7z l -slt`, excluding NSIS's own `$PLUGINSDIR` and absolute-path entries.

| Installer | Size | SHA-256 | App files |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BilibiliCrawler-Setup-3.3.0-x64.exe` | 53,600,679 | `6d59a130…f58f802` | 1299 |
| `BilibiliCrawler-Setup-3.4.0-x64.exe` | 53,480,344 | `60202e26…78d715` | 1297 |

The 3.4.0 hash matches the release record, confirming provenance.

## Result: residue is real

Three paths are in v3.3.0 and not in v3.4.0, so an in-place upgrade strands them:

```
resources\backend\sidecar\_internal\api-ms-win-core-fibers-l1-1-1.dll
resources\backend\sidecar\_internal\api-ms-win-core-kernel32-legacy-l1-1-1.dll
resources\backend\sidecar\_internal\api-ms-win-core-sysinfo-l1-2-0.dll
```

One path is new in v3.4.0 — `bilibili_crawler\resources\stopwords.txt`, the packaged word list from batch F. Expected.

## The root cause matters more than the three files

Nothing *declared* changed between the two releases: `requirements-desktop.lock` is identical and `pyinstaller==6.17.0` is unchanged.

These are Windows API-set forwarder DLLs, and whether PyInstaller collects them depends on the build machine's UCRT/SDK state. v3.3.0 was built in the existing environment; v3.4.0 was built in a freshly created CPython 3.13.15 venv. Corroborating evidence: the local `resources/backend` worktree still contains all three, while the shipped 3.4.0 does not.

**Build-environment variance alone is enough to strand files, and it appears in no lockfile.** That invalidates two things the document previously said:

- the "lock unchanged, so the packaged set did not shrink" inference — disproved by the project's own artifacts;
- the plan to wait for a *declared* trigger, which cannot detect this class at all.

## What changes

- Section 3 is rewritten from "not demonstrated" to the measured result, with method, hashes, the diff, and the root cause.
- **A′ moves from trigger-gated to scheduled** for the next time the installer or release flow is touched. Its two unresolved design problems are unchanged and still block implementation.
- **New P3: keep the payload manifest as a release asset** and diff the next build against it. Given the root cause, this is the only detection that actually works — and it turns "found by unpacking installers afterwards" into a release gate.
- The three stranded files are deliberately left alone: severity is low and A′ will clear them on those users' next upgrade. Pushing a dedicated cleanup would need the same safety work first.

## Severity, stated honestly

Low but not asserted to be zero. API-set forwarders are normally resolved through the apiset schema rather than a file on disk, but the application directory does precede the system directory in DLL search order, so this remains in the shadowing risk class. No failure reports are attributed to it. Users who did a clean reinstall — including this machine — are unaffected.

## Validation

Documentation only. `git diff --check` passed.

author: dlipicar
body:
Follows [logos-protocol#79](https://github.com/logos-co/logos-protocol/pull/79), which revises 0.9 to key subscription continuity by **target module**: losing a provider takes every subscription to it down at once, so the status callback is installed on the client rather than on each subscribe.

The hub followed the old shape, installing a watcher per `(module, event)`. Under the revised protocol that delivers **N copies of one loss** and terminates the same client subscriptions N times over. `ensureLossWatcher()` now installs it once per module, and `notifyModuleLost()` fans out to every event of that module — which is what the runtime was reporting all along.

`Held` and `Abandoned` are treated as losses too. `Held` cannot occur here (the bridge never sets a manual policy), but it means the same thing to a downstream client, and a silent fall-through would resume a stream with a hole in it — exactly what `rpc.subscription_terminated` exists to prevent.

The README's "requires logos-protocol ≥ 0.9" claim is unchanged and still accurate; only the symbol named in the rationale moved.

## Verification

**49/49** unit tests pass against the revised protocol (built locally with `--override-input logos-module-builder/logos-protocol`, since #79 is not merged yet).

> Depends on logos-protocol#79. CI here will stay red until that lands and this relocks.

author: osterman
body:
## what

- Adds a **Remediation Targets** section to the organization security policy: Critical 7 days (72 hours where reachable with an upstream fix available), High 30 days, Medium 90 days, Low next regular release.
- Targets are measured from confirmation rather than from the report date.
- Scoped with the sentence "These targets apply to Cloud Posse's actively maintained software products, including the Atmos CLI."

## why

- These targets were approved internally but have never been published, so an assessor reading <https://github.com/cloudposse/atmos/security/policy> sees a disclosure process with no remediation commitment. A published SLA is expected evidence in supply-chain assessments and for Iron Bank.
- This file is the organization-level default, inherited by every Cloud Posse repository. A repository-local `SECURITY.md` would override the whole file for that repo, which means maintaining two nearly identical copies — so the targets go here instead, with an explicit scoping sentence so they do not read as a commitment across dormant module repositories.

Reviewers: the scoping sentence is the part worth arguing about. "Actively maintained software products" is deliberately narrower than "every repository in this organization." If we would rather commit organization-wide, drop that qualifier.

## references

- Raised during the Atmos supply-chain security assessment.
- Related: `cloudposse/atmos` PR adding `docs/SSDLC.md`, whose Section 8 cites these same targets.

body:
全站手機優先的**第 0 期：不動任何頁面**，只鋪地基。計畫全文見〈全站手機優先遷移〉。

## 為什麼需要這一支

專案的 `respond-to` mixin 是 **`max-width`** —— 整個 codebase 以桌機為基準往小螢幕覆寫，**40 支 SCSS** 這樣寫。所以「改成手機優先」不是補斷點，是**翻轉方向**。

現況（掃出來的，不是估的）：

| 角色 | SCSS | 有斷點 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| teacher | 4 | **0** |
| parent | 10 | **0** |
| admin | 77 | 34 |

最該用手機的兩個角色，響應式覆蓋是零。

## 1 · `respond-from`（min-width），與 `respond-to` 並存

既有 40 支**不動** —— 它們不是錯的，只是方向舊。並存讓遷移逐頁進行，不必一次改完（那會是一支動 40 檔的 PR，沒有人 review 得動）。

`+ 0.02px` 不是講究，是**避免重疊**：`respond-to('mobile')` 是 `max-width: 640px`，若這裡寫 `min-width: 640px`，在正好 640px 的裝置上兩個區塊同時生效，哪個贏取決於原始碼順序 —— 那是只會在真機上發現的 bug。

## 2 · 觸控目標尺寸

**實測**（在 demo 上用 `getComputedStyle`，不是查文件）：

| 元素 | 實際 | 門檻 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 小按鈕 | **34px** | 44 |
| icon-only 小按鈕 | **36×36** | 44 |
| 一般按鈕 | 41px | 44 |

而 `styles.scss` **從來沒有設過 button 尺寸 token** —— 所以那 129 處 `size="small"` **不是 129 個問題，是 1 個**。

**用 `@media (pointer: coarse)` 而不是視窗寬度**：要問的是「這東西被什麼操作」，不是「視窗多寬」。桌機開窄視窗不需要 44px；平板再寬也需要。**桌機完全不受影響 —— 手機優先不等於桌機劣化。**

每一個變數都在活的頁面上確認存在過。`--p-togglebutton-padding-y` 與 `--p-checkbox-*` **不存在，所以沒寫** —— 幽靈 token 不會有任何錯誤訊號，只會靜靜地什麼都不做。

順帶把 `.clessia-filter-bar` 那條 `min-height: 38px` 的硬底在觸控下抬到 44（它會蓋過 token）。

## 3 · harness ratchet

- **檔案第一次出現在清單裡 → 紅燈**（有人又寫了桌機優先）
- **檔案從清單消失 → 提醒更新基線**（遷移成果記下來）
- 持續印出剩餘進度：目前 **40 支 / 61 處**

沒有這道 ratchet，遷移會停在「大家都同意要做」然後永遠不動 —— 因為每一次「就這一次先照舊寫」都是局部理性的。

## 驗證

**gate 雙向都故意弄壞過**：新增桌機優先寫法 → 紅；把一支遷移完 → 提醒更新基線。

5 支新 harness 測試。其中一條特別說明：**「正則 lastIndex 漏報」那條也弄壞驗證過**。`g` flag 的正則有狀態，沿用同一個實例跑第二個檔案會從上次位置繼續找 —— 症狀是**間歇性漏報**，而漏報的 gate 看起來跟通過的一模一樣。

`npm test` **865 passed** ・ `npm run harness:test` **45 pass / 0 fail** ・ `npm run harness` 綠 ・ production build 綠

## 一個我犯的錯，記在這裡

`checkMobileFirst` 一開始被我插進 `checkUsageContrast` **內部**，而且落在它 write 模式的 early return 之後 —— 所以 `harness:write` 永遠跑不到它。症狀很怪：基線檔生不出來，但 check 模式照樣紅 40 支。

這是我第二次犯同一類錯（腳本插入落在錯的 scope）。

author: frisitano
body:
# Description

This PR refines the EIP-8025 spec with the following changes:
- Changes the `ProofData` type to be `ByteList` with a size limit
- Remove the max size checks on gossiped execution proofs as they are implied and enforced by the size limit of `ProofData` and the container types
- Remove the block root consistency check between the beacon block and the execution payload as this is already enforced by the execution payload handler outside the scope of eip-8025
- Remove the explicit check on the block state associated with the block root. If a payload exists for the block root then the beacon block must be valid
- Update tests to reflect these changes

author: arrrrny
body:
## Honest scope assessment

This PR addresses the bulk of the pre-existing CI failures on master that have been blocking every PR (including this one) for the past 12+ hours. After investigation, the full set of master CI failures is larger than these three buckets, but each remaining failure is a different shape of bug and warrants its own focused PR.

## What landed

### 1. Strip 99 comment-policy violations (fixes `lint`)

The `check-no-comments` policy bans all comments (JSDoc and line) in `packages/agent-core-v2`, `packages/kap-server`, and `packages/transcript` — a 12-hour regression from recent compaction/squeeze-model work that landed after the no-comments rule. Strip the violations mechanically (TypeScript AST, preserving `oxlint-disable` / `eslint-disable` directives).

- 99 violations → 0
- 41 files changed
- Mechanical strip; no logic change

### 2. Fix TS4111 bracket-notation (fixes `typecheck`)

`packages/oauth/test/free-models-only.integration.test.ts` accessed `process.env.OPENROUTER_API_KEY` etc. via dot notation, which TypeScript's `noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature` rejects. Switch to bracket notation on all 4 sites. The file is integration-only (skipped without API keys), but the typecheck error blocked CI for the whole monorepo.

- 4 errors → 0

### 3. Fix OpenAI plain-object 429 conversion (fixes 2 of 22 failures in `test (1/5)`)

The 429 wire-behavior tests in `packages/agent-core-v2/test/kosong/provider/composition.test.ts` expected `APIProviderRateLimitError` from the `openai` and `openai_responses` providers, but got a generic `ChatProviderError`.

Root cause: `openai-legacy.ts` and `openai-responses.ts` throw `convertOpenAIError({ status, message: JSON.stringify(errorData) }, hook)` with a plain object (not an `OpenAIAPIError` instance), and the converter had no fallback for plain objects with a numeric `status` field. Add a fallback that routes through `normalizeAPIStatusError` (which already maps 429 → `APIProviderRateLimitError`), and forward the response headers so `parseRetryAfterMs` can extract the `Retry-After` value.

- 2 'openai' and 'openai_responses' 429 tests fixed.
- 20 other failures in `composition.test.ts` are pre-existing on master and out of scope.

## What's still failing on master (out of scope for this PR)

The remaining failures each warrant a separate, focused PR with proper investigation:

- 20 failures in `agent-core-v2/test/kosong/provider/composition.test.ts` covering `process.env` shadowing, thinking-part detection, and encoding pipelines — all pre-existing on master.
- 17 failures in other `agent-core-v2` test files (full-compaction, profile, services) — pre-existing on master.
- A `FullCompaction` snapshot drift and a v1↔v2 parity test failure.
- An e2e `invalid-input-matrix` timeout (likely network/timeout-related).

## Files

- 41 files in `packages/agent-core-v2/{src,test}`, `packages/kap-server/test`, `packages/transcript` — comment stripping
- `packages/agent-core-v2/src/kosong/provider/bases/openai/openai-common.ts` — plain-object fallback in `convertOpenAIError`
- `packages/agent-core-v2/src/kosong/provider/bases/openai/openai-legacy.ts` — pass `headers` through to converter
- `packages/agent-core-v2/src/kosong/provider/bases/openai/openai-responses.ts` — pass `headers` through to converter
- `packages/oauth/test/free-models-only.integration.test.ts` — bracket-notation for `process.env`

## Risk

The comment-strip change is mechanical and should have no behavioral effect. The plain-object fallback adds a new branch to `convertOpenAIError` that is only reached when an upstream error is shaped as `{ status: number, message: string, headers?: Headers }` — this is exactly the shape the OpenAI providers already throw, so the new branch replaces the previous fall-through-to-`ChatProviderError` behavior with a structured one.

## Recommendation

Merge this PR — it unblocks the rest of the queue (PR #45, PR #44, and any follow-up). The remaining pre-existing failures are tracked separately and not introduced by this change.

author: vicenteespinosa
body:
# 🔗 Relevant links

- 📋 Related to: <!-- No specific ticket -->

# 🏞️ Additional context

`DEPAS_AVAILABLE_BY` was the last requirement that pretended to be a preference. It
read as a deadline — `available_from IS NULL OR available_from <= ?` — so a flat that
freed up one day late was never announced, while one that freed up five months early
passed untouched and unscored.

Neither reading is what a move-in date means. What you want is the flat that frees up
*near* the date you are moving, which is a distance rather than a bound — and a
distance belongs in the grade, beside every other thing the pool is not consulted
about.

The two sides of that distance are not the same shape, though. Taking a flat before
you need it costs you the overlap and nothing else, so with the date two months out
every *entrega inmediata* on the market is still a flat worth being told about. Taking
it after leaves you nowhere to live.

# 💡 Solution

- **A twelfth graded component, `availability`.** The window between **today and your
  date** is one span: anything free inside it is `MET` or better, `MET` at the near end
  and `BEST` on the date itself. Past the date a **week** is a whole span of its own —
  there is no fallback on that side, you cannot move in later than the day you have to
  be out — so it falls to `MET` a week late, `BREACHED` two weeks late and 0 at three.
  With the date two months out:

  | entrega | score |
  | --- | --- |
  | already free (*entrega inmediata*) | 80 |
  | in two weeks | 85 |
  | in a month | 90 |
  | on the date | 100 |
  | a week late | 80 |
  | two weeks late | 40 |
  | three weeks late | 0 |

- **A date already reached is read as today**, not as however long ago the portal wrote
  it — the same *entrega inmediata* rule the cards already print.

- **The setting is renamed to match its slot**: `DEPAS_AVAILABLE_BY` →
  `DEPAS_AVAILABILITY_TARGET`, with `DEPAS_AVAILABILITY_WEIGHT` beside it. `BY` promised
  a bound; `TARGET` is the slot that only costs score. Migration 012 renames the row
  rather than re-seeding it, so whatever was set from the chat is what the new component
  scores against.

- **Silence is unanswered, not late.** Most portals publish no date at all, and a
  listing that stated none is left unscored on the component — which is already how the
  grade punishes silence: coverage shrinks the score toward 40 instead of a filter
  quietly waving the listing through.

- **Nothing filters on the date any more**: it is out of `ALERT_REQUIREMENTS` and out of
  `depas show`, whose `--available-by` flag was a `<=` on a value that no longer has a
  wrong side. The Telegram menu moves it from 🔍 Búsqueda to 🏠 Depto, where the other
  targets live.

author: innovadataco
body:
## Problema (brief A-72, Jelkin probando RPT-6DGNC5)
La protección de ráfaga marcaba `Reporte.esRafaga` contando **solo por el identificador reportado** (nick + plataforma). Resultado: **varias personas independientes reportando la misma cuenta se marcaban como ráfaga** y caían a `REVISION_MANUAL`. La corroboración múltiple es la señal BUENA — penalizarla es al revés.

## Arreglo
`detectarRafaga` ahora cuenta **por origen**: N reportes sobre el mismo identificador **desde el mismo origen** dentro de la ventana. Orígenes distintos sobre el mismo nick = corroboración, no ráfaga.

El origen ya se captura: `crearFuenteReporte` guarda `FuenteReporte.ipHash`/`fingerprintHash` (sal obligatoria, IP truncada /24, `x-forwarded-for`) en el POST de `/api/reportes` **antes de encolar**. **Sin migración** — la premisa del brief ("`Reporte` no guarda IP") apuntaba a la tabla equivocada; corregido con verificación en fuente (candado 15v5).

## Por qué se adaptó `detectarRafaga` y no se cambió el callsite a `detectarRafagaFuente`
`detectarRafagaFuente` usa otros parámetros (scoring, no `reportes.rafaga.*`), no aplica historial-previo, no marca el pico ni registra el paso del expediente → un swap sería regresión. Se reusa su **predicado de origen** (`ipHash`/`fingerprintHash`), conservando la semántica del pipeline.

## Alcance / coordinación
- Único callsite del `detectarRafaga` por nick: `reporte-processing/index.ts:107` (candado 22v5).
- `finalizacion.ts` solo recibe el booleano `esRafaga` — firma intacta → **sin colisión con A-71**.
- Sin modelo ni columna nueva. La query de la ventana pasa a `findMany`+`updateMany` por id (Prisma no filtra relación en `updateMany`).

## Pruebas
- `reporte-processing/rafagas.test.ts` (4): mismo origen → ráfaga y marca todos; orígenes distintos → NO ráfaga; sin origen → NO ráfaga; historial previo del mismo origen corta la ráfaga.
- `api/reportes/procesar/route.test.ts` (17): nuevo caso — 3 reportes del mismo nick, orígenes distintos → NO ráfaga (siguen a CLASIFICADO); los casos previos se sembraron con origen para ejercer el camino real.
- Puertas locales verdes: tsc, arch, tokens (1083), locks, ratchets, lint, specs-discipline.

body:
Ajoute une intégration continue GitHub Actions.

## Déclenchement
- **`pull_request`** vers `develop` et `main` → les tests tournent **avant** le merge ;
- **`push`** sur `develop` et `main` → couvre aussi les merges et pushs directs.

Une exécution obsolète est annulée automatiquement (`concurrency` + `cancel-in-progress`).

## Deux jobs parallèles
| Job | Contenu |
| --- | --- |
| **Tests** | PHP 8.3, cache Composer, `.env` + `key:generate`, puis `php artisan test` (502 tests) |
| **Front** | Node 20, `npm ci`, `npm run build` |

Aucun service de base de données n'est nécessaire : la suite tourne sur **SQLite en mémoire** (`phpunit.xml`).

## Un changement nécessaire côté tests
`app.blade.php` utilise `@vite` : sans build, toute réponse Inertia échouait sur « Vite manifest not found ». `tests/TestCase.php` appelle désormais **`withoutVite()`**.

Bénéfice au-delà de la CI : les tests ne dépendent plus d'un build local éventuellement **périmé**. Vérifié en supprimant `public/build` → **502 tests passent**.

## Point de dette signalé
`npm run types` n'est **pas** branché : le dépôt porte **11 erreurs TypeScript préexistantes** (dont `react-hook-form` et `@radix-ui/react-tabs` non installés, sur des composants visiblement inutilisés). L'inscrire rendrait la CI rouge dès le premier run. Le job est prêt à l'accueillir une fois la dette résorbée.

author: ajparsons
body:
## The problem

Schema generation and validation disagree about any column pandas stores as `object` dtype.

`build_table_schema` types columns from the dtype alone, so it describes every object column as `string`. Validation reads the file natively through frictionless and sees the real Python values. A column of lists or booleans is therefore **described as a string by this code and then rejected against that same description**:

```
Type error in the cell "[]" in row "158" and field "attachments" at position "26": type is "string/default"
```

`dataset validate` fails, and because `bump_version_to` validates before it will bump, `dataset version ... --publish` fails too — so the nightly build of any affected repository stops before publishing.

This was masked until `frictionless` 4 was replaced by 5 (`data-common` now requires `>=5`). The frictionless 4 reader handed back stringified cells, so everything matched `string`. Verified against an unchanged dataset: frictionless 4.40.3 reports 0 errors, frictionless 5.19.0 reports 1000 on the same parquet and the same schema.

## The fix

Type object columns from their contents:

- lists / tuples / sets / dicts / numpy arrays → `any`. Frictionless has no type that accepts a numpy array — both `array` and `object` reject one — so `any` is the only description that admits the data and validates.
- booleans → `boolean`
- no values → left as pandas described it

Three related fixes fall out of the same disagreement:

- **Do not claim uniqueness for a non-scalar column.** Validation records seen cells in a dict, so a numpy array raises `unhashable type: 'numpy.ndarray'` before any comparison happens. Latent crash for any unique-looking list column.
- **Do not build an enum for a column containing blanks.** The check stringified the column first, which renders a missing number as `"nan"` — never counted as blank — so the enum held a `nan`, which nothing can satisfy, because a `nan` does not equal itself.
- **Strip trailing whitespace from the generated YAML.** Wrapping a long value leaves a space before the line break, which every repository then carries in its resource files and trips `git diff --check`.

`dataset update-schema` now re-derives the schema even when the data is unchanged. It previously skipped that whenever the file hash matched, so a repository could not adopt a corrected schema without its data changing first — exactly the situation this fix leaves existing repositories in.

## Note for consuming repositories

Adopting this changes declared field types, which `derive_bump_rule_from_change` classifies as `MAJOR`. Repositories at `0.x` are unaffected (major is downgraded to minor below 1.0), but a repository at `1.x` using `--auto-ban major` will need a deliberate version decision on the first run. Only repositories with non-scalar or boolean columns are affected, and those are currently unable to validate at all.

## Testing

- New `tests/dataset/test_table_management.py` covers the typing, the round-trip validation of a generated schema, description preservation, the uniqueness constraint, and the blank/enum case.
- Full suite passes (41 tests including the consuming repo's).
- Verified end to end against `uk-parl-written-questions`, whose build this currently blocks: both packages go from `Invalid resource` to `No errors for package`, and `dataset version static --auto-ban major --all --dry-run` completes without a version change.

Das Prüfwerk aus v31.99 meldet Vorbehalte — und liess den Nutzer damit stehen. Den Knopf „Weiteres Foto hinzufügen" gab es seit v30.74, aber seine Bedingung war die **Selbsteinschätzung des Modells**:

```js
if ((r.next_photo_hint && conf < 85) || (conf > 0 && conf < 60))
```

Genau das falsche Signal. Meldet das Modell 94 % und die Prüfung findet zwei Widersprüche, stand dort nichts.

- Der Knopf hängt jetzt an `_pw.warn > 0` und steht **dort, wo das Urteil steht** — nicht weit unten auf der Karte.
- Die untere Karte bietet ihn dann nicht mehr an: zwei Knöpfe für dieselbe Handlung sind keine Auswahl.

## Und noch eine unlesbare Stelle

`contrast_check` misst im Scan-Fenster jetzt **46 statt 40** Stellen — der Prüfstand tut so, als läge ein erstes Foto vor, damit der neue Knopf überhaupt rendert. Prompt fiel etwas auf, das vorher **gar nicht messbar war**: die Prozentzahl neben einer Verwechslungsmöglichkeit, weiss auf `#ef5350` = **3,49:1 in beiden Modi**. Die drei Farben dort waren für Flächen ohne Text gedacht.

**Die Lehre:** ein Prüfstand misst nur, was wirklich gerendert wird. Wer eine Ansicht misst, muss sie auch in ihren Zuständen herstellen — sonst ist „0 Fehler" eine Aussage über zu wenig.

## Prüfstände

`scan_check` **19/19** — zwei Fälle mehr: Knopf bei Vorbehalten trotz 94 % Modell-Sicherheit · kein Knopf bei sauberem Fund · kein doppelter Knopf für dieselbe Handlung.

`contrast_check` 0/0 · `render_check` 0/0 · `planer_check` 22/22 · `save_check` 10/10 · `wiring_check` 43 Öffner / 0 kaputt · `touch_check` 0 · `data_check` 0/0.

author: ilyakuprov
body:
## What was wrong

In `kernel/plotting/plot_uf.m`,
`axis_f2=(-sweep_conv/2:res_conv:sweep_conv/2-1)+parameters.offset(2)`
subtracts the dimensioned literal `1` (i.e. 1 Hz) from the upper
endpoint of the colon range, instead of subtracting one `res_conv`
step as intended (mirroring how `axis_f1` is built a few lines below
using `0:(uf_dim_size-1)`).

## Why it matters physically

`res_conv=1/(2*Ta*parameters.nloops)` is commonly well below 1 Hz for
realistic ultrafast-NMR loop counts, so
`floor((sweep_conv-1)/res_conv)` undercounts the number of grid points
by exactly one relative to `floor(sweep_conv/res_conv)`. `axis_f2`
therefore comes out one element shorter than the spectrum's column
count for ordinary (not contrived) acquisition parameters, and
`contour(axis_f2,axis_f1,flipud(spectrum_uf))` fails with a dimension
mismatch. A user with a normal, sub-Hz-resolution ultrafast dataset
cannot plot it at all.

## Fix

Replaced the literal `1` with `res_conv`, so the axis endpoint is one
grid step below the half-sweep, matching the digital resolution.

## Stock probe output

```
Ta=0.01 sweep_conv=50 res_conv=0.5
buggy axis_f2 length=99, correct (sweep_conv/res_conv) length=100, ga_points_number(rows)=9
RESULT: error: The size of X must match the size of Z or the number of columns of Z.
```

## Patched probe output

```
Ta=0.01 sweep_conv=50 res_conv=0.5
buggy axis_f2 length=99, correct (sweep_conv/res_conv) length=100, ga_points_number(rows)=9
RESULT: plot_uf succeeded, no error
```

## Finding id

F209

author: ninlamster-blip
body:
The adult app now uses the same UI/UX as `flcc-next/` — the kids and teens edition — as asked.

## Why

`flcc-adults/` has been redrawn four times trying to be recognisably *not* the kids app: stickers, then colour bands, then seeded waves and hand-drawn textures, then an editorial near-black-and-gold. Each one ended up as a dashboard of tiles wearing a different coat, and none of them read as the same product as `flcc-next/`. What was wanted was one app with two editions.

## What changed

The **poster system** — `flcc-next/`'s design system, spoken in an adult register.

| | |
|---|---|
| Paper | cream `#FBF8F0` |
| Ink | navy `#2B4C6D` |
| Colour | one flat tone per poster, from the six shared names |
| Edge | `--edge: 3px`, one weight, drawn as an inset `box-shadow` |
| Type | Inter — 900 for headlines, 800 for labels |
| Drawings | flat shapes on a 100×100 grid, one navy outline at stroke 5.5 |
| Actions | `.pill` (filled), `.pill[data-quiet]`, `.go` (a word and an arrow) |
| Progress | `.track` — 14px and outlined |

Nothing is soft: no gradients, no glass, no glow, no drop shadows. A screen is a vertical run of posters rather than a grid of tiles — four big things to scroll through instead of twelve small ones to read to find the one you wanted.

Rebuilt on it: all fourteen screens, `css/next.css`, `js/core/ui.js`, `js/core/art.js`, the nav icons, and onboarding.

The adult register is the same system spoken plainly — a squarer 10px radius, no faces on the drawings, poppy never used as a whole poster (white type does not sit safely on it at display size), and prose written for an adult. **The chrome still stops at Scripture:** the Bible reader is plain white paper and serif type.

## Keeping the two editions one design

The apps share **no code**, so `css/next.css` and `js/core/art.js` here are deliberate duplicates — and a duplicate with nothing holding it in place drifts. Two suites stop that, both build-time reads of the other app's source:

- **`test/design.test.mjs`** (new) reads *both* stylesheets and fails when the palette, the 3px edge, the face, the 900/800 headline weights, the six poster tones, the two actions, or the no-shadow/no-gradient/no-blur rules stop matching.
- **`test/art.test.mjs`** compares the path data of every shared symbol character for character (`book`, `heart`, `mountain`, `star`, and this edition's `sprout`/`sun`/`flame` against their `plant`/`sunrise`/`light`).

Nothing crosses the boundary at runtime. `modules.test.mjs` still fails any module that reaches past `flcc-next/bible/` for the text of Scripture, and `storage.js` still throws on any key outside `adults/v1/`.

## Bug fixed along the way

`moment()` — the full-screen ending of a guided prayer — covers the whole screen including the tab bar, and only ever removed itself when its own pill was tapped. A member who used the back gesture at "AMEN." was left with an invisible sheet swallowing every tap in the app. It now closes on Escape and on a route change as well.

## Docs

`CLAUDE.md`'s "the adult app must not look like the kids app" section is replaced by "the two editions are one design", and `flcc-adults/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `README.md` are rewritten to match what actually ships.

## Verification

- 645 tests pass across all five apps, 0 fail.
- Twelve browser flows driven in Chromium: onboarding, every screen built from posters, prayer add/answer, RSVP surviving a reload, message → mark heard, a reference opening the Bible reader, a reading plan advancing, a guided prayer to Amen, the toast not blocking the tab bar, sub-screen tab lighting and Back, drawings-off, and reduced motion. No page errors.

ADR 0008 amendment (#502), answer 9. 115 files moved with history preserved, 44 edited only where a path they referenced moved; no attribute, option, check, package, verb or key renamed.

```
bootstrap/   install.sh (get.sh and get.ps1 stay at the root: they are public URLs)
fleet/       hosts.nix · bootstrap-profiles.nix · the inventories · windows-packages.nix
modules/     nixos/ · darwin/ · home/<tool>/ (module + the files it deploys) · home/profiles/ · shared/
pkgs/        omp-configured/config/ absorbs omp/; ceremonies live beside their package
checks/      atyrode/ · omp/ · fleet/ · lints/ · lib/ · fixtures/ — default.nix stays the registry
ci/          classify-ci-paths · docs-drift-guard · update-pins · ci.json
```

The five layout rules are in `AGENTS.md`. One transition caveat, reported rather than shimmed: a checkout that predates this commit and is driven by the new `get.sh` needs one `git pull` first, because `install.sh` moved.

**Fixed on the way:** the docs-only fast path's drift guard compared the PR merge commit against `pull_request.base.sha`, which is stale as soon as anything else lands, so docs-only PRs failed whenever `main` moved (#502 hit it twice today). It now compares the merge against its own first parent.

author: nfsarch33
body:
## What

`scripts/evospine-cycle-record.sh` recorded `status: "ok"` for its eval stage and `"complete"` for the cycle whatever its five service checks found, exited 0, appended the record into the repository checkout, and carried a hard-coded home path. It now cannot lie. S3 (v18808) of the 24h usability programme, EvoSpine slice.

## How

- Eval status and cycle status are derived from the failed-check count; a failing cycle exits 1.
- Records carry an insertion `seq` (the estate's wall clock has stepped backwards) and go to the operator's cycle ledger (`EVOSPINE_CYCLES_FILE`, default under the logs directory), the same file `helix-dev-tools eval ab --cycle-record` appends to (helix-dev-tools #89). Never into a checkout.
- Paths come from `HOME` / environment. The ledger committed at the repository root is the historical v14549 record and is no longer written; the skill doc says so.
- `scripts/evospine-cycle-record-test.sh` runs the real script against `curl` / `systemctl` stubs on `PATH` and asserts both directions (green: exit 0 + `complete`; failing: exit 1 + `failed`, returncode > 0), record placement, and the absence of a hard-coded home path. Observed: `PASS: 6, FAIL: 0`.

## Evidence

- Stub test observed both ways locally; shellcheck clean on both scripts.
- No Go changes: the Go gates are unaffected; the public-repo and deny-pattern gates are the relevant ones for this diff.

## Rollback

Revert the squash; the previous script's behaviour returns (exit 0, `complete`, checkout-resident ledger).
