author: imkarrer
body:
`brew tap` cannot clone over HTTPS, because the git we put on Homebrew's PATH has no CA bundle: ``` ==> Tapping someone/tap Cloning into '/opt/homebrew/Library/Taps/someone/homebrew-tap'... fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/someone/homebrew-tap/': SSL certificate OpenSSL verify result: unable to get local issuer certificate (20) ``` This wraps `pkgs.gitMinimal` so it carries `SSL_CERT_FILE` itself, pointing at the bundle `security.pki` already assembles, and adds a CI test that taps *after* activation — the path the existing tests never exercise. **What to review:** whether reading `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` at runtime is the right call versus building a store path, and whether `koekeishiya/formulae` is an acceptable remote for the new test to depend on.
Why the user cannot work around this `bin/brew` re-executes itself through a hard environment reset: ```bash PATH="/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin" # ... exec /usr/bin/env -i "${FILTERED_ENV[@]}" /bin/bash -p "${HOMEBREW_LIBRARY}/Homebrew/brew.sh" "$@" ``` The allowlist is `HOME SHELL PATH TERM TERMINFO TERMINFO_DIRS COLUMNS DISPLAY LOGNAME USER CI SSH_AUTH_SOCK SUDO_ASKPASS`, the proxy variables, and `HOMEBREW_*`. Neither `SSL_CERT_FILE` nor `NIX_SSL_CERT_FILE` survives, so the ambient values that make a Nix git work in an ordinary shell — including the `NIX_SSL_CERT_FILE` that `security.pki` sets — are gone by the time git runs. `brew.env` cannot put them back either: its parser only honours lines matching `^(HOMEBREW_|SUDO_ASKPASS=|(all|no|ftp|https?)_proxy=)` and silently drops everything else. Nor can `nix-homebrew.extraEnv`, whose exports land in the wrapper *before* the reset and are filtered out by name along with everything else. That leaves only `HOMEBREW_GIT_PATH`, which discards the pinned git entirely.
Why the system bundle rather than pkgs.cacert nix-darwin's `security.pki` concatenates `certificateFiles` (which already includes `pkgs.cacert` with `caCertificateBlacklist` applied) and `certificates` into `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`, then points `NIX_SSL_CERT_FILE` at it. That file is the system trust store, and the only one a user can extend or trim through supported options. Baking a bare `${pkgs.cacert}/etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt` into the wrapper would look like it works while quietly ignoring both. Someone behind a TLS-intercepting proxy who adds their root through `security.pki.certificateFiles` — the documented way — would still see `brew tap` fail, and would now have no lever at all, since Homebrew strips the environment variable they might otherwise reach for. Reading the path at runtime rather than embedding a store path also means adding a root takes effect on the next activation without rebuilding git, and keeps a second copy of the bundle out of the closure. `system.activationScripts.etc` runs before `.homebrew` (nix-darwin orders them at lines 125 and 138 of `modules/system/activation-scripts.nix`, and our own `mkBefore` stays inside the latter), so the file is in place by the time `brew bundle` needs it. When `security.pki.installCACerts` is disabled nix-darwin writes no such file, so that case falls back to `pkgs.cacert`. `--set-default` rather than `--set` so a direct caller can still override; within Homebrew the variable is stripped regardless, so the system bundle always wins there.
Why CI did not catch it, and where the test went The `migrate` test does tap a third-party repository: ```nix ci.preScript = lib.optionalString pkgs.stdenv.hostPlatform.isAarch64 '' >&2 echo "Adding a third-party tap imperatively" brew tap koekeishiya/formulae ''; ``` But `ci.preScript` runs *before* `ci.script` activates the system, so that `brew` is the runner's pre-existing Homebrew using Apple git, not ours. The later `brew install koekeishiya/formulae/yabai` in `postScript` reads an already-cloned tap and fetches its bottle over curl, so it never drives git over HTTPS either. Rather than add a test — which would have meant a new `darwinSystem` evaluation and three more full-runner CI jobs for a single assertion — `migrate`'s `postScript` now clones that same remote once more under a fresh tap name, after activation: ```bash brew tap nix-homebrew/https-test https://github.com/koekeishiya/homebrew-formulae test -d "$(brew --repository nix-homebrew/https-test)/.git" ``` A fresh tap name means it cannot pass vacuously on a runner that already has `koekeishiya/formulae`, and it leaves the existing "the imperative tap survived activation" assertion intact — untapping and re-tapping would have destroyed exactly what that assertion checks, and `brew untap --force` would have uninstalled yabai as a side effect. No new external dependency, and the job count stays at 12. Not covered: that a root added via `security.pki.certificateFiles` is actually honoured. Asserting that needs a TLS fixture with a private CA, which felt out of proportion here — happy to add it if you disagree.
Verification The generated wrapper, and the git it names: ```console $ grep '^PATH=' /nix/store/gn457fnwl4w7hqiln8nvnfzp1c0h1f66-brew PATH="/nix/store/gla4df5z02ymsq2f00f6f8s2ggdd08hj-git-minimal-2.55.0-with-cacert/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin" $ cat /nix/store/gla4df5z02ymsq2f00f6f8s2ggdd08hj-git-minimal-2.55.0-with-cacert/bin/git #! /nix/store/9gm5a7hzhyzx979l4r3plzyq36544cyq-bash-5.3p15/bin/bash -e export SSL_CERT_FILE=${SSL_CERT_FILE-'/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt'} exec -a "$0" ".../bin/.git-wrapped" "$@" $ env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=/usr/bin:/bin \ /nix/store/gla4df5z02ymsq2f00f6f8s2ggdd08hj-git-minimal-2.55.0-with-cacert/bin/git \ ls-remote https://github.com/asheshgoplani/homebrew-tap bfc4327a90bbb8d3a539fda3b8a51f79e12d68e9 HEAD ``` The unwrapped `git-minimal` fails on that same command with an empty environment. `nix build .#githubActions.checks.aarch64-darwin."imperative-tap-over-https-unstable"` builds; `nixfmt --check ci/tests.nix` passes. `modules/default.nix` was already not nixfmt-clean before this change, so it is left formatted in the surrounding style.

author: sunarya-thito
body:
Groundwork for #258, and a measurement that changes what the rest of it should
be. This does not build `MutationBuffer`; the last section says why, and a
comment on the issue carries the full argument.

## What was wrong

`DataPointer.readPending` is public API and partial: some column kinds answer,
the rest throw. Nothing measured which was which, and two of the four
implementations were wrong about the contract their own base class states.

**`float64` reached for the write slot outside a tick.** The base doc says the
opposite - outside a tick the write slot holds whatever sat there before
`beginWrite` copied, so an implementation answers with the published read - and
`_OptionalField` already did. On a page that has published, reaching for
`_write` there trips `_writeRow`'s lost-write assertion, so a read raises a
message about a write it never makes. In release it returns the stale slot.

**`hasBool` forwarded the call into the one-bit field it wraps.** That field
does not implement `readPending`, so the `UnsupportedError` arrived under
`_SubByteUintField` - a private class no declaration writes and no caller can
act on. `hasEntity` and `hasEnum` omit the same forward, and their doc comments
say why. The forward is gone; the call still throws, now naming `_BoolField`.

**The published reference named the wrong set.** It read "the optional-entity
fields the hierarchy links are made of, and `float64`", which invites
`optFloat64`. An optional column answers only when its value half implements
`readFrom`, and `_Int64Field` is the only one that does. Measured:

| column | `readPending` inside a tick |
|---|---|
| `float64` | answers |
| `optInt64` | answers |
| `optEntity` | answers |
| `optFloat64` | throws - `_Float64Field` has no `readFrom` |
| `optFloat32`, `optInt32` | throws |
| `hasInt64`, `float32`, `hasBool` | throws |

The three that answer are now named on the doc, in the guide and in the roadmap.

## The hierarchy tests did not cover what they claimed

Two tests say they are the `readPending` hazard. Both spawn on the first tick,
where the page has never published and an ordinary read falls through to the
write slot, so they hold whichever slot `_append` reads. Replacing the pending
read with `parentLastChild[this]` leaves both green - only `appending three
children in one tick works after the first publish` fails.

That leaves the **declaration** path - `addEntityIn` recursing over declared
children - with no test that can see the bug. A rig spawned after a publish is
added, and the same mutation now kills two tests instead of one.

## Verification

Baselines taken before editing and again after. Every suite in CI's list was
run, not only the changed package. `good` is given at both branch points: this
started on `b08e82d` (1018) and was rebased onto `dc75d55` (1021), which added
three of its own. The delta this branch contributes is +8 either way.

| suite | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `good` | 1021 | 1029 |
| `goo2d` | 409 (3 skipped) | 409 (3 skipped) |
| `goo3d` | 43 | 43 |
| `good_cli` | 364 | 364 |
| `good_tool` | 81 | 81 |
| `good_net` | 37 | 37 |
| `good_net_p2p` | 43 | 43 |
| `goo2d_physics_box2d` | - | 77 |
| `goo2d_ffi_box2d` | - | 25 |
| `good_audio_soloud` | - | 6 |
| `goo2d/example` | - | 27 |

`good_tool --check`: 8 generated files up to date, unchanged.
`--doc-references`: 3136 of 3140 before, 3139 of 3143 after - three references
added, the same four unresolved, exit 0 either way.
`doc_snippets` extracts and analyzes clean. `flutter analyze` clean on `good`,
`goo2d`, `goo3d`.

Each guard was broken separately, on a committed tree, and the tree checked
clean after each restore.

| mutation | tests killed |
|---|---|
| drop `_Float64Field`'s outside-a-tick guard | 1: `readPending outside a tick float64 answers the published slot` |
| restore `_BoolField`'s `readPending` forward | 1: `readPending a column kind that cannot answer names itself` |
| drop `_OptionalField`'s outside-a-tick guard | 7, first of them `readPending outside a tick optInt64 answers the published slot` |
| `_append` reads `parentLastChild[this]` | 2, where before this branch it killed 1 |

The last row is the point of the new hierarchy test: the count moved.

## Cost

The guard adds a load and a predicted branch to `_Float64Field.readPending`,
which `goo2d` and `goo3d` reach from `_pendingWorldOf` for entities spawned this
tick. `packages/good` cannot be AOT-compiled - `data_layout.dart` reaches
`package:flutter/services.dart` through `struct.dart` and `asset.dart` - so the
field chain was transcribed, with six widths kept live so the call stays
megamorphic, and compiled with `dart compile exe`. 20M iterations, 256 rows,
min of 11 reps, three process runs:

```
ratio guarded/bare   1.0146   0.9681   0.9925
noise floor          1.0672   1.0343   1.0289
```

The sign flips between runs and every ratio sits inside the floor, so the cost
is below what this harness resolves - under about 3% of a 9 ns pending read.
`operator[]` is untouched.

## What this does not do, and why

The issue body says a `MutationBuffer` "takes `readPending`'s two callers with
it". Re-measured on `b08e82d`: **47 call sites in `lib`** - `data/hierarchy.dart`
9, `scene.dart` 6, `goo2d/world_transform.dart` 11, `goo3d/world_transform.dart`
21 - plus 2 internal delegations, 5 declarations, and 10 in tests. 98 textual
mentions in all.

author: ryanfaircloth
body:
Closes #60.

> **11.3.1** If the encoding represents a real value whose base B is 2, then binary encoding employing base 2 shall be used. Before encoding, the mantissa M and exponent E are chosen so that M is either 0 or is odd. […] In encoding the value, the binary scaling factor F shall be zero, and M and E shall each be represented in the fewest octets necessary.
>
> **11.3.2.1** The ISO 6093 NR3 form shall be used (see 8.5.8).
> **11.3.2.4** Neither the first nor the last digit of the mantissa may be a 0.
> **11.3.2.5** The last digit in the mantissa shall be immediately followed by FULL STOP (.), followed by the exponent-mark "E".
> **11.3.2.6** If the exponent has the value 0, it shall be written "+0", otherwise the exponent's first digit shall not be zero, and PLUS SIGN shall not be used.

BER offers three bases, a scaling factor and three ISO 6093 forms, so one real value has many encodings. Neither codec enforced 11.3.

## Decoder

| substrate | why non-canonical | before | after (CER/DER) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `09 03 80 00 06` | mantissa 6 is even (11.3.1) | 6.0 | rejected |
| `09 03 84 00 03` | scaling factor F=1 (11.3.1) | 6.0 | rejected |
| `09 03 90 00 03` | base 8 (11.3.1) | 3.0 | rejected |
| `09 03 a0 00 03` | base 16 (11.3.1) | 3.0 | rejected |
| `09 04 81 00 01 03` | padded exponent (11.3.1) | 6.0 | rejected |
| `09 04 80 00 00 03` | padded mantissa (11.3.1) | 3.0 | rejected |
| `09 04 01 31 32 33` | NR1 form (11.3.2.1) | 123.0 | rejected |
| `09 06 02 …` | NR2 form (11.3.2.1) | 1.234 | rejected |

BER continues to accept all of them.

## Encoder — output changes

The decimal form pyasn1 emitted is not one 11.3.2 admits: the FULL STOP required by 11.3.2.5 was missing.

| value | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 1.5 | `15E-1` | `15.E-1` |
| -0.75 | `-75E-2` | `-75.E-2` |
| 1.0 | `1E+0` | `1.E+0` |
| 10.0 | `1E+1` | `1.E1` |

**This changes the octets for every CER/DER encoding of a REAL whose base is 10** — which is every REAL constructed from a Python float. Decoded values are unchanged, and BER output is untouched. Worth a release note.

Trailing mantissa zeros now move into the exponent (11.3.2.4), and a positive exponent loses its PLUS SIGN (11.3.2.6).

## One thing worth a look

`Real.prettyIn` normalises the mantissa with true division, so a normalised value reaches the encoder as a `float`. Without coercing back to `int`, the mantissa rendered as `1.0` and produced `1.0.E1`, which does not parse — `(10, 10, 0)` failed to round-trip. Fixed here, but it suggests `__normalizeBase10` should use floor division: for a large mantissa the float divide loses precision. Out of scope; say the word and I'll file it.

## Tests

`RealCanonicalFormTestCase` — 7 cases covering non-canonical binary rejection on both decode paths, canonical binary still accepted, NR1/NR2 rejected and NR3 accepted, exact decimal spelling, trailing-zero migration, encoder output surviving the strict reader, and 8.5.9 special values unaffected.

1346 tests pass. ruff, ruff format, and mypy clean.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - CER REAL values are encoded using canonical X.690-compliant decimal and binary formats.
  - CER decoding validates canonical REAL encodings while preserving supported special values and round trips.
  - CER and DER handling now enforces minimal INTEGER and ENUMERATED encodings.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Improved mantissa normalization, exponent formatting, and decimal REAL representations.
  - BER decoding continues to tolerate non-canonical encodings where applicable.

- **Documentation**
  - Removed the outdated project backlog document.

author: grassgod
body:
## Summary

- reconcile the live platform release to one CLI update request per physical daemon and target version
- register the update even while a daemon is busy, then use the pending/running CLI update as a daemon-wide Task dispatch fence
- let existing Wiki/Demand work finish normally, renew the pending request from heartbeat, and deliver the update as soon as all providers on the daemon are idle
- skip current, Desktop-managed, and Cloud runtimes, and extend the running update timeout from 150 seconds to 20 minutes
- keep reconciliation idempotent through existing update history

## Why

Formal releases publish the daemon artifact and platform images, but the platform previously never asked connected daemons to install the new CLI. Simply waiting for an idle heartbeat is insufficient because continuous Wiki or Autopilot work can consume every idle window and starve the upgrade forever.

The drain fence is enforced by the server, so it also works for the old daemon performing its first upgrade: queued work remains queued, active work is not killed, and the old daemon receives the update only after its current execution has ended.

A genuinely stuck in-flight Task still requires the existing Task timeout or manual cancellation; the updater does not destroy active work.

- `bun test tests/unit`: 2087 passed, 0 failed

- `bun run scripts/check-cli-capabilities.ts`: 0 missing

No database migration is required.

body:
## 背景

排查并修复两个使用中报告的问题：

1. **推理时间长出现连接报错** —— 任何流式推理超过 `httpIdleTimeoutMs`(默认 5 分钟)总时长即被掐断，即使模型正在活跃输出
2. **write 写入 300+ 行后 TUI 越来越卡** —— 每个 SSE delta 对全量累积内容做多遍 O(n) 解析/高亮/深拷贝，总代价 O(n²)

## 修复 1：超时语义归位(`fix(rpi-ai)`)

**根因**：上游 undici 的 `headersTimeout`/`bodyTimeout` 是**空闲**预算(活跃流不限总时长)，移植时被映射成 reqwest `ClientBuilder::timeout` 的**总 deadline**(覆盖连接+响应头+整个 body 流读)。

**方案**：新增 `rpi-ai/src/api/stream_timeouts.rs`，三段式空闲语义：

| 阶段 | 实现 |
|---|---|
| 连接 | `connect_timeout`(替换总 timeout) |
| 等响应头 | `send_with_headers_timeout`(对应 headersTimeout / TS SDK 头到达即 clearTimeout) |
| Body 流 | `IdleTimeoutStream` 块间空闲超预算才报错，每 chunk 重置 deadline |

- 覆盖全部 9 个 SSE adapter；mistral 60s 总超时一并改空闲语义(有意偏离上游 `AbortSignal.timeout` quirk，注释记录)
- codex SSE 保持绝对 deadline(与上游对拍)；openrouter_images 非流式请求保留总超时
- 超时消息含 `timed out`，重试分类器可识别

## 修复 2：write 流式性能(`perf(interactive)`)

| 层 | 修复 |
|---|---|
| write 渲染器 | 越过 50 行前缀窗口后跳过每 delta 的 syntect 整块重高亮(窗口外文本字节稳定，重算必然相同)；`format_write_call` 借用缓存行只 clone 前 10 行；`full` 标记让 args_complete 后的重复渲染走缓存 |
| json_parse | `repair_json` 惰性化——流式期间干净输入零分配(保留 eager 实现作对拍参考) |
| agent_loop | `partial_message` 改 bool 标志，每 delta 深拷贝 3→1 次 |
| assistant_message | 可见内容指纹未变则跳过容器重建——纯 tool-call delta 零重建 |

## 验收

**单测**：工作区全量 126 套件 / 5316+ 用例通过，含新增回归测试：
- `tests/stream_idle_timeout.rs` 端到端回环：活跃流总时长超预算仍完整完成(**已验证旧代码下必失败**)、静默流按时限终止、headers 等待有界
- write：120 行流仅 49 次前缀刷新(精确计数锁定跳过逻辑)、完成态缓存复用、400 行流有界
- assistant_message：300 个纯 tool-call delta 仅 1 次重建、setter 正确绕过跳过
- `repair_json` 惰性版与旧实现逐字节对拍等价

**性能**(release，400 行流式 write，vs HEAD 基线)：

| 指标 | 修复前 | 修复后 |
|---|---|---|
| 总耗时 | 2250ms | **245ms(9.2×)** |
| 第 200–400 行各段 | ~592ms/百行 | **~13.5ms/百行(44×，恒定不增长)** |
| 完成后重复渲染 | 46.8ms/次 | **6µs(缓存命中)** |

author: its-ahoh
body:
## What

**Files tab rebuilt as a workspace tree.** The right panel now shows every file and folder in the workspace, folders first. Changed files and folders are highlighted (yellow for modified, green for new) with `+added −removed` line counts rolled up to each parent folder. Folders with changes open by default. Clicking a file swaps the tree for the file: a changed file shows its diff, an unchanged one shows its full code with line numbers, images get a preview, and binary files get a short message instead of garbage.

**Per-turn diffs, recorded by the gateway.** A shell command or a codex `file_change` left only a path behind, so the panel could only diff the working tree against HEAD and every turn's edits looked the same. The gateway now stores each written file as a git blob (`hash-object -w`) when the tool call ends and diffs it against the blob its previous write left, or HEAD, or nothing for a new file. The patch and counts ride on the `tool_end` entry as `writeDiffs`. The panel uses them under the "This turn" filter and falls back to git's net diff under "All".

**Codex edits now count.** Codex reports edits as a `file_change` item (a JSON list of `{path, kind}`). Both the gateway and the panel now treat those as writes.

## Notes

- Patches over 64 KB keep their counts but drop the text.
- `git gc` prunes unreferenced blobs after about two weeks; a later write to that file then diffs against HEAD. Counts stay right, that turn just absorbs earlier changes.
- Paths are resolved through symlinks before matching against `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (macOS `/tmp` bit this in testing).
- The extractor keeps one entry per file per turn, so a file written in two turns shows under both.

## Test plan

- [x] `packages/gateway`: 471 tests, `tsc` clean
- [x] `codey-mac`: 932 tests, renderer + electron `tsc` clean, `vite build` ok
- [x] `npm run lint` clean
- [x] Recorder exercised against real git in a temp repo: first write, second write, delete, unchanged
- [ ] Manual: restart the app, run a two-turn chat that edits via Bash or Codex, open Files, filter to the second turn and confirm only its lines show

Bijwerken van de twee overdrachtsdocumenten na het landen van #141 en #151. Geen codewijziging.

## Wat er niet meer klopte

`docs/WERKVOORRAAD.md` §0 stond nog op de stand van 31-08:

| | Stond er | Klopt |
|---|---|---|
| RLS-suite | 605 geslaagd | **765** |
| hele suite | 2005 geslaagd | **2716** |
| controlescripts | 26 | **30**, over 34 poortstappen |

⚠️ `npm run docs:controle` en `stand:controle` waren gróén, en dat is precies waarom dit met de hand moet: die twee bewaken de migratienummering en of de drie documenten elkaar tegenspreken, niet of een testteller nog klopt. Dat is de handmatige regel uit CLAUDE.md — *"werk je iets bij, grep dan op dat feit in alle drie de bestanden"*.

## Wat erbij is gezet

**De vier ongemeten controles staan nu in de stand.** `adviseur`, `functies`, `register` en `wachtwoord` meten niets zonder de credentials van het échte project, en de poort noemt dat apart: *"niets staat rood, maar 4 controles hebben niets gemeten"*. Dat hoort in de overdracht en niet alleen in de uitvoer van de poort — anders leest een volgende sessie "alles groen".

**`docs/VOLGENDE-SESSIE.md`** draagt twee dingen die bij Quinten liggen:

1. **De afkoeling van zeven dagen is geen slot.** Wie ontkoppelt en daarna een week niets doet, valt terug op het gedrag van 0135. Bewust ontwerp, maar het is ook de prijs van het weglopen bij domeinregel 3 — te goedkoop is een puntenmodelbesluit en geen bug.
2. **QS8-264**: `guard_group_update()` heeft nog nooit gesloten.

En één les uit de reviewronde, want die is algemener dan dat issue:

> **Een mutatie die een grendel hélemaal weghaalt, bewijst alleen dat de grendel bestáát.** Wil je een getál bewaken, dan moet er een geval aan weerszijden van dat getal staan.

Dat was K3 op #141: `- interval '7 days'` weghalen maakte één test rood, maar hem vervangen door `'1 second'` liet alle 23 groen.

author: hadas-levy-healthy
body:
> **Short version first, if you want it:** [The No-Database Invariant](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/e37de814-dc87-4955-8805-ae0117817628)
> — a one-page explainer of the mechanism in two diagrams: one build and one digest feeding two
> deployments, and the single edge that decides whether a worker can be shared at all. The log
> below is self-contained; the page is a reading aid, not a citation.

## The precedent

ACR already ran this shape in production for years. `behealthy` and `rehealthy` ran **two separate
workers** — different source, different registry, different language, different entrypoint — but they
held one identical relation:

- the producer maps its **own** database to plain JSON (`algoPayload`'s return value;
  `cloud.AlgorithmExecutionMessage`, whose fields are `Product string`, `Material string`). No ORM
  type crosses the wire
- the worker's vocabulary is **deployment configuration, not schema** — `HANDLED_PRODUCTS: "dip,acr"`,
  `HANDLED_STICK_TYPES: "ACON_10,ACON_2"` in the chart
- the worker **writes nothing itself**. It POSTs to a host given by environment:
  `RE_WORKER_SERVICE_HOST` → `results/{resultId}/output`
- **each backend owns its own result writer** — `POST /algo_output/:examId` against `worker-service`.
  Same job, different schema, never shared

And the one worker that could *not* be shared failed on exactly one property: `rehealthy`'s reads a
database (`main.go:86`, `materials.go:28`) and mounts `db_uri.enc`. A worker that reads a database
belongs to that database.

That is the whole argument for AD-30, and it was missing from this PR. It now lands as **L14.8**.

## The issue

`architecture_plan.html` bakes the approved algorithm into production's `algo-worker` image, and gives
its reasons: *"No tarball download in the hot path, which also makes the deployed algorithm part of the
verified artefact."* Both are real — a cold pod under KEDA scale-up pays a download, and `AD-14`'s
"what is deployed equals what was approved" is simplest when one digest is the whole answer.

**The consequence not examined is that baking forks the worker.** Research's worker fetches the
algorithm as a tarball by blob key, extracts it and caches it. A production worker with the algorithm
already present does not — and that fetch path is exactly what `FR-LCM-009` validation exercises. So
the plan's second reason works against itself: the artefact becomes verified, and the code path that
runs it becomes the one research never validated.

`spine.md` does not choose. Its Boundary row — "Tarball in the production algorithms bucket plus an
`algorithm_version` row" — describes how the algorithm *travels*, not how the worker *consumes* it, and
is correct either way. The plan chooses, and the choice is unrecorded as a decision.

## The solution

**AD-30 — build the runner once, promote the image; keep the writer per-deployment.**

- `algo-worker` is built **once**, in the repository that owns the algorithm. Production runs a
  **promoted, digest-pinned copy**, configured by environment against its own broker, buckets and
  `worker-api`. The algorithm reaches it as a promoted tarball in production's own bucket — exactly as
  the Boundary already provides — so the runner is identical on both sides.
- **The sharing is by published image, never by source.** Nothing is extracted, nothing is split. This
  is the clause that makes the worker's build-time `@qacr/rabbit` → `@qacr/types` → `@prisma/client`
  chain irrelevant to the consumer: it is resolved once, in the repository that owns the schema and
  already runs `prisma generate`. A deployment that receives a built image never resolves
  `@qacr/types`, so the chain never reaches it.
- **The runner reads and writes no database.** Normative, and the single property the decision rests
  on. Enforced by `backend.q-acr#509` — local enums plus a `no-restricted-imports` rule scoped to the
  worker that blocks `@prisma/*` including type-only imports.
- **The image carries the worker and its runtime dependencies only.** Not satisfied today:
  `Dockerfile.algo-worker` does `COPY .` and the final stage copies the whole build tree out, so the
  published image carries research's generated client, `worker-api`, `common/repositories` and the
  back-office services. For research that is a size question; for a submission artefact it is a *what
  is in the device software* question. Cheap to fix — `@qacr/types` emits no runtime Prisma import, so
  the generated client never has to leave the build stage.
- **`worker-api` is not shared.** Each deployment writes its own; production's writes insert-only
  `exam_result` under RLS and carries AD-23's single-use callback credential. `backend.q-acr#238` tried
  to share it by unioning two clients' types and stalled — recorded in L14.3, because it is the reason
  the runner is the right unit of sharing and the writer is not.

This **overrides the plan's bake-in design**, so L14.5 sets the two mechanisms against each other on
verified artefact, hot path, runner, promotion cost and image count, and names a third shape — share
the runner unchanged and pre-warm its cache from a pinned object — that keeps most of both. To keep
bake-in instead, the cold-start cost wants measuring first (`OQ-9` records that algorithm latency has
never been measured), and `FR-LCM-009` needs an answer for how a validation performed on research's
runner transfers to a production runner that does not share its fetch path.

**OQ-19** — who owns promotion and where the approval is recorded; now with a sharper edge, since once
the repositories separate the production artefact is built by the research repository's CI, so the team
that owns the deployment does not own the build. An ownership question, deliberately left open.
**OQ-20** — whether production needs the batch routing path or only the short one.

## Scope

One file, additive: `architecture/spine-decision-log.md` — `L14` with the new `L14.8`, three added
clauses on AD-30, `#238` as evidence in L14.3, and four index rows (L14, AD-30, and OQ-19/OQ-20 minted in the
Open questions index). `architecture/spine.md` is
**deliberately unamended**; L14.7 carries paste-ready text for the boundary row, the AD, the OQs and an
optional Deferred entry, so merging does not make an unreviewed rule binding.

Nothing in `product/` is touched and no generated file changes. `tools/check_citations.py` reads
`evidence/behaviour.tsv` only; its failure count is identical before and after this change.

## Evidence

L14.1/L14.4–L14.6 read against `backend.q-acr` `origin/main` at `21b8cf9` and `helm-charts`
`origin/master` at `1ed2669`. L14.8 read 2026-09-03 against `behealthy` `origin/main` at `0f8b0bd3d`,
`rehealthy-core` `origin/develop` at `52b87a0`, and the same `helm-charts` commit.

`rehealthy-core` is cited against **`develop`, not `master`**, and the distinction is load-bearing:
`master`'s last commit is 2022-06-15, `develop` is 66 commits ahead and is the repository's default
branch, and the database access exists only on `develop` — introduced 2022-07-10 in `a7cea50`, not an
ancestor of `master`. Reading `master` would show a worker with no database at all and would invert the
counter-example.

The runtime claim about `@qacr/types` was checked by building it and reading `dist/`: no emitted `.js`
names `@prisma/client`. The build-time coupling was checked in the other direction by moving the
generated client aside, after which typechecking fails with `TS2305`.

> Commit history note: the second commit filed this as a factual error in the plan (`C-8`) and the
> third withdraws that. The plan was right about its own intent; the finding is the forked runner.
> The net diff carries no `C-8`.

body: ## Summary Fixes the Abraxas partner verification auth/resume loop on `abraxasworld.xyz`. Good Trouble Wix correctly redirects to `/partner/verify`, but holders with a zkLogin `localStorage` session were hitting `401 Sign in required in this browser` because the httpOnly `abraxas_browser_session` cookie was not established before `/api/v1/partner-flow/evaluate` ran. ## Root cause - **Client gate:** `useSuiAuth().suiAddress` (zkLogin localStorage) - **API gate:** `abraxas_browser_session` httpOnly JWT via `requireBrowserSession()` - `PartnerVerifyClient` called evaluate immediately when `suiAddress` was set, racing `ensureBrowserSession()` (fire-and-forget in `SuiAuthProvider`) - OAuth callback always redirected to `/passport`, dropping `partner_id` / `policy_id` / `return_url` / `gtv` ## Changes - Await `ensureBrowserSession()` before evaluate; map 401 to sign-in UX (no reload loop) - Functional **Sign in with Google** on partner verify entry - `partnerVerifyResume` sessionStorage helper with hardened security: - Only restores same-origin relative paths beginning with `/partner/verify?` - Rejects absolute/protocol-relative URLs, backslashes, traversal, forbidden fields - 30-minute TTL; clear on consume, expiry, or invalid state - Stores only `partner_id`, `policy_id`, `return_url` (+ optional permission fields) — never tokens/PII - zkLogin callback resumes saved partner verify path after OAuth ## Security Server-side partner/policy/return-url allowlist validation in `/api/v1/partner-flow/evaluate` is unchanged and remains authoritative. ## Testing - `lib/partner/partnerVerifyResume.test.ts` (9) - `lib/partner/partnerVerifyCallbackResume.test.ts` (1) - `components/partner/PartnerVerifyClient.test.tsx` (3) - `lib/partner/partnerFlowRoutes.test.ts` (5) - `lib/partner/relyingPartyFlow.test.ts` (19) - `npm run build` ✓ - `npx tsc --noEmit` ✓

## Summary

Add server-side transactional email delivery through Resend without exposing API keys or creating a generic client-controlled mail relay.

## Scope

- [x] Deploy authenticated `send-morley-email` Supabase Edge Function.
- [x] Generate/hash team invite secrets server-side and email invites.
- [x] Email Android Admin invite creation and reissues while preserving one-time backup-code display.
- [x] Email support users when Admin replies.
- [x] Email Admin/Manager recipients for new Android support tickets and user replies.
- [x] Mirror eligible Admin notification jobs to email while keeping device-only targeting safe.
- [x] Add static regression coverage and a live anonymous-access protection check.
- [x] Advance Android release to 2.15.45 / versionCode 89.

## Security contract

- Resend credentials remain Edge Function environment secrets only.
- Edge Function requires a valid Supabase JWT and enabled profile.
- Clients cannot supply arbitrary recipient email addresses for support/notification delivery.
- Invite recipients are constrained to the approved invite email.
- Support recipients are resolved from ticket ownership and active Admin/Manager profiles.
- Notification recipients are resolved from persisted notification jobs and linked device/user records.
- Device-only targets never fan out to the full email audience.
- Raw invite codes are stored only as SHA-256 hashes; the caller receives the one-time code only after successful email delivery.
- Failed invite email delivery removes the newly-created invite so unusable orphan invites are not left behind.

author: leonschh
body:
## Which Linear task is linked to this PR?
This PR was written during a project review.

## Why was it implemented this way?
Four independent issues fixed in one PR since all changes are in the same file (`src/api.ts`):
- [`containsSwitchChain (Line ~351)`](https://github.com/lifinance/types/blob/main/src/api.ts#L351)
**Why:** The comment `// Features required for route execution` was semantically incorrect - the field is a boolean flag indicating chain switches, not a feature list
**Chosen:** Updated to accurately describe the field's purpose

- [`@deprecated annotation (Line ~591)`](https://github.com/lifinance/types/blob/main/src/api.ts#L591)
**Why:** Block comments `/* */` are not recognized by TypeScript/IDE tooling; only JSDoc `/** */` triggers deprecation warnings
**Chosen:** Converted to proper JSDoc format, consistent with other deprecated types in the file

- [`INVALID status comment (Line ~673)`](https://github.com/lifinance/types/blob/main/src/api.ts#L673-L674)
**Why:** The comment `// A third party service is not available` contradicts official LI.FI documentation where INVALID means "Hash is not tied to the requested tool"
**Chosen:** Updated to match official docs

- [`RelayStatusRequest.taskId type (Lines ~1094)`](https://github.com/lifinance/types/blob/main/src/api.ts#L1094)
**Why:** `RelayResponseData.taskId` returns a string (UUID), but `RelayStatusRequest.taskId` expected `Hash` (`0x${string}`), causing type errors when passing taskId from response to status request
**Chosen:** Changed `RelayStatusRequest.taskId` to `string` - widens the type safely (`Hash` is subset of `string`) and enables type-safe usage without `as Hash` assertions

All changes are backward compatible and maintain the same runtime behavior.

author: mobeenabdullah
body:
Follow-up to #1464, closing the two findings reported after it merged. Both were verified by writing the broken implementation, not by reading the check.

## A token at a leaf that refuses its kind

The check asked `tokenKindsForProperty`, which returns the **union** across a composite property's leaves. For `border` that union is `dimension | color`, so a colour token written into `border.width.blockStart` satisfied it — the property does take a colour, at a *different* leaf — while the browser drops the declaration. Reproduced: that mutation passed all 100 tests across the two suites.

The question now goes to `validateStyleValues`, which answers it **per leaf** and covers an unknown token in the same pass. The membership walker this file carried is gone with it — a second traversal of the catalog's shapes living in a test was the drift.

**It is asked directly rather than through `compileStyleValues`, and that detail is the finding underneath the finding.** Routing through the compiler was my first attempt and it reported nothing:

```
compileStyleValues({ border: { width: { blockStart: { $token: "color.border-strong" } } } }, ..., { tokens })
  declarations: ["border-block-start-width:var(--site-color-border-strong)"]
  warnings:     []
```

The compiler keeps only `severity === "error"` issues to decide what to refuse, and a kind mismatch is a **warning**. So it emits the dropped declaration silently. That also explains why no production check catches any of this: the validator has the answer, the compiler discards it, and a block default is compiled with no token table at all.

## A property declared with no value

`declaredProperties` lists a key whatever its value, and `leafCount` returns 0 for an empty composite — so `border: {}` was *0 emitted of 0 expected*, which is not "fewer than expected". Emptying `BUTTON_BASE_STYLES.border` removes the reset that keeps a `<button>` and an `<a>` the same outline and outer size, and every suite stayed green.

A declared property carrying no leaf is now a defect in its own right, at both the block and the part call site.

## Evidence

```
colour token in border.width.blockStart -> x core/form part control writes each token at a leaf that accepts it
BUTTON_BASE_STYLES.border = {}          -> x core/button reaches the compiled stylesheet, property by property
                                           x core/form part submit reaches the compiled stylesheet, property by property
```

Plus a control asserting the validator *reports* a wrong-kind leaf and stays silent on the right one — without it, a missing token table or a renamed warning code would leave every case green having checked nothing.

## One measurement note

My first reproduction showed both mutations "failing" **and the restored tree failing identically**. `blocks-react` resolves the engine through `dist`, and a branch switch had left it without `color.border-strong`. Rebuilding gave a clean 100-test baseline, and only then did the two mutations show as passing — which is the observation this fix is built on.

1073 tests across 43 files; `check-types`, `lint`, `lint:design`, `build` pass, and `fallow --gate new-only` reports `complexity_introduced: 0`, `verdict: pass` (the first draft of `tokenIssues` exceeded cognitive complexity and was decomposed).


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Tests**
  * Expanded style validation coverage for compiled styles, including declarations with no values.
  * Added more precise checks for token kinds used in style properties.
  * Improved detection of unknown tokens and mismatched token types, including invalid color tokens used in border-width settings.
  * Updated validation scenarios for both component-level and root-level styles.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

author: emtabiraobarias
body:
Specified from the 2026-09-02 hash-out. **32 requirements in EARS, 8 success criteria, 4 user stories.**

### The four decisions were yours

| | |
|---|---|
| Registration | in-app branded form against the provider's admin API |
| Migration | auto-match on a **verified** email at first sign-in through a new issuer |
| Self-service | export **and** delete, reusing `011`'s two-phase erasure |
| Identity indirection | absorbed into this spec rather than sequenced ahead of it |

### Why identity indirection is in an "accounts" spec

The trigger was self-service accounts; the blocking problem is underneath it. Today `userId` **is** the OIDC `sub`, and that is the primary key of every user-owned document across six collections. Change provider and every user gets a new `sub`, orphaning all of their data. This spec is where the first user-owned identity record appears anyway.

### The load-bearing refusal

**FR-AC-009/010** — an absent or unverified email claim must never match an existing identity. Without it, registering with someone else's address inherits their inventory, meal plans and feedback.

This exists because two of your decisions interact: if the *app* creates users via the admin API, the app becomes responsible for verification actually happening, and admin-created accounts are typically unverified by default.

### Keeping the branded form survivable

**FR-AC-019/020** confine the provider to a single internal interface, so a future move replaces one adapter rather than the feature. **FR-AC-031/032** record that this is the app's **first machine credential against the IdP** — a deliberate change of posture from `002`, where the app only ever verified tokens.

### EARS

Five drafts bundled two responses and were split. That is the whole reason this repo adopted EARS: a bundled requirement can be half-implemented and still read as met.

`FR-D-017` carried through unchanged — no fifth navigation destination.

### Next

`/speckit.clarify` if anything reads ambiguous, then `/speckit.plan` on `impl/nextjs`.

author: jeeneetardshelp-cpu2027
body:
## The gap

`migration list` reports three pending migrations. The table described one. The
two undescribed files now have rows, written from reading them rather than
guessing:

- `20260902164500_search_gap_log.sql`
- `20260902170000_search_aliases.sql`

Every file in `supabase/migrations/` now has a row.

## The one that matters

`20260902164500_search_gap_log.sql` carries a **DO NOT APPLY YET** banner, and the
README said nothing about it.

It creates a table storing the text of searches that returned nothing. The design
is careful: no user id, no session, no IP, no fingerprint, no referrer, and the RPC
takes no identity parameter, so no row can be joined to a person. The hold is not
about the design. It is that this is a new server-side path carrying free text a
student typed, and `src/PrivacyPolicy.jsx` does not name the table yet. Whether the
log should exist at all is an owner decision recorded in
`docs/legal_release_inputs.md`, and `src/searchGapPrivacyContract.test.js` holds the
banner in place until the disclosure lands.

Applying it before then would collect data the policy says is not collected. This
audience is largely under 18.

## The consequence no single row shows

Push takes **every** pending migration in timestamp order, and the held file sorts
first. So there is no `db push` that applies the two search migrations behind it
without also applying the search gap log.

The entire pending queue is blocked behind an owner decision. That is called out
under the table, including the two ways someone might try to route around it —
`--include-all`, or renumbering a file to jump the queue — and why neither is the
answer. The ordering is not the obstacle; the undisclosed data collection is.

## Verification

- `src/steeringDocs.test.js`, `src/searchGapPrivacyContract.test.js` and
  `src/legalTruth.test.js`: 26 passed.
- `npm run lint`: clean.
- Every migration filename now matches a row in the table.

Documentation only. No code, no SQL, nothing applied.

利用者報告「化学組成をつなごうとしたら ID が縦軸単位になっていて、データセットを見たら**全部の ID が縦軸単位**。DOI になる時もあります」の真因と修正。

## 真因

表示メタを**述語 IRI だけ**で引いていた（`_ir_predicate_display`: `meta.setdefault(iri, {}).update(extra)` ＝ 述語ごとの**最後の勝ち**）。値のカタログには `ensure_value_catalog_labels` が**全部に** `rdfs:label` を書くので、これは例外ではなく**既定**で起きる。IR の並び順で勝者が変わるのが「DOI になる時もある」。

局所再現（修正前）:

```
CompositionMap -> ['縦軸単位']   # 期待: 化学組成
UnitYMap       -> ['縦軸単位']
```

## 修正

1. `_ir_display_entries` に 1 パス化し、**行の表示は (述語, 列) で引く**。map 名（`CompositionMap`）も subject テンプレート（CURIE→展開 IRI）も RML 化で書き換わるが、**列の参照名は残る**ので命名規約に依存しない結合鍵になる
2. 述語ごとの全体像に落ちてよいのは、**その述語の束縛列が 1 つだけ**のときに限る（複数列に束縛された述語で落とすと、まさに他の map のラベルを借りる）
3. つながり画面の `_crosswalk_predicate_labels` は、同じ述語に別ラベルが複数あれば**黙る** — この関数の約束は docstring どおり「設計が選んだ言葉を言う、さもなくば黙る」で、借りた言葉はその約束を破る（実機で候補が『縦軸単位 / 化学組成…』と名乗った）

## 検証

- **実データ 3 件で前後不変**（starrydata-curves 2 版・元素表 — 既に正しかった表示は 1 文字も変わらない）
- api 601 passed（新 3 本: 述語衝突／曖昧述語は借りない／つながり側は黙る）、ruff 緑

利用者の最新設計 `starrydata-curves-9ee6477e` を実物確認したところ、x/y が `json_array`+`xsd:double`、project_names が `json_array` で **v0.37/38 の JSON 展開が実配線で作動**していました。列の重複束縛もゼロです（スクショの「横軸データ ×2」は、その版より前の下書きと見られます）。

author: silasfelinus
body:
### Task
conductor/t-139: `check_pr_merged_drift.py` re-verifies only the first candidate PR it flags, so a task reclaimed and re-progressed after an earlier reconciliation can hide a second, later drift (kind: software)

### What changed / what I produced
- `scripts/check_pr_merged_drift.py`:
  - `scan_in_progress_tasks` now also returns each task's `note` text (needed for the new pass below; harmless extra dict key, no consumer asserted an exact key set).
  - New `BARE_PR_REF_RE` + `find_all_pr_refs()`: extracts every PR reference from free text, combining the existing alias-based `"<alias> PR #<n>"` phrasing with a new bare `"<owner>/<repo>#<n>"` form (the shape `implementation_pr` itself uses, and how a note often cites a follow-up PR).
  - New `find_field_stale_findings()`: for each task already confirmed merged via its `implementation_pr` field (pass 0), scans its own title+note for any OTHER PR reference that is (a) merged and (b) title-confirmed as implementing this exact `<project>/<task-id>` (same title-match bar the authoritative search pass already uses, so a note that merely quotes the PR whose kaizen suggestion *filed* the task doesn't false-positive). A match means the recorded field is likely stale.
  - Wired into `check_drift()` as a new `field_possibly_stale` result bucket, `render()`'s output, and `main()`'s exit-code contract (shares exit 1 with `high`/`remaining_scope_resolved` — a genuine drift signal, not a bare weak one).
  - Deliberately scoped to `field_findings` only (never `field_unresolved`/malformed-field tasks), and best-effort: a failed lookup on an *extra* note reference is silently skipped rather than downgrading an already-resolved task into `unresolved`. This preserves every existing "field-present task must not make [more/further] API calls" test invariant.
- `tests/test_check_pr_merged_drift.py`: 1 existing test updated for the new `field_possibly_stale` dict key (`test_check_drift_clean_when_no_evidence_either_way`), 17 new tests covering `find_all_pr_refs`, `find_field_stale_findings` directly, `check_drift`-level tests modeling the exact incident shape from t-139's note (interface-vision/t-104: field says kind_robots#2301, note also cites a later title-confirmed merged kind_robots#2303) plus its two guardrails (a note reference whose title doesn't match the task is ignored; a failed extra lookup is silently skipped, not added to `unresolved`), and two `render()` tests for the new output block.

### How I verified
- `PYTHONPATH="$(pwd):$(pwd)/scripts" pytest tests/test_check_pr_merged_drift.py -q` — 59/59 pass (45 original + 1 updated + 13 new... actually 59 total, see below).
- `PYTHONPATH="$(pwd):$(pwd)/scripts" pytest tests/ -q` — full repo suite: 1585 passed, 1 skipped, 35 subtests passed, no failures.
- `python3 -m py_compile scripts/check_pr_merged_drift.py tests/test_check_pr_merged_drift.py` — clean.
- Manually traced the exact incident shape from the task note (field=#2301, note also cites #2303, #2303's title contains the task id) against the new pass to confirm it fires, and confirmed the two documented false-positive risks (kaizen-filing-PR note reference; a network failure on the extra lookup) are both suppressed.

Note on running tests in this sandbox: the isolated `pytest` tool needed `uv tool install pytest --with pyyaml --force` (the documented PyYAML gap in AGENTS.md) *and* `PYTHONPATH` extended to include `scripts/` itself, since `scripts/consume_art_queue.py`'s bare-import fallback (`import consume_art_queue_core`) needs that directory on `sys.path` directly under pytest's own import mechanism, even though plain `python3` resolves it fine via cwd. Neither of these is new to this PR — flagging in case it's worth a `pytest.ini`/`conftest.py` fix for the next session that hits it fresh (kaizen candidate below).

### Stakes
reversible

### Flags for Reviewer
- I chose to add the new finding to a separate `field_possibly_stale` bucket rather than folding it into `high`, so `high`'s existing one-finding-per-task shape from pass 0/1 stays unchanged for any downstream consumer. Both share the same exit-code tier (1) and are rendered as separate, clearly-labeled blocks — open to folding them together if you'd prefer a single list.
- The bare `owner/repo#N` regex is intentionally *not* restricted to `REPO_ALIASES` (mirrors `IMPLEMENTATION_PR_RE`'s existing reasoning) — it'll technically match a non-PR "word/word#number" shape in prose, but false positives there die at the `gh_pr` lookup (404/unrelated) or the title-match check, so I didn't think a tracked-repo restriction was worth the extra maintenance surface. Say if you'd rather scope it.

### Kaizen suggestion
`pytest.ini` sets `pythonpath = .` but that doesn't cover `scripts/`'s own bare-import fallback pattern (`scripts/consume_art_queue.py`'s `import consume_art_queue_core` line) under the isolated `pytest` tool's import mechanism — every session that runs this suite fresh has to rediscover the `PYTHONPATH="$(pwd):$(pwd)/scripts"` workaround by hand (on top of the already-documented PyYAML gap). Worth either adding `scripts` to `pytool `pythonpath` in `pytest.ini`, or having `consume_art_queue.py`'s fallback import insert `Path(__file__).parent` onto `sys.path` itself before the bare import.

### Notes for reviewer
This is a conductor-repo-only software task — no cross-repo target, the conductor PR itself is the full implementation. Task claimed via `claim_task.py` (session `claude-20260902T134524Z-cond-t139`), status set to `review` via `close_task.py` on a separate `close/conductor-t-139-...` branch/PR before opening this one.

author: danielh2018
body:
## What changed, and why

Backblaze's storage-cap alert fired on 2026-09-02 at 75%, with the transaction budget nowhere near its limit. `longhorn-backup-tiering.md` prices every decision in transactions and says nothing about the free tier's other cap, 10 GB of stored bytes. Three facts had to be worked out live, under an alert, and none of them was written down anywhere:

- **Deleting files inside a volume does not shrink its backup.** Removing `/config/backups` from valheim-config took the filesystem from 1.33 GB to 58.6 MB and left `actualSize` at 4.26 GB. A filesystem delete unmaps nothing underneath, so the next backup still references those blocks.
- **`fstrim` on the node's mount is what releases them,** and only partly: it freed 2.1 GiB, taking `actualSize` to 3.61 GB rather than to 58.6 MB, because two snapshots that retained backups are made of still hold 1.53 GB and 2.02 GB. The rest returns as `retain: 2` rotates them out.
- **A B2 delete does not move the billed figure for seven days.** The bucket's one lifecycle rule is `daysFromHidingToDeleting: 7`. Deleting the eleven seed backups took live bytes from 7.59 GB to 6.14 GB and left the console reading 7.59 GB.

The new section records all three with the measurements and the commands.

## The correction

The retention section called `longhorn-reap-orphan-backups.sh` the only owner of unowned backups. A seed carries no `RecurringJob` label at all, which the reaper reads as the current tier's own — its dry run listed zero reapable against eleven live seeds. `drop_seed_backups.yml` (merged in #784) is their owner, and the section now says so.

## Why the tier map needed a line

Rule 2 in the opening already names "rewritten zips" as the thing that costs. valheim-config was added after the 2026-08-12 audit that produced that rule, so nobody had applied it there. The row now records the diversion, matching how tdarr's `Backups/` zips are already described.

## Rejected

- **A memory file instead.** `MEMORY.md` is over its 85-line cap, and this belongs with the doc that already carries the transaction axis. Splitting the two axes across two stores is how the second one gets missed again.
- **A new doc.** The reasoning only makes sense next to the transaction budget it contrasts with.

## Services touched

None — docs only.

## Deploy

- [ ] Deployed after merge (`./scripts/deploy.sh --changed <pre-merge-SHA>` from `/home/ubuntu/server`)
- [ ] Deliberately deferred — reason:
- [x] Nothing to deploy (docs-, test-, or `tasks/`-only)

## Verification

- [ ] `uv run python scripts/diagnostics/probe.py health <svc>` passed — n/a, docs-only
- [x] Exercised the changed behaviour itself — every figure in the new section was measured in this session before it was written: the `fstrim` output, the `actualSize` before and after, the snapshot sizes from the Snapshot CRs, the lifecycle rule from `b2_list_buckets`, and the live-versus-hidden byte split from `b2_list_file_versions`.

`prek run --all-files` is clean, Vale included:

```
Prose style (Vale, scoped to ADRs + every top-level docs page)...........Passed
Run Python unit tests (toposort + monitor-bridge + readonly-hook + smoke + gitops)...Passed
```

Vale rejected `reapable`, `unmaps` and `filesystem's` as misspellings; all three are added to the Homelab vocabulary rather than written around, since the first is the reaper script's own term and the second is the precise word for what a trim does.

## Blast radius

- [ ] This is a **broad** change
- [ ] New check, guard, or probe

author: roomote-roomote[bot]
body:
> ​<!-- roomote:pr-attribution:start -->Opened on behalf of @mrubens.<!-- roomote:pr-attribution:end --> Follow up by mentioning @roomote-roomote, in [the web UI](https://roomote.roomote.ai/sessions/11f93d43-790b-4a6a-b872-d2a76ed8bb80?utm_source=github-comment&utm_medium=link&utm_campaign=standard), or in [Slack](https://app.slack.com/archives/C0BDXC7FWBY/p1788354727731199?thread_ts=1788354727.731199&cid=C0BDXC7FWBY).

## What changed

- Extend replay-safe Fast inference recovery beyond the previous six-retry episode and 12-retry progress cap. Durable retries now continue for a persisted 15-minute provider-outage horizon, with a 128-attempt guard for pathological near-zero delays.
- Persist the first provider-recovery timestamp and carry it with the retry count through delayed queue handoffs, so process restarts preserve both the deadline and backoff progression instead of resetting recovery.
- Bound every resumed provider prompt by the remaining horizon. A retry whose wait would cross the deadline terminates instead of scheduling beyond it.
- Preserve the original human request when automatic recovery truly exhausts and replace the generic provider dead end with an actionable continuation message. Auth, credits, unavailable-model, content-filter, and explicit non-retryable provider outcomes still terminate immediately.

## Why this change was made

Short bounded retry bursts still let meaningful transient provider outages end an otherwise replay-safe Fast turn. Users then received a contextless generic error even though the original request was already durably admitted and safe to resume.

## Impact

Replay-safe turns now use the existing exponential delays of 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, and 32s, then a 60s ceiling with 0-20% positive jitter; rate limits continue to honor provider `Retry-After`. The 15-minute wall-clock horizon normally binds first, while the 128-attempt cap protects against malformed near-zero provider schedules. Turns that performed non-replayable side effects keep the existing in-process safety path and are never handed to another owner.

The full Fast-agent suite, relevant durable queue/event suites, repository lint, fast typechecks, and Knip pass. Browser proof was not captured before the proof deadline; this provider lifecycle has no stable browser state, and the behavior is covered by focused service, persistence, and queue regressions.

## Depends on

- #2040 supplies durable retry parking, delayed wakeups, and retry-notice continuity. This stacked PR adds the multi-minute outage policy and actionable exhaustion behavior.

author: felipcsousa
body:
## Onda 3.5 — credibilidade de campo

Corrige os cinco problemas encontrados no field test em 4 repositórios reais
(tripkit, forkclaw, lumpfish, siftos), na ordem sugerida: bugs cirúrgicos que
destruíam a validação primeiro, depois o maior ganho de recall, por fim o
caminho do usuário.

### #32 — GOLD_REGRESSION falsos (P0, bug)
O check de regressão aplicava só o gold, sem o hidden verifier — PRs que
legitimamente atualizavam testes existentes (expected values) eram
rejeitados mesmo com base+verifier+gold passando tudo. Agora o regression
aplica gold + verifier; `CheckSpec` ganha descriptions explícitas por check
e as mensagens de skip derivam o atributo de config do getter.

### #33 — crash no commit inicial com árvore vazia (P0, bug)
PR cujo base é o commit inicial (adiciona o repo inteiro) produzia tar de 0
entradas → `tarfile.ReadError` abortava o build inteiro. Agora: guard em
`build_task_package` (árvore vazia → `ReconstructionError`), o build
persiste a rejeição `HISTORY_UNSUPPORTED` **por PR** e continua com os
demais candidatos; `WorkspaceManager` endurecido contra tar corrompido.

### #31 — squash-merges invisíveis (P0, maior ganho de recall)
`merged_prs` agora faz duas passadas na mesma janela: merge commits
(`Merge pull request #N`) e squash (subject terminando em `(#N)`; o commit
É o PR: base = parent, head = merge = commit), dedup por número com
merge-commit vencendo. `analyze` mostra **Merge style** e **Recall vs
GitHub** (ground truth via `gh pr list --state merged`, mesmo clock/janela)
e avisa quando há squash minado por subject ou recall < 70% (rebase-merge
permanece invisível ao git — nomeado no aviso, não escondido). Era o caso
forkclaw: 13 squash PRs invisíveis; tripkit: 3,7% de recall.

### #35 — honestidade do feedback (P1, bug)
Exit code 1 em "no valid tasks" confirmado correto no código atual (relato
de campo veio de release antiga) e **travado com testes de regressão CLI**
(build/refresh/build-before-analyze). Label mentirosa "Validated eval
candidates" → "Candidates passing hard filters". Novo
`repobench candidates --show <PR>` junta candidates⋈tasks⋈task_validations
e imprime cada check com result + tails de output — o diagnóstico sai do
sqlite. A mensagem de erro do build aponta para o comando.

### #34 — monorepo/polyglot (P1, enhancement)
Detecção de subprojetos um nível abaixo da raiz (`backend|api|server`,
`apps|packages|services/*`) compartilhando a implementação da raiz
(`_detect_in`), com regra npm honesta em todos os sites: `npm test` só é
sugerido quando `package.json` declara `scripts.test` (bug lumpfish:
sugestão inexistente = BASELINE_BROKEN garantido). Novo knob
`project.cwd` (relativo, sem `..`) faz install/test/regression rodarem no
subprojeto — valida no `_run_spec`, runner no install/verifier; o harness
continua na raiz do workspace (agente vê o repo inteiro). Substitui o
impossível `cd X && Y` mantendo argv puro. Doctor/init listam cada
subprojeto com hints e nunca auto-selecionam cwd.

## Verificação

- Suíte completa: **458 → 498 testes** (40 novos), hermética, verde.
- Cada issue implementada por um subagente com revisão e commit por fase
  (A: #32+#33 · B: #31 · C: #35, #34).

Closes #31, closes #32, closes #33, closes #34, closes #35

body:
…stagiaire

Un compte à la fois stagiaire ET rôle bureau configurable (FORMATEUR/SECRÉTARIAT/AUDITEUR) se voyait refuser la signature d'un document dans son espace stagiaire : « Accès en lecture seule : modification non autorisée pour cette rubrique. »

Cause : enforceSectionMode (garde-fou du MENU backoffice) rattache tout POST /documents/* à la rubrique /stagiaires. Or /stagiaires est en lecture seule pour ces rôles → le POST /documents/:id/sign de SA PROPRE signature tombait sous le garde, alors même que signDocument l'autorise (propriété du document : l.user_id = req.user.id).

Signer est un acte de PARTICIPANT, pas une écriture backoffice de la rubrique. On l'exempte donc du garde (comme l'exception préexistante comptabilite/revenus). L'autorisation réelle reste celle de signDocument (propriétaire, ou rôle signataire) — aucune brèche : un stagiaire ne peut toujours signer que SON document ; créer/supprimer un document et le lien de signature partageable (/sign-link, acte bureau) restent cadenassés sous /stagiaires.

Test signature-deux-casquettes : /sign exempté, /sign-link + création/suppression gardés, exception revenus préservée. 718 tests, 0 échec.

body:
V227 repository hygiene and dependency-safety follow-up on the exact current main.

Root cause carried forward from superseded PR #202: Angular runtime and build packages have exact peer relationships, so isolated Dependabot updates can produce npm ERESOLVE when @angular/* packages move at different patch levels.

Scope is intentionally narrow:
- add one `angular-framework` Dependabot group for all `@angular/*` patch/minor updates
- preserve the existing production-runtime and frontend-toolchain groups
- make `.github/dependabot.yml` changes trigger the canonical professional quality gate, so dependency-governance edits cannot bypass CI silently
- no application runtime, payment, EFT, Supabase, customer, admin or production data behavior changes

Exact base at branch creation: `04b02e0373e47a8d047a79223f4681beb22ae061`.
Exact head: `d58bc02d7507544caafe5a763bdd1665d62a1dee`.

After this replacement is verified and merged, stale PR #202 will be closed as superseded to keep the repository clean.

author: aleksandradovgopolova-boop
body:
## Зачем

У кита две «двери» в один код: пакет `ai_ops_kit/` и плоский слой `tools/` (114 shim'ов, которые лишь переадресуют в пакет). Отсюда вечная путаница «где настоящий код». Ревью пометило это HIGH-долгом. Решение владельца — снести `tools/`, но при подготовке выяснилось, что `tools/` — **живой контракт входа дочки** (её обёртка и доки зовут `.ai/managed/tools/*.py`), поэтому мгновенный снос ломает установленные дочки.

Правильный путь — **деприкация перед мажором**: этот PR (3.x) переводит ВСЕХ на пакетный путь, не ломая старый; физический снос `tools/` — отдельным PR в v4.0.

## Что сделано (не ломающая правка — `tools/` ещё на месте, оба пути работают)

- **Вход дочки** (`templates/runtime/ai-ops-entry.sh`) зовёт `ai_ops_kit/cli/ai_ops_cli.py` напрямую (+PYTHONPATH), как обёртка самого кита.
- **Внутренние ссылки** кита переведены на пакет: `verification_tiers` (список критической инфраструктуры), gate-runnables (`# runnable:`), mutation-probes (проба обёртки + путь `mutation_probe`).
- **Доки/скрипты**: QUICKSTART, child-repo guide, qualification-runbook, check-clean-install, check-upgrade-path — на `ai_ops_kit/<pkg>/*`.
- **Побочный фикс реального дефекта**: `ALWAYS_FULL_PATTERNS` указывал на shim-пути → правка настоящего `execution_pipeline`/`orchestrator` могла не поднять полную проверку. Теперь указывает на реальные файлы.

## Проверка

Полный быстрый набор зелёный (5133 passed), контрактные (164), own-medicine OK (пути гейтов существуют), проба обёртки совпадает с шаблоном, скрипты валидны. Managed-файлов не добавлено.

Следующий PR (v4.0): физический снос `tools/` + `alias_bytes`-бюджет + alias-тесты + `VERSION`→4.0.0 + MIGRATION_GUIDE.

Files #327, #328, #329 from findings. Dispositions posted on sixteen open issues.

## The product owner re-aimed the charter

Given directly on 2026-09-02, quoted in § D456 rather than paraphrased:

> These are good goals, but not at the expense of game play.

**`charter P2`'s refusal test could only ever fail in one direction.** It asks whether a change makes the product say *less*, so every change that added refusal text passed it and no change could fail it. The pillar has been working as a ratchet, and it had been ratcheting onto the surfaces a player actually reads. **#208 and #211 are that ratchet reported from the other end**, by people who could see the result and not the cause.

Three changes, none of which softens a figure:

1. **P2 gains a second test.** *Can the player still play?* A refusal that is correct and stops the loop is a defect. Refusals may not accumulate into a wall, take the space the next action needs, or require a statistical vocabulary before they can be acted on.
2. **§ 2 states that a pillar is not the reason the game exists.** A change satisfying all five and leaving the game less worth playing is refused by the same review that would refuse a softened figure, and the resolution is never to weaken the pillar and never to accept the loss quietly.
3. **`charter S6` is reworded**, from *state why the simulator refused a number* to *say what a refusal means for your next change, and no tester is stopped by one*.

**The S6 trade is written into the charter rather than dressed as a strengthening.** It is weaker on articulation — a tester who says *it will not give me an average yet, so I should clear the backlog first* now passes — and strictly harder on blocking, because one tester abandoning the loop fails it outright where four of ten could previously be stopped. `charter P1` and `charter S8` are untouched, and S8 is the criterion with the working instrument, so the honesty commitment did not move.

One sentence is **withdrawn rather than reworded**: `docs/30` said the refusal *"is the thing this product is actually for"*. A tower-management game is for the session; refusing an unsupportable figure is a constraint the session is built under.

`docs/32` § 4.3 already argued this in miniature — *a refusal and a miss may not share a visual treatment* — and needed no amendment. The charter needed to catch up with it.

## The corpus, measured on the integrated tree — both moves are zero

§ D457, and it discharges what wave M's ledger left owing. Base at `39c1f1c` re-measured first in a detached worktree, where it reproduced its published row **exactly in both tiers**, the sixth consecutive wave.

| | base `39c1f1c` | integrated `aea42b5` | move |
|---|---|---|---|
| always-on strings | 575 999 | **575 999** | **0** |
| deep strings | 718 633 | **718 633** | **0** |
| surfaces, both tiers | 55 / 56 | **55 / 56** | **0** |
| cases · simulations · failing cases | 49 / 60 · 606 / 4 710 · 0 | **unmoved** | **0** |

**Wave M's zero is arithmetic, not luck.** #283 added two `DESIGNER_COPY` keys, which `surfaces.ts` iterates generically, and deleted two `DESIGNER_ABSENCES` entries, which the build-notes adapter seeds. +2 − 2 = 0 per case, so 49 × 0 and 60 × 0.

**Wave L's zero is the one worth reading, because I got it wrong first.** I wrote *"the row is stale by two waves"* into a scheduled check-in before measuring, reasoning that `CLAUDE.md` was last touched by wave K while wave L had edited the corpus's own surface file. Measured, wave L moved both tiers by zero and the row was accurate. A row that *looks* stale and a row that *is* stale are different claims, and only one can be settled by reading commit history.

**The forecast wave M published was wrong in the worse direction.** It predicted *a small per-case constant*; the constant is zero. § D454 recorded forecasts short by one string per case. Predicting motion where there is none teaches the next reader to treat a correct zero as a failed measurement.

Surface **sets** were diffed rather than counts compared: identical in both tiers, nothing added or removed, and the deep tier's one-surface lead is still exactly `campaign/judge.ts#judgeStage`.

## The blocked set, re-read for the first time

Four read-only lanes checked whether snapshot C's blockers still held. **The sorting was wrong in every group**, and all four lanes found their issue's recorded state wrong.

| snapshot C said | measured |
|---|---|
| blocked on a server — six issues | **the cluster does not exist.** Complete deployed API, 329 passing tests, and #179 closed 2026-09-01. **#221 is unblocked and gates four other things** |
| blocked on a tester — four issues | **one of the four is.** #211's gate was lifted by a human on 2026-08-26, three days before the snapshot asserting it was uncloseable |
| blocked on a ruling never built | #123 holds and is narrower than filed. **#275's blocker merged 2026-08-26** and it sat blocked for a week |

**#237, the only P0, rests on a refuted premise**: 3 passing / 14 owned / 4 planned, and all **40** named test files exist. Its own second criterion was satisfied before it was filed. Posted with a measured rescope; it needs a ruling, not a lane.

I fetched #211's comment thread myself rather than relaying the lane's report, because a claim that contradicts a snapshot and re-aims an issue is worth checking directly.

## Two register corrections, both in the same direction

**`RISKS.md` R45** is new: *a blocker that clears is not an event anything watches for.* Realised three times in one wave, and the observation was written down by snapshot C on 2026-08-29 and never built — R42 with a process note as its subject. #329 owns it.

**R42's own citation was stale** and is corrected: it cited a `docs/16` sentence that exists nowhere in the tree. The register that tracks stale claims was carrying one.

## Verified

`npx tsc -b` clean · `validation/documentation.test.ts` + `citations.test.ts` **35 passed** · the four suites that read the changed documents (`refusalsAreCurrent`, `buildNotes`, `honesty/faults`, `honesty/honesty`) **4 files, 63 passed, 1 skipped** · corpus measured on the integrated tree, both tiers in one sitting, base re-measured first.

No code changed, so the full platform suites are CI's to run rather than a claim made here.

author: hotlong
body:
Fixes #7256

## What the card measured

cloud's control plane lands a signed-in customer on `/_console/apps/cloud_control/page/welcome` — the app declared with `isDefault: true`, whose first navigation item is the Welcome page. The top bar's logo then said `/_console/home`: the ENVIRONMENT layer's launcher (ADR-0075), where "Build an app" and "Start from a template" act on an environment the control plane does not have, and "Your apps" lists the control plane's own internal management apps ("Cloud", "Account"). One product, two homes, two voices.

## Premise re-verified against `origin/main` (`63b4e0e71`)

Both producers the dispatch predicted are real, and are the two named below:

- the landing: `apps/console/src/components/RootLandingRedirect.tsx` — `resolveLandingPath()` reads `app.isDefault`, which cloud's `CLOUD_APP` declares (`packages/app-cloud/src/cloud.app.ts`, with `nav_home` → the `welcome` page first in `navigation`);
- the logo: `packages/app-shell/src/layout/AppHeader.tsx:419` — a literal `Link to="/home"`.

Three further affordances carried the same literal: `UnifiedSidebar`'s "Home" nav row and its mobile-sheet Home row, and `AppSidebar`'s app-switcher "Home" entry. All four now read `useHomePath()`.

## The posture signal is the declaration, not a hostname or a product name

`resolveDeclaredHomePath()` reads `app.isDefault` and nothing else. `cloud_control` appears nowhere in the shared bundle: re-introducing that name is precisely what retiring `PREFERRED_APPS = ['cloud_control']` removed, and hostname sniffing is ruled out by the card. A deployment that declares no landing is unaffected — every Home affordance still resolves to `/home`.

## The trade-off the card asked me to state: what becomes of the generic home

After this change the control-plane chrome offers **no** route into `/home`: the logo and all three Home rows resolve to the declared landing. So the card's alternative half — hide "Cloud"/"Account" by role and drop the environment-side action cards — is not owed here; there is no control-plane entry point left to sanitise.

What stays reachable, named rather than quietly omitted:

- typing `/_console/home` by hand;
- the "this app is gone / access denied" recovery redirects in `console/AppContent.tsx` and `console/ConsoleShell.tsx`, plus `AiChatPage`'s home button, `StudioDesignSurface`'s close, and `AcceptInvitationPage`.

Those are error-recovery paths, not Home affordances. Retargeting them moves a `/home` expectation that ~a dozen existing fixtures pin, with a blast radius nobody has measured — deliberately left out of this card rather than folded in.

## Why `/`'s resolver keeps its own reading of the declaration

The first version of this PR had `resolveLandingPath` import `resolveDeclaredHomePath`, so the declaration had exactly one reader. It turned 11 tests red: `RootLandingRedirect.route.test.tsx` and `SetupRoute.test.tsx` replace `@object-ui/app-shell` wholesale with a chrome-free hand-rolled mock, and adding the symbol to that mock would have put the FIXTURE under test instead of the shipped policy.

So the resolver is unchanged, and what forbids drift is a behavioural matrix comparing **both shipped answers** — `apps/console/src/components/landingHomeParity-7256.test.ts`, 8 deployment shapes plus two drift canaries (which of several declarations wins; a nameless declaration). That is strictly stronger than a source scan of either file.

## Tests

Three new files, 20 + 8 assertions:

- `packages/app-shell/src/utils/__tests__/homePath.test.ts` — the policy;
- `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/__tests__/useHomePath.test.tsx` — the hook's answer, including the in-flight app list;
- `packages/app-shell/src/__tests__/homeAffordancesFollowDeclaration-7256.test.ts` — a source scan pinning that no chrome affordance re-types the literal;
- `apps/console/src/components/landingHomeParity-7256.test.ts` — the parity matrix above.

**Reverse verification** (fix committed first, then mutated): restoring `to={homePath}` to `to="/home"` in `AppHeader.tsx` turned the scan red in the expected direction — `Tests 2 failed | 6 passed (8)`, both failures on the "top-bar brand logo" cases. The mutation was confirmed on disk before the run (injected-literal count 0→1, removed-expression count 1→0, blob hash `62364926` vs HEAD `1ea6f4dc`); the restore leg was confirmed by hash equality with the HEAD blob and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

## Gates run at `6147b3c86`

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` — exit 0 (its script is `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the new test files ARE covered)
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console type-check` — exit 0
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell build` — exit 0, `dist completeness: 1 package(s) complete (902 emitted files verified)`; `@object-ui/console` build exit 0
- vitest, affected surface (`app-shell` layout / console / utils / hooks / __tests__ + `apps/console/src/components`): `Test Files 199 passed`, `Tests 2151 passed` besides the pre-existing red below
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell --filter @object-ui/console lint` — exit 0, 0 errors (216 pre-existing warnings)
- `check:control-bytes`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:self-import`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:eager-closure`, `check:side-effects-array`, `check:esm-specifiers`, `check:readme-exports`, `check:entry-guard`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check-changeset-no-major` — all printed their own OK line

Lint narrowing: run per PACKAGE (`eslint .` from each package, i.e. eslint's own config-derived population for both packages this diff touches, not my guess at a file list); the repo's flat config enables no type-aware linting (no `project` / `projectService`), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it does not contain.

## Pre-existing reds, not caused by this diff

- `packages/app-shell/src/console/__tests__/anonSeedScope-5746.enumeration.test.tsx` — 7 red. Ablation: reverting all six of my modified source files to `63b4e0e71` (confirmed on disk, `homePath` reference count 0,0,0) leaves the same 7 failures. Already filed as objectui#7271 (Node 26 localStorage probe).
- `packages/auth/src/__tests__/signOut-client-cache-purge-5198.test.tsx:5777` — 1 red, same family. `packages/auth` declares no dependency on `@object-ui/app-shell` and this diff contains no file in that package, so it cannot be reached from here.

## Changeset

`.changeset/7256-chrome-home-follows-declared-landing.md`, `patch` on `@object-ui/app-shell` + `@object-ui/console`.

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

Closes #155
Parent: #137
Reconciliation: `04_개발/docs/BACKEND_HANDOFF_RECONCILIATION_20260902.md`

## What this adds
- migration `028_community_comment_replies.sql`
  - nullable `parent_comment_id` on canonical `community_comments`
  - composite parent FK enforcing same comment post + complex
  - self-parent guard
  - reply lookup index

- contract test wired into backend `npm run check`

No parallel reply table or moderation model is introduced. The relation is generic; no product-specific maximum nesting depth is hard-coded.

- UI redesign
- mention/tag notifications
- comment/reply reaction policy
- operator scope changes
- owner-policy HOLD decisions
- production deploy/migration

Exact-head Backend CI (including `community-replies-postgres-lifecycle`), Pre-Infra Integration CI, and Live Release Gate must all be green before squash merge.
