author: lhns
body:
A C++ build on a remote-docker share dies at the linker, verbatim from a
real workspace:

```
/usr/bin/ld: cmTC_438e8: final close failed: Stale file handle
```

**The shape is the diagnosis.** That is CMake's throwaway "does the
compiler work" test:

- **Compiling succeeds** — the `.o` is created, written and closed on the
  share.
- **Linking dies at the final `close()`.**

So writing to the export works, and it is specifically `ld` *finishing* an
output file that does not. That makes it a file-handle problem, not a
write problem.

## Why this PR is only a reproduction

Nothing in the suite had ever built a binary on a share, which is how this
shipped. CI is the only place it can run — it needs a real kernel NFS
client — so the reproduction goes up on its own and runs before any fix is
written.

The section asserts the two steps **separately**, with distinct exit
codes, because the bug passes the first and fails the second; a boolean
could not tell them apart and would have reported "the build failed".

**If it passes, that is information rather than success.** CI runs a dind
on the same machine, while the report came from a workspace on another
host. That difference would then be the next thing to chase, and the
section says so in place.

## What I ruled out before writing it

| candidate | verdict |
|---|---|
| symlinks unsupported | **No.** NFSv3 has SYMLINK/READLINK and go-billy implements them |
| file locking | **No.** `nolock` is in the mount options (`core/workspace/export.go:304`) |
| handle-cache eviction | **No.** `handleCacheSize = 1_000_000` against a test touching ~5 files |

## The leading hypothesis, for whoever picks this up

go-nfs maps a handle to a **path, not an inode**, and
`helpers.CachingHandler.InvalidateHandle` **deletes it outright** on REMOVE
(`nfs_onremove.go:61`) and RENAME (`nfs_onrename.go:90`). A real NFS server
keeps a handle valid for a file that is open, which is what makes
unlink-while-open and write-then-rename work.

`core-client/nfsserve/handles.go` currently argues that ESTALE below the
share root is safe because *"Linux retries a path lookup once on ESTALE
with LOOKUP_REVAL"*. **That is true for a lookup and false for an
already-open descriptor** — the fd names a handle and the kernel cannot
silently re-resolve it. That invariant needs correcting whatever the cause
turns out to be.

Two further findings, neither of them this bug, recorded so they are not
lost: `CachingHandler.FromHandle` walks *every live handle* on every call,
which with a 1M limit is a real cliff on a large tree; and hard links are
not served at all, since `Link` is in go-nfs's optional `UnixChange`
interface while the export is a plain `billy.Filesystem`.

author: kevintseng
body:
Found dogfooding 4.8.3 against the real graph: the same agent was receiving
messages under two different spellings of its own name, into two inboxes, and
only one of them was ever read.

## The verdict per pair — three of the four brief hypotheses were wrong

**Pair A — `/root` (20 deliveries) vs `root` (25): SAME agent. Repaired.**

- Every row of both spellings carries `sender_host = 'codex-mcp-client'`.
- The `sender` field flipped in the *same* transition, under exactly the
  `/root/` prefix: `/root/full-board-scan-luna` ↔
  `full_board_candidate_scan_luna`. One caller's convention changed; it is not
  two agents.
- Both appear across the same four projects, interleaved on the same days, and
  every receipt on both has `actor == recipient` — the same agent received and
  acknowledged under each.
- `/root` is an absolute path, and `getProjectName` cannot return one at any of
  its three layers. It is a caller spelling its own home directory where its
  name belonged.

**Pair B — `session_X` vs `claude-code:session_X`: NOT the same. Deliberately
left apart.**

The brief's hypothesis ("a prefixing convention that changed") is **falsified**:
`grep -rn 'claude-code:'` over src, dist, hooks, skills, docs and tests returns
nothing, and `git log -S 'claude-code:' --all` returns **no commits**. The
convention never existed in this product, so there is nothing to normalise
against. Corroborating: they were used with *different* `target_kind` (which is
part of the fetch key), and **neither carries a single receipt**, so the
split-inbox symptom is not even demonstrable here. Stripping the prefix would
merge a legitimate `claude-code:reviewer` with a different agent named
`reviewer`.

**Pair C — `memesh` (38) vs `memesh-llm-memory` (28): SAME project, and the
repair still does not merge it.**

`gh api repos/PCIRCLE-AI/memesh-llm-memory` answers `PCIRCLE-AI/memesh` —
GitHub's own redirect proves one repository, renamed. Layer 1 of
`getProjectName` yields `memesh` (this checkout's `remote.origin.url`), layer 2
yields the repo-root basename `memesh-llm-memory`; both are outputs of one
function for one working directory.

It is left alone on purpose. The evidence that proves it is a network call
against one owner's GitHub account, while a `runOnceMigration` fires unattended
from whatever directory the user's first post-upgrade open happens to be in.
Resolving it from `getProjectName(process.cwd())` would be mechanical **and
wrong** — the result would differ per user by accident. The owner-driven path
is made to work instead (below).

**Pair D — `/Users/ktseng/Developer/Projects/memesh-llm-memory` (1): provably
unreachable.** Repaired to its last segment.

## What changed

`src/core/agent-scope-id.ts` (new) owns three things: the canonical form (NFC +
trim), the absolute-path refusal (POSIX / Windows drive / UNC only —
`team/reviewer` is still accepted), and the one list of columns that hold a
routing identity.

**Not in `paths.ts`**, and that is the point: every `MessageSchema` variant
*requires* `project` and `executeAgentMessageAction` passes it straight
through. Messaging never derives a project from `getProjectName` — which is
also why pair C is unfixable there.

The scope set is `project`, `recipient`, `actor` — **the same set** the
boundary refuses, the repair rewrites, and the invariant watches. `sender` is
excluded everywhere: it is provenance, it keys no inbox, and it keys
`agent_message_idempotency (project, sender, idempotency_key)`.

Gated at the boundary (`MessageSchema` **and** `BriefingSchema`), again in core
before SQL, and at `memesh agent setup --project/--principal` — the fourth
producer of a routing identity, which previously wrote the host config
unvalidated. `briefing` counts the same inbox key and now asks in canonical
form; without that an NFD recipient would be told `0 unread` while `poll`
returned messages.

### `memesh kg rename-project` now moves the message scopes too

A project identity is half an inbox key as well as an entity tag, and renaming
only the tags is exactly why the pair-C split survives. It now counts and moves
the `project` column of the durable message tables in the same transaction,
still dry-run by default, still backing up before `--apply`, and no longer
stops at "no entities carry `project:<x>`" when only messages do.

## Repair, on a copy of the snapshot

```
rewrote 96 filesystem-path message scope value(s)
  (/Users/ktseng/Developer/Projects/memesh-llm-memory → memesh-llm-memory, /root → root);
96 joined an identity that already existed; 2 duplicate poll cursor(s) dropped.
```

Differential proof, repaired copy `ATTACH`ed to a pristine one:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| deliveries whose (project,recipient) changed | the `/root → root` and abs-path rewrites only — **and nothing else** |
| deliveries vanished / appeared | 0 |
| messages with changed sender, payload, or created_at | 0 |
| deliveries with changed target_kind or message_id | 0 |
| receipts changed | only the same triples |
| **pair C untouched** | `memesh` 38 → 38 |
| **pair B untouched** | 14 → 14, 17 → 17 |
| cursors | 65 → 63; for each dropped token the canonical row already existed |

Those two cursors are the one user-visible consequence: an agent still holding
them gets an explicit scope error on its next `poll --cursor` rather than a
silent restart. They are dropped because the unique index is on
(project, recipient, event_sequence) and the path-spelled token is unreachable
— `poll` now refuses the spelling it is bound to. Deliberate asymmetry: the
unattended repair drops such a cursor; the owner-driven `rename-project` leaves
a colliding row in place and counts it.

## Verification, at `2d2293ee`

```
node scripts/run-tests-isolated.mjs   -> exit=0
  Test Files  229 passed | 1 skipped (230)
  Tests  3297 passed | 11 skipped (3308)
npm run verify:release                -> exit=0   (all nine steps)
invariant vs unrepaired snapshot      -> exit=1   (names /root ×20 and the abs-path project across 4 tables)
invariant vs repaired copy            -> exit=0
```

Break-tests — mutate, run, restore, byte-identical restore asserted:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `isFilesystemPathScopeId` stops refusing absolute paths | exit=1 → restored exit=0 |
| `canonicalAgentScopeId` strips a `claude-code:` prefix | exit=1 → restored exit=0 |

The second is the **dangerous** direction — a canonicaliser that merges two
genuinely different agents — not the easy one.

## Behaviour change worth knowing

An agent that has been addressing `/root` now gets an explicit error naming the
field and a valid value, instead of a silently separate inbox. That is the
intent, but it is a change: callers spelling a path where a name belongs will
see a failure they did not see before.

## What is not proven, stated plainly

- **Pair C ships unrepaired by design.** The largest split stays; an owner
  closes it with `rename-project`, which now moves the messages as well as the
  tags.
- **`rename-project` does not move `agent_principals.project`**, so a renamed
  project needs its host config reissued. Documented, not fixed.
- **The router and presence tables are outside the repair and the invariant**
  (`agent_principals`, `agent_session_instances`, `agent_session_connections`,
  `agent_presence_facts`, `agent_dispatch_attempts`). Their `project` comes
  from an owner-written host config; all five hold only `memesh-llm-memory` on
  the real graph, so there is nothing to repair, and the entry point is gated
  instead. Validation is a deliberate superset of repair.
- **Pair A's verdict is strong circumstantial evidence** — same host, paired
  sender names, overlapping projects, self-acknowledging receipts — not a
  recorded identity claim. No code path ever emitted either string.
- **NFC canonicalisation is forward-looking only**: no non-NFC or untrimmed
  scope value exists in the measured graph.

## Two gate side-effects, both with a reason

`scripts/mcp-doc-contract.json` wa

author: foglienimatteo
body:
Replay of **group 6** from the `oneapi` branch onto `threads`, plus the `WindowFIntegrated` half that was missing there.

## What

`spline_F` and `spline_integrF` rebuilt a `GridInterpolations.RectangleGrid` from scratch on every call. They are called once per integrand evaluation in every TPCF integration, i.e. millions of times per multipole map.

Rebuilding the grid is not free. `RectangleGrid`'s constructor:
- allocates `cuts = vcat(cutPoints...)`, a full copy of every cut point,
- builds one `Set` per dimension to check for duplicates,
- runs `issorted` per dimension,
- allocates `cut_counts` and `myCutPoints`.

With the reference maps in `test/datatest`, that was **per single call**:

| function | map | per-call waste |
|---|---|---|
| `spline_F` | `F_REFERENCE_pi2.txt` (101 × 148) | 2 `Set`s (101, 148) + 249-element `vcat` |
| `spline_integrF` | `IntegrF_REFERENCE_pi2.txt` (79 × 148) | 2 `Set`s (79, 148) + 227-element `vcat` |

The grid depends only on the cut points, which are fixed once the struct exists. So it is now a field, built once in the constructor.

## Changes

- `src/WindowF.jl`: `grid::GridInterpolations.RectangleGrid{2}` field on `WindowF`, built in the inner constructor; `spline_F` uses `str.grid`.
- `src/WindowFIntegrated.jl`: the same for `WindowFIntegrated` / `spline_integrF`. The two commented-out constructors were kept consistent so they still compile if uncommented.
- Both struct docstrings list their fields explicitly, so `grid` was added there with a note on why it is stored.

## Correctness

Results are unchanged: the grid built per call and the grid built once are constructed from the same cut points.

Two behavioural notes:

1. The constructor's validation (cut points sorted, no duplicates) now runs at `WindowF`/`WindowFIntegrated` construction instead of at the first evaluation. A malformed input map fails earlier, with a clearer origin.
2. The stored grid is safe to share. `RectangleGrid` keeps no per-call scratch space — unlike `SimplexGrid`, which stores `x_p`, `ihi`, `ilo`, `n_ind` — and `interpolants(::RectangleGrid, x)` only reads `cut_counts` and `cuts`. This matters for the threading work planned on this branch: had the grid carried mutable scratch, hoisting it into a shared struct would have introduced a data race.

## Testing

I could not run the suite — no Julia toolchain in this environment, and the download is blocked by the sandbox proxy. Please run `Pkg.test()` before merging. `test/test_WindowF.jl` and `test/test_WindowFIntegrated.jl` exercise both constructors and both interpolators, and `test_Cosmology.jl` builds a full `Cosmology`, which goes through both paths.

`GridInterpolations.RectangleGrid{D}` was checked against upstream `master` to confirm `D` is the dimension count, so `{2}` is the right annotation here.

## Follow-up, not in this PR

`reshape(str.Fs, (:, 1))` / `reshape(str.IFs, (:, 1))` still allocate a wrapper per call. Small next to what is removed here, but it could be hoisted the same way.

body:
## 어떻게 찾았나

게이트에 들어 있지 않은 **미래 시계 진단**(`npm run e2e:future`)을 돌렸다. 이 저장소가 한 번도 돌려 보지 않은 조합이다.
866 passed / 1 failed 이 나왔고, 그 한 건을 좇다가 **시계와 무관한 진짜 제품 결함**을 찾았다.

## 결함 (제품)

배정 밖 설치(무단 사용)의 **제거 요청이 대장에 등록된 보유자에게** 갔다. 그 소프트웨어를 실제로 지울 수 있는
사람은 그 호스트를 쓰는 사람인데도. 시드는 둘이 갈리는 경우를 의도적으로 담고 있다:

| 출처 | AST-2021-000432 |
|---|---|
| 대장 (`lib/store.ts:124`) | 상태 `유휴` · 보유자 `-` · **자산관리팀** · 본사 3F 자산창고 |
| 설치 관측 (`SWI-0002`) | 호스트 RND-432 · **이한결** · **연구개발팀** |
| 재물조사 차이 (`DIF-04`) | 기대 `유휴(창고 보관)` ↔ 실제 `사용 중 — 미승인 불출 추정` |

그래서 제거 요청은 **창고 팀 앞으로** 나가고, 정작 무단 사용 중인 이한결은 아무것도 듣지 못했다.
화면은 버튼 옆에 `(연구개발팀)`이라 적어 두므로 **보이는 값 ≠ 실제 발송처**이기도 하다.

```
고치기 전:  AST-2021-000432(-·자산관리팀) 소유 부서 통지·감사 적재
고친 뒤:    AST-2021-000432(이한결·연구개발팀) 소유 부서 통지·감사 적재
```

## 결함 (검사)

그 자리를 지키던 검사 `라이선스 제거 요청 수신자: … 자리표시자 수신자 방지` 가 **감사 로그 행**을 읽고 있었다.

```
1행 (감사 로그):  … 제거 요청 — AutoCAD LT @ AST-2021-000432 (이한결·연구개발팀) …   ← .first() 가 집던 행
2행 (발송 이력):  MSG-4202 이메일 라이선스 제거 요청  이한결 (연구개발팀)  …          ← 수신자가 있는 행
```

감사 행은 가운뎃점(`·`) 표기를 쓰므로 `!includes('- (자산관리팀)')`은 **수신자가 무엇이든 언제나 참**이었다.
게다가 `includes('자산관리팀')`을 정답으로 요구해 **결함을 기대값으로 굳혀** 두고 있었다.

## 고침

| 대상 | 고침 |
|---|---|
| `requestOffSeatRemoval` | 수신자를 설치 관측 레코드(`swInstalls`)에서 읽는다 — 없을 때만 대장으로 폴백 |
| e2e 발송 이력 검사 | `MSG-` 로 **발송 행**을 특정하고, 수신자 이름을 양성으로 확인 |
| e2e 신규 검사 | 카드 메시지가 설치 관측처를 가리키는지 확인 |
| 스모크 신규 2건 | 액션이 `swInstalls` 를 읽는다는 결합 + **시드에 갈리는 경우가 남아 있다**는 양성 대조 |

마지막 것이 없으면 시드가 일치하도록 바뀌는 순간 e2e 는 통과하면서 아무것도 증명하지 못한다.

## 검증

- `npm run smoke` **1127 passed / 0 failed** (1125 → 1127)
- `npm run e2e` **868 passed / 0 failed** (867 → 868)
- 재현으로 고침 전후 수신자를 직접 대조했고, 발송 이력 행 원문을 읽어 감사 행과 다름을 확인했다.
- 전량 게이트 실행 예정.

author: microbit-robert
body:
Extract common carousel component which will be used across apps that support multiple projects.

Currently exports three components, although only `CarouselRow` would be used as things stand.

### Exports
- `CarouselRow` - heading with optional actions and carousel below
- `Carousel` - the common carousel row of 260px wide cards with responsive slides-per-page based on the window width
- `SwiperCarousel` - a thin Swiper wrapper with list semantics, translated ARIA annotations and edge-pinned
  prev/next buttons. Swiper props pass through.

### Deliberate changes from the app copies

- `containerLabel` (pre-translated string) replaces `containerMessageId`
- `title`/`actions` are ReactNodes
- The three internal aria strings ship in this package's catalogs under `ui-carousel.` ids (seeded from the apps' existing translations; ar/cy/it are English backfill until Crowdin).
- RTL follows `useLocale()` instead of being hardcoded to false and the carousel direction updates dynamically
- `isNativePlatform()` prop removed, apps can pass `navigation={false}` instead
- The `_shortHeight` padding override moves to the CreateAI call site
- Ensure that `slidesPerGroup` is never calculated as 0

### Post-merge actions

- Upload `packages/ui-carousel/lang/ui.en.json` to Crowdin as `new/packages/ui-carousel/` before the next translation sync

author: nickyclin
body:
## 問題

`src-tauri/src/remote.rs` 原本是嚴格相等比對：

```rust
if hello.protocol_version != PROTOCOL_VERSION {
    return Err(("protocol", "The Agent uses an incompatible protocol."));
}
```

只要兩端版本號不同就直接拒連。**落後的那台因此連不進去——而那正是需要有人連上去幫它更新的機器。**

至今所有版本都是 `PROTOCOL_VERSION = 2`，所以目前 0.29 ↔ 0.33 碰巧連得起來；但歷史上 v1→v2（#69 加檔案傳輸）就是這樣硬斷的。而且錯誤訊息只說「協定不相容」，連哪一邊舊都不講。

## 修正

**協商取代相等比對。** 新增 `MIN_COMPATIBLE_PROTOCOL_VERSION` 與 `negotiate_protocol_version()`：檢視端接受版本落在支援區間內的 Agent，並降到對方的版本溝通。比自己新才拒絕——無法猜測新版加了什麼。

**錯誤訊息明講該更新哪一台。** `ProtocolMismatch` 分成 `PeerTooOld`（更新對面那台）與 `PeerTooNew`（更新這台）兩種，Display 直接寫出來。

**Hello 解碼略過不認得的尾端位元組。** 原本只容許 `terminal` 那一個選填位元組，多一個就整包 `InvalidHello`——等於之後任何欄位追加都會讓舊檢視端連不上。現在讀完認得的部分就好，訊息大小上限照舊把量兜住。新欄位仍只能用追加的方式加，不能改動既有欄位的位置或長度。

**中繼站不受影響**：它在 `linked` 之後只盲目轉送密文，不看協定版本，所以不必跟著兩端一起升級。

## 誠實的範圍

已經釋出的舊版檢視端仍是舊的嚴格解碼器，這個 PR 救不了它們——能做的是讓**這一版之後**的建置對更舊的對端保持相容，並把「欄位只能追加」寫成規則。`MIN_COMPATIBLE_PROTOCOL_VERSION` 目前是 2，因為 v1 的線格式已經沒有任何地方支援。

## 驗證

- `cargo test --lib`：relay crate 68 tests（新增 3）、app 315 tests（新增 2）
- 新測試涵蓋：整個支援區間的 Agent 都連得上、兩側越界時錯誤訊息各自指名該更新哪台、附加未知尾端位元組的 Hello 仍解得出既有欄位
- `cargo fmt --all --check` 乾淨；`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` 兩個 manifest 都乾淨
- `npm run check`：typecheck、70 檔 394 tests、build，入口 453.96 KiB / 500 KiB

未驗證：真的用兩個不同協定版本的建置互連（目前線上只存在 v2，要造出 v3 才能實測）。

body:
## 🔴 מילוי אוטומטי של הדפדפן בלע הגשות שלמות

השדה הנסתר בטופסי האתר נקרא `name="company"` — קטגוריית autofill מוכרת לדפדפן (ארגון). בדף הנחיתה הממומן הוא אף נשא `<label>חברה</label>`, האות החזקה ביותר שאפשר לתת לכרום. `autocomplete="off"` לא הגן: דפדפנים מתעלמים ממנו בשדות שהם מזהים לפי שם.

**נמדד בפרודקשן (2.9.2026):** שאלון אמיתי נדחה בשרת כ"בוט", ההגשה נחתה ב-`failed_leads` עם `"company":"206897654"` — ח.פ של גן פרא — והמגיש ראה מסך "נשלח".

- השדה עבר ל-`_gotcha` בשאלון ובשני טופסי `landing-misradim.html`, ואיתו מפתח ה-payload.
- ⚠️ **באג שני שנתפס תוך כדי:** הבדיקה בצד הלקוח בדף הנחיתה הייתה `form.querySelector("[name=company]").value` — שדה חסר מחזיר `null`, `.value` עליו זורק, ומטפל ה-submit מת. כלומר שינוי שם השדה לבדו היה הופך את הכפתור בדף שעולה 120 ₪ ליום לכפתור שלא עושה כלום. עבר לגישה אופציונלית.
- הצד המשלים בדשבורד: [PR #125](https://github.com/yarin-debug/ganpereh-dashboard/pull/125). **שני הצדדים בטוחים בכל סדר פריסה.**

## שתי בקשות של ירין

- **תקרת הבחירה** ב"מה הכי חשוב שהחלל ייתן לכם?" — 4 מתוך 6 במקום 2.
- **מסך הדיזיינר** — הדילוג הפך מקישור קטן ואפור לכפתור משני מלא-רוחב, "אענה בשאלות במקום", עם שורת הרגעה מתחת: *"אפשר גם בלי הלוח — התשובות בשאלות מספיקות לנו לגמרי."* הלוח נראה כמו תנאי להמשך, ומי שלא רוצה לצייר נטש במקום לבחור את הנתיב השני. ה-`.q-skip` הקטן נשאר ברירת המחדל בכל שאר המסכים.

## אימות בדפדפן (375px)

- **דף הנחיתה, טופס אמיתי:** מלכודת מלאה ⇒ **0 קריאות רשת**; מלכודת ריקה ⇒ 2 קריאות (`/api/leads/inbound` + Formspree). אפס שגיאות קונסולה. הקריאות עוקבו ולא נשלחו.
- **שער הפרטים בשאלון:** `_gotcha` קיים, `company` איננו, `scrollWidth === innerWidth`.
- **תקרת הבחירה:** הרמז מציג "אפשר לבחור עד 4", וחמש לחיצות משאירות 4 מסומנים.
- **הכפתור המשני:** 335×53 מול 335×55 של הראשי, קו מתאר 1.5px בירוק המותג, פינה 999px.

body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

I noticed [build-pr-creator-image](https://prow.ci.kubevirt.io/job-history/gs/kubevirt-prow/pr-logs/directory/build-pr-creator-image) failing due to `I don't have any idea what to do with '1.25.1'`. this is caused by:
The golang image caches **1.26.4**. Consumer Containerfiles and some project-infra jobs still set `GIMME_GO_VERSION=1.25.1` and call `runner.sh`, which does not read `go.mod`. gimme then tries to download 1.25.1, causing the job to fail. 
This follows the `covreport` Containerfile and #5254 (`entrypoint.sh` + `GO_MOD_PATH`):
- project-infra golang jobs: `runner.sh` -> `entrypoint.sh`, `GIMME_GO_VERSION` -> `GO_MOD_PATH: go.mod`
- project-infra image Containerfiles that compile this repo: `entrypoint.sh`, drop the 1.25.1 pin

author: iderex
body:
Two documents in this tree carried a present-tense claim that had stopped being
true, and both are corrections rather than additions.

`docs/gate-parity.md` ended its mutation evidence section by saying the suite is
green with the bound moved. #173 landed a test that drives that bound at the byte
it takes effect on, so the sentence has been false since 2026-08-27, and a reader
taking it at face value concludes this repository still carries a bound nothing
drives. The dated reading stays, because it is the finding and the worked example
rests on it; what is added is the other end of the sequence, which is the same
one-character edit run against the mainline today reddening the suite, and the
commit that killed the mutant.

`CONTRIBUTING.md` closed its signing section by saying nothing here refuses an
unsigned commit and that the requirement had not been granted, with a pasted
ruleset reading that no longer reproduced. The ruleset gained
`required_signatures` on 2026-08-25. A contributor reading the old text would take
signing for optional and meet the refusal at the merge, on a commit made days
earlier, which is exactly the failure that section exists to prevent. The parity
document's entry for the same requirement now records that its cost is paid rather
than proposed, and keeps the reading that the reference gate still does not require
signatures.

Both corrections keep what was true when it was written rather than deleting it.
The guide says the requirement was not in force until 2026-08-25, and the parity
section keeps its 2026-08-11 mutation run as a dated reading.

These are two issues on one branch on purpose: both land only prose, both touch
`docs/gate-parity.md`, and two branches carrying that file would conflict for a
reason neither change is about.

## The issue this closes

Closes #182
Closes #98

## The means, and why it fits

Markdown prose in the two files that already carry these statements, because the
artefact here is a sentence that says something false and the repair is the same
sentence saying something true. Nothing about either correction is a behaviour, so
a check, a test or a new file would be a second place for the same claim to drift.
The evidence each correction rests on is a command and its output, pasted into the
document beside the claim, which is the form both files already use.

## The evidence

The mutation section's claim, reproduced at the head of this branch. The edit moves
the token length comparison by one position and the suite refuses it:

    sed -i '68s/len(token) > maxTokenBytes/len(token) >= maxTokenBytes/' internal/orchestration/credential/verify.go
    go test ./internal/orchestration/credential/ -count=1
    --- FAIL: TestTheLengthBoundIsDrivenAcrossTheByteItTakesEffectOn (0.05s)
        credential_test.go:490: a credential of exactly 4096 bytes was refused: credential refused: too-large: the token is 4096 bytes, over the 4096 this project reads
    FAIL
    FAIL	github.com/iderex/relais/internal/orchestration/credential	0.545s

    git checkout -- internal/orchestration/credential/verify.go

What killed it, which is what the section was missing rather than what it had
wrong:

    git log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short -1 -S 'TestTheLengthBoundIsDrivenAcrossTheByteItTakesEffectOn' -- internal/orchestration/credential/credential_test.go
    009557e 2026-08-27 Drive the token length bound at the byte it takes effect on

The ruleset the guide describes, read now rather than assumed:

    gh api repos/iderex/relais/rulesets/20487474 --jq '{enforcement, bypass: .bypass_actors, types: [.rules[].type]}'
    {"bypass":[],"enforcement":"active","types":["deletion","non_fast_forward","pull_request","required_status_checks","required_signatures"]}

The tree with both changes applied:

    go build ./...; echo "exit=$?"
    exit=0

    go test ./... -count=1
    ok  	github.com/iderex/relais/cmd/relais	0.810s
    ok  	github.com/iderex/relais/internal/mediaplane	0.536s
    ok  	github.com/iderex/relais/internal/orchestration/config	0.551s
    ok  	github.com/iderex/relais/internal/orchestration/credential	0.754s
    ok  	github.com/iderex/relais/test/architecture	0.552s
    ok  	github.com/iderex/relais/test/coverage	0.410s
    ok  	github.com/iderex/relais/test/determinism	0.386s
    ok  	github.com/iderex/relais/test/doclint	0.239s
    ok  	github.com/iderex/relais/test/fuzz	0.614s
    ok  	github.com/iderex/relais/test/issuestate	0.367s
    ok  	github.com/iderex/relais/test/prhygiene	0.270s
    ok  	github.com/iderex/relais/test/scanseverity	0.369s
    ok  	github.com/iderex/relais/test/sourceheader	0.254s

    golangci-lint run; echo "exit=$?"
    0 issues.
    exit=0

Every path this branch touches, against the union of the two declared scopes,
which are `docs/gate-parity.md` and `.`:

    git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD
    CONTRIBUTING.md
    docs/gate-parity.md

## What was not checked

The mutation tool was not re-run. Both runs quoted in the repaired section are the
2026-08-11 run kept as a dated reading and a hand edit made now, and the section
says so, so nothing here is a claim about what a fresh `gremlins` run would report
on the current tree.

The signing correction is a reading of the ruleset through the API and of two
documents. Whether a commit pushed to this branch is actually refused when unsigned
was not provoked: doing so would mean pushing an unsigned commit deliberately, and
the requirement's effect is read from the ruleset rather than from a failed merge.

The guide's other sections were not audited for the same class of drift. Only the
two passages that named the ruleset were re-read against it.

No second person has read this change. This board has no second reader tonight, so
the evidence above stands in place of one, and the two corrections are the smallest
form each could take.

author: maxhandmade
body:
## The measured harm

PR #5 merged. The `main` run failed because `https://wpalemi.com/currency-switcher/` was unreachable from the runner — three attempts, ~80 seconds. From a workstation immediately after: **200, three for three, ~0.5s**. Transient.

But `check:external` sits in front of the deploy step, so the merged change sat unpublished until a manual re-run.

## A bad answer and no answer are different findings

The script now counts them separately.

| Finding | What it means | Fatal? |
|---|---|---|
| `BROKEN [HTTP nnn]` | the link is wrong | **always, no opt-out** |
| `REDIRECTED AWAY [soft 404]` | the link is wrong | **always, no opt-out** |
| `UNREACHABLE` | nobody answered, three times | context-dependent |

`EXTERNAL_UNREACHABLE_IS_FATAL` **defaults to 1 — fail closed.** A laptop, a cron, or a new workflow gets the strict behaviour. `deploy.yml` sets it to `0` for the push that follows a merge and only there: on a `pull_request` the links are being introduced or changed, so an unreachable host must block; on the merge push the same links passed minutes earlier.

## Negative controls — proven, not asserted

With the loosening active (`EXTERNAL_UNREACHABLE_IS_FATAL=0`):

```
HTTP 404 fixture                                    → exit 1
soft-404 fixture (wordpress.org unpublished slug)   → exit 1
    REDIRECTED AWAY [soft 404]: .../mhm-currency-switcher-not-a-real-slug-xyz/
                    landed on: .../plugins/search/mhm-currency-switcher-not-a-real-slug-xyz/
```

That second one is **the finding this checker was written for** — it stays fatal on every event. Full matrix:

| Scenario | Env | Expected | Got |
|---|---|---|---|
| clean | default | 0 | 0 |
| unreachable | default (fail closed) | 1 | 1 |
| unreachable | `=0` | 0 + loud warning | 0 |
| HTTP 404 | `=0` | 1 | 1 |
| soft 404 | `=0` | 1 | 1 |

The warning on the loose path says explicitly that it is **not a pass**, and that a host appearing on the next run too is no longer an outage.

## What keeps this from being a net loss

Link **rot** happens over time. With the deploy path downgraded it would otherwise only surface at the next pull request — possibly months away.

So `release-drift.yml` gains an `external-links` job: **strict, daily, no env var set.** No `npm install` there — the checker is bash and curl over the authored source.

## Summary

The evaluations table's column order lived in `localStorage`, so it followed the browser rather than the experiment it describes — which of an experiment's evaluators are worth a column, and in what order they read, is a property of the experiment, not of the machine looking at it. Column visibility was not persisted at all. Both now live on the experiment: a **Save columns** button appears at the toolbar's leading edge once the live layout differs from the saved one, and disappears again once it matches.

## Changes

- `ExperimentGroup` gains `column_layout` (`order` + `hidden`). The entity store is schema-on-read, so **no migration is required**. Update follows the existing `pareto` convention: an omitted `column_layout` preserves what is saved rather than clearing it.
- The field is **nullable** so "never saved" stays distinct from "saved with nothing hidden". The client applies its own default hidden columns only in the null case, so a deliberate "show everything" survives a reload instead of being re-hidden — and the Save button does not appear on a freshly loaded page.
- Visibility is stored as the **hidden ids** rather than a map over every column, so a column that appears later (a new evaluator, a new metadata key) shows up by default instead of being invisible because a layout saved before it existed never mentioned it.
- Studio seeds column order and visibility from the experiment and persists them through the existing `PUT /experiments/{name}`.
- `StudioDataViewToolbar` gains a `slotStart` (surfaced as `toolbarSlotStart` on `StudioDataView`), rendered before the search bar. This is additive and optional; existing callers are unaffected.
- Regenerated `openapi/` and the web SDK.

### Behavior change worth calling out

This replaces the `localStorage` column-order persistence (`nemo-studio:experiment-columns:<id>`). Anyone holding a local layout will see it reset once to the experiment's saved (initially absent) layout. Keeping both stores seemed worse than picking one.

- [ ] Tests not applicable — justification:

- `uv run --frozen pytest services/intake/tests/integration/test_experiments_crud.py -k "column_layout or pareto"` — 3 passed. Covers the null default, the PUT round-trip, preservation on an update that omits the field, and that an empty layout stays distinguishable from null.

Removed on request. What it showed on a real estate is the argument: **200 rows of `_3d.cpython-314.pyc`, `_a_n_k_r.py` and `.pfb` font files**, every one *"Active · No reason recorded"*, grouped under *"No rule recorded · no proposed action"* — a queue for deciding disposition, listing the whole estate, none of which any rule had proposed anything for, directly above the "Lifecycle results · supported documents" section that already answers the same question for the files that matter.

## The mount goes, the code stays

Per CLAUDE.md's standing instruction: restoring it should be one commit, so `DispositionReviewWorkspace.jsx` and `LifecycleEvidencePanel.jsx` are left exactly where they are.

## The mount was not isolated

Both the estate summary's per-count figures and its "Review disposition queue" button scrolled to `#lifecycle-review`, as did the rule ledger's matched-count link. Deleting only the queue would have left **three controls that are keyboard-reachable, announced as actionable, and answer nothing** — worse than no control at all.

So the summary and the ledger now render those counts as plain figures when no handler is supplied, and the buttons appear only when someone is listening. Both keep full behaviour for any caller that *does* listen, so neither component is crippled by the removal.

## Recording the orphan

`dispositionReviewRemoved.test.jsx` asserts nothing mounts or imports it — because the other half of that instruction is that an orphan nobody writes down reads as shipped. This component returns markup for any props it is given, so *"never mounted"* and *"mounted with the wrong props"* look identical from outside and the suite stays green either way. It also asserts the component files still exist: if someone deletes them instead, the reversibility this trade was made for is gone.

`unmountedComponents.test.jsx` caught the removal on the first full run and required the record updated in the test **and** CLAUDE.md's list together. Worth noting: earlier in this session I checked for that guard, found nothing, and reported the list was hand-maintained again — it has since been added, and it works.

body:
https://liferay.atlassian.net/browse/LPD-104084

## What Is Being Fixed

A database from 2024.q1.27 through 2024.q1.30 cannot be upgraded to master. The upgrade ends with `Major upgrade finished with result unresolved` and the schema is left partially migrated:

```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Unable to upgrade com.liferay.portal.configuration.persistence.impl to 2.0.1 from 1.0.4
```

LPD-75854 was implemented on master and backported to 2024.q1 under a different schema version on each branch: master registered it on `2.0.0 -> 2.0.1`, 2024.q1 on `1.0.3 -> 1.0.4`. That leaves those databases at `1.0.4`, a version master's chain never mentions, so `ReleaseGraphManager` finds no path, no upgrade runs, and `UpgradeExecutor` throws when it compares `Liferay-Require-SchemaVersion` against the release row. Deterministic on MySQL 8.0, PostgreSQL 14.4, SQL Server 2019, DB2 11.5.7.0, and Oracle 19.3.

## How It Is Being Fixed

`1.0.4` is adopted into master's chain. `ConfigurationDBPartitionUpgradeProcess` moves onto the `1.0.4 -> 2.0.0` edge, and a `DummyUpgradeProcess` bridges master-lineage databases from `1.0.3` to `1.0.4`, so both populations converge on one real step and no upgrade work is registered on two edges:

- master lineage: `1.0.3 -> (dummy) -> 1.0.4 -> 2.0.0 -> 2.0.1`
- 2024.q1.27+: `1.0.4 -> 2.0.0 -> 2.0.1`

A 2024.q1 database has never run `ConfigurationDBPartitionUpgradeProcess`, since that branch has no equivalent step, so placing it after `1.0.4` keeps that work running for them. `2.0.1` remains the single end vertex, so `UpgradeExecutor`'s end-node check still holds. Note that a 2024.q1 database re-runs `v2_0_1.ConfigurationUpgradeProcess`, whose work the backport already did; it is idempotent, recomputing the same `companyId` from the same `groupId`.

`ConfigurationPersistenceUpgradeStepRegistratorTest` replays the registration and asserts that `1.0.4` is a registered starting version and that every registered version walks the chain to the bundle's `Liferay-Require-SchemaVersion`, so no future edge can orphan another version.

## PR Check

**pr-check: PASS** — tested on `18b4aa6d9e8d4cdf133a546fb43f9d64aea2f903`

| Validation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Source Format | PASS |
| Transaction Usage | PASS |
| Per-Module Compile | PASS |
| Integration Test Compile | PASS |
| Baseline | PASS |
| Java Unit Tests | PASS |

Source Format found nothing to fix and made no commit.

Per-Module Compile deployed one module, `apps:static:portal-configuration:portal-configuration-persistence-impl`. No consumer expansion was needed: the change adds no `public` or `protected` member and removes none, and the class sits in an `internal` package. Two modules name the type and both are already accounted for. Its `compileJava` reported `UP-TO-DATE`, so the change was confirmed byte level in the compiled class and the deployed bundle rather than trusted from the task line.

Integration Test Compile reported `NO-SOURCE` for `portal-configuration-persistence-impl`, which holds no integration tests by design — they live in the sibling `-test` module. That module recompiled and the amended assertion was confirmed in the bytecode: the test class now carries the `1.0.4` literal, and its mtime postdates the source.

Baseline found one inherited finding, in `modules/apps/portal/portal-db-partition-test-util`, which this branch does not touch: `com.liferay.portal.db.partition.test.util` `VERSION INCREASE REQUIRED` MAJOR, packageinfo `6.0.0` to `7.0.0` and `Bundle-Version` `6.0.7` to `7.0.0`, from a removed `protected static getExportedPartitionName(long)` on `BaseDBPartitionTestCase` that predates this branch. Both repairs were restored rather than committed, since the bump belongs to that module's owner. All seven Ant projects confirmed `1 executed`. Neither changed module carries `Export-Package:`, so no branch owned module was baselineable.

Java Unit Tests found no test class to run: `portal-configuration-persistence-impl` has no `src/test` directory, so there is no parallel name unit counterpart, and the new test is an integration test, which this validation puts out of scope.

author: geoffreylaff-stack
body:
The index knew when **52 of its 2,008 composers** lived, all typed by hand. Everyone else was a bare name — which withholds what a reader usually wants first: is this someone you could commission from, or someone three centuries dead?

Coverage now: **1,385 of 2,008, with 253 living.**

| Form | Meaning | Count |
|---|---|---|
| `1841–1904` | both years known | 943 |
| **`b. 1948`** | **living** | **253** |
| `d. 1904` | birth unrecorded | 164 |
| `1556–?` | death unrecorded | 25 |
| *(nothing)* | neither known | 623 |

The UI already wrapped dates in parentheses, so these render as `(b. 1948)` beside the existing `(1841–1904)`.

## Where the dates come from

`tools/harvest-composers.mjs` reads the structured person record IMSLP keeps on each composer's category page:

```
{{#fte:person
|Born Year=1948|Born Month=|Born Day=
|Died Year=|Died Month=|Died Day=
```

**Forty API calls cover 1,970 composers.** That beats a general source for these particular people: most of this index came from IMSLP, so its own page titles identify each composer exactly with no name matching to get wrong — and its long tail of obscure arrangers exists nowhere else in a form a lookup could find.

## The empty death year is the whole difficulty

It can mean the composer is alive, or only that nobody recorded the death, and the difference decides whether an entry claims someone is still working. **The data settles it rather than a guess:** of the composers with a birth year and no death year, twenty-five were born before 1900 and every other one in 1920 or later — with **nobody at all in between**.

A gap that wide makes the boundary safe to draw anywhere inside it. So from 1900 onwards with no death recorded reads `b. 1948`, and earlier reads `1556–?` — not `b. 1556`, which beside `(b. 1969)` would claim a 470-year-old is still at work.

## What is left undated, and why it is not a gap

The 623 without dates are Renaissance and Baroque figures whose IMSLP pages predate the structured record, plus *Anonymous* and the folk-song collections. **None is a missed living composer: not one has a work in this index dated after 1950.**

Twenty-nine composers have no IMSLP page at all — Walton, Villa-Lobos, Glass and others that reached the index through Wikipedia. Their dates are typed into `data/curated.json`, where a hand-checked date outranks the harvest. Two of the twenty-nine are living.

## Also here

`CLAUDE.md` records the **Wind Repertory Project** (windrep.org) as a standing source for living composers, at the owner's instruction, together with its access limits — which differ from the sources already in use: it runs MediaWiki, but its `robots.txt` disallows `api.php` outright and sets a five-second crawl delay, so the IMSLP approach is not available there.

The monthly refresh runs the new harvester with `continue-on-error`, since existing dates stay valid if IMSLP is briefly unreachable.

## Checks

11,591 works by 2,008 composers. **31 parser tests and 127 browser checks pass.**

author: ako
body:
Follow-up to the authorable-layouts arc (#304). Two gaps it left behind: the CI gate builds no image widget, and the user manual for layouts was never updated.

No behaviour changes — one test-coverage commit and one docs commit.

## 1. The doctype gate built zero image widgets

`03-page-examples.mdl` said *"No pluggable replacement exists. Image examples are therefore not included in this test file."* That was wrong — `image` routes to `com.mendix.widget.web.image.Image`, and only the **built-in** `staticimage`/`dynamicimage` are deprecated (CE0582).

The consequence: the gate ran green through two separate image defects, both fixed in 597db1b2 with nothing here to catch a regression. `bug-tests/` documents them, but `TestMxCheck_DoctypeScripts` only executes `doctype-tests/*.mdl` — that is what CI runs.

Three variants, chosen so the coverage is not a smoke test:

| Widget | Why |
|---|---|
| `pixels` / 36 | `width` is a **visible** property, taking the authored value by the ordinary route |
| default units | `width`/`height` are **hidden** under `auto` — the path that actually regressed |
| `imageUrl` mode | source lives in a text template, not the `Image` field |

The middle one is the point. A hidden property must be written with its **declared default** rather than skipped; skipping leaves whatever the widget template captured, and `image.json` was extracted from a 48px logo — 48 against a declared 100 is CE0463 on every image widget. Nothing in the authored MDL distinguishes the two behaviours, which is why it needs a gate rather than a test asserting what the script says.

**Non-vacuity measured, not assumed.** With `hiddenUnnamedProperties`' default-writing stubbed back to the pre-597db1b2 skip, the gate reports **CE0463 on all three widgets**; with it in place, **0 errors**. Omitting the `Image:` line likewise turns `mx check` red with `"No image selected."`.

Full gate run: green (578s).

## 2. The layout reference on the site was wrong, not just thin

`docs-site/` was the one artifact the layouts arc never updated. `create-layout.md` predated all of it:

- **Its synopsis does not work.** It documented `CREATE LAYOUT module.Name { widget_tree }` — no header. Run verbatim: `Error: layout needs a layouttype`.
- **`class` was absent**, and it is load-bearing: Atlas scopes its layout rules to `.layout-atlas`, so a layout without one builds cleanly, passes `mx check`, and renders with no topbar bar and no sidebar rail.
- **Missing entirely**: `OR REPLACE`, the `scrollcontainer` / `region` / `placeholder` / `navigationtree` vocabulary, and the Marketplace refusal.
- **It sent readers away**: *"For advanced layout customization, use Mendix Studio Pro"* — for something mxcli has done since #304.
- **Neither "Example" was a `CREATE LAYOUT`.** Both were `CREATE PAGE` statements naming an Atlas layout.

`alter-layout.md` is new — `ALTER LAYOUT` and the bulk `ALTER PAGES … SET LAYOUT` migration form had no page on the site at all. It covers addressing a region by slot, why `ALTER` beats `CREATE OR REPLACE` for a layout you did not write, and the guard's refusal semantics.

`alter-page.md` already documented the single-page `SET Layout` correctly, so it gains only the placeholder-guard note and a pointer.

Also: `layout` is a real top-level syntax path but was missing from the hand-maintained topic list in `help.go`, so `mxcli syntax layout` worked only if you already knew the word.

### Everything documented was executed

Every code block ran against a real 11.13 project (result: **0 errors**), and every quoted error message was produced by running the case that raises it — the Marketplace refusal, the unknown-header-property error, the no-placeholder refusal, and the placeholder guard with its `MAP` remedy.

That caught one claim I would otherwise have written from memory: a cross-platform `layouttype` is **not** refused. `layouttype: 'Popup'` is accepted and creates a *native* Popup layout, because the platform is inferred from the type. The page says "inferred", because that is what happens.

## Testing

- Unit suite: green
- `TestMxCheck_DoctypeScripts` (integration): green, 578s
- Every documented statement exec'd against a real project → `mx check` 0 errors
- Controls: pre-fix engine behaviour → 3× CE0463; missing `Image:` → `"No image selected."`

## Note on scope

An earlier version of this branch also carried a fix for the image defects. It turned out to be redundant — `597db1b2` had already fixed both on `main`, by a better route (changing the hidden-property invariant for *every* widget rather than editing one template's values). That work was dropped and the branch restarted from current `main`; only the coverage and docs remain.

author: huhn511
body:
**Problem**

- Nominatim antwortet auf „Talstraße 5, 66424 Homburg“ ohne Fehler mit der Straßenmitte (`osm_type: way`, `addresstype: road`, keine `house_number`). `geocodeAddress()` fragte mit `addressdetails=0` und gab nur `{lat, lon, displayName}` zurück, `ensureStopCoordinates()` kopierte nur lat/lon/source – nichts stromabwärts konnte den Straßen-Treffer von einer Hausnummer unterscheiden. Die Stoppkarte zeigte keinen Hinweis, und der Navigationslink übergab die Koordinaten der Straßenmitte (`maps.apple.com/?daddr=49.3251226,7.3443936…`). Der Fahrer wird in die Mitte der Straße navigiert. Im Store dieses Rechners stehen zwei solche Einträge im `geocache` (Talstraße 5, Kaiserstraße 60-62), beide ohne Hausnummer im `displayName`.
- Ein Stopp, dessen Adresse gar nicht gefunden wurde (`lat: null`, z. B. „Gibtsnichtweg 999“), hatte überhaupt keinen Navigationsknopf (`StopCard.tsx`: `navigationUrl` nur bei Koordinaten). Der Fahrer konnte die getippte Adresse nicht einmal an die Navi-App weiterreichen.

Beides reproduziert: `POST /api/deliveries/geocode` auf dem laufenden Main-Server liefert für Talstraße 5 den Cache-Treffer ohne jede Kennzeichnung; eine direkte Nominatim-Abfrage mit `addressdetails=1` bestätigt `addresstype: road` ohne `house_number`.

**Änderung**

- `apps/bakery-api/src/services/delivery-geo.core.js`: `addressdetails=1`; `geocodeAddress()` liefert zusätzlich `precision` – `'house'`, wenn der Treffer eine Hausnummer trägt, sonst `'street'`. Der Kandidat ohne Hausnummer zählt immer als `'street'`: gibt Nominatim dafür doch irgendein Haus zurück, ist es nicht das gesuchte. Die Regex für „ohne Hausnummer“ steht jetzt einmal in `stripHouseNumber()` (vorher inline, jetzt zwei Verwendungen).
- `apps/bakery-api/simple-server.js`: `ensureStopCoordinates()` setzt `stop.geocodePrecision = found.hit.precision || null`; das Feld wird beim Seed, beim Anlegen (`POST …/stops`) und beim Adresswechsel (`PATCH`) auf `null` gesetzt. `delivery-tours.core.js`: manuell gesetzte oder gelöschte Koordinaten setzen `geocodePrecision = null` – ein Straßen-Treffer darf nicht an von Hand gesetzten Koordinaten kleben.
- `@bakery/delivery/routing`: neue `buildAddressNavigationUrl(address, userAgent?)` – Google `destination=<Adresse>` bzw. Apple `daddr=<Adresse>`, ohne Koordinaten.
- `StopCard`: bei `geocodePrecision === 'street'` Hinweis „Nur die Straße wurde gefunden, nicht die Hausnummer – die Navigation bekommt die eingegebene Adresse.“ und Navigation per Adresstext. Bei `lat: null` bleibt „Adresse nicht gefunden – …“, ergänzt um „Die Navigation bekommt die eingegebene Adresse.“, und der Navigationsknopf erscheint jetzt auch dort. Hausnummern-Treffer unverändert (Koordinaten, kein Hinweis). „Ganze Tour navigieren“ bleibt koordinatenbasiert.
- `Stop`-Typ (`delivery-api.ts`) um `geocodePrecision: 'house' | 'street' | null` ergänzt; `apps/bakery-delivery/CLAUDE.md` beschreibt die Ausnahme von der Koordinaten-Regel und die Cache-Semantik.

**Verifikation**

- `check.sh delivery delivery-routing`: **CHECK PASSED** – prettier, `nx lint bakery-delivery`, `tsc --noEmit`, `next build --webpack`, 35 Routing-Tests (3 neu für `buildAddressNavigationUrl`, beide UA-Zweige, Kodierung von „Talstraße 5, 66424 Homburg“).
- `npx jest -c apps/bakery-api/jest.config.js --testPathPattern 'deliveryGeo|deliveryTours'`: 56/56 grün. Neu: `tests/unit/deliveryGeo.test.js` (10 Tests; `fetch` gestubbt, Fake-Timer für die 1-s-Drossel): Hausnummer → `'house'`, Straßenmitte beim ersten Kandidaten → `'street'`, dritter Kandidat mit Haus-Antwort → `'street'`, verkürztes „36“ → `'house'`, Adresse ohne Nummer → `'street'`, kein Treffer / kein Netz → `null`, Kandidatenreihenfolge. `deliveryTours.test.js` prüft zusätzlich `geocodePrecision` bei manuellen Koordinaten.
- Eigene Server aus dem Worktree (API 5300, App 3300, echtes Nominatim): Tour mit „Talstraße 5“ → `geocodePrecision: 'street'`, „Gibtsnichtweg 999“ → `lat: null`, „Saarbrücker Straße 10“ → `'house'`. Playwright-Skript mit Pixel-5- und iPhone-13-Profil: Straßen-Stopp und unauffindbarer Stopp zeigen den Hinweis und einen Navigationslink mit `destination=Talstra%C3%9Fe%205%2C%2066424%20Homburg` (Google) bzw. `daddr=…` (Apple); der Hausnummern-Stopp hat keinen Hinweis und `destination=49.3210178,7.3407751`. Keine Konsolenfehler, Layout auf dem Handy unverändert.
- `npx playwright test -c apps/bakery-delivery-e2e/playwright.config.ts` gegen 5300/3300: 10/10 grün (5 Tests × Desktop/Pixel 5), inkl. neuem Test „bietet auch fuer eine nicht gefundene Adresse die Navigation an“.

**Hinweise**

- Bestehende `geocache`-Einträge von vor diesem PR haben kein `precision`; ein damit gefundener Stopp bekommt `geocodePrecision: null` (unbekannt), nicht `'house'` – für ihn bleibt die Navigation wie bisher koordinatenbasiert ohne Hinweis. Bereits angelegte Stopps mit Koordinaten werden ohnehin nicht neu gesucht. Wer die alten Einträge nachprüfen will, löscht den `geocache` in `apps/bakery-api/data/delivery-store.json` (gitignored, pro Rechner); eine Migration gibt es bewusst nicht.
- Straßen-Stopps bleiben mit ihrer Straßenmitte auf der Karte und in Reihenfolge/Kilometern – besser als nichts; nur die Zieleingabe an die Navi-App ändert sich.
- Der neue e2e-Test hängt wie die bestehenden am echten Nominatim (er erwartet, dass „Gibtsnichtweg 999“ nicht gefunden wird).
- Nicht angefasst: die TypeScript-API (`libs/api/delivery`), die ohnehin nicht startet.

author: zannis
body:
## Thinking Path > - Paperclip is the open source app people use to manage AI agents for work > - The server publishes an OpenAPI document. Its `x-paperclip-authorization` extension tells integrators which actor type may call each operation. > - The annotation comes from hand-maintained tables in `server/src/routes/openapi.ts` (`BOARD_ONLY_OPERATIONS` / `BOARD_ONLY_PREFIXES`), not from the `assertBoard(req)` guard the handler actually runs. > - Any board-only handler missing from the tables falls through to `authenticated`. The document then publishes `{actor: "board_or_agent"}` and lists `AgentBearerAuth` among the accepted schemes. The contract advertises the opposite of what the server enforces. #12661 reported 48 such operations; a live-server probe confirms the class (each probeable one returns `403 Board access required` to a valid agent token). > - This pull request corrects the tables for every affected operation and adds a scan-based regression test, so a new board-only route cannot ship unannotated. > - The benefit is a served API contract that matches enforcement for every operation, and a test suite that keeps it that way. ## Linked Issues or Issue Description - Fixes: #12661 - Closes #12665 (byte-identical duplicate of #12661) - Refs #12411 - Refs #11946 - Refs #9726 (merged single-route precedent — this PR fixes the class and closes the hole that reopens it) ## What Changed - **124 operations that fell through to `authenticated` now publish their real restriction.** 95 entries added to `BOARD_ONLY_OPERATIONS` and 29 to `INSTANCE_ADMIN_OPERATIONS`. Every entry was confirmed individually against its handler: the assertion runs on every path that can reach a success response. Entries follow the file's existing grouping. - **14 prefix-covered operations reclassified to instance-admin.** `DELETE /api/plugins/{pluginId}`, the five plugin admin operations (`enable`/`disable`/`upgrade`/`config`/`jobs/{jobId}/trigger`), `GET /api/admin/users`, `GET /api/admin/users/{userId}/company-access`, `GET /api/instance/scheduler-heartbeats`, and the five `instance-settings.ts` write operations each open with an unconditional instance-admin assertion, but were covered only by a board prefix — the document told an ordinary board token it could call them. - **A regression guard in `openapi-routes.test.ts`.** The route scan that already backs "spec paths match mounted routes exactly" now also reports which handlers run a top-level board assertion, resolved transitively from `assertBoard`. A new test requires the spec to annotate each of those `{actor: "board"}`. A second closure tracks the stricter instance-admin tier, and a companion test requires each of its routes to carry `instanceAdmin: true` — so a demotion from instance-admin to plain board fails the suite even though the actor stays `board`. - **Table hygiene tests.** Every entry in all six hand-keyed operation tables must still match a served operation (stale entries silently downgrade the published authorization — and a stale `PUBLIC_OPERATIONS` entry whose path is reused would ship the new route with `security: []`). No operation may sit in two auth tables — precedence silently shadows the loser, which is how a dead `POST /api/companies` board entry (removed here) survived. The scan's own detection rules are pinned by a separate test against synthetic sources. - No change to how auth levels are declared, and no change to any handler's behaviour — only to what the generated document says about it.
How the scan decides, and the reconciliation against #12661's count of 48 ### How the scan decides It reads block structure, so it first masks string, template, comment and regex-literal contents (preserving offsets), and fails loudly on any route file it can no longer brace-balance rather than silently under-reporting. It resolves the assertion set transitively rather than matching a list of names. `assertBoard(req)` is the single primitive that rejects a non-board actor, but almost nothing calls it directly: `authz.ts` wraps it in `assertBoardOrgAccess` and `assertInstanceAdmin`, and individual route files wrap those again in local helpers — `assertCompanySecretWrite` in `secrets.ts`, `requireBoardUserId` in `sidebar-preferences.ts`, `assertBoardPermission` in `tool-gateway.ts`, `assertCanManageAdapterLogin` in `agents.ts`, and `activeToolMembership` → `assertToolConnectionConfigureAccess` in `tool-access.ts`, which is two hops out. The scan computes the closure: any function whose body unconditionally calls a known assertion is itself an assertion, iterated to a fixpoint, seeded from `assertBoard` alone and extended per route file with that file's own helpers. Enumerating names by hand is what let this drift in — three separate passes over the table each missed a different wrapper. Two guard shapes cannot reach `assertBoard` textually and are handled explicitly. A guard that inlines `req.actor.type !== "board"` instead of calling `assertBoard` — `assertCanAccessInstanceEnvironments` in `environments.ts`, which gates all 16 environment write/admin routes, and `assertCanManageInstanceSettings` in `instance-settings.ts` — is seeded into that file's assertion set by name, verified by reading, and keyed by file so a same-named helper elsewhere is not trusted by association. The other is callback-shaped: `POST /api/companies/{companyId}/adapters/{type}/login-sessions` passes `deriveOwner: () => assertCanManageAdapterLogin(req, companyId)` into a shared spine that awaits it before any side effect. No text scan can honestly claim to see that, so it stays a hand-maintained entry with a pinned spec expectation that keeps it from being silently dropped. A call counts only when `req` (or `_req`) is its first argument, which lets a wrapper take further arguments without letting `svc.assertBoard(other)` through. Prettier-wrapped calls and trailing commas still match. `return assertBoard(req);` counts when the `return` is itself a statement, and stays conditional when it hangs off a braceless `if`. An inline middleware argument before the real handler does not end the scan: every function argument runs unconditionally, so each top-level arrow body in the registration span is checked in turn — an arrow nested inside another argument's object literal is conditional machinery and never counts. Return-type annotations are balanced over even when the type itself carries braces. `try { ... }` is transparent; `if`/`else` and every other block are not — `POST /api/issues/{id}/interactions`, whose `assertBoard` sits in an `else` branch, is correctly excluded. The scan is bounded to each registration's own argument list, so a neighbouring helper's assertion is never attributed to a route that does not run it. Routes registered with a shared path constant are resolved too. One limit is deliberate: an early `return` before the assertion does not disqualify it. Several handlers open with `const x = await getAccessibleResource(...); if (!x) return;` and assert straight after — that branch has already written a 404, so the handler reaches no success response without a board check. This is the one direction in which the scan could over-report, which is why every entry it reports was confirmed against its handler before being added. Detection is otherwise one-directional: a handler that gates board access some other way is simply not reported, so the guard never demands an annotation on a guess. Two conditional guards are excluded, and the test asserts they stay excluded: `POST /api/invites/{inviteId}/revoke` asserts instance admin only for bootstrap-CEO invites, and `POST /api/agents/{id}/heartbeat/invoke` explicitly admits an agent actor and asserts only when a provider trace is requested. Both are genuinely `board_or_agent`. Masking rather than parsing: TypeScript 7 no longer publishes the syntactic compiler API from its main entry, and the official lexer survives only under an ex

author: asolache
body:
Cinc tandes de feina. Cadascuna surt d'una cosa que **no fallava mai** i que per això no mirava ningú.

## El color que es veu s'ha guanyat

El roster del Comando ja dibuixava una rodona per persona, i era un hash del nom (`_colorFromName`) assegut al costat del color del tier. Dues coses dient qui ets, i la grossa era la que no en deia cap.

Es va **mesurar abans de decidir**, amb la regla escrita abans de mirar el número: 60/300/1.000 persones, tres passades, mediana. El canvas no és el cost —al rànquing, un punt CSS només estalviaria el 40%— i al roster el cost no creix amb la xarxa perquè `comandoRoster()` ja ha pagat la part cara. El sostre real és un altre: amb 1.000 persones el roster triga 1,8 s abans de dibuixar cap rodona. **Veda 123.**

## Cada superheroi té el seu número, i no el reparteix ningú

Un comptador en un servidor seria mentida per tres motius alhora: hi hauria d'haver un amo, es guanyaria escrivint un nom, i el dia que caigués no hi hauria número enlloc.

Aquí es **dedueix**: és la posició en una llista pública i append-only. L'alta és un compromís `sha256('sos-alta-v1' | did:sos | hash de la primera aportació signada)`; es guanya amb signatura *i* encadenat; i l'ordre és el de publicació, o sigui que endarrerir un apunt no acosta ningú al número 1.

**El cost, mesurat sobre el paquet de debò:** una alta ocupa 26 bytes, una versió de fins a ~3.900 altes cap sota els 100 KiB i Turbo/ArDrive no cobra per sota d'aquest llindar. Els 150.000 sencers són 3,72 MB en 39 versions: **0 €** aprofitant-lo, i **0,09 $** pagant-ho tot a tarifa. A qui es dona d'alta no li costa res, i no com a oferta sinó com a propietat.

I el que revela i no s'amaga: les fulles són públiques a posta, o sigui que qui ja tingui el teu `did:sos` hi pot trobar el teu número. Va al README com a asserció de la prova, no com a nota al peu. **Veda 125.**

## La tercera anotació hi era, i es llençava

`confirmPending` signa el vistiplau —i verifica— i el posava al llibre retallat a `{name,did,ts}`. **La firma es queda fora.** El llibre deia «confirmat per Bru» sense que ningú ho pogués comprovar, i el rànquing en repartia punts en una pantalla que a sota diu «només puntua el que està signat».

El vistiplau entra sencer; només els signats puntuen; i el **rebut** existeix com a objecte portàtil, amb l'apunt tal com es va signar i el resum llegible comparat amb la firma. La formació, que no anomenava mai la triple entrada, ara diu què elimina (la conciliació) i què no (l'auditoria, i la veritat del fet). **Veda 126.**

## Còpies, taxonomia, MATRIU i menú

- **Còpies per defecte**: un navegador no pot desar un fitxer sol, o sigui que es demana sol amb llindar declarat, l'estat es desa quan hi ha fitxer i mai es diu «estàs protegit».
- **Taxonomia**: cinc cares (llei · obra · prova · saber · arxiu), `MAPA.md` generat des de l'arbre — crear una carpeta sense dir què és trenca el CI. No mou res: moure `v2…v9` trencaria el web públic.
- **MATRIU**: pàgina nova que es compara amb el codi, no amb la documentació. La guarda va trobar dues divergències que ja hi eren (10 plantilles quan n'hi ha 14; un sisè criteri de graduació que no deia ningú). **Veda 128.**
- **Menú**: sis pàgines tenien sis menús. Ara quatre grups i una acció, declarats un cop i escrits a 13 pàgines, amb `<details>` i zero script injectat. **Veda 127.**

author: wsmoses
body:
Part of #2968.

A `scf.while` cannot iterate a third time in two cases, and then unrolls (under the forward-progress guarantee) to

```
body(init); if (cond) { after; body(next) }
```

1. The exit test is a pure function of carried state whose next-iteration values are loop-invariant: a third iteration would start from exactly the second's state and take the same exit decision, so the loop would never terminate. Only the state the exit test reads needs invariant yields; an accumulator can be carried alongside (`bilininteg_curlcurl_pa.cpp`'s `scf.while (%k, %acc)` sums with `%k` yielded as a constant and `%acc` passed through).
2. The bits known of the second iteration's state decide the exit test. They are computed with `llvm::KnownBits` from the initial operands through the first iteration's condition operands and yields, and through the `arith` ops, `arith.select`s and `scf.if`s on the way (an `scf.if` with an unknown condition intersects its two yields).

MFEM's strided copy loops (`k = tid; do { copy(k); k += stride; } while (k < n)`) reach us the first way once the range analysis folds the increment to a constant, e.g. in `bilininteg_curlcurl_pa.cpp`:

```
scf.while (%arg23 = %102) { ... %113 = arith.cmpi ult, %arg23, %80; scf.condition(%113) } do { scf.yield %c4_i32 }
```

The second way covers clang's done-flag loops, e.g. `tmop_pa_h3d.cpp` (assemble diag):

```
scf.while (%arg13 = %true, %arg14 = %59, %arg15 = %58) { ... scf.condition(%arg13) } do { scf.yield %false, %61, %62 }
```

the rotated single-trip loop around `bilininteg_batchitrans.cpp`'s team solve, whose trip flag is the result of an `scf.if` on the previous flag and is yielded `false`, and the reduction over a leading dimension of one or two in `bilininteg_vectorfemass_pa.cpp`:

```
scf.while (%acc = %cst, %k = %c0_i32) { ... %next = arith.addi %k, %c1; %bits = arith.ori %k, %odd; %again = arith.cmpi eq, %bits, %c0; scf.condition(%again) %sum, %next } do { scf.yield }
```

where the second iteration's `%k` is 1, so `%k | %odd` has its low bit set whatever `%odd` is.

The `tmop_pa_h3d.cpp` loop carries an `llvm.alloca` (`%58`, a nested `mfem::future::tensor` struct) through the loop as an iter arg, which keeps `ConvertLLVMAllocaToMemrefAlloca` from converting it; that TU then fails raising on the surviving `llvm.alloca`. Running the unroll as a `canonicalize-parallel` pattern, i.e. before the final `llvm-to-affine-access`, lets the alloca convert normally (with #3064's gep fold for the 8-byte offset). Replaying that TU's imported module through the full pipeline with this branch, the `llvm.alloca` failure is gone and raising proceeds to the next (independent) blocker, a lane-private `memref<9xf64>` scratch (#2996's scope); the union's `flattenLLVMArrayAllocas` helper is not needed for it.

This supersedes #3013's raiser-local `unrollInvariantYieldWhiles`, with one soundness correction: #3013 accepted any pass-through of a value forwarded by `scf.condition` as invariant, and its own `@dowhile` test (`%next = %k + 16`, `scf.condition(%cond) %next`, `scf.yield %j`) is a genuine multi-iteration loop that it unrolled to two iterations. Here after-block arguments resolve through the forwarded condition operands, and the exit condition must be pure over loop-external values and the before-block arguments (no memory reads, since the body may write what the test reads). The negative cases in the test cover the varying pass-through against an unknown bound, a condition that loads memory, a yield computed in the after region from the carried state, an exit test that reads the accumulator, a trip flag yielded `true`, and a masked (`andi`) counter whose second value is not decided.

Test: `test/lit_tests/canonicalize_parallel_while_unroll.mlir`.

author: 1efeng
body:
## What

Integrates a filesystem-first LLM Wiki capability into the existing Mastra conversation harness.

- Adds a `llm-wiki` Mastra Skill with on-demand protocol/compile/query references.
- Uses `raw/` as source-of-truth and `wiki/` as generated knowledge.
- Uses the Agent's existing native Workspace tools: `grep`, `file_stat`, `mkdir`, `read_file`, `write_file`, and `edit_file`.
- Keeps vector DB / embeddings / chunking out of this path.
- Supports Wiki-first retrieval, raw fallback, explicit Sources ledger, incremental update and audit.
- Registers the skill in prompt release metadata.
- Makes the existing user Workspace resource-scoped so the same authenticated user shares files across conversation threads while different resources remain isolated.
- Adds/updates tests for skill wiring, Workspace tool policy, cross-thread sharing, and resource isolation.

## Architecture

This intentionally follows the Mastra Agent Harness single-Workspace model:

`Conversation Agent -> Mastra Workspace (resource-scoped) -> raw/ + wiki/ + user files`

The LLM Wiki is a Skill/protocol over the existing Workspace. It does **not** introduce custom knowledge tools, a second filesystem, a RAG runtime, database, background worker, or durable execution path.

## Scope semantics

- Same `resourceId`, different `threadId`: shared persistent Workspace.
- Different `resourceId`: isolated Workspace.
- Thread-specific API routes still authorize the requested thread before exposing the authenticated resource Workspace.

## Source inspiration

Adapted to the existing Mastra architecture from the Karpathy LLM Wiki idea and `Kenshin/simpread-karpathy-llm-wiki-compiler`, while keeping the official Mastra Harness Workspace pattern.

## Validation

Draft PR runs repository CI: lint, typecheck, tests, workspace probe, and build.

author: xiaoyxue
body:
Part 1 of #363 — name the attachment set. Part 2 (moving the `impl Renderer`
method groups into the `render/` modules that own their resources) follows on
top of this, as the issue's open question 1 proposed.

## What changed

`DepthTarget` and `MsaaColorTarget` were structurally identical (`{ view, width,
height }`), and three attachment sets each open-coded "recreate when the viewport
size changed" — `Renderer::ensure_depth`, `MsaaColor::ensure`, and
`PickTarget::resize`. A new `render/attachments.rs` names the concept once:

| type | job |
|---|---|
| `Attachment` | one allocated attachment — not optional, so holding one means it exists |
| `AttachmentSpec` | how to allocate one; `color` / `depth` / `id_color` constructors pair format with usage |
| `ViewportAttachment` | the one "rebuild when the size changed" rule; `ensure` returns `&Attachment`, so no call site unwraps |
| `MeshAttachments` | the mesh pass's set — the MSAA color it *may* own plus the depth it always has |
| `PassViews` | one frame's views, handed back by `resize` |

### The three conventions this converts into types

The issue set this as the bar the refactor has to clear, so, explicitly:

1. **format ↔ usage.** The literals at `pipeline.rs:174`, `pipeline.rs:218` and
   `picking.rs:145` are now `AttachmentSpec::{depth, color, id_color}`. A depth
   attachment cannot be built with the wrong format, and the pick target cannot
   lose `COPY_SRC`.
2. **depth and color share a sample count.** `ensure_depth` used to reach into
   `self.msaa.sample_count()`. `MeshAttachments::new(format, sample_count)` now
   builds both specs from that one argument, and nothing else reads the count —
   `MsaaColor::sample_count()` is gone.
3. **the depth attachment exists before the pass begins.**
   `MeshAttachments::resize` returns `PassViews { color: Option<&Attachment>,
   depth: &Attachment }`, and `encode_pass` builds its descriptor from that call
   directly. `expect("prepare_frame sized the depth attachment")` is deleted, not
   reworded — the sizing moved out of `prepare_frame` for exactly this reason.

### The two `Option`s, separated

`MsaaColor::target` was `None` both when MSAA is off and when nothing is
allocated yet. Those are now different fields: `MeshAttachments::color` is `None`
iff `sample_count == 1` (decided at construction), while "not allocated yet" is
the `Option` inside `ViewportAttachment`. The `stageN_noaa_*` goldens are what
prove the split is right, since `Msaa::Off` is the `color: None` path.

### Also

- `PickTarget` keeps its name — it has `COPY_SRC` and staging, so it really is a
  destination — and is recomposed as `{ id, depth, staging }` over two
  `ViewportAttachment`s. `Picking::target()` becomes `Picking::pass() ->
  Option<PickPass<'_>>`, flattening the target's own `Option`s so the encode and
  read-back stay unwrap-free with the same single `?` the caller already had.
- `slots_dirty` moves onto `SceneUniforms`, beside the slot array it describes;
  `write_pbr` drops its `write_slots` argument and clears its own flag. All three
  writers go through it: `edit_appearance` and `remove_mesh` call
  `mark_slots_dirty()`, and `grow_pbr_slots` sets it itself, since reallocating
  the slot buffer discards every slot.
- `pipeline.rs` shrinks 817 → 651 lines; `renderer.rs` 1,726 → 1,655.
- **No public API change**, and no pixel may change: same formats, usages, sample
  counts, texture labels, `view_formats: &[]`, `.max(1)` clamping and resize
  policy.

**Test level: L3** — touches `crates/trd-core/src/render/**` (render path).

## ✅ Verification

| Gate | 🪟 Windows | 🐧 Linux/Nix |
|------|:---:|:---:|
| 🎨 `cargo fmt --check`         | ✅ | ⏳ |
| 📎 clippy native `-D warnings` | ✅ | ⏳ |
| 🕸️ clippy wasm32 (lib)         | ✅ | ⏳ |
| 🧪 `cargo test --workspace`    | ✅ | ⏳ |
| 🔀 `decoder_parity` (2)        | ✅ | ⏳ |
| 📚 rustdoc (0 broken links)    | ✅ | ⏳ |
| 🌐 `tsc --noEmit` + Biome      | ⏳ | ⏳ |
| 🖼️ `golden_render` (GPU)       | ⏳ | ⏳ |
| 🎮 `gpu_tests` + `gui_render`  | ⏳ | ⏳ |
| 🖥️ window e2e (§4.2/4.3)       | ⏳ | n/a (headless) |
| 🎬 video-editor e2e (§4.5/4.6) | ⏳ | n/a (headless) |
| 📼 large-file seek (§4.7)      | n/a — no media-layer path in the diff | n/a — no media-layer path in the diff |

> Draft: filling the matrix in. §4.7 is proposed `n/a` per the issue's open
> question 2 — nothing under `media/` or `web/gui-video-editing/src/media/` is

Three UI simplifications from the design review, one commit each. Net **−319 lines** (+349 / −668 across 9 files, including a new 42-line unit test and three README rows).

## 1. Remove selection mode (pasta-zam.5) — +135 / −361

The second SwiftUI `List` for "selection mode" (`isSelectionMode`, `bulkSelectedIDs`, `selectionModeSections`, `SelectionModeRowView`, `ContentTypeBadge`, the bulk Copy/Delete/Done toolbar, the "Select" entry point, and the now-unused `TimeGroup`) is deleted. The NSTableView already had `allowsMultipleSelection`.

**Behaviour preserved**
- ⇧/⌘-click multi-selection unchanged; the normal toolbar's copy already handled multiple rows.
- New `⌘A` selects every visible row (ignored while the search field has focus, so text select-all still works there).
- `⌘⌫` and the toolbar trash button now act on **all** selected rows (`deleteSelectedEntries()` → `deleteEntries(ids)` for >1, `deleteEntry` for one). The trash button keeps its confirmation alert, with a count-aware title.
- `⌘C` still copies every selected row (`copySelectedEntries` now shares `selectedEntriesInDisplayOrder` with delete).
- README shortcut table gains ⌘A / ⌘C / multi-select rows.

## 2. Single source of truth for filters (pasta-zam.6) — +110 / −123 (incl. +42 test)

`contentTypeFilter`, `urlDomainFilter`, `sourceAppFilter` and `pinnedOnlyFilter` were four `@State`s kept in step with `filterSelection` by two mirrored sync routines (`PanelContentView.handleFilterSelectionChange` + `handleContentTypeFilterChange`, and `FilterSidebarView.applySelection` + `syncSelectionFromBindings`). Now:

- `FilterSelection` gains `contentType`, `urlDomain`, `sourceApp`, `isPinnedOnly` (`.domain("")` = "All Domains" → `.url` with nil domain).
- `PanelContentView` exposes the old names as computed properties, so `+Search`, analytics and `hasActiveListFilters` are untouched; one `onChange(of: filterSelection)` resets "values only" when the content type changes and refreshes.
- `FilterSidebarView` drops the two extra bindings and both sync functions.
- `SearchBarView` takes the selection binding (its never-read `sourceAppFilter` binding is removed); chip dismissal and the ⌘P picker map onto it. Re-picking URL while a specific domain is active keeps the domain, as before.
- The `.applyContentTypeFilter` notification (Quick Search chips), `clearFilters`, and the on-hide reset write `filterSelection` only. The on-hide reset still only clears type/domain selections, exactly as before.
- New `Tests/PastaUITests/FilterSelectionTests.swift` covers the derived properties.

## 3. Simplify SearchBarView chrome (pasta-zam.7) — +108 / −188

- One `.regularMaterial` background + 1pt border (accent when focused), one soft shadow, no blurred glow, no spring-scaled icon; 36pt tall using `PastaTheme.Radius.large` / `Spacing` tokens.
- Gear is a plain `Button { } label: { Image(systemName: "gear") }.buttonStyle(.borderless).help("Settings (⌘,)")`; the `SettingsButton` NSViewRepresentable / `HoverButton` NSButton subclass (wrong idle colour in light mode, flicker on `mouseExited`) is deleted.
- Remaining fades are gated on `@Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion)`.
- Result-count badge block and the `SearchField` representable/Coordinator are untouched.

author: gouarin
body:
- [x] I have installed [pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com/) locally and use it to validate my commits.
- [x] The PR title follows the [conventional commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) convention.
- [x] This new PR is documented.
- [x] This new PR is tested.

> Stacked on #492, #495, #493, #494, #500 and #501 and contains them, so they should go in
> first. Its own commit is the last one: `feat(mr): min_level_in(region, level) on mra_config,
> replacing --refine-boundary`.

## Description

`--refine-boundary` mixed three things: a numerical workaround for wide flux stencils reading
outer ghosts, a protection of the multiresolution detail against the boundary, and a genuine
modelling intent - keep this part of the boundary resolved because the data there varies. The
first two disappear with #501: prediction no longer reads outside the domain where it can
avoid it, and the outer ghosts of a level are written from that level alone. The third is not a
boundary-condition concern at all but a **mesh constraint**, and it gets a contract:

> `mra_config().min_level_in(region, L)`: on `region`, every cell is at a level `>= L`.

It is a value on `mra_config`, next to `epsilon`, applied as a tag contribution - `refine` below
`L`, `keep` at `L` - which composes with the multiresolution criterion through the maximum the
adaptation already takes. It is a **guarantee** rather than a best effort, because graduation
only ever adds refinement and can never lower a level the constraint asked for.

It is strictly more expressive than the flag it replaces: `keep_boundary_refined` only ever set
`keep` at `max_level`, so it could *hold* a fine boundary but never *create* one, and it applied
to the whole boundary at once. A region is a `Box<double, dim>` in real coordinates, so a
constraint need not touch the boundary at all, and several constraints can be declared. The
region is a value and not a callable, deliberately: time dependence works already, since the
config is passed to each adaptation, and a callable re-evaluated inside the fixed-point loop is
exactly the set-traversal cost this rewrite measured and removed.

The region is converted into cells at each level from the cell length directly, not through
the box approximation a mesh applies to its own domain: a strip a tenth of the domain wide is
far below the coarsest cell, and the approximation would have rounded it up to the whole domain.

`--refine-boundary` and `args::refine_boundary` are removed; the warning of the flux-based
schemes that pointed at the flag now names the constraint.

## Related issue

None. Last slice of the boundary-machinery rewrite; follows #492 to #501.

## How has this been tested?

`tests/test_level_constraint.cpp`, on a field the criterion would coarsen everywhere, so the
constraint is the only reason a fine cell exists:

- a constant field with a strip along the left boundary held at `max_level`: the strip is at
  `max_level`, the far half of the domain is at `min_level`;
- starting from a mesh already coarsened to `min_level`, a constraint on an interior patch
  *creates* level 4 there, and does not go finer than asked;
- a moving feature adapted four times with a constraint on the opposite corner: the corner
  stays at its level at every step;
- a region of the wrong dimension is refused with `std::invalid_argument`.

The whole suite passes (489 tests).
