## Card 2516480b: [MERO-RECURRING-BLOCKER-01][M]

Extends Mero from manual one-shot observation to a recurring, bounded, read-only blocker census. Mero reads CardStore lifecycle, blocker attributes, worker joins, review joins, and SKMail signals, then emits typed append-only recommendations. Jarvis or another explicitly fenced consumer performs any mutation; Mero never does.

### What is implemented

`src/skcapstone/mero_census.py` (+1027 lines) and `tests/test_mero_census.py` (+669 lines, 48 tests).

**AC1 - Bounded census (all eight classes + selector-ready counts):**
- dead_claim: claim held while the worker process read shows no sessions and identity evidence is stale
- stale_claim: DOING claim older than the SLA with no progress events after the claim
- completed_dependency: open card whose every declared dependency has completed
- contradictory_verdicts: block is the latest outcome while an earlier completed PASS exists (PASS_FOR_REVIEW deliberately does not contradict a block, matching blocker_referent semantics)
- malformed_blocker_referent: blocker events violating the BLOCKED contract's four typed values (dependency/human/capability/card) and their referent shapes
- void_dependency_edge: open card still depending on a structurally voided card
- superseded_live_card: open card a void or completed successor has superseded
- review_identity_gap: review receipts written by the wrong seat or assigning a non-distinct reviewer
- selector_ready counts: ready / blocked / total open
- Bounded: MAX_CARDS_EXAMINED (4000) and MAX_FINDINGS_PER_RUN (200) caps; suppression is counted, never silent

**AC2 - Typed recommendations:** every finding pins card id, card revision, claim revision, blocker generation, generation, source event refs, evidence SHA-256 hashes, risk class (info/low/medium/high), proposed consumer action, and stop conditions.

**AC3 - Dedupe:** the recommendation id is a deterministic digest of the semantic finding, passed as the CardStore transition_id. An unchanged board emits nothing; re-emission happens only on a new authoritative generation or a missed recommendation SLA (48h default). The id deliberately excludes observed_at and card_revision because emitting a recommendation bumps the card's updated_at; folding that into the id would self-stimulate new ids and defeat dedupe. This exact trap is covered by tests.

**AC4 - Negative tests (16 tests):** Mero is refused for claim, release, launch, stop, reassign, rotate, repair_worker, merge, deploy, evaluate_merge; holds exactly OBSERVE and RECOMMEND; only the mero actor can emit census recommendations (jarvis, link, workers, chef, full agent identity all refused); default runs are pure reads (event-count and lifecycle-state invariance asserted); the module exposes no create/claim/release/launch/stop/merge/deploy path; no subprocess/selector invocation; no capauth/keyring/env/credential surface in source.

**AC5 - Checks run:** focused suite (48/48), full default suite (7058 passed, 42 skipped; the 2 dashboard_assistant failures are pre-existing on pristine origin/main on this host and unrelated), ruff clean, black clean (line-length 99), diff review, secret scan, Unicode scan (pure ASCII, no BOM, no homoglyphs).

### Compliance notes
- Branch-first, committed on feat/2516480b-mero-blocker-census, pushed, PR opened. No commit to main, no merge, no deploy.
- No timer installation, service action, or runtime mutation performed by this card. Emission is an explicit, authority-fenced call; scheduling it is a later, separate decision.
- Commit attributed to pi-mero-chiap03-2516480b only.

## Summary
- Adds a Pi extension that patches the exhaustive "read pi .md files completely and follow links to related docs" system-prompt rule ([earendil-works/pi#9014](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9014)) with task-scoped guidance, closing #1.
- Patch (`src/scoped-pi-doc-reading.ts`) matches the exact known upstream text only, fails closed (leaves the prompt untouched) on zero or multiple matches, and distinguishes "already-upstream", "custom-prompt", and "unrecognized" states instead of guessing.
- Extension (`src/index.ts`) wires the patch into `before_agent_start`, exposes `/prompt-tweaks-status`, and proactively raises a one-time warning notification the first time a session hits "unrecognized".
- `test/upstream-drift.test.ts` is a canary that reads the actual installed `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` build and fails if the pinned old text no longer matches exactly once — so upstream wording drift is caught by CI, not silently swallowed.

Reviewed in two rounds by an Opus 5 subagent, which independently verified the patch against the real installed Pi 0.84.4 build, built an end-to-end harness exercising the default/custom/drifted-prompt scenarios, confirmed `notify()` rendering by reading the actual source of Pi TUI/RPC, T3 Code, and both known PI WEB implementations, and simulated `pi install git:...`'s `npm install --omit=dev` to confirm no runtime deps get pulled in. Final verdict: approved, no blocking issues.

author: taprootfreak
body:
EN:
App screens size to the visible viewport via `--app-height` and a shared `AppShell`.
Fill routes keep Continue in a footer sibling; flow routes (forum, public rules, inbox) scroll the document through `PageChrome`.
Telegram and other WKWebViews no longer show empty space under CTAs.
Linux visual baselines in this PR match the new shell.

DE:
App-Screens nutzen `--app-height` und eine gemeinsame `AppShell` für die sichtbare Fläche.
Fill-Routen halten Continue im Footer; Flow-Routen (Forum, öffentliche Regeln, Inbox) scrollen das Dokument über `PageChrome`.
Telegram und andere WKWebViews zeigen keinen Leerraum mehr unter den CTAs.
Die Linux-Visual-Baselines in diesem PR gehören zur neuen Shell.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

`--app-height` is set from `visualViewport.height` (CSS fallback `100dvh`) in a blocking head script plus a hydration listener. The bootstrap string lives in a server-safe module; the hook runs only on the client.

`AppShell` modes:
- `fill`: height `--app-height`, inner scroller, optional footer sibling for setup Continue/Skip/Agree
- `flow`: min-height `--app-height`, document scroll, no `justify-center` on `<main>`

Header, footer, and left chrome use portals into host nodes so setup forms do not re-render in a loop. Fill shells center horizontally; onboarding footers share the form column width.

Marketing and 404 use `min-h-[var(--app-height)]`. Fill app pages render `AppShell` directly. Flow app pages use `PageChrome`, which is the `mode="flow"` wrapper.

</details>

author: oknkc8
body:
## Summary

회비를 관리합니다. 반기 회비와 세션별 참가비 두 축이고, 회원은 자기 것을, 운영진은 전체를 봅니다.

**스키마를 쓰기 전에 시트를 실측했고, 그 덕분에 큰 착각 두 개를 피했습니다.**

## Purpose

회비는 1.0을 막는 마지막 기능으로 문서에 적혀 있었습니다. 지금은 스프레드시트에만 있고 앱에서는 볼 수 없습니다.

## 시트를 읽고 나서 바뀐 것

**`월간 회비(2026년)`은 월별 회비가 아닙니다.** 세션별 정산 그리드입니다 — 1행이 그 세션의 1인당 금액, 2행이 날짜, 3행이 수영장, 4행부터가 회원별 납부입니다. 그러니 **금액은 회원의 속성이 아니라 세션의 속성**입니다. 이걸 모르고 짰으면 회원마다 금액을 들고 있는 테이블이 나왔을 것입니다.

**`연간 회비관리(태훈)`은 회비 데이터가 아닙니다.** "2026년 EYSL 운영(안)", 단위 천원짜리 **연간 예산안**이고 회원별 납부가 한 줄도 없습니다. 원천에서 뺐습니다.

**지각비는 완전히 다른 축입니다.** `attendance`에 붙어 있고 `late_fee_requires_late` CHECK로 **지각일 때만** 성립합니다(`0001:113`). 0057은 근처에 가지 않습니다.

## Changes

- 마이그레이션 `0057` — 테이블 넷, RPC 13개
  - `dues_periods` (연도, 반기, 금액) — **2027 상반기 추가는 INSERT 한 줄, DDL 없음**
  - `dues_payments` (기간, 회원)
  - `activity_fees` (활동 1:1) — 세션의 가격
  - `activity_fee_payments` (활동, 회원)
- 화면 넷 — 내 회비, 회비 관리, 세션 참가비 관리, 세션별 명단

**참가비를 `activities`의 컬럼이 아니라 별도 테이블로 둔 이유가 처음 생각과 다릅니다.** "대회·기타에도 금액이 생긴다"가 제 이유였는데, 진짜 이유는 더 셉니다 — **`activities`는 회원이 쓸 수 있습니다.** `0015:96-98`과 `:111-114`가 승인된 회원에게 자기 `kind='event'` 행의 INSERT·UPDATE를 주고, `:132`가 `authenticated`는 이미 그 테이블에 쓰기 권한이 있다고 적어 뒀습니다. **정책은 행을 허가하지 열을 허가하지 않으므로**, 금액 컬럼은 회원이 이미 허가받은 UPDATE 안에 들어앉습니다. 컬럼 단위로 도려내려면 `grant update(col,...)` 목록이 필요하고 그건 컬럼이 늘 때마다 조용히 낡습니다.

**행 없음 / 금액 0 / 금액 N은 서로 다른 세 사실입니다.** 시트의 빈 칸과 `0`이 다른 뜻이라서 그렇고, 그래서 **삭제 경로가 필수입니다** — 잘못 넣은 `0`을 "해당 없음"으로 되돌릴 방법이 없으면 그 구분은 쓰기 전용이 됩니다.

## 잔액을 계산하지 않습니다

여기서 제 브리핑이 틀렸습니다. 소계·참여횟수·월별은 청구 행에서 나오지만 **잔액은 잔고이고 잔고에는 입금 쪽이 필요합니다.** 입금 쪽은 `계좌거래내역` 시트인데, 그건 은행 자료라 `parse.ts:14-20`이 임포트에서 **일부러 제외**하고 있습니다. 이 저장소는 공개니까요.

그래서 **잔액과 총 납부 누계는 넣지 않았습니다.** 마이그레이션 주석이 이유를 적고 있습니다 — *"입금 내역이 이 데이터베이스에 없어서 뺄셈을 하면 이미 낸 회원에게 미납이라고 말하게 된다."* 한쪽이 빠진 금액은 없는 것보다 나쁩니다.

방장님께 여쭐 질문입니다: **회비는 미리 입금해두고 세션마다 차감하는 방식인가요, 그때그때 내는 방식인가요?** 답에 따라 원장이 필요한지가 갈립니다.

## Verification

테이블 넷 모두 RLS 활성·정책 0개, `public`·`anon`·`authenticated` 권한 회수, 모든 문이 SECURITY DEFINER 함수입니다. 스크립트로 **revoke 13개·grant 13개가 함수당 한 쌍씩이고 진짜 `create policy`는 0개**임을 확인했습니다.

`tsc --noEmit` 0, Vitest 통과, `vite build` 0.

**변이 9종을 적용했고 전부 잡혔습니다.** 잔액 계산 방향 뒤집기, 부분 납부를 완납으로, 연도 넘김 제거, 금액 자릿수 구분 앵커 제거, 청구액을 납부액으로, 미납만이 아니라 전체를 세기, 반기 경계를 6월에서 옮기기, 초과 납부를 완납으로 접기, 호출자 배열을 제자리 정렬하기. 생존 0.

빌드 로그에서 하나 짚을 것이 있습니다 — **마지막 줄이 "built in 15ms"인데 그건 2모듈짜리 서비스워커 빌드**이고 앱 빌드는 313모듈 283ms입니다. 꼬리만 읽으면 진짜 빌드가 가짜처럼 보입니다.

확인하지 못한 것: **마이그레이션을 아직 적용하지 않았습니다.** 0053~0055와 달리 라이브 ACL도 동작도 확인 전이고, 머지 전에 적용해서 되질의하겠습니다. 화면도 브라우저로 열어보지 않았습니다.

## 남은 질문 둘

**회원 칸의 `0`이 무슨 뜻인지** 모릅니다. "참석했지만 면제"인지 "참석했지만 아직 미납"인지에 따라 화면 문구가 달라집니다. 스키마는 어느 쪽이든 충실합니다(시트가 담은 숫자를 그대로 저장하므로).

**분할 납부는 모델링하지 않았습니다.** (기간, 회원)당 한 행이라 3월에 3만원·5월에 2만원을 내면 한 행에 나중 날짜로 접힙니다. 시트가 칸 하나라 원천과는 맞습니다.

## References

- `0015:96-98`, `:111-114`, `:132` — `activities`가 회원 쓰기 가능
- `0016:127-131` — 상반기·하반기 경계. 0057은 다시 정의하지 않습니다
- `0001:113` — `late_fee_requires_late`
- `parse.ts:14-20` — 은행·회비 시트를 임포트에서 제외하는 화이트리스트

---

### Checklist

- [x] 올리기 직전 본문을 한 번 훑었습니다 (`/humanize-korean`는 이 머신에 없습니다 — `CLAUDE.md:280`)
- [x] `dev`에서 분기했고 `dev`로 머지합니다
- [x] 키·토큰·`.env`를 커밋에 포함하지 않았습니다 (이 저장소는 공개입니다)
- [x] 운영 Supabase 프로젝트를 향하는 설정이 들어가지 않았습니다
- [x] 회원 실명·연락처 등 실제 개인정보가 코드나 테스트 픽스처에 들어가지 않았습니다

## Summary

Adds the H1-04 architecture conformance campaign for canonical permission inheritance, evidence-aware joins, retry/resume safety, cancellation, and bounded execution.

- Shared tests consume the public CapabilityAuthority and evidence/join/retry contracts.
- Runner tests consume public policy exports and verify child narrowing, policy fail-closed behavior, and cancellation before provider execution.
- The campaign documentation maps nested and parallel branches, sub-workflows, wait/resume, failure injection, duplicate-effect protection, budgets, and cross-runtime children to the focused and existing suites.

body:
Reportado como "All Hands Meeting Q3 · 43 asistentes · 102%". Eran dos causas independientes, las dos por contar el numerador y el denominador con criterios distintos:

1. Denominador asimétrico. El numerador contaba a todo asistente del grupo; el denominador, solo a quienes las fechas de ingreso/egreso de Personas marcan como activos ese día. Quien asistió pero cuyas fechas dicen que no estaba (dato desactualizado, o el evento cargado después de un ingreso) sumaba arriba y no abajo. Ahora el universo incluye a todo asistente registrado: si hay registro de asistencia, esa persona estaba — es mejor evidencia que una fecha cargada a mano.

2. Asistentes sin deduplicar. agruparAVPorEvento acumulaba una entrada por registro, y con carga manual es normal que haya dos filas de la misma persona para el mismo evento. Eso inflaba el conteo de la tabla y el numerador. Los asistentes de un evento son personas, no registros.

El mismo criterio se aplica al % por persona (tabla y panel lateral), que tenía la asimetría espejada, y el "(N activos)" del label ahora sale del mismo denominador que el porcentaje en vez de recalcularse aparte.

author: andikrue
body:
## What is built

**Ask First**: a complete static web app (Vite + TypeScript strict, vanilla DOM, hand-written CSS, zero runtime dependencies) in which an agent proposes consequential actions through WebMCP tools and a human approves or declines each one on the page, with a receipt.

**Tools** (all registered through `document.modelContext.registerTool` in `src/webmcp/register.ts`):

| name | class | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `list_expenses`, `find_duplicates`, `summarise_month` | open, `readOnlyHint` | run immediately, ledger row `executed` / `policy:open` |
| `categorise_expense`, `flag_expense`, `draft_reimbursement` | gated | proposal → inline card → approve / decline with reason and `retry_hint` |
| `pay_reimbursement` | sealed | card with an "Irreversible" tag; the human must type the amount (`340`, `340.00`, `340,00`); the gate enforces the match, the button only reflects it |
| `commit_approved_action` | open, two-call transport only | returns the committed tool's result, the refusal, `pending_approval`, or `invalid` for unknown/used tokens |

**Gate** (`src/gate/gate.ts`): class is read from the definition, never from input. `execute` never rejects: refusals, validation failures and pending states are resolved JSON values, because a rejected promise reaches a WebMCP caller as an opaque `UnknownError`. Every result carries `receipt_id`. `options.signal` is honoured: an aborting caller yields a `cancelled_by_caller` row and the card is withdrawn.

**Transports**: `hold` (default, `DEFAULT_TRANSPORT` in `src/gate/config.ts`) keeps the gated `execute` promise pending until the human decides. `two-call` resolves at once with `{status:"pending_approval", approval_token, instruction}` and the agent commits later. `?transport=hold|two-call` selects per page load; the footer select switches in place and re-registers tools. Tool descriptions are generated per transport.

**Ledger** (`src/ledger/ledger.ts`): append-only, in memory, newest first on the page, row count in the heading, Export JSON (`ledger-<iso>.json`). Rows carry `latency_ms`, `decision`, `decider`, `transport`, `api`, `confirmation_used`, `outcome`. Not signed; the README says so.

**WebMCP surface** (`src/webmcp/polyfill.ts`): feature detection per method. A complete native `document.modelContext` is left alone. A partial one keeps what it has (native `registerTool` still receives every registration) and gets the missing methods added on top. `navigator.modelContext` is aliased onto `document`. The full polyfill is installed only when nothing exists and `?nopolyfill=1` is absent. Diagnostics list which methods were native and which were shimmed.

**`executeTool` argument shape (interop finding)**: the draft IDL passes the input as an object; Chrome 150 expects a JSON string and rejects an object with `UnknownError: Failed to parse input arguments`. The polyfill accepts both shapes (a malformed string rejects with the same `UnknownError`). The tool console sends the string form first against a native API and falls back to the object form on `UnknownError`; against the polyfill it sends the object form. The console's path line reports which shape was used.

**Page**: dark charcoal, one amber accent. Expense table and drafts (live-updating), pending cards (raised surface with an amber edge glow, white effect line, two-column argument grid, solid amber Approve, outlined Decline, a dim cost-of-reversal note; inline, oldest first, focus + `aria-live`, keyboard operable, collapse to a receipt linking to the ledger row), ledger rows with an amber check or grey cross, diagnostics toggle, Reset to fixture, `?console=1` tool console. No runtime requests.

**Fixture**: 26 expenses across Dana, Femi, Lin, Rafael for 2026-08; exactly 2 near-duplicate pairs; exactly 3 uncategorised (E-007 Notion subscription); D-001 340.00 EUR to Contractor X for invoice 2026-114; D-002 a personal purchase that must not be paid; D-003 already paid.

**Docs**: README (structure and placeholders kept; "What production would need" is four items), `SUBMISSION.md` (first person, under 350 words), `VIDEO-SHOTLIST.md`, `docs/VERIFICATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. `.github/workflows/check.yml` runs `npm ci && npm run check`.

## How to test locally

```
npm ci
npm run check            # typecheck, 50 unit tests, build, SPDX header lint
npm run e2e              # headless Chrome for Testing via document.modelContext, both transports
npm run e2e -- --native  # also drives Chrome 148's own API behind --enable-features=WebMCPTesting
node e2e/native-probe.mjs  # which flags expose a native modelContext, and with which methods
npm run dev              # then open /?console=1 to play the agent yourself
```

## What was verified where

From a fresh `npm ci` on Node 22 (copied from `docs/VERIFICATION.md`):

- `npm run check` green: typecheck, 50 unit tests (gate, transports, polyfill incl. both argument shapes, per-method shim, fixture, tools), build, header lint.
- `npm run e2e` green, Chrome for Testing 148.0.7778.97, polyfill mode, both transports: `executeTool` with an object and with a JSON string, malformed string → `UnknownError`; open call with no card; gated approve; gated decline with reason reaching the caller as `{status:"declined", reason, retry_hint}` and a re-proposal with different arguments; sealed payment with the wrong amount refused (also when the button is forced), the right amount paying and draft + expense turning `paid`; must-not-pay draft declined with `never`; caller abort → card withdrawn, `cancelled_by_caller` row; export download containing every decision kind with `latency_ms`; reset; bare URL shows no console, `?console=1` shows it and reports the argument shape used, `?transport=two-call` registers `commit_approved_action`, default is `hold`; `toolchange` fires once per change; no console errors, no outbound requests.
- Same path green in native mode (Chrome 148 + `WebMCPTesting`, both transports), with diagnostics naming the native and shimmed methods and the console using the JSON string form first.
- Two native cases are known:

| Browser | Where | Methods | Page behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chrome for Testing 148 (Linux) under every flag tried (`WebMCPTesting`, `WebMCP`, both, experimental web platform features, `--enable-blink-features=WebMCP`); nothing without a flag | `navigator.modelContext` only | `registerTool` | aliased onto `document`; `getTools`, `executeTool`, `toolchange` added; badge *native WebMCP (partial, completed by the page)* |
| Chrome 150.0.7871.182 (Windows, `#enable-webmcp-testing`), author's tests on the deployed preview and on local build 36675d4 with `?console=1&nopolyfill=1` | `document.modelContext` | `registerTool`, `getTools`, `executeTool`, `ontoolchange` | nothing added; registration succeeded natively, `getTools()` listed the tools, `executeTool` invoked them natively with a JSON-string argument and returned the correct JSON with `receipt_id`; an object argument rejects with `UnknownError: Failed to parse input arguments` |

- **Native hold measurement, Chrome 150 (author, local build 36675d4)**: `categorise_expense` E-007 → meals through native `executeTool` produced a card and no result; after 110 153 ms the human declined with reason "Notion is software"; the promise then resolved with `{status:"declined", reason, retry_hint:"different_arguments", receipt_id:"L-0001"}`. No `cancelled_by_caller` row. Chrome holds `execute` open for at least 110 s, so the `hold` transport is sound on Chrome itself. In Chrome 148 nothing can invoke a tool natively, so the native e2e run calls through the page-added `executeTool` (same registered `execute`, same gate).

## Post-merge checklist for the author

- (a) Confirm the Cloudflare Pages production build: `npm run build`, output `dist`, Node from `.node-version`. If the build image ignores it, set `NODE_VERSION=22` on the Pages project.
- (b) Open the production URL in the ChatGPT desktop app, check the "Site tools" panel shows 3 re

author: guyong-zapo
body:
## 这次改了什么

### 摘要

#3359 为阻止用户同意隐私政策前发送单安装 `EAS-Client-ID`，把启动、回前台和手动 OTA 都绑定到了 analytics consent。企业 SSO 按既有产品约定不经过协议门、也不写 analytics consent，因此 `consent=false + Canary=true` 的用户会被永久挡在 OTA 之外。

本 PR 将两件事解耦：

- 自建 OTA 的 release / canary / beta 请求都用固定共享 UUID 覆盖 `EAS-Client-ID`，不再发送单设备标识；Canary/Beta 继续携带 `x-cindy-update-channel`。
- 启动、回前台、手动检查不再依赖 analytics consent。
- TapDB consent 逻辑保持原样；企业 SSO 不调用 `acceptPrivacyConsent()`。
- 增加 `SSO + consent=false + Canary=true` 回归测试，并守护 SSO 不进入 TapDB opt-in 路径。

Expo 会把下载更新时的 URL / requestHeaders 记录下来，并在下次启动时据此筛选 bundle。因此固定 ID 同时写入自建包原生 `updates.requestHeaders`，与 JS override 共用同一配置源，避免只改 JS 后出现已下载 bundle 的 header 不匹配。

### 变更类型

- [x] `fix` 缺陷修复
- [ ] `feat` 新功能
- [ ] `refactor` / `perf` 重构或性能优化
- [ ] `docs` / `test` / `chore` 文档、测试或工程维护
- [ ] 其他：

### 范围

- 关联 Issue / 需求：#3359 的企业 SSO Canary OTA 后续修复
- 本 PR 包含：自建 OTA header 匿名化；移除三条 OTA 路径的 analytics consent 闸门；原生配置与回归测试
- 明确不包含：服务端改动；EAS / TestFlight 更新链路；TapDB consent 产品逻辑；SSO 协议豁免逻辑
- 用户可见变化：企业 SSO 用户即使 analytics consent 为 false，也可在 Canary 通道通过启动、回前台和手动检查获得 OTA
- 是否存在 breaking change：无 API breaking change；但自建 Mobile runtime fingerprint 会变化，需冷包交付

### UI 变化

不涉及：`settings.tsx` 仅删除更新检查的 consent 依赖注入，没有修改渲染、交互、样式或 UI 文案。

- 引用的设计规范：不涉及：纯更新链路与测试改动

## 怎么验证的

### 自动验证

```text
pnpm --filter mobile run typecheck
结果：通过

pnpm test:unit:related
结果：通过。因本地 origin/main 落后而保守升级为全仓单测；test runner 502 passed / 1 skipped，所有可运行 workspace（含 Desktop、Mobile、maker-core）均通过

pnpm check:dco
结果：通过，1 个真实提交已签名

git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD
结果：通过
```

### 手工验证

不涉及：未生成签名 APK/IPA，未进行双平台真机 OTA 流程。

### 未执行的验证

- Android / iOS 真机抓包未执行：需用新版自建包确认 manifest 与资源请求均只携带共享 `EAS-Client-ID`，且两台设备取值一致。
- 新旧 runtime 的完整发布演练未执行：需在发布链路验证旧包经 `/latest` 安装新 APK/IPA 后进入新 runtime，并只接收新 runtime 的 OTA。

## 风险

### 风险分类

- [ ] 无已知风险
- [ ] SQLite / migration
- [ ] system prompt
- [ ] 协议兼容
- [x] 权限 / 安全 / 用户数据
- [ ] 存量插件兼容（批准状态 / 指纹 / manifest 校验 / 安装布局 / 包格式）
- [x] 原生层 / fingerprint / OTA
- [ ] 跨平台差异
- [ ] 其他：

### 影响与回滚

- 影响范围：自建 Android / iOS 的启动、回前台、手动 OTA；非自建链路不变。
- 冷更不可避免：原生 `updates.requestHeaders` 必须与 JS override 保持一致，否则 Expo 可能因 requestHeaders 不匹配而不再选择已下载 bundle。该配置会形成新 runtime。
- 存量装机：`consent=false` 的旧客户端不会主动检查 OTA，无法通过旧 runtime 的热更自救；必须先通过匿名 `/latest` 分发新版 APK/IPA，再向新 runtime 发布 OTA。
- 发版节奏建议：先完成 Android / iOS 冷包和真机抓包，再更新 `/latest`，最后只向新 runtime 发布 OTA。
- 回滚 / 降级方式：revert 本提交并重新发布冷包；不要用旧 runtime OTA 单独回滚 header 配置。
- 合并门槛：本 PR 改变 Mobile runtime fingerprint，合并前必须取得仓库指定把关人针对冷更的明确确认。

### 提交前检查

- [x] 已 review 完整 diff
- [x] 每个 commit 都带 DCO 签名（`git commit -s`，见 [DCO](../DCO)）
- [x] UI 改动已在「UI 变化」注明引用的设计规范（不涉及视觉/交互）
- [x] 未提交凭证、令牌或授权文件
- [x] 已补充必要测试
- [x] 已确认测试结果并说明未执行项

body:
Implements the v1 contract from the rewritten `current-plans/automation-interface.md` (agreed in design review; zero-compat window, so v0's preview label is simply replaced). Everything from the delta plan except the structured-wire-error fast-follow, which stays a separate PR:

- **Channel**: `--results FILE|-` on cp and cp-prune; with `-` the machine owns stdout (syq suppresses its own human stdout — no `-q` dance). Direct remote-to-remote refuses the flag rather than silently dropping the stream.
- **Records**: schema_version 1 envelope; `run` (run_id, started_at, mode, mapping/dry_run, sanitized endpoints) emitted before anything can fail; sampled in-stream `progress`; `trace` records under `--dry-run` with the reason enum lifted from the `-v` vocabulary (files, dirs, symlinks, specials, metadata, deletions); `operation_result` gains `class`/`os_kind` on failures (local `io::Error` downcast) and covers cp-prune `delete` with per-entry `blocked` under `--max-delete`; terminal `result` gains `dry_run`, `failed` status, and `deletions_*` aggregates.
- **Fatal terminal records**: `run()` is split so progress+writer exist first; a handled fatal emits `result{status:"failed", exit_code:1}` — only a real crash leaves the terminal missing.
- **Hard rule**: the terminal `ResultRecord` is built before the human summary, which renders from the same struct (the summary's dirs figure becomes "dirs created" accordingly).
- The spec's transient reintroduction of per-entry `skipped` records is corrected back to the reviewed aggregate-only contract (spec + code agree); MAPPINGS.md's results section now describes v1, including the unsettled-status consumer rule.

Verified: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, full `--all-targets` suite (227+290+9) with new integration tests for dry-run traces, fatal terminal records, stdout ownership, and cp-prune deletion coverage. Not exercised: remote endpoints for `--results`; wire-level error fidelity is the named follow-up. The normative `docs/automation-v1.md` + JSON Schema + golden fixture files land in the docs pass after this merges, per the agreed docs-after sequencing.

## Summary

Adds OpenSpiel 2.0.2 from its official GitHub release archive.

## Dependency handling

- Uses conda-forge packages for Abseil, nlohmann-json, pybind11, and pybind11-json instead of the copies included in upstream wheels and sdists.
- Uses upstream-derived minimums for CMake, setuptools, nlohmann-json, pybind11, pybind11-json, and Python dependencies without unnecessary upper bounds.
- Keeps Abseil at the exact 20250814.1 LTS release because OpenSpiel explicitly pins that ABI-bearing dependency upstream.
- Ignores only the erroneous Python-named run export from Python 3.12.14 release build 2 (introduced by python-feedstock#913); the explicit Python dependency and `python_abi 3.12.* *_cp312` export remain intact.

- Verifies that no dependency headers, C/C++ sources, or static libraries leak into the installed package.

## Platform handling

- Keeps upstream's POSIX-only UCI bot bindings on Unix while omitting their header and API on Windows, matching the existing core CMake behavior.
- Tests the platform-specific UCI API surface explicitly.

author: partouf
body:
Fixes #9088.

Two separate problems that both surface in the executor's "All compilation options" popover.

### Masking

An executor request returns from `compile()` through the `executorRequest` branch, which never reaches `afterCompilation` — so `cleanupResult()` was never called on that path at all, and the popover showed the raw temp dir:

```
-g -o /tmp/compiler-explorer-compilervVkv5C/output.s ... /tmp/compiler-explorer-compilervVkv5C/example.cpp
```

Masking now happens in `handleExecution()`, before the `cachePut`, so a cold build, an execution-cache hit and a package-cache hit all render identically. `cleanupResult()` also recurses, because what the executor actually displays is `buildResult.compilationOptions`, not the top-level options — neither change does anything without the other.

It has to happen on the way out rather than at build time: `storePackageWithExecutable()` serialises the package before any masking, and `loadPackageWithExecutable()` rebuilds `inputFilename` as a fresh temp path *after* unpacking. So a request that compiles nothing and just pulls the executable from S3 still needs masking applied to what it returns.

### Availability

The project/CMake path produces no `buildResult` at all; it reports what it compiled with on the inner `result`. The popover read `result.buildResult.compilationOptions`, got `undefined`, and rendered "No options in use" — while the compiler pane right above it showed the full line, because it reads `result.result ?? result`. Fixed client-side by falling back to that field; the data was already being sent, it was just being read from the wrong place.

### Verification

Against a local dev server, and the CMake shape checked against production:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Single-file executor, cold build | `/tmp/compiler-explorer-compiler*/example.cpp` | `/app/example.cpp` |
| Single-file executor, executable from package cache | unmasked | `/app/example.cpp`, `inputFilename: example.cpp` |
| CMake executor | "No options in use" | `-fdiagnostics-color=always -std=c++20 -O3 -flto -isystem/opt/...` |

The package-cache case was exercised with two requests sharing a build key but differing in execute args, so the second skipped the execution cache and went through `loadPackageWithExecutable` (confirmed by `packageDownloadAndUnzipTime` in the response).

I also verified the masking call is load-bearing by disabling just that line with the recursion left in place — the options come back unmasked, since nothing else on that path calls `cleanupResult`.

`npm test` (2653 passed), `ts-check` and `lint` all clean. New unit test covers the nested masking.

### Note on the cache

Masking happens on write, matching the approach in #9057, so what is stored equals what is shown. Execution-cache entries written before this deploy keep their unmasked options until they turn over.

Found while testing #8960, which touches neither the executor nor the CMake path.

author: powerfulmoves
body:
## Why this comment exists

`PROVIDER_KEY_CHECKLIST.md` row 17 files `MINIMAX_TOKEN_PLAN_API_KEY` as a *"variant"* whose primary is `MINIMAX_API_KEY`. **That row is wrong**, and it invites a one-line "fix" pointing this provider at the PAYG key.

GitHub Prod carries both as **separate secrets on separate rotation schedules**:

```
MINIMAX_API_KEY              2026-03-31
MINIMAX_TOKEN_PLAN_API_KEY   2026-08-26
```

`MiniMax-M3` is the token-plan model, so aliasing would bill token-plan traffic against the pay-as-you-go account.

I made exactly that edit before it was corrected. The comment now says *do not "fix" this* and gives the reason — because the misleading checklist row is still there and the next reader reaches the same wrong conclusion.

## The real gap is delivery, not naming

Everything downstream is already correct:

| | |
|---|---|
| funnel validates the key | `secrets_funnel_populate.py:130` |
| gateway loads `env.tier-llm` | `x-tier-llm-hardened` anchor |
| **no compose change needed** | the key just has no value in `env.shared` |

`sync-secrets-local.yml` carries it (line 129) but dispatches to `ai-lab` runners — the 4090 has none registered and `pmoves-spark-ailab` is **offline**. CI cannot deliver here today.

Operator lane, once:
```bash
export PMOVES_ROTATE_VALUE=<the token-plan key>
make -C pmoves secrets-rotate KEY=MINIMAX_TOKEN_PLAN_API_KEY
```
(Setting a known value — never generating one; a provider key is issued by MiniMax.)

## Measured consequence while absent

TensorZero fails its **entire** config load on this one key and crash-loops every 60s. That takes down all model routing **and** degrades Cipher — its `embed()` calls TensorZero first, and on null it falls through to a lexical path that ignores the query text. A deliberately nonsensical query returned five confident, unrelated memories.

No behaviour change — comment only.

author: tahiriqbal095
body:
Implements #22. The Storefront modelled every visitor through a shared
authenticated-style User record and let conversational intent mutate the Cart.
This replaces both, and ends the scope at a behavior-tested Checkout Readiness
seam rather than a half-built checkout.

## What changed

**Guest Sessions** (#23, #24, #25, #26) — every visitor is an unauthenticated
Customer owned by a browser-scoped Guest Session, created lazily on the first
stateful action and carried in a secure HTTP-only cookie that stores only a
token hash. 30-day sliding expiry, with cleanup of expired unprotected Cart and
Conversation state that preserves immutable Audit Events. Runtime User and Brand
Admin identity is removed; there is no Admin surface.

**Deterministic Cart controls** (#27, #28, #29, #30) — add, increment,
decrement, and remove are the only ways the Cart changes, each an explicit
Customer action. Every mutation carries a client-generated idempotency key, so a
retry replays its original result; concurrent distinct actions are all
preserved, and an unreconcilable command returns a typed conflict with the
latest authoritative Cart. The client never optimistically alters a quantity,
price, or total.

**Read-only Commerce Agent** (#28, #31) — the Agent gets a narrow Cart
inspection capability and no mutation capability. "Add the first one" resolves
Products and returns Add controls without writing the Cart. Commercial values
are rendered by deterministic application code, never by generated prose.

**Checkout Readiness** (#32, #33) — an explicit Review for checkout records a
fixed Customer Action Entry with generated provenance and renders a
deterministic, versioned card without invoking the model. A Cart is ready only
when it is non-empty, every Product is available within current stock and the
Cart Item limit, its Currency is INR, and its Cart Subtotal calculates. Blockers
name the Cart Item at fault and offer the existing explicit controls; any later
Cart mutation marks earlier cards Outdated while their history stays visible
across a refresh.

## Boundaries held

No inventory reservation. No Checkout Proposal, Approval, Order, Razorpay
object, payment attempt, or payment UI. Product prices are immutable, INR is the
only Currency, and pre-checkout analytics stay pseudonymous.

## Deploy notes

Six new migrations. Per #22 this is a destructive pre-production schema
replacement, not a compatibility migration: User-owned records are not migrated,
and speculative checkout and payment schemas are removed (ADR-0009). Reset and
reseed rather than upgrading in place.

## Testing

126 unit tests and 40 database integration tests, written first at the three
seams #22 names: the Storefront (React Testing Library), route handlers
(Request/Response), and persistence. Integration tests need Postgres
(`docker compose up -d postgres`), then `npx drizzle-kit migrate`.

`app/storefront-bundle.test.ts` fails if the Storefront's client entry reaches a
server-only module — the Node suites resolve `dns` happily, so a database import
reaching the browser bundle breaks the build without failing any behavior test.

## Where future checkout begins

From the versioned Checkout Readiness result. It should revalidate inventory at
that point rather than trusting a stored card, and make fresh decisions about
protected commercial records and retention — none of which this scope creates.

author: prsauer
body:
## Problem

Every fork PR's `build_on_mac` check has been red since 2026-08-02, regardless of the code in it.

GitHub withholds repository secrets from `pull_request` runs whose head is a fork, so `CSC_LINK` and `CSC_KEY_PASSWORD` reach the mac job as empty strings. electron-builder does **not** fall back to an unsigned build when `CSC_LINK` is empty — it still enters the signing path, resolves `""` as a path, and aborts:

```
• empty password will be used for code signing  reason=CSC_KEY_PASSWORD is not defined
⨯ /Users/runner/work/wowarenalogs/wowarenalogs not a file
```

Nothing expired and no certificate is at fault — the job fails before one is ever loaded. The signing setup landed 2026-03-18 and only ever passed on same-repo branches:

| Date | Branch | Head repo | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-06-26 | `fix/windows-noobs-native-build` (#500) | `wowarenalogs/wowarenalogs` | ✅ |
| 2026-06-26 | `feature/combatreplay-toggle-floating-text` (#499) | `wowarenalogs/wowarenalogs` | ✅ |
| 2026-08-02 | `webhook-v2-shuffle-rounds` (#498) | `okwinza/wowarenalogs` | ❌ |
| 2026-08-31 → now | #503, #505, #506, #507, #508 | all forks | ❌ |

What changed three months ago wasn't the cert or the workflow (the June commits are Windows-only) — it's that PR traffic moved to forks.

## Change

Probe for the credentials, then pick a build mode:

- **Present** → sign as before, then verify `codesign`, `TeamIdentifier`, `spctl --assess`, and `xcrun stapler validate`.
- **Absent** → build unsigned with `CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=false`, skip the two verification steps, and log why. `scripts/notarize.js` already no-ops when `APPLE_*` is unset.

Testing the secrets directly rather than checking whether the head is a fork also covers Dependabot PRs, which use a separate secret store.

`CSC_FOR_PULL_REQUEST: true` moves onto the signed step — it's what makes electron-builder sign at all on a `pull_request` event, so the signed path still needs it.

## Scope

**Signing coverage does not decrease anywhere it was possible before.** There is no signing on fork PRs today to lose — the runner has no certificate.

`release-app.yml`, the only workflow that publishes, is untouched. It runs on push to `release/wowarenalogs/app` or `workflow_dispatch` — both base-repo events that always receive secrets — and still gates its `gsutil cp` to `download.wowarenalogs.com` on the full codesign + spctl + stapler check. `build-app.yml` has no upload step at all, so the unsigned artifact never leaves the runner.

## Verification

This PR is same-repo, so its own `build_on_mac` run takes the **signed** path — a green check here confirms the signed path still signs, verifies, and staples. The unsigned path is exercised by the next fork PR.

author: adamhadani
body:
## Summary

Low-risk bug fixes from the matrix audit (findings C2, C3, C5), each with a regression test that fails on `develop`.

- **`multi_labeled` with plain string labels** passed the 1-D array straight to `MultiLabelBinarizer.transform`, which iterates each string's characters. Only single-character labels (the digits example) ever worked; `["cat", "dog"]` binarised to all zeros. Scalars are now wrapped as one-element label sets.
- **`fill_ancestors` on DAGs** dropped the root by position (last key of the BFS distance dict). When another ancestor ties the root's distance, a real ancestor was dropped and the root kept, raising `IndexError` with the string `ROOT` or silently miscomputing hierarchical recall with an integer root. The root is now excluded by identity. The trailing `graph.reverse(copy=False)` "undo" was a no-op on a view and is removed.
- **`nnz_columns_count`** returned the number of columns, not the number of non-zero columns.

Replaces #3, which GitHub auto-closed when its base branch was deleted after #2 merged. Now based on `develop`. No performance impact.

### After review
- The label encoding is decided once per array from its first element rather than per element: scalars are wrapped, sets/lists of labels pass through unchanged (set-valued labels previously broke with "unhashable type: set"), and an already-binarized 2-D indicator matrix raises a clear `ValueError` instead of being misread row by row.

## What was broken

|---|---|
| **C1** | **Editing from the preview was unreachable on touch.** Overlay controls were gated on hover *and* set `pointer-events: none` when hidden, so a tap could neither reveal nor focus them. Affected the mobile Preview view and iPads. |
| **C2** | **Keyboard users could dismiss an AI suggestion but not accept one.** `Popover` portals its panel to `document.body`, putting it outside the trigger's tab sequence, and never moved focus in. Also affected the résumé card menu and the ATS help popover. |
| **C3** | **An ambient decoration could take down the authenticated app.** `new Renderer({ webgl: 2 })` was unguarded, `PlasmaBackground` wraps every `/dashboard/*` route, and there was no `error.tsx` anywhere in `app/`. |
| **C4** | **The six-step job-search wizard lost everything on refresh** — 13 `useState` hooks, no persistence — and had no cancel path. |
| **C5** | **Deleting a résumé entry destroyed it with no confirm or undo**, from a button a few pixels from the drag handle. Custom sections deleted silently while built-in ones prompted; jobsearch rules deleted silently while every sibling confirmed. |
| **F1** | **The UI typeface had never shipped.** `globals.css` declared `font-family: Inter` but nothing loaded it — every visitor got `system-ui`. |
| + | Editor navigation dropped pending edits (`beforeunload` doesn't fire for client-side routing); export had no in-flight state; the five AI calls had no timeout. |

## Notable decisions

**Inter is self-hosted, not `next/font/google`.** The Google variant worked and then failed on retry — `fonts.gstatic.com` isn't reliably reachable from a restricted builder, which would break production builds. `@fontsource-variable/inter` needs no network at build time and matches how the repo's eight other fonts are already sourced. Trade-off: no automatic metric-matched fallback, so first paint may shift slightly.

**Entry deletion stays instant, with undo.** Gating every removal behind a modal would punish the common case; the undo toast reuses the pattern `ResumeCard` already uses. Undo re-inserts against the *live* array, so a concurrent edit made while the toast was up isn't discarded.

**Wizard Cancel keeps the draft.** Discarding would make Cancel itself an unconfirmed destructive action — the exact pattern C5 fixes. Reopening resumes; the draft clears only on successful creation.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- `npm run lint` — 0 errors, 3 warnings (all pre-existing, unchanged)
- `npm run test:run` — **208 files, 2029 tests passing**, up from 207 / 1986 (**+43 tests**)
- `npm run build` compiles

Every fix has regression coverage, including the cases that are awkward to reach by hand: simulated WebGL failure, `(hover: hover)` off, malformed persisted draft, and undo-after-concurrent-edit.

## Review notes

The font change has the widest blast radius — every metric in the app was previously tuned against a fallback face. Worth an eyeball pass over the navbar and accordion badges.

## Known gap

The AI panels still have **no user-initiated cancel button**. The timeout makes a stalled request recoverable rather than permanent, which was the harmful part, but a visible cancel needs UI in three panels and belongs with the shared-primitives work in Phase 2.

## Remaining phases

- **Phase 2 (foundation, ~60 findings):** semantic colour tokens (1,044 raw utilities today), shared `Button`/`Input`/`Card`/`Badge` primitives (18 distinct class strings for one primary button across 183 hand-styled buttons), route-level `loading.tsx` skeletons, one icon system (three coexist today).
- **Phase 3:** responsive pass (45 breakpoint prefixes across 16k lines; 33 components have none) and the remaining WCAG work.
- **Phase 4:** settings/account surface, pricing, and the duplicated-Terms divergence.

author: enriquea
body:
Promotes #326 to `main`. Single commit; `dev` is otherwise level with `main`.

## What this fixes

`hvantk hgc mt2vcf` was silently deleting nearly every hom-ref genotype on
DeepVariant-derived callsets.

DeepVariant gVCF reference blocks are `GT:GQ:MIN_DP:PL` — they carry `MIN_DP`
and no `DP`. Hail's VDS combiner keeps what it finds, so `reference_data` ends
up as `{END, GQ, MIN_DP}`, and after `to_dense_mt` the `DP` field (which does
exist in the entry schema, inherited from `variant_data`) is **undefined** on
every reference-derived entry.

The gnomAD `adj` filter is `(GQ >= 20) & (DP >= 10) & (allele balance)`. With
`DP` missing, `DP >= 10` is missing, and `True & missing` is missing — so `adj`
came out MISSING rather than `False`. `filter_entries(adj, keep=True)` retains
only `True`, so those genotypes were dropped.

A schema check cannot catch this: `DP` is in the schema while being undefined
on the reference side.

## Measured impact

Found on a 1005-sample CHD WGS cohort where the delivered VCF showed >60%
genotype missingness across every sample. On the real chr20 VDS:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| hom-ref entries with `adj = MISSING` | 1,204,040,679 / 1,248,206,641 (96.5%) | 0 |
| call rate | 0.34 | 0.92 |
| mean AN (of 2010) | 679 | 1841 |

`AC` was unaffected — het/hom-var entries come from variant records, which
always carry `DP`, and their `adj = MISSING` count was exactly 0. But `AN`
collapsed, so the reported `AF` was inflated ~2.7x. Because `variant_qc`
recomputes AC/AF/AN afterwards, the output looked self-consistent and the bug
went unnoticed.

## The change

1. **`adj.py`** — depth falls back to `MIN_DP` when `DP` is absent
   (`hl.coalesce(mt.DP, mt.MIN_DP)`), and `GT`/`AD` fall back to `LGT`/`LAD` so
   `adj` is computable on an unsplit densified matrix. Using `MIN_DP` is
   conservative: it is the block minimum, so the filter can only be stricter
   than a true per-site `DP` would be.

2. **`converters.py`** — a `resolve_reference_depth` step folds `MIN_DP` into
   `DP` before export. Without it the recovered genotypes export as
   `0/0:.:.:50` with no depth, and a downstream `FORMAT/DP >= 10` filter would
   delete exactly the genotypes this fix restores — 62.1% of called genotypes
   on chr20, pushing apparent missingness straight back to 64.7%. Folding
   `MIN_DP` into `DP` at joint-genotyping is the standard convention (GLnexus
   `orig_names: [MIN_DP, DP] -> DP, combi_method: min`; DRAGEN and GATK print
   hom-ref `MIN_DP` as `FORMAT/DP`). No-op on callsets without `MIN_DP`.

3. **`converters.py`** — `_assert_adj_is_computable` guard: samples the head of
   the matrix and raises if `adj` is systematically MISSING, so a matrix built
   this way fails loudly instead of exporting a wrecked VCF. Escape hatch via
   `mt2vcf --no-check-adj`.

4. **Tests** — 8 Hail regression tests on a matrix shaped like a densified
   DeepVariant VDS, covering the missingness itself, that the fallback still
   *discriminates* (low `MIN_DP` and low `GQ` still fail), that dropping
   `MIN_DP` reproduces the bug, both guard directions, and `resolve_reference_depth`
   including its no-op path.

## Validation

End-to-end on the real chr20 VDS (1005 samples) through the fixed
`hvantk hgc mt2vcf`: 6m05s, 192 GB peak. Output has 0 entries with missing
`adj`, 0 called genotypes without `DP`, and 317,399 variants at `AC>=10`
against 316,209 from the original pipeline — 0.4% apart, with true AF (AC/2N)
0.19554 vs 0.19600, confirming the variant *selection* survived the bug even
though the genotype matrix did not.

Full diagnostic write-up is in `local/hpc/refblock-missingness/DIAGNOSTIC.md`
(not committed — `/local` is gitignored).

## What & why

Closes #133 — PRD #124. Independent of the wave's bump: prose only, two files.

**Restatement (the spec this diff was built against).** When this session ends, a decision record says the kit carries a kit-only tier-to-model mapping, why it is never shipped, and why hard rule 10 exists; it follows the MADR template; the index row and the supersession of the diary-recorded line are in the same commit; the gate is green.

**Demo evidence:**

```console
20:| [0003](0003-the-kit-maps-its-own-tiers.md) | The kit carries its own tier-to-model mapping, and never ships it | Accepted 2026-09-02 — supersedes the diary-recorded decision of 2026-08-27 below |
52:  the state a consumer starts in too. **Superseded by ADR-0003** (2026-09-02):
$ sh scripts/check.sh
OK  docs gate: all checks passed (shared-layer 0.15.0, engine: harness)
```

## Checklist

- [x] **One slice** — this PR does one thing; refactoring and behavior change are not mixed in a single commit (shared invariant §10)
- [x] **Tests first** — the self-host suite's kit-own enumeration (E4) is the covering check: it went red on the record before bootstrap's deletion list named it, and green after; the docs gate holds the index
- [x] **Docs match reality** — the index and the record agree with the kit-only config on disk; the gate is green
- [x] **Decisions recorded** — this PR is the record
- [x] **Conventional Commits**, commits curated before review

## Behavior findings for a human

- **The record states a reviewer rule the manual did not spell out**: when the session itself runs on the model the reviewer tier maps to, the reviewer runs on the implementer tier's model instead. That is what this wave's reviews did; confirm it is the policy and not an accident worth its own record.
- **The deciders line names you**, with the practice dated 2026-08-27 and the record 2026-09-02. Confirm the attribution.

## Notes for review

No ADR-0001 amendment: this record supersedes an index-recorded diary decision, not a record. The rotting-identifiers caveat is carried from the config file's own header.

## Background

The index carries a section for decisions recorded in the diary rather than as records. One of them said the kit maps no tier to any model; the kit has mapped its own since the same day, in a file bootstrap deletes. The housekeeping pass caught the contradiction.

## Intuition

A rule on the wall says "no exceptions"; a drawer holds one, made for a good reason. This writes the exception on the wall beside the rule.

## Walkthrough

`docs/adr/0003-the-kit-maps-its-own-tiers.md`: context, four options, five clauses, consequences. `docs/adr/INDEX.md`: the new row, and the diary-recorded line marked superseded in place.

## Quiz

**1. Does ADR-0003 change what a consumer receives?**

- A. Yes, the shipped config now carries model ids
- B. No; the shipped config stays empty and the kit-only file never ships
- C. Yes, hard rule 10 is stamped into consumer manuals
- D. Only for consumers on the same harness

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**B.** Clause 1 and clause 2. Nothing the kit ships names a model.

body:
## Why this exists

[#356](https://github.com/ChuckBuilds/ledmatrix-plugins/pull/356) shows as merged but its content is **not on `main`**. My mistake: I based it on `docs/7-segment-clock-readme` so it could use the render tooling before that tooling existed on `main`. [#355](https://github.com/ChuckBuilds/ledmatrix-plugins/pull/355) then squash-merged that branch into `main` *before* #356 merged into it, so the AFL work has been sitting on a branch nothing points at.

This is the same content, cut from `main`. Nothing to review differently — but worth knowing #356 is a dead end, and the branch can be deleted.

Every plugin PR from here targets `main` directly; the stacking was only ever needed while the tooling was unmerged.

## What it does

Documentation only; no behaviour change.

The README covered ~15 of the plugin's ~120 settings, had no images, and its defaults table had drifted from the schema — it listed `show_favorite_teams_only` as defaulting to `false` (it is `true`), `display_duration` as `30` (it is `15`), and showed `show_odds: false` in an example labelled as the defaults.

**Game selection gets its own section.** Three distinct code paths, chosen by whether `favorite_teams` is empty and whether `show_favorite_teams_only` is on:

| Selection mode | `upcoming_games_to_show` means |
|----------------|-------------------------------|
| No favourites | A **total** across the league |
| Favourites, exclusively | A budget **per favourite team** |
| Favourites first, then others | A **total** for the favourites portion only |

Three favourites with a value of `3` is nine cards or three, depending on one unrelated checkbox.

**Four dead ends, each verified:** `show_odds` is a no-op for AFL (ESPN publishes no odds block for the league — a full finals-week payload contains zero — yet it still issues one odds request per selected game); `show_ranking` has no poll to read; `dynamic_duration.min_duration_seconds` and `background_service.max_workers` are in the schema but never applied.

## Re-verified against current main, not assumed

`main` moved under this work (#353 and #354 changed `sports.py` and the schema), so I re-checked rather than trusting the old branch:

- Every documented default still matches `config_schema.json` — checked all 81 documented rows programmatically.
- The committed images **re-render byte-identical** against main's `sports.py`, via `render_docs_assets.py --check`. That is the reproducible-render setup earning its keep.
- `check_plugin.py` — 24/24 PASS.
- Version bumped from main's current `1.19.0`, not the `1.17.3` the stranded branch carried.

## One collision to be aware of

[#357](https://github.com/ChuckBuilds/ledmatrix-plugins/pull/357) (the logo placeholder fix) also bumps afl-scoreboard to `1.19.1`. Whichever of the two merges second needs a re-bump to `1.19.2` — say the word and I'll handle it once you've picked an order.

## Summary

Documentation only — no behavior, type, or API changes.

- Add contract doc comments to `SessionListItem`, `ListSessionInboxOptions`, `SessionInboxStore`, and its `list` / `snapshot` methods.
- Add `PROVIDER_ACCOUNTS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` to the control plane's required secrets list.

## Why

**Inbox contracts.** The inbox `list` and `snapshot` paths return *viewer-specific* rows — read state is resolved per requesting user — and that scoping is not evident from the type names alone. The comments state what each type and method returns, rather than narrating how it is built.

**Required secret.** `PROVIDER_ACCOUNTS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is a required Worker secret binding. The README already says so indirectly, under the *optional* `provider_accounts_encryption_key` Terraform variable ("Terraform supplies the required `PROVIDER_ACCOUNTS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` Worker secret binding"), but the key itself was missing from the "Required secrets include:" list alongside `REPO_SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. Someone reading that list to provision a deployment would miss it.

## Testing

- `prettier --check` on all three changed files — clean.
- No typecheck/test run is meaningful here: the TypeScript changes are five comment lines and the README change is one list entry. This exact content is already carried downstream and passed a full `eslint .`, `typecheck`, and the control-plane unit + integration suites there.

- Goal creation persists drafted criteria as `verify_criteria` rows and records their ids on `config.acceptance.criteriaIds`; all creation paths (`/goal` tool server runtime, client executor, modal) pass them through, and `GoalService.create` guards API callers that send criteria with a bare requirement by folding them into the prose via `buildGoalRequirement`.
- The terminal Goal-acceptance Work is dispatched with `verifyCriteriaIds`, so its verify plan materializes exactly the goal's criteria — a deterministic checklist that picks up edits — instead of AI re-deriving checks from prose. New `goal.setAcceptanceCriteria` and `verify.getCriteria` endpoints back the goal page's criteria section (inline edit / remove / add, collapsed accordion under the exploration graph).
- `buildGoalRequirement` composes structured markdown (bold criterion titles, judge notes as in-item hard-break lines — a nested bullet would steal the editor's list ordinals and render 1/3/5), since the requirement doubles as the page's editable markdown document.
- Verify-plan generation for tasks without criteria now goes through AI decomposition with the requirement as context; the hardcoded holistic check remains only as the generation-failure fallback and its title localizes client-side (`HOLISTIC_CHECK_TITLE`).

#### 💬 Goal chat with goal-context injection

- The goal detail page's right panel hosts a conversation with the responsible agent, so a user can simply ask how the goal is going. The viewed goal travels `ConversationContext` → `RuntimeInitialContext.goalOverview` on both transports (client streaming executor; gateway appContext → server `operationPrep`).
- `GoalContextSyntheticInjector` (context-engine) injects the graph overview as a synthetic `getGoalContext` tool-call pair right after the last user message — exactly one pair per request regardless of turn count, with real tool chains kept intact (unit-locked; verified live with a real web-search turn through a local SearXNG backend).

#### 📶 Process control & liveness

- Liveness combines `goal_nodes.updatedAt` with the run operation's lease heartbeat (`graph()` returns `runHeartbeats`), so a task quietly inside a long tool call is no longer reported as lost while its lease is fresh.
- Decision-gate cards: coordinator vocabulary localized client-side (`coordinatorCopy.ts`), plain problem statement, attempt ledger, tidier spacing, no example sentence in the note placeholder.
- Finished frontier rows display in work numbering (#1, #2); recency only decides which recent rows stay visible.
- Graph polish: `depends_on` edges drop their text label; coordinator-created node titles localize through `coordinatorNodeTitleKey`.
- Portal widths are remembered per view and per scope (goal page vs chat) with a wider default for task/goal drill-downs; goal tabs title with the goal name; copy-link yields a shareable web URL instead of `app://renderer`.

#### 🧹 Collapsed tool rows

- Collapsed tool inspectors and the running workflow headline show a plain "action + one keyword" line (`extractToolKeyword`); the rich inspector is restored when expanded.

#### Test

- [x] Tested locally — six acceptance rounds against a local full stack (Vite SPA + server + Postgres + s3rver + QStash), driven through the real UI with agent-browser; includes a live multi-turn goal-chat run with a real web search (local SearXNG) asserting exactly one synthetic context pair per model request and intact real tool chains.
- [x] Added/updated tests — `GoalContextSyntheticInjector`, `buildGoalRequirement` markdown shape, `goalGraphViewModel` (heartbeats, done-row ordering), `coordinatorCopy`, `extractToolKeyword`, portal width scoping, goal service criteria persistence.

author: dknauss
body:
**The six-row matrix run on `52ff4e9` was green and wrong.**

Reading the per-job environment rather than the job names shows **three rows all ran `UPDATER=operable MAJORS=true MULTISITE=false`**. So:

- the `majors=false` row **never ran**
- the multisite row was **silently rewritten to single site**

Adding the operable rows in 52ff4e9 therefore *removed* multisite coverage from the matrix, while reporting six passing jobs. That is worse than not having added them.

## Why

GitHub merges `include` entries whose shared keys match. The three `6.9.6` rows were identical except for the keys I added, so the later entries' `updater`/`majors` were folded into the existing combination and `multisite: true` was overwritten.

## The fix

**Every row carries a unique `id`**, so no two entries share every key they have in common, and the job name leads with it. Three jobs named `6.9.6 to 6.9.7 (PHP 8.2, en_US)` told a reader nothing — and **a collapsed matrix reads exactly like a passing one**.

| id | | |
|---|---|---|
| `6.4-floor` | 6.4.9 → 6.4.10 | PHP 7.4 |
| `6.8-fr` | 6.8.7 → 6.8.8 | fr_FR |
| `6.9-multisite` | 6.9.6 → 6.9.7 | multisite |
| `7.0-line` | 7.0.3 → 7.0.4 | |
| `6.9-operable-minor` | 6.9.6 → 6.9.7 | updater operable, majors off |
| `6.9-operable-majors` | 6.9.6 → 6.9.7 | updater operable, majors on |

## And it now says what it did

A step prints the effective policy each row configured — `MULTISITE`, `AUTOMATIC_UPDATER_DISABLED`, `WP_AUTO_UPDATE_CORE` — **read back from the built site**, not echoed from the script.

That distinction is the reason this was missed for a round: my first attempt at verification grepped the `run:` block, which logs *both* branches of the conditional in every job and proves nothing about which executed. Every job appeared to set every constant.

48 test files pass; PHPCS clean.

**The matrix must be re-run on the merge commit** — the previous run's evidence does not stand.

body:
This PR turns the existing empty `Backend/` scaffold into a runnable CommonJS Express service, defaulting to port 4000 with environment override support. It also establishes a minimal layered backend implementation using in-memory storage so the service is usable immediately without external infrastructure.

- **Runtime bootstrap and configuration**
  - Wired `src/app.js` and `src/server.js` as the executable entry path.
  - Added env loading in `src/config/env.js` with `PORT` defaulting to `4000`.
  - Updated `package.json` to point `main` at `src/server.js` and added `start`, `dev`, and `test` scripts.

- **Layered asset API implementation**
  - Implemented `GET/POST/PUT/DELETE` asset endpoints under `/api/assets`.
  - Connected route → controller → service flow with parser/normalizer boundaries.
  - Added an in-memory asset store with create/read/update/delete semantics and generated IDs.

- **Middleware and response behavior**
  - Added request validation for asset payloads.
  - Added centralized error middleware with consistent JSON error shape.
  - Added base `/health` endpoint and default 404 handling for unknown routes.

- **Project docs and environment contract**
  - Added `README.md` with API surface, run instructions, and in-memory persistence caveat.

author: ahmadrehman1
body:
## Problem

`app_track_record.json` — the app's "proof the model works" panel, `docs/BUSINESS_PLAN.md`'s **P0 blocker** — has sat at `backtest_run_id: null`, `metrics: []`, `parameters_backtested: 0/71` the entire time.

Cause: the only job that populates it (`weekly_backtest.yml` → `run_backtest.py`) runs `backtest.run()` **and** `backtest.recalibrate()`. The recalibration tail (lambda-grid SCIP re-solves) alone exceeds Actions' 6h hard cap — real dispatches on 2026‑08‑25 and 2026‑08‑30 were **both cancelled at ~5h**, never reaching `export_track_record.py`.

## Fix

New `nightly_backtest.yml` runs **`run_walkforward.py`** — `backtest.run()` only, no recalibration. That's the ~2‑3h half that fits comfortably in one job (`run_walkforward.py` already runs green in `ml_experiment.yml` since #73). Then `export_track_record.py` + commit.

- **Nightly**, not weekly: the walk‑forward's numbers only move when the M1‑M6 model code changes — and this repo changes it often (#93, #105, #111, #113). A fix merged during the day is re‑measured by morning.
- **No recalibration**: this job never proposes or promotes a parameter version. Recalibration stays weekly + human‑gated in `weekly_backtest.yml` / `review_recalibration.py`.
- **No race with the twice‑daily pipeline**: `run_report.py`'s existing `_would_regress_track_record()` guard merges (refreshing `planner_decision_accuracy` in place) rather than overwriting the backtest metrics this job commits.
- 02:00 UTC — clear of the 06:00/18:00 pipeline and Sunday's 03:00/05:00 jobs.

## Follow-up (not this PR)

`weekly_backtest.yml`'s `backtest` job (the recalibration half) still hits the 6h cap and will keep getting cancelled. Making recalibration itself fit a cloud job — or splitting its lambda grid — is a separate piece of work.

author: yourdigitalgroup
body:
Three connected fixes. Console **V5.19.0** · engine **5.9.1**.

## 1. Full campaign now actually generates
Root cause: the **per-cycle allocation caps** were choking multi-month generation. Generating all months at once, 6 months × 3 GBP posts hit the "3 per cycle" ceiling after month 1 — every recurring kind (GBP posts, pillars) stopped after the first month's worth, silently. In the campaign-driven path the seeded deliverable rows *are* the funded plan (exactly one row per contracted piece per month), so the allocation gate there was redundant double-counting — removed. Pieces the keyword pools can't fund stay `planned` and the audit notes name them.

## 2. Publish dates follow the campaign calendar
Each approved piece now schedules inside **its own campaign month** (from the deliverable it was created for + `engagement_start_date`): spread evenly within that month, minimum 2 days apart, never in the past. Month-3 blogs auto-publish in month 3. Previously all pieces spread across the current calendar month, and any stale/absent date collapsed to WordPress's "now + 5 minutes" safety fallback — producing Scott's "everything scheduled the same day it was generated." Scheduler math verified: month-1 pieces land through month 1, month-3 pieces spread across month 3. WordPress auto-publishes `future` posts at their date — no human action needed.

## 3. Trello mention actually reaches Kellar
A Trello `@mention` only **notifies** people who are members of the card/board — otherwise it renders as plain text. The submit flow now resolves **every** `@handle` in the handoff comment (strategist and `@kellarelliot` alike), adds each to the card, *then* posts the comment — so everyone mentioned gets a real notification. Unresolvable handles surface in the toast warning.

## After merge (Scott)
1. Redeploy **run-audit** (engine 5.9.1 — the generation fix) and **trello** (the mention fix). If the last submit predates your trello redeploy, the missing comment was the stale deployment — this PR makes it robust either way.
2. Verify `kellarelliot` is the exact handle at `trello.com/kellarelliot`.
3. Re-generate the test client's package: the queue should fill every month, and the deploy file's schedule column should show month-by-month dates.

author: kingparamount
body:
A follow-up to the ZS3 performance view. It does not depend on #595 (the ZS3 cue note) and the
two can be taken in either order, but #595 is worth reading first: the note is another thing
this hierarchy has to make room for.

Playing from the view on a real stage showed up something the mock-ups never could: everything
on it carries roughly equal visual weight. The cue title is white, the two readouts along the
bottom are yellow and rather loud, and the topbar title is the same white as the cue name. In
a dark pit the eye has to hunt for the one thing that actually matters mid-number, which is
which cue you are on.

This orders the screen by how urgently each part is needed:

- **The cue title takes the yellow**, so it leads. It is the only thing on this screen anyone
  reads at a glance from a distance.
- **The program change and position readouts go green and dimmer.** You need to be able to
  find them when you go looking — "am I at 12 of 38?" — but they should not compete with the
  cue name when you are not.
- **The topbar title dims while the performance face is showing**, and is restored on the way
  out. This uses the per-screen `fg` that `set_title()` already supports, so it touches
  nothing global and no other screen changes.

**The status area is deliberately left alone.** The DPM and its indicators are house furniture
that every screen carries, and a single screen has no business restyling them.

## One thing I would like your opinion on

The readout green is a hardcoded `#008000`, which nothing else on this screen is — every other
colour comes from `zynthian_gui_config`. That is because the palette has exactly one green,
`color_hl` (`#00c000`), and nothing dimmer in that hue, and `color_hl` is bright enough to be
part of the problem being fixed here.

Three ways to resolve it, and I do not want to guess which you would prefer:

1. Use `color_off` (`#5a626d`) instead. Palette-clean, but it is a slate grey rather than a
   green.
2. Add a constant to `zynthian_gui_config`, in keeping with the rest of the palette being
   overridable by `ZYNTHIAN_UI_COLOR_*`.
3. Keep `color_hl` and accept the brighter green.

Say which you would rather have and I will change it — or if you would prefer the colours left
as they are entirely, this PR can simply be closed; the cue note PR does not depend on it.

author: jadoonf
body:
## Summary Adds a `@pnpm.e2e/runs-nx` registry fixture that depends on `nx@23.2.0` (with its build allowed), and a recorded fixture-install workflow that installs every fixture carrying its own `pnpm-workspace.yaml` with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, under the Garnet sensor. author: harisforges
body:
`content/forgemarketing-firebase-brief.md` — a copy-pasteable email for Daniel, plus the spec behind it.

## What it asks for

Three problems the page cannot solve on its own:

1. **Nothing is kept** — good copy is gone on refresh, no record of what was sent
2. **It repeats across devices** — the anti-repeat shuffle bag is memory-only, so two people on two phones can send near-identical copy in the same week
3. **It ignores the current situation** — every generation is the same whatever month it is

Only the second genuinely needs a backend. The rest is storage, and the brief says so rather than overselling the work.

## The design

Hangs off replacing **one function**. `pick()` becomes usage-aware — scoring each fragment by how often and how recently it has been used across every device — and falls back to the existing in-memory bag when signed out, so the page keeps working offline and unauthenticated.

Fragment ids are an FNV-1a hash of the **text**, not an index, so usage history survives reordering the bank and correctly resets when the copy itself is edited.

Reuses the existing `leadforge-ffeef` project and its auth rather than standing up a second one, and pins the same SDK version so both tools share a cache. The config is **referenced, not duplicated** — one place to change it, and no credential spread into a new file.

## Security

The repository is public, so the rules are the only thing protecting the data. Every path requires `auth != null`; nothing is world-readable. Rules validate JSON, and the brief says to merge rather than replace, since LeadForge's paths share the database.

## Honest limits, stated in the brief

- **Not run against a live Firebase project.** Written against the tool's real internals, but Daniel should expect to debug the wiring.
- It changes *which* fragment comes up, not how good the copy is. New angles are a copy job, not a deployment job.
- No stored data licenses a proof claim. The rule stands: nothing invented, and the pricing and scope questions in `marketing/RECONCILIATION.md` still need settling before any of this copy ships.
- Adding the SDK means the page stops being request-free — flagged explicitly, since LeadForge already made that trade.

- No throttle is consumed, no brief state is changed, no KV write occurs

author: jakechampion
body:
Part of #6643 — precondition 4 of `docs/NATIVE-CONVERGENCE.md` §3a, the browser playground being built on native codegen. Five commits, each a thing a host needs and could not get.

Every one of them was found by trying to drive a Fern wasm module from outside and hitting a wall.

## 1. An `@export` taking a string or list exports the guest allocator

The canonical ABI hands a string or list parameter to an export as `(ptr, len)` pointing into the **guest's** linear memory, so the host has to allocate that buffer inside the module before it can call. A plain `-emit core-module` build exported nothing to allocate with: `cabi_realloc` was pinned and surfaced only for preview-2 component wrapping (`ForceMemorySection`) or a composite-result `@import` extern.

That leaves a host instantiating the core module directly — JS calling `fern#compile(src)` with no component wrap — picking an address by hand. Measured on `@export("fern","shout") function shout(s: string): string`:

| input | hand-picked scratch at 0xF000 | via exported `cabi_realloc` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 B | works | works |
| 20 KB | `RangeError: offset is out of bounds` | works |
| 200 KB | `RangeError` | works, memory grows 64 KiB to 256 KiB |

Nothing in the module said where the guest heap had reached, so the small-input case was a coincidence, not a contract.

The pin and the export are now gated on the **parameter types** — the rule the self-host has had all along (`export_needs_realloc`, `examples/self_host/wasm_ir.fern:10659`), so the two compilers agree on what an `@export` module surfaces. A string **result** still exports no allocator: its wrapper allocates the return area inside the guest and the host only reads.

## 2. Pinning `cabi_realloc` pins the allocator it calls

Which the first commit exposed. `cabi_realloc`'s body aligns the bump cursor and forwards to `__fern_alloc`, looked up **by name**; an absent callee reads back as funcidx 0, so the emitted call lands on whatever function happens to sit there — `main`, in a small program — and the module fails to validate.

It stayed hidden because every caller so far pinned it for a program that also allocates. Two shapes reach it without allocating: `@export function len_of(s: string): i32 { return s.len() as i32; }`, newly routed here by the first commit, and — **already broken on `main`** — the preview-1 shape `internal/wasm/playground` builds for the browser's "Run (wasm)" pane, where `function main(): i32 { return 42; }` emitted an invalid module (`unknown memory 0`, and a `cabi_realloc` calling `main`).

`runtimeNeeds.add` now closes over the dependency, so no pin site has to know the body calls an allocator. Pinning `__fern_alloc` turns the memory section on, which the second shape needed too.

## 3. A preview-1 `_start` exits with main's result

The synthesised `_start` called main and dropped what it returned. Right for preview-2 wrapping — `wasi:cli/run` carries ok or err and nothing wider, which is why `PrintMainResult` exists to smuggle the value out over stdout — wrong for a preview-1 command, which has proc_exit.

The playground shows the cost: its two Run panes each print an exit line, and they disagreed. `function main(): i32 { return 20; }` reported `main() returned exit code 20` under the interpreter and `exit 0` under the compiled run. Only an explicit `exit(n)` came through, which is not how most of the page's own examples are written.

`ExitWithMainResult` ends the wrapper with `__fern_exit` instead. main's i32 goes to a local first so `PrintMainResult` can still consume a copy; a void or non-i32 main exits 0. Preview-2 wrapping keeps the drop.

## 4. `-emit command-module`

The shape that carries all of the above, and the shape `web/wasi-shim.js` runs — reachable only from `internal/wasm/playground`, never from the CLI. Built on `examples/self_host/playground_run.fern` (13 MB, validates), under wasmtime:

| mode | result |
| --- | --- |
| `-check`, good program | exit 0, silent |
| `-check`, bad program | exit 1, `1:24: error[E002]: return type mismatch…` |
| `-interp` | prints the program's output, exits **42** — the program's own code |
| compile | 14 KB of WAT on stdout, exit 0 |

## 5. The shim gives the guest its stdin and its argv

The page's half. `web/wasi-shim.js` implemented no `fd_read` — a guest calling it trapped with "unsupported WASI call" — and reported `argc = 0`, so the driver above could receive neither its source nor its mode, however it was built.

`runCoreWasm(bytes, { stdin, args })` supplies both. stdin is served once and then reads empty, because a reader loops until a zero-byte read and a restarted buffer would hang it; a read on any fd but 0 is EBADF rather than an empty read, which a guest would take for a valid empty file. `args_sizes_get` and `args_get` count the same NUL terminators, since the first is how the guest sizes the buffers the second writes into. Both default to empty, so a guest that calls neither sees no change.

That closes the capability gap. What is left is wiring: `web/index.html` still loads `web/fern.wasm`, the Go compiler under `GOOS=js`, and would have to fetch and drive the self-host driver instead. Not in this PR.

## Tests

- `internal/codegen/wasmbin/export_guest_alloc_test.go` — the export gate (two positives, three controls that must **not** export an allocator), `TestExportedAllocatorGrowsMemory` invoking it under wasmtime for 200000 bytes, `TestCabiReallocPinsItsAllocator` asserting the dependency directly on `runtimeNeeds` so it carries signal with no external tool, and `TestNonAllocatingModulesWithCabiReallocValidate` on both non-allocating shapes.
- `internal/codegen/wasmbin/exit_with_main_result_test.go` — five exit codes end to end, a control proving `SynthStart` alone still drops, the print-and-exit case that would fail if the two channels shared one stack value, and a void main.
- `internal/wasm/playground/playground_test.go` — the page's own regression: a returned value, zero, and output-plus-a-code.
- `cmd/fern/emit_command_module_test.go` — the exit code through the CLI, the contrast that a core module runs nothing, and four refusals (no `-o`, a native target, the http reactor which has no main, and an unknown form whose error must name both).
- `web/test/shim/shim.test.mjs` — nine cases compiling real programs with `-emit command-module` and running them through the real shim: stdin round-trips including non-ASCII bytes, is consumed once, defaults to empty; argv arrives in order and its count comes back as the exit code, so `args_sizes_get` and `args_get` must agree; streams stay separate. Five of the nine fail against the old shim. No dependencies — `node:test` is built in — so it runs as a third job on the playground workflow, ahead of the two browser suites.

Each positive case was checked against its own commit stashed.

## What was run

`go vet` and the full test run for `internal/codegen/...` (all six backends), `internal/wasm/...`, `cmd/fern`, and `internal/sourcelint` (which pins the workflow path filters), plus a `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm` build of `cmd/fern-wasm` and the shim suite under node 22. `go test ./internal/e2e/ -run 'Export|Extern|Wasm|WASM|Preview'` — the ~60 WIT export/extern e2e tests — came back `ok` in 1022 s on the first commit; the rest is CI's.

(Type parameters are spelled without angle brackets above: GitHub strips anything that reads as an HTML tag from a PR body, and `list` followed by a bracketed `T` was silently eaten twice.)

author: platypii
body:
When HypAware forwards recorded data to a sink such as the central server, it keeps a watermark per partition: the sequence number of the last row it shipped. Every minute the daemon asks the cache for rows newer than that watermark. The intent is that a quiet minute costs almost nothing, because nothing new has arrived.

That is not what happened. The cache answered the question by reading every data file in the partition, decoding every column of every row, and only then comparing each row's sequence number to the watermark and throwing it away. On a laptop with a 573 MB partition, one idle minute cost about 6.6 seconds of CPU and pushed the daemon's memory to 2 GB, sixty times an hour, for no rows.

The fix hands the watermark to the reader as a predicate. Each data file's manifest already records the lowest and highest sequence number it holds, so files entirely at or below the watermark are skipped without being opened. The same idle minute now costs half a millisecond. The old row-by-row check is kept as a safety net, and it stays the only check for older rows that predate the sequence column, because those have no sequence number to compare.

## Details

`scanRowsFromTable` in `src/core/cache/iceberg/store.js` now builds a `_hyp_ingest_seq > since` expression and passes it to icebird's scan alongside any existing lookup predicate. icebird prunes data files by manifest bounds before opening them and filters the remaining rows. The yielded-row filter is unchanged. When `includeLegacy` is set the predicate is not pushed, because a null seq would fail it and those rows must be yielded. This is the file-skip that LLP 0040 section 2 asks for.

## Measured on a real cache (729 MB, central sink configured)

| Partition | Idle tick before | Idle tick after |
|---|---|---|
| ai_gateway_messages source=claude (573 MB, 240 files) | 6,645 ms, RSS to 2.0 GB | 0.5 ms |
| ai_gateway_messages source=codex (53 MB, 103 files) | 1,416 ms | 0.7 ms |
| 50 new rows above the watermark | n/a | 6 to 13 ms |

## Test

`test/core/sink-reads-since.test.js` gains a case that records which Parquet files the local resolver opens. A read from a watermark opens only the file above it, and a read from the tip opens none.

## CPU and memory pass

The change adds one small expression object per scan and no per-row work. Nothing new grows with data volume or uptime.

## Notes

`npm test`: 5792 pass. Two failures are pre-existing on master: `hyparquet-floor-pin` (local node_modules layout) and `claude-telemetry-unparseable-body`, which is flaky on master when run alone.
