## description

When an enterprise license-key policy requires account login and a saved account token is already available, keep the current native recording grant while the account credential is checked. A key-only device still revokes immediately, and explicit account denial still fails closed.

This removes the stop/restart race without changing credential priority, denial behavior, or the native recording lifecycle.

related issue: n/a

### historical intent

Reviewed the relevant history before changing behavior:

- #6404 introduced the native grant and intentionally preserves verified in-process authorization across transient failures while revoking explicit denials.
- #6311 made recording lifecycle acquisition nonblocking to avoid a long startup wait.
- #6838, already on latest main, reuses startup authentication for recording access.

This change complements #6838 at the later frontend credential-handoff boundary and does not modify its Rust startup-auth path.

## AI assistance and human ownership

- AI tool(s) used: Codex
- autonomy level: agent
- what I personally verified: pending human owner review; Codex ran the automated checks listed below and the ownership checkboxes are intentionally left unchecked.

- [ ] I personally submitted this PR, understand every material change, and can explain it without asking a model to answer maintainers for me.
- [ ] The problem statement, rationale, and replies to maintainers are my own.

## evidence type

- [x] UI or behavior change — deterministic hook-level before/after regression below; no packaged-app recording was performed
- [ ] Backend change — regression tests and relevant logs/results
- [ ] Performance change — reproducible before/after benchmarks
- [ ] Docs, CI, or pure refactor — relevant checks and an explanation; no video required

## before

    verified key -> account required -> revoke native grant -> capture stops
                                                |
                                   account check succeeds
                                                |
                                   restart races teardown

The added regression fails before the implementation change with authentication state `account` instead of `checking`, and observes the native revoke.

## after

    verified key -> account required + saved token -> keep grant/checking
                                                        |
                                           account check succeeds
                                                        |
                                           grant updates; no stop

The test holds the account request pending to prove that recording authorization is not revoked in the handoff window.

No Windows VM or packaged-app recording was performed; this PR is intentionally scoped to the deterministic credential state machine requested for this incident.

1. From `apps/screenpipe-app-tauri/`:

   ```sh
   auth_test_storage=$(mktemp)
   NODE_OPTIONS="--localstorage-file=$auth_test_storage" bun run test:vitest -- lib/hooks/__tests__/use-enterprise-policy.test.tsx
   ```

   Result: 44 passed.

2. `bun run typecheck` — passed.
3. `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — passed.
4. Red/green verification: with the implementation branch removed, the new regression failed with `expected checking, received account`; after restoring it, the focused suite passed.

author: altair-bueno
body:
The `actionsx/prettier` repository has been deleted (`github.com/actionsx/prettier` returns 404), so the `prettier-fmt` job now fails during action resolution before running anything:

```
##[error]Unable to resolve action actionsx/prettier, repository not found
```

This blocks **every** open PR, not just the one where it was spotted (#44).

## Changes

Swaps in [`creyD/prettier_action@v4.6`](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/prettier-action) in `dry` mode, which runs the prettier CLI without committing anything back.

Two details that are not a straight copy of the old arguments:

- **The globs are unquoted.** The action interpolates `prettier_options` into an unquoted shell expansion (`npx prettier $INPUT_PRETTIER_OPTIONS`), so the quotes from the previous invocation would end up as literal argument characters. Verified against this tree: quoted gives `[error] No files matching the pattern were found: "'!CHANGELOG.md'"` — the negation is lost, CHANGELOG.md gets checked and fails. Unquoted passes. Braces survive because bash does not brace-expand variable contents, so prettier receives the pattern intact and expands it itself.
- **`dry: true` with no `no_commit`.** With `--check` nothing is written, so the job fails via prettier's exit code. Adding `no_commit` would take the dry branch that echoes and exits 0 — inert today, but it would silently swallow failures if `--check` ever became `--write`.

Prettier is pinned to `3.9.6` rather than the action's `latest` default, so an upstream prettier release cannot turn CI red on an unrelated PR. Dependabot will keep bumping the `@v4.6` action tag, but it cannot see `prettier_version`, so that one is a manual bump.

## Verification

`prettier@3.9.6 --check` with these globs reports `All matched files use Prettier code style!` on the current tree, so no reformatting is needed alongside this change. CI on this PR exercises the new job for real.

author: thisisabhash
body:
## Issue \#

N/A — security hardening  no linked GitHub issue.

## Description

Fixes **script injection in GitHub Actions workflows**: several `detect` steps interpolated user-controllable GitHub context values directly into their `run:` shell body via `${{ … }}`. A value like the PR base ref or head ref is a branch name, which is attacker-controllable and can break out of the shell string to inject arbitrary commands into the runner.

**Fix.** Bind each context value to a step-level `env:` var and reference it as a quoted shell variable, so the Actions runner never re-parses attacker input as shell — GitHub's recommended mitigation.

Before:
```yaml
run: |
  base='${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref || 'main' }}'
```
After:
```yaml
env:
  BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref || 'main' }}
run: |
  base="$BASE_REF"
```

**What changed.**

- `integ_test.yml`, `integ_test_api.yml`, `integ_test_datastore.yml`, `build_minimum_supported_swift_platforms.yml`, `build_xcode_preview.yml` — `detect` step now passes `github.event_name` (`EVENT_NAME`) and the PR base ref (`BASE_REF`) via `env:`.
- `unit_test.yml`, `build_amplify_swift_platforms.yml` — same, plus `inputs.identifier` (`IDENTIFIER`) via `env:`.
- `api-breaking-changes-detection.yml` — not part of the original scan but the same vulnerability class, and higher-risk (it has `contents: write` and pushes commits): `github.sha` (`HEAD_SHA`), `github.event.pull_request.base.sha` (`BASE_SHA`), and `github.head_ref` (`HEAD_REF`) now flow through `env:` before use in `git fetch`/`checkout`/`push`.

**Not changed (already safe).** Matrix `- platform: ${{ github.event.inputs.* == 'false' && … }}` entries evaluate to fixed literals (not shell); `issue_*`/`notify_release` workflows already use the `env:` pattern; `with: ref: ${{ github.head_ref }}` is an action input, not a shell splice.

**Behavior.** No functional change — the workflows compute the same merge-base diff and gating decisions as before; only how the context values reach the shell changed.

**Validation.** All eight workflow files parse as valid YAML. The `env:`-bound variables are drop-in replacements for the previous inline expressions.

## General Checklist

- [ ] ~~Added new tests to cover change, if needed~~ (N/A — CI workflow hardening)
- [ ] ~~Build succeeds with all target using Swift Package Manager~~ (N/A — no source/manifest changes)
- [ ] ~~All unit tests pass~~ (will be exercised by this PR's CI)
- [ ] ~~All integration tests pass~~ (will be exercised by this PR's CI)
- [x] Security oriented best practices and standards are followed (e.g. using input sanitization, principle of least privilege, etc) — untrusted GitHub context values are bound via `env:` rather than interpolated into `run:` scripts (fixes ACAT script-injection finding)
- [ ] ~~Documentation update for the change if required~~ (N/A)
- [x] PR title conforms to conventional commit style
- [ ] ~~New or updated tests include `Given When Then` inline code documentation and are named accordingly `testThing_condition_expectation()`~~ (N/A — no Swift tests changed)
- [ ] ~~If breaking change, documentation/changelog update with migration instructions~~ (not a breaking change)

author: jiwonjung94
body:
## Summary

Round 5 on PR #3087 (issue #3061), the scope-manifest delegation seam. PR #3201's sixth independent, builder-blind verification of round 4's repair (PR #3197) graded two of round 4's three closures still open and one Surface. This session closed all three.

**Hole 1 (compound command via wildcard, still open) — fixed.** `_SHELL_OPERATOR_TOKENS` never named `\n`/`\r`, so a newline- or CR-separated command pair still slipped through a wildcard entry via `fnmatch`'s DOTALL `*`. Rather than adding those two tokens (a third point-fix of the same enumeration failure), `_is_provably_single_command()` now requires `resource.isprintable()` — a Unicode-category-driven test that cannot fail by omission the way a hand-enumerated token list already had, twice — alongside the existing enumerated operator tokens for actual shell-chaining syntax. Refuses newline, CR, CRLF, form feed, vertical tab, NUL, and Unicode line separator; the harmless literal cases from PR #3201's own report still pass.

**Hole 2 (malformed manifest, Surface) — fixed.** A lone Unicode surrogate in a manifest string field passed type validation and crashed `grant()` uncaught at the UTF-8 disk-write step. `_is_utf8_safe()` now validates every manifest string field (tool/resource/repo) round-trips through UTF-8 at the same choke point both `grant()`'s write path and every read path already share, raising the same `MalformedManifestError` every other malformed shape produces.

**Hole 3 (audit() episode binding, still open) — fixed.** A session log truncated mid-episode was silently treated as complete, letting `audit()` report a clean, avoidable-stop verdict over an episode it never saw the end of. `audit()` now checks `trajectory_analyzer.final_result_event()` to tell a genuinely-finished episode from one that ran off the end of a truncated or still-running log, reporting the latter in a new `indeterminate` bucket — never flagged, and never silently folded into "not flagged" either.

Code delivered directly onto PR #3087's own branch (commits `5a7e790c`, `6f600355`, on top of round 4's `1e27c69b`). This PR carries only this session's own record.

author: phrocker
body:
Fixes #280

## Problem

`edgeAllows` in `pkg/explorer/authorized/graph.go` authorized a single edge by
fetching both of its endpoints individually, and `filterNeighborhood` in
`bounded.go` did the equivalent per node. Both loops also called
`PolicyStore.Edge` once per candidate edge. For a page with E edges that is
roughly 3E unbatched point lookups plus one per node, all on the hot
authorization path.

`MemoryPolicyStore` is the only implementation today and is an in-memory map, so
this costs nothing now. The moment `PolicyStore` is backed by a distributed
store it is a classic N+1 with network latency multiplied by edge count.

## Change

- `PolicyStore` gains `Nodes(ctx, []shoal.ID) (map[shoal.ID]NodeRegistration, error)`
  and `Edges(ctx, []shoal.ID) (map[shoal.ID]EdgeRegistration, error)`.
- `MemoryPolicyStore` implements both by processing each identifier in request
  order through exactly the steps `Node` and `Edge` take for it — context check,
  argument validation, lookup, clone — so the per-identifier result and the
  error the batch fails with are the ones the equivalent point loop produces,
  and each identifier is charged exactly one context check.
  A context cancelled partway through the batch, a malformed identifier, and a
  registration that fails to clone all surface in the same order they would one
  call at a time.
- `Neighborhood` and `filterNeighborhood` are restructured into two passes:
  validate and filter the raw page first, collecting candidate node and edge
  identifiers, then resolve each set in exactly one batch call, then authorize
  from the resolved maps with no further round trips.
- Identifiers are deduplicated before every batch, so round trips are
  proportional to distinct items per page rather than to edge count.
- `edgeAllows` keeps its signature for `retrieval_validation.go` and resolves
  both endpoints in a single deduplicated call, including the self-loop case.

Three deliberate differences from a literal point loop are documented on the
methods rather than glossed: repeated identifiers are looked up once though the
context is still checked per occurrence, an empty request still checks the
context and the receiver, and the read lock is held for the whole batch so the
result is one consistent snapshot. The `PolicyStore` interface comment states
the request-order failure precedence it actually requires and names those
deviations as permitted, rather than claiming implementations must reproduce a
point loop exactly.

## Fail-closed semantics

Presence is carried only by map membership, so an identifier absent from a batch
result denies exactly as `Node` / `Edge` returning `!ok` denies. Batching cannot
turn a missing node or edge into an allow.

- `resolveNodes` / `resolveEdges` copy only *requested* identifiers out of the
  store's response, so a misbehaving or over-broad store cannot widen a page.
- A failed batch returns a catalog read error rather than an empty map, so a
  store failure is never mistaken for a silent blanket deny.

Verified by mutation. Each of the following was applied temporarily and the
named test failed, then the mutation was reverted:

| Mutation | Test that killed it |
| --- | --- |
| missing endpoint returns allow instead of deny | `TestEdgeAllowsResolvedDeniesEndpointMissingFromPage`, `TestEdgeAllowsDeniesEndpointMissingFromBatch` |
| node batch result returned unconfined | `TestResolveNodesDeduplicatesAndConfinesResults` |
| edge batch result returned unconfined | `TestResolveEdgesDeduplicatesAndConfinesResults` |
| point-lookup fallback for an edge absent from the batch | `TestNeighborhoodDeniesEdgeMissingFromBatchResult` |
| same fallback on the bounded path | `TestBoundedNeighborhoodDeniesEdgeMissingFromBatchResult` |
| per-edge `Edge` and per-endpoint `Node` lookups restored | all three round-trip tests |
| per-edge `Edge` loop inside `resolveEdges` | both neighborhood round-trip tests and the latency test |
| `edgeAllows` reverted to two point lookups | `TestEdgeAllowsBatchesEndpointsInOneRequest` |
| batch validates all identifiers before any lookup | `TestMemoryPolicyStoreBatchFailsOnTheFirstFailingIdentifier` |
| batch checks the context once instead of per identifier | `TestMemoryPolicyStoreBatchSpendsContextChecksLikeAPointLoop` |
| context precheck restored unconditionally, charging the first identifier two checks | `TestMemoryPolicyStoreBatchSpendsContextChecksLikeAPointLoop` |
| context precheck removed entirely, so an empty batch ignores cancellation | `TestMemoryPolicyStoreEmptyBatchStillChecksContext` |

## Measured round trips

`countingPolicyStore` counts **every** policy-store read — `Node`, `Nodes`,
`Edge`, `Edges`, `Revision`, `CurrentRevision` and `SourceClaim` — not just the
ones this PR fixes. `TestCountingPolicyStoreCountsEveryPolicyStoreRead` reflects
over the `PolicyStore` interface and fails if a method is added without being
classified as counted or deliberately uncounted, then invokes each counted read
and checks its counter moved, so a read promoted from the embedded store cannot
go silently untracked.

Measured on a 4-document page, comparing the merge base against this branch with
identical fixtures:

| Page | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Neighborhood`, 3 edges | 19 (`Node` 11, `Edge` 3, `CurrentRevision` 5) | 8 (`Node` 1, `Nodes` 1, `Edges` 1, `CurrentRevision` 5) |
| `Neighborhood`, 6 edges | 28 (`Node` 17, `Edge` 6, `CurrentRevision` 5) | 8 — identical to the 3-edge page |
| `BoundedNeighborhood`, 3 edges | 20 (`Node` 12, `Edge` 3, `CurrentRevision` 5) | 8 (`Node` 1, `Nodes` 1, `Edges` 1, `CurrentRevision` 5) |

Doubling the edge count previously added 9 round trips. It now adds none, which
is the acceptance criterion in #280.

## Residual per-item cost, stated plainly

Three of the eight remaining round trips are batched or per-request. The other
five are **not** batched: `CurrentRevision` is still resolved one document at a
time during canonicalization. That is proportional to distinct documents in the
page and never to edge count, so it does not violate #280's criterion, but it is
a real per-item cost and it dominates the post-change number. There is also one
`Node` point lookup per request seed for seed authorization.

Batching `CurrentRevision` is deliberately deferred and tracked in #285, which
also covers the genuinely result-size-proportional loops in `documents.go`,
`retrieve.go`, `bounded.go:81` and `client.go:390`.

## Round-trip assertions are deterministic

The latency test previously bounded a correctly batched call by wall clock.
`time.Sleep` guarantees only a minimum delay, so that ceiling could flake on a
loaded host, and it was simultaneously loose enough that a reintroduced per-edge
lookup stayed under it — confirmed by mutation. The upper bound is now asserted
on the counters. The lower bound remains on the clock, where it deterministically
proves the fake's injected latency is charged once per round trip.

## Accepted behaviour change

Batching requires validating all raw nodes and edges before the store call, so
when the base returns an invalid node *and* the store read fails, the reported
error changes from a catalog read error to an inconsistent-base error. Both are
"base garbage / store broken" conditions and no existing test observes the
difference. This is at the traversal layer only; `MemoryPolicyStore.Nodes` and
`Edges` themselves preserve point-loop failure ordering exactly.

## Testing

```
go test -count=1 ./pkg/explorer/...
```

All packages pass. Every existing test in `pkg/explorer/authorized` passes
unmodified. `go test ./...` is not run because `cmd/shoal-capi` has pre-existing
Windows build errors unrelated to this change; `-race` is left to CI as CGO is
unavailable locally. `gofmt` was checked against the committed blobs rather than
the CRLF working tree.

body:
## Summary

This is a measurement-and-design session for `Reports/creature-genome-flexibility-2026-09-02.md` §13's articulated-body proposal — a short chain of rigid parts, each following the one ahead, offered as the answer to the owner's "creatures shouldn't all look like a chain / bigger creatures become snakes." Per the task, **no body plan was built and neither `src/` nor `assets/` was touched** — another session is live in `creature.rs`, `brain.rs`, the species files and the material table. This PR is measurement, instruments, and a report only.

Full writeup: [`Reports/creature-shape-reachability-2026-09-02.md`](https://github.com/sgladstein/Pixel_Physics/blob/claude/creature-shape-reachability-ecm8ts/Reports/creature-shape-reachability-2026-09-02.md)

- **Q1 — does articulation recover mobility?** Partially. A rigid footprint's blocked-move rate is set by **width**, not height or cell count, and it's a step rather than a gradient (12 seeds each, `rolling` preset): ≤2 cells wide blocks 8–13% median; ≥3 wide blocks 47–58% median. The never-measured 2x2 (the shipped `beetle`) lands at 12.4% median. Both taper directions (small-head/big-abdomen and its mirror), measured as monolithic 14-cell bodies, land at the same ~54–57% regardless of which end carries the wide part — so articulation's measured value is **length at near-chain mobility if every part stays ≤2 cells wide**, not the "small head, big abdomen" insect silhouette the proposal is reaching for, which costs the same with or without articulation.
- **Q2 — is shape legible at 36 cells?** No, on the instrument that exists. Two 36-cell bodies of different composition score ~0.5% apart on `ink` (5 seeds, range 0.1–1.6%), not the ~15% a legibility-threshold-crossing would predict — `creature-appearance-design.md`'s 9-cell finding generalises rather than being a small-size artifact. Effect-size/power note included per §14i's methodological gap.
- **Q3 — can the owner tell them apart?** Posted as a blind gallery review card (six candidate silhouettes, cell counts in `meta`), id `20260902T194120383Z-3860b1`, unanswered as of this report — fire-and-forget, per the review skill.

**Recommendation:** build the narrow-part (≤2-wide-everywhere) case only if §3's verdict says these silhouettes read as animals — it buys length, not the wide insect outline the owner specifically wants. If the real want is "creatures that read as more than a chain," the evidence here points at **extent, not architecture**.

Three new `examples/*.rs` harnesses (all listed in `Reports/instruments.md`), zero `src/`/`assets/` changes:
- `creature_body_probe` — isolates footprint width from height/cell count and measures the two taper shapes as monolithic bodies
- `creature_shape36_probe` — the 36-cell ink/contrast re-run of `creature-appearance-design.md` §4, reusing `creature_look.rs`'s method without touching that file
- `creature_candidate_render` — renders candidate silhouettes at `creature_scale mode=size`'s own crop/zoom for the blind gallery card

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets --release --locked -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `bash scripts/docscheck.sh` — clean (report indexed in `Reports/README.md`, instruments indexed in `Reports/instruments.md`)

body:
## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Editing an AgentCore agent showed a truncated runtime ARN and silently corrupted it on save

How it solves it:

- Recovers the ARN from the stored model string with a regex instead of matching split("/") segments by position
- Rejects a malformed or truncated ARN before save with a clear inline error

## User Flow

Before: opening an AgentCore agent's settings and saving without any changes corrupts its runtime ARN

1. Admin opens the Agents page, clicks an AgentCore agent, then "Edit Settings"
2. The "Agent Runtime ARN" field shows only `arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:eu-central-1:123456789012:runtime`, missing everything after `runtime/`
3. They click "Save Changes" without editing the field
4. The agent's stored ARN is now permanently truncated, and calls through this agent fail

After: the same flow shows and saves the complete ARN every time, and a bad value is caught before it can be saved

1. Admin opens the Agents page, clicks an AgentCore agent, then "Edit Settings"
2. The "Agent Runtime ARN" field shows the complete ARN, including the resource id after `runtime/`
3. They click "Save Changes" without editing the field
4. Reopening "Edit Settings" shows the identical, complete ARN
5. If they instead type a truncated or malformed ARN and click "Save Changes", the field shows a validation error and nothing is saved

## Relevant issues

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-6737

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes)

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Setup shared across cases: local proxy + Postgres, and the dashboard dev server, both from this branch. An AgentCore agent was created through `POST /v1/agents` with `litellm_params.model` set to `bedrock/agentcore/arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:eu-central-1:123456789012:runtime/hosted_agent_4vm3i-BaTdfOELAs`, then edited through the Admin UI (Agents -> agent -> Settings -> Edit Settings).

### Before (a677242d6f)

#### Edit form displays and saves the runtime ARN

1. Open Settings -> Edit Settings for the agent. The "Agent Runtime ARN" field renders truncated, missing the resource id after `runtime/`:
   ![Before: truncated ARN field](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yassin-berriai/litellm-pr-media/main/lit-6737/01-before-truncated-field-zoom.png)
   ![Before: full settings form](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yassin-berriai/litellm-pr-media/main/lit-6737/02-before-truncated-field-full.jpg)
2. Click "Save Changes" without editing anything. The toast confirms the save, and `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}` now returns the truncated value:
   ```
   $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:16737/v1/agents/071bfa0d-0a38-46ec-9e10-142ce2fe90a9 -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" | jq -r .litellm_params.model
   bedrock/agentcore/arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:eu-central-1:123456789012:runtime
   ```
   The resource id is gone for good and the agent is corrupted

#### Malformed ARN is rejected before saving

1. There is no client-side validation on this commit, so the exact same click in the previous case is the "before" for this case too: whatever the field holds, truncated or otherwise, saves silently with no warning

### After (443f8df808)

#### Edit form displays and saves the runtime ARN

1. Open Settings -> Edit Settings for a freshly created agent carrying the same full ARN. The field now renders the complete value:
   ![After: full ARN field](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yassin-berriai/litellm-pr-media/main/lit-6737/03-after-full-arn-field-zoom.png)
   ![After: full settings form](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yassin-berriai/litellm-pr-media/main/lit-6737/04-after-full-arn-field-full.jpg)
2. Click "Save Changes" without editing anything. `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}` returns the byte-identical full ARN:
   ```
   $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:16737/v1/agents/f3b2207f-88b6-49d3-b841-f65e524424a3 -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" | jq -r .litellm_params.model
   bedrock/agentcore/arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:eu-central-1:123456789012:runtime/hosted_agent_4vm3i-BaTdfOELAs
   ```
3. Reopening "Edit Settings" shows the same complete ARN, confirming the round trip:
   ![After: reopened after save](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yassin-berriai/litellm-pr-media/main/lit-6737/05-after-roundtrip-reopened-zoom.png)

#### Malformed ARN is rejected before saving

1. In the same edit form, replace the ARN with a truncated value (`arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:eu-central-1:123456789012:runtime`, missing the resource id) and click "Save Changes". The field shows a validation error and the request never goes out:
   ![After: validation error blocks save](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yassin-berriai/litellm-pr-media/main/lit-6737/06-after-validation-error-full.jpg)
2. `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}` confirms the stored value is unchanged (still the full ARN from the previous case)

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats

### Low

- The validator checks the overall shape of a Bedrock AgentCore runtime ARN (partition, region, account id, and a non-empty resource id after `runtime/`); it is not a full ARN grammar validator, matching the acceptance criteria's ask for a lightweight check

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

author: ggn-thomas
body:
## Pourquoi

Quatre composants de confirmation coexistaient, avec trois grammaires
différentes : `TxConfirmSheet` (Send / Shield / Jito) disait
From / To / Token, `StlfConfirmSheet` et `SwapReviewSheet` disaient
You pay / You receive / Rate, et `BuyConfirmSheet` (Store) faisait sa
propre chose. Le Swap n'avait ni swipe ni état de succès. Et les sheets
affichaient encore « Cash account », que le glossaire pinné interdit
explicitement en UI.

## Ce que fait la PR

**Nouveau `src/components/confirm/`**

- `ConfirmSheet.tsx` — la sheet unique : backdrop flouté, hero, carte de
  lignes, swipe-to-confirm, état de succès avec lien Solscan. Les deux
  mécaniques de règlement divergentes (`autoPending` côté send,
  `settlement` côté STLF) deviennent `optimistic` + `status`. `fiat` est
  optionnel : le Swap n'a pas de prix USD, son hero affiche le montant token.
- `rows.ts` — `transferRows()` / `tradeRows()` / `feeRows()`, purs, plus les
  constantes `PUBLIC_BALANCE` / `PRIVATE_BALANCE`. Les deux registres vivent
  là, donc la grammaire ne peut plus diverger d'un flow à l'autre.
- `__tests__/rows.test.ts` — 6 tests sur les builders.

**Supprimé** : `TxConfirmSheet.tsx`, `StlfConfirmSheet.tsx`,
`SwapReviewSheet.tsx` (~1080 lignes de layout dupliqué).

**Migrés** : `SendFlow`, `ShieldFlow`, `StakeFlow` (qui n'avait aucune
confirmation avant cette PR), `StlfTradeFlow`, `SwapScreen`.

**Vocabulaire** : « Cash account » disparaît de l'UI — y compris les
3 occurrences hors sheets (`TransactionsScreen`, `ClaimsScreen`, un
commentaire de `ChoiceSheet`). Le Store garde sa chrome mais ses 4 chaînes
« encrypted balance » disent « private balance ».

## Changements de comportement

- **Swap** : slide-to-confirm + état de succès en place ; plus de
  `router.back()` automatique avec toast.
- **Stake / Unstake** : le succès est porté par la sheet, plus par un toast,
  et le solde wallet est invalidé en plus du solde JitoSOL.

## Vérifications

- `npm run lint` — 0 erreur (5 warnings pré-existants)
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — propre sur tous les fichiers touchés (le repo a des
  erreurs pré-existantes ailleurs : `env.test.ts`, résolution de
  `secureStore`, `ProofLib`)
- `npm test` — 446/446, dont 6 nouveaux

Rien n'a tourné sur simulateur : **le rendu des 5 sheets migrées reste à
valider à l'écran**. Jito, STLF et Swap sont mainnet-only, donc non
testables de bout en bout en devnet.

## Divergences connues, laissées hors périmètre

- Le Home affiche « Public Balance » / « Private Balance » en Title Case
  (`homeGridCards.ts:43,52`, `BalanceDonut.tsx:17-18`,
  `app/private-balance.tsx:50`) là où le glossaire impose la sentence case.
- Le glossaire pin toujours « Encrypted balance » ; la décision du jour y est
  annotée (fichiers locaux, non versionnés). À noter qu'il y a deux
  glossaires, `glossary copy.md` étant plus récent que celui que pointe
  CLAUDE.md.
- xStocks n'a toujours pas de sheet de confirmation ; c'est désormais un
  `tradeRows()` + `<ConfirmSheet>`.

## Why
FDRE's core application packages are already reasonably domain-oriented, but operational scripts, reusable-library tests, and active documentation have accumulated as large flat directories. This refactor gives those surfaces explicit ownership boundaries without changing research methodology, API behavior, database schema, or production data.

## Target layout
- `scripts/benchmarks/` — retrieval and cross-sectional evaluation tooling
- `scripts/ingestion/` — SEC ingestion, catalog, repair, and operational utilities
- `scripts/pipelines/` — top-level orchestration
- `scripts/research/` — reproducible research entry points
- `scripts/research/historical_universe/` — HU audits, evidence, materialization, and gates
- `scripts/maintenance/` — repository-maintenance checks
- `tests/unit/fdre/` — reusable-library unit tests; app tests stay colocated with their apps
- `docs/architecture/`, `docs/evaluations/`, `docs/research/` — active docs grouped by purpose

## Deliberately unchanged
- `apps/web/` keeps standard Next.js structure
- `apps/api/app/` keeps models/routes/schemas/services structure
- Alembic and deployment files stay in their conventional locations
- `src/fdre/research` public/internal module paths remain stable in this pass to avoid unnecessary import/API churn
- no research parameters, evidence status, universe logic, retrieval behavior, or data are changed

## Guardrail
CI now runs `python -m scripts.maintenance.check_architecture` to reject new flat script entry points, stale flat-script references, and uncategorized active docs.

## Validation
Final head: `d75904ff5445ec718d7e6354e6fa9ef15c922ee1`

GitHub CI run #448 is fully green:
- repository architecture validation
- Ruff
- mypy
- pytest
- Alembic migration validation
- PostgreSQL retrieval-index validation
- Docker Compose validation
- GitHub Actions validation
- frontend dependency audit, lint, typecheck, build, and Playwright E2E

The fresh Vercel preview is `READY`, its status check is green, and the branch preview responds HTTP 200. Temporary write-enabled migration/fix workflows used during the refactor were removed before final validation.

author: devsdmf
body:
on_gateway_shutdown only dispatched app on_shutdown hooks and returned early when no lifecycle dispatcher was set; it never stopped the backend processes spawned by start_enabled_app_backends. On gateway stop those backends were left running -- reparented to init and still bound to their ports -- until _reap_stale_app_backends cleared them at the next startup, surfacing as false "connected" state in downstream clients.

Add stop_all_app_backends() in apps/backend.py: snapshot the process registry under _lock, release it, then stop_app_backend each best-effort so one failure cannot block the rest. Call it from on_gateway_shutdown after the shutdown hooks and unconditionally -- a missing dispatcher now only skips hooks, not process teardown. Offloaded to the subprocess executor, mirroring teardown_app_runtime's hooks-then-process ordering. _reap_stale_app_backends remains as the crash safety net.

## Problem / Motivation

App backend processes are orphaned after the gateway stops. When the gateway shuts down (`kirocrew stop` → SIGTERM), the backends it spawned at boot via `start_enabled_app_backends()` are **not** terminated. They survive, get reparented to PID 1, and keep running — still bound to their assigned ports. `kirocrew status` correctly reports the gateway as stopped while the orphaned backends silently keep serving (e.g. still answering their health endpoint and heartbeating downstream clients), which manifests as a false "connected" state in anything talking to them. Reproduced with the default `lifecycle: "gateway"`.

## Why it matters

Every enabled app with a `backend` block leaks a live process on every gateway stop/restart. The orphans hold their ports and keep emitting traffic, so clients see a running backend when the gateway is down; a subsequent gateway start then contends with (or reaps) the stragglers. It affects every install, is silent, and compounds across restarts.

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

- **Symptom:** after `kirocrew stop`, an app backend PID is still alive with PPID 1, still listening on its port.
- **Root cause:** the gateway-shutdown path (`dashboard/server.py` `_hooks_shutdown` → `apps/hooks_integration.py::on_gateway_shutdown`) only dispatches each app's `on_shutdown` hook, and returns early when `_lifecycle_dispatcher` is unset. It never calls `stop_app_backend` / any process teardown. Backends were only reaped lazily at the *next* startup via `_reap_stale_app_backends`. `apps/teardown.py` does stop backends for every app, but teardown is not invoked on gateway shutdown.
- **Change:**
  - New `stop_all_app_backends()` in `apps/backend.py` — snapshots the `_processes` names under `_lock`, releases the lock (each `stop_app_backend` re-acquires the non-reentrant `_lock`, so holding it would deadlock), then stops each best-effort so one app's failure can't block the rest.
  - `on_gateway_shutdown()` now runs the shutdown **hooks first**, then stops the backend **processes**, and does so **unconditionally** — the early `return` is gone, so a missing lifecycle dispatcher only skips hooks, not process teardown. The blocking stop is offloaded to the `subprocess_executor`, matching `teardown_app_runtime`'s hooks-then-process ordering and offload.
  - `_reap_stale_app_backends` is kept as the crash/hard-kill safety net.

## Tests

`test/test_lifecycle_hooks.py::TestGatewayShutdownStopsBackends`:
- `test_shutdown_stops_backends_after_hooks` — locks in the ordering (shutdown hooks dispatched **before** backends are stopped) and that `stop_all_app_backends` is invoked.
- `test_shutdown_stops_backends_without_lifecycle_dispatcher` — the core regression guard: with `_lifecycle_dispatcher` unset, backends are **still** stopped (the old early `return` skipped process teardown entirely).

Full file passes (28 tests); the previously-passing `test_apps_instances_loop_offload` and `test_dashboard_server_startup_coverage` remain green.

## Manual verification

Reproduced on macOS with an enabled app that declares a `backend` block, running the gateway from source:

1. `kirocrew gateway` → confirm the backend is a child of the gateway: `pgrep -f "apps/<app>/backend/server.py"` shows PID with PPID == gateway PID.
2. `kirocrew stop`.
3. Re-check the PID.

- **Before this change:** the backend PID is still alive with **PPID 1** and still listening on its port (orphan).
- **After this change:** the backend PID is **gone** immediately after `kirocrew stop`; no app-backend processes remain.

## Related Issues

Fixes #<issue-number> <!-- replace with the filed "App backend processes are orphaned after the gateway stops" issue -->

## Pattern harvest

Rule candidate: review-prompt / semgrep
Pattern: a lifecycle/shutdown handler guarded by an early `return` on an *optional* collaborator (here `if not _lifecycle_dispatcher: return`) that also skips *mandatory, unrelated* teardown below it. Cleanup that must always run should sit outside such guards; guard only the concern the collaborator owns. Generalizes to any `on_*_shutdown`/`on_cleanup` that both runs hooks and must release OS resources (processes, sockets, temp files).

## Checklist

- [x] At most two commits (one is the norm), with a Conventional Commits title (`feat|fix|docs|refactor|perf|test|chore|ci|build|revert: ...`)
- [x] Existing tests pass and new tests added for new functionality
- [x] Self-review completed; code follows project style guidelines
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable) — N/A, no user-facing docs affected
- [x] No secrets, credentials, or internal references in the diff

body:
## What

Executes the four recommendations of `knowledge/stats/pages/e-betting-metrics-2026-09-02.md` (the operator's 2026-09-01 question on using testing-by-betting for metrics insight, checked against seven papers in `knowledge/stats/raw/`). All additive; no verdict, statistic, threshold, fire tick, α accounting or wealth book moves.

1. **`DetectorVerdict.evidence?`** (`types/verdict-extensions/evidence-surface.ts`, ADR 0027 amendment 8) on the five per-tick wealth detectors: log-wealth, realized log-increment, bet, `nats_to_threshold` with `threshold_kind ∈ {ville, bootstrap, priced}`, realized growth rate, `anytime_p = 1/max wealth`. The mixture records its uncapped log past the 120-nat cap of the linear view. The validity boundary is on the type: on an estimated-baseline path these are bookkeeping, not evidence (`validity-envelope.ts` records the Family A plug-ins at E[e|H0] → ~1e8).
2. **e-BH `log_threshold_e` / `log_margin`** (`fleet/e-bh.ts`, both variants): margin ≥ 0 iff selected, checked on 200 random snapshots.
3. **`fleet/calibration-monitor.ts`**: Tessera's runtime calibration monitor ported with its tests (bounded/gaussian increments, per-λ capital average, sticky revocation), contract-agnostic, plus the increment estimator `E[exp(Δ log M)]` as a reported instrument.
4. **`detectors/mixture-confidence-sequence.ts`** + study `validation/mixture-cs/` (pre-registered at `f477ae4` before the module existed; 19/19 endpoints HELD at N=4000). The CS is the mixture the detector already runs, inverted (Howard 2021 eq. 14; Ramdas 2023 eq. 22); wired onto the mixture result as a reported field per the registered outcome rule. The estimation premise is priced in closed form (P3) and measured as deployed (P4: 0.58 / 0.33 / 0.09 uniform miss at m = 30/100/500).

## Papers

Howard–Ramdas–McAuliffe–Sekhon 2021 (eq. 14, §3.6, §6); Ramdas–Grünwald–Vovk–Shafer 2023 (§2.4, §2.7, §5.1, §6.3); Grünwald–de Heide–Koolen 2024 (§6); Waudby-Smith–Ramdas 2024 (Prop. 2, Thm 3, App. B.3); Shafer 2021 (§2.3); Johari et al. 2017 (§4).

- Suite 384/384 (`npm test`); dist rebuilt and committed.
- Certification cards re-frozen in a dedicated commit; `cert:verdict` byte-identical before/after; README row states the five detector source shas that moved and why.
- Consumers: DeploySignal's `DetectorTripV2` drops `evidence` until amended (a forward-compatible consumer PR is in flight); `tessera-rng`'s `buildSurface` ignores the new e-BH fields until it reads them. Both need a re-pin to see any of this.

author: tryoooooofff
body:
## Why

Investigating "why does the server keep sending HTTP responses?" turned up two things:

1. **The old HTTP keepalive cron was still running.** `.github/workflows/ping-render.yml` curled two Render URLs every 14 minutes (~200+ HTTP responses/day) — and half of them hit `molorr-server.onrender.com`, a hostname that no longer exists (the current services are `molorr-server-t34o` / `molorr-server-sg`), so every run also burned 3 curl retries on DNS failures. External **UptimeRobot** now covers keepalive, so this workflow is pure noise.

2. **No visibility into the remaining HTTP.** Real gameplay is 100% WebSocket (binary frames after the RFC 6455 `101` upgrade), so any plain-HTTP response the server emits is by definition foreign traffic (Render health probes, UptimeRobot, stray browsers/crawlers) — but nothing logged *who* it was or *where* it went.

## Changes

- **Delete `.github/workflows/ping-render.yml`** (−22 lines). Stops the recurring HTTP; the dead hostname disappears with it.
- **`entry.js`: per-minute HTTP audit log** (+38 lines, most of it comments):
  - counts every plain-HTTP response when it is actually flushed (`res.on("finish")`) — WebSocket upgrades travel the proxied raw-TCP pipe and are **never** counted;
  - every 60s prints **one** aggregated line with `count× METHOD path → status | route (entry-direct vs proxy→Next.js:3080) | user-agent`, flagging it as non-game traffic;
  - completely silent in minutes with zero HTTP; no behavioral change to the proxy, no new requests, no response changes.

Example output (verified with a local simulation):

```
[http-audit] ⚠ 6 plain-HTTP response(s) in the last 60s — gameplay is WebSocket-only, so this is external traffic; act on the sources below. Where it went: 4× GET / → 200 via proxy→Next.js:3080 | ua=Render/1.0 | 1× GET / → 200 via proxy→Next.js:3080 | ua=UptimeRobot/2.0 | 1× GET /status → 200 via entry(direct answer) | ua=curl/8.0
```

After this, the only HTTP left on the game servers is the mandatory one-time `101` handshake per WebSocket connection plus platform health probes — and any of it will now show up, labeled, in the logs.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --check entry.js` — syntax OK
- [x] Simulated server run: aggregation, per-route/per-UA grouping, and silent-minute behavior verified
- [ ] Observe Render logs after deploy for the `[http-audit]` lines

author: 0xteme
body:
## Summary

This PR enables full end-to-end support for custom types in template-based enrichers, adds configurable relationships between graph nodes, and resolves several edge cases in Neo4j graph serialization.

## Key Changes

### 1. Custom Type Resolution in Template Enrichers
- **Template Enricher:** Resolves custom input and output types through `TypeRegistryService` when `owner_id` and `db` are provided (main runtime and `/test` endpoint).
- **Template Discovery:** Fixed enricher lookup so user templates are returned when filtering by custom type categories, rather than short-circuiting to an empty list.
- **Dynamic Pydantic Models:** Mapped JSON Schema property types (`string`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`) to proper Python types during dynamic model construction.
- **Template Context:** Exposed all input fields to Jinja rendering rather than only the single designated `key`.

### 2. Configurable Node Labels and Relationships
- **Output Key:** Added optional `output.key` to `TemplateOutput` allowing templates to specify which mapped response field serves as the entity's `nodeLabel`.
- **Configurable Relationships:** Added optional `relationship` to `Template` (e.g. `OWNS_DOMAIN`), defaulting cleanly to `HAS_<OUTPUT_TYPE>` if omitted (replacing the hardcoded `HAS_SOCIAL_ACCOUNT`).
- **Template Generator:** Updated the LLM system prompt to document `relationship` and `output.key`.

### 3. Neo4j & Graph Fixes
- **Cypher Escaping:** Backtick-escaped node types and relationship labels in `MERGE`/`MATCH` queries to support custom types with hyphens or spaces (e.g. `Test-org`).
- **Deserialization:** Correctly set `entity.nodeLabel` when deserializing Neo4j dictionaries so node labels are preserved.
- **Fallback:** Handled `None` `nodeLabel` by defaulting to an empty string in edge serialization.

## Verification
- Unit tests added covering custom type resolution, dynamic model types, template rendering, relationship creation, and Cypher escaping.
- Tested against a live local dev environment and Neo4j instance.

author: sarveshtechlearning-star
body:
## Summary
First-time uploads across all 6 PDF-attaching trackers now get a standardized name like `Polity_FundamentalRights_1.pdf` instead of keeping the raw uploaded file's own name (e.g. a phone scan's `IMG_2354.pdf`). Replacing an existing file always keeps its current name unchanged.

## Why
Requested directly.

## Implementation
- `nextFileNamePrefix(records, rec, groupKeyFn, labelParts)` builds `Subject_Subtopic_N` (no extension) - N is 1 + however many *other* rows in the same tracker, matching the same group key, already have a file. Per-subtopic numbering, not global.
- `fileNameToken()` strips everything except letters/digits, so `"Art & Culture"` becomes `"ArtCulture"` rather than a messy run of underscores.
- Wired into all 6 `DriveFileCell` call sites, each using whatever identifying fields that tracker actually has:
  - Classes, Single Pager: Subject + (Subtopic, or Topic if Subtopic is blank)
  - Current Affairs: Subject + (Subtopic or its own `relevantSyllabusTopic` field)
  - Tamil Reading/Writing: fixed `"TamilLiterature"` label + Topic (no Subject/Subtopic field exists there)
  - GS Answer Writing: GS Paper + Topic (no Subject field there)
- `uploadDriveFile` gains an optional `desiredName` param - falls back to the raw file's own name if not provided, so nothing breaks for any future call site that doesn't pass one.
- **Deliberate design decision, not an oversight**: a *replace* always keeps the file's current name exactly as-is and never recomputes it. Reusing the counting logic on replace risks two files colliding on the same number whenever upload order and row order diverge (a row uploaded second as "_2", later replacing an earlier row that's "_1", would independently recompute and land on "_2" again, since a plain count can't recover which specific number a row originally got). Only the very first upload on a row is ever renamed.

## Testing
`npm run build` - clean. Validated the naming/counting logic with 9 synthetic scenarios (first upload, second upload in the same group, an independent counter for a different subtopic, special-character squashing, a blank-subtopic-falls-back-to-topic case, self-exclusion from the count, Tamil's topic-only grouping, and GS Answer Writing's paper+topic grouping showing two papers stay independent even sharing a topic name) - all matched expected output. Separately verified the replace-keeps-existing-name behavior directly (confirmed it holds even though a freshly computed prefix would suggest a different name), plus extension handling (uppercase `.PDF` preserved, a missing extension falls back to `.pdf`).

I don't have browser/Google Drive access this session to confirm an actual end-to-end upload - please verify on the preview link before merging.

## Database Changes
None - this only changes what name gets sent to the Google Drive API on upload; the app's own stored data shape (`{id, name}`) is unchanged.

## Breaking Changes
None. Already-uploaded files keep their existing names untouched (nothing renames retroactively) - this only affects files uploaded from now on.

## Screenshots
Not applicable (Drive-side behavior) - please test an actual upload via the preview link if you have Google Drive configured.

author: dmedinasalcedo
body:
Paquete de especificación del SIG. Solo toca `docs/` — ningún cambio de código.

## Qué trae

**Reconciliación de las cuatro specs con lo construido.** Decían «sin implementar» después de 87 commits que lo implementaron todo, y el modelo de roles había colapsado de cuatro a dos. Las cuatro quedan en v1.1 con el estado real y con nota de lo que se especificó y no se construyó.

**REQ-SIG-06 · Gestión Tecnológica.** Niveles de activo, dependencias, ambientes, mapa tecnológico y flota de equipos. Dos decisiones de modelo que sostienen lo demás: un despliegue no es un activo (como activos, las 130 filas habrían generado ~1.200 riesgos sin valorar), y la dependencia no es la jerarquía.

**REQ-SIG-07 · Operación del SGSI.** Eventos e incidentes, verificaciones programadas, métricas con umbral, solicitudes con aprobación y accesos con vigencia. Una entidad `EventoSeguridad` con el veredicto adentro; la severidad es derivada del mayor de los tres impactos y no existe en base. Las verificaciones son el motor de tareas del módulo A con un resultado colgado de la asignación, no un segundo planificador.

**Control de integración.** Revisión de las llaves foráneas reales contra el esquema, no contra las specs. Las once relaciones entre módulos salen todas del hallazgo: el activo solo desagua en riesgos y ningún módulo lo apunta, así que la base del sistema hoy no es el activo. Se listan las seis costuras que faltan; `ActivoAfectado` de REQ-SIG-07 entrega la primera.

**Revisión de políticas.** Las siete de Gobierno de la Seguridad y los ocho documentos de Continuidad: 19 obligaciones con periodicidad explícita, 14 escritas como «con la periodicidad que defina la organización» y por lo tanto imposibles de generar, y dos discrepancias entre documentos propios.

**Análisis de FOR-TEC-04.** `7. Desarrollo Seguro` resultó ser un módulo entero: doce hojas, ocho fases, seis puertas de control y 73 ítems de verificación trazados al Anexo A. Choca con REQ-SIG-06 §3.5, que queda marcada como provisional. Material para REQ-SIG-08.

**Dieciséis decisiones** en `docs/handoff_sig/decisiones-2026-09-02.md`, que es la fuente de verdad: si una spec dice otra cosa, manda ese documento.

**Prototipos.** Pantalla de Impacto nueva —el grafo de dependencias leído en las dos direcciones y en cadena—, Producto rehecho con las puertas de control, y la quinta pestaña renombrada de «Operación» a **Actividades** en los seis artboards que la dibujaban.

## Nota de seguridad

Esta rama se reescribió antes de publicarse. Dos documentos de mayo contenían un **secreto de aplicación de Azure AD en texto plano**. La protección de push de GitHub lo bloqueó, se verificó que no estaba en ninguna rama remota, y se reemplazó por un placeholder en los siete commits.

**El secreto hay que rotarlo en Azure de todos modos:** estuvo en disco sin cifrar y en el historial local. Incumple además el ítem 31 del catálogo PTR-TEC-03, que le exigimos por contrato a los proveedores.

## Por dónde empezar

1. `docs/handoff_sig/decisiones-2026-09-02.md` — las dieciséis decisiones
2. `docs/handoff_sig/control-de-integracion.md` — qué está construido y qué no
3. `docs/handoff_tecnologia/hoja-de-vida-for-tec-04.md` — leer antes de tocar REQ-SIG-06 §3.5
4. `docs/superpowers/specs/` — las siete specs

author: iamnamananand996
body: ## Summary An array path parameter makes the **whole generated crate unbuildable**, not just the endpoint that declares one. `getPathParameterExpression` returned the parameter name unchanged for every container type, so a `list` path parameter was interpolated directly: ```rust pub async fn path_array(&self, ids: &Vec, options: Option) -> Result { &format!("params/path-array/{}", ids), ``` `Vec` does not implement `Display`, so that is `E0277` and `cargo build` fails for the entire SDK — every other endpoint in it becomes unusable too. ## The fix ```rust &format!( "params/path-array/{}", ids.iter().map(|element| element.to_string()).collect::>().join(",") ), ``` - **Comma-separated**, because that is OpenAPI's default path style (`simple`). - **`to_string()` per element** rather than `Vec::join`, because `join` is only available when the element is already a `String`. This form works for every `Display` element type, which is what a path parameter can be. - **`optional`, `nullable` and `map` keep their previous behaviour.** An optional path parameter is a contradiction — the path cannot be built without it — and a map has no defined path serialization. Inventing one here would be a guess. ## Scope, stated plainly This makes the crate compile and serializes the **default** style correctly. The non-default `label` (`.a.b`) and `matrix` (`;ids=a,b`) path styles remain unimplemented. That is worth doing, but it is a separate change — and while the crate does not build at all, those styles cannot even be measured. ## How it was verified - **Reproducible at HEAD, not just in an old release.** `container: () => paramName` is still on `main`, and both published `0.45.0` and `0.46.4` emit the broken interpolation. I checked `0.46.4` specifically, in case a newer release had already fixed it — it has not. - **End to end**, not just at the unit level: built `dist/cli.cjs`, rebuilt the generator image, regenerated a real SDK from a spec declaring `/params/path-array/{ids}`, and `cargo check` is clean where it previously failed with `E0277`. - **42/42 tests pass** in `generators/rust/sdk`, including three new ones in `PathParameterGenerator.test.ts`. One asserts the expression is no longer a bare interpolation, so the regression cannot return silently. - `tsc --noEmit` clean. ## Why this was found It surfaced in a Fern↔Postman behavioural conformance harness, where this single error blocked **37 behaviours** on one fixture: nothing about that SDK could be measured because the crate would not build. That is the practical cost of an `E0277` in generated code — it is not one broken endpoint, it is a dead SDK. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---

body:
## **User description** ## Summary - `PUT /api/scoring/lead-intent` let **any** authenticated user, from any team, overwrite the lead-scoring weights used by `leadScoringService` — no admin-role check, no input validation. - `leadScoringService` is a module-level singleton; `updateWeights()` mutates its `this.config` in place — a single process-wide object, not scoped per team. Any team could silently corrupt or disable lead-intent scoring for every other team on the instance (cross-tenant integrity/DoS), and since `weights` was spread in unvalidated, arbitrary values (negative/`NaN`/`Infinity`/unknown keys) flowed straight into the scoring formula for every subsequent `scoreAndPersist`/`batchScoreLeads` call, for every team, until the process restarted. - Fixed by (1) requiring an admin role (`ORG_ADMIN`/`SYSTEM_ADMIN`/`SUPER_ADMIN`, matching the pattern already used by `admin/audit` and `admin/agent-audit` for other cross-tenant-impact configuration) and (2) validating `weights` to the three known keys, each a finite number in `[0, 10]`. - No `apps/web` route exposes this; its duplicate `LeadScoringService.ts` has its own `updateWeights` but nothing calls it. - Logged as OPEN-134 in OPEN_ITEMS.md. ## Test plan - [x] New `route.test.ts` (4 tests): non-admin rejected, unknown weight key rejected, non-finite/out-of-range value rejected, valid admin update succeeds. - [x] Full apps/api suite: 824 tests pass. `tsc --noEmit` clean. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01KpZeFNb6AsNJ9QDHJVaqJ3 ___ ## **CodeAnt-AI Description** Restrict and validate lead-scoring weight updates ### What Changed - Only organization, system, or super admins can update lead-intent scoring weights - Requests are rejected unless weights use the three supported keys and contain finite values from 0 to 10 - Added coverage for unauthorized users, invalid weights, and successful admin updates ### Impact `✅ Prevented cross-team scoring changes` `✅ Safer lead-intent scoring configuration` `✅ Clearer invalid-request errors`

author: aic0d3r
body:
PR: spec: adaptive draft sizing (--spec-draft-adaptive) - port of LaurentZuijdwijk's controller
> aic0d3r:adaptive-verify (25a641c7f, rebased on strix-halo-vulkan df1671a03) -> Nathanw1014:strix-halo-vulkan
> Closes #11 (validation data there). Draft for review before opening.

Controller design and constants are LaurentZuijdwijk/llama.cpp b10641 - full credit for the idea. The censoring-aware EMA (full accepts probe additively, partial accepts average the exact stopping point), the constants (alpha 0.25 / probe 1.0 / init 2.0), the n_min semantics, and the content-class framing are all from his fork. This PR is the port onto strix-halo-vulkan (rebased on current tip df1671a03, one commit, ~75 lines in `common/` only, no backend changes) plus fresh validation on the rebased base.

## Mechanism

Per-seq EMA of accepted-tokens-per-draft, censoring-aware:
- partial accept -> EMA of the exact stopping point (backing off is averaged)
- full accept -> only proves acceptance >= n_drafted, so probe upward additively instead of averaging a ratcheting-down bound

Each draft is sized `clamp(round(EMA), n_min, n_max)` instead of always n_max. Defaults off; two new flags (`--spec-draft-adaptive`, `--spec-draft-n-min`), wired into the dflash and mtp draft loops.

## Validation on the REBASED base (all fresh, this week)

**PPL (spec-independent):** wikitext-2, 580x512, Qwen3.8-27B Q5_K_XL-v2:
- fa on, b4096: `7.0801 +/- 0.04626`
- fa off, b1024: `7.0838 +/- 0.04628`
- delta 0.0037, inside combined error bars; matches the pre-rebase values (7.0819 / 7.0826). Clean across kernel paths.

**Greedy determinism (honest revision of the earlier "bit-identical" claim):**
- no-spec baseline: byte-identical across independent boots (same sha256 across two fresh servers, temp 0, seed 42, first request per boot).
- spec-on arms (fixed n4 AND adaptive n3-7): each diverges from no-spec at temp 0 (divergence starts inside reasoning; fixed differs at ~char 679, adaptive at ~char 378, n=1 sample per arm). This is the known GPU verify-batch reduction class on this backend (batch composition flips near-tie argmax) - it affects fixed n4 identically, so it is a property of speculative decoding on Vulkan/FA here, not of the controller. The pre-rebase byte-identity result (issue #11) is not reproducible on the rebased base (the windowed kv-cache `get_prev_tokens` port landed in between) - reported as superseded rather than silently dropped.

**Throughput (content-class ratchet, from issue #11, same-binary A/B, every cell measured):**

| content class | fixed n4 | adaptive n3-7 | |
|---|---|---|---|
| arithmetic/patterned emission | 41.8 | 51.5 | +23% |
| agent tool-call scan loops (JSON) | 38.5 | 48.3 @ 93.8% acc | +25% |
| file edit re-emission | 35.1 | 36.7 @ 90.3% acc | +4.5% |
| JSON record generation | 34.2 | 34.3 | par |
| novel code @ 28k fill | 23.9 | 22.7 | -5% |

Not a universal win - it drafts what the acceptance histogram supports. Default recommendation stays fixed n4 for prose-heavy work; adaptive for agent/emission-heavy sessions.

**In-harness (issue #11):** three full game-build runs (low/med/high effort) with adaptive on, try-1 success each under a runtime smoke gate, decode aggregate 18-26 t/s.

## Relation to adaptive-mtp-port

Complementary, not competing: that branch is Stew's independent controller (hysteresis climb-counter with a rise-cost table, MTP-scoped, with tests); this one is the EMA design, draft-type-agnostic (dflash path included - the Qwen agent stack here runs dflash). Both independently land on the same content-class behavior; happy to run a controller-vs-controller A/B on the same binary if useful, or to rebase the dflash wiring onto that branch instead of carrying two controllers.

## Honest limits

- Loses 3-5% when acceptance genuinely decays (novel code/prose) - tracks fixed n4 minus probe overhead.
- Constants are Laurent's, not re-tuned here. Validated on one machine, one model family, dflash+mtp paths.
- Temp-0 reproducibility: see determinism section - spec decode on this backend diverges from no-spec at temp 0 regardless of controller; adaptive adds no NEW divergence mechanism (draft sizing only changes verify batch composition, same as changing n_max).

## What & why
Your team trains and onboards each student in person (and sends them the guide). Directing students through the self-serve rules gate (click ✅ / `!agree`) proved hard, so this retires student self-onboarding in favour of **one team-run command** — **without weakening channel security.**

## New: `!onboard @student <level>` (+ `/onboard` slash with a native member picker)
Fully sets up one student in a single, idempotent step:
1. registers them in the DB
2. grants the `✅ Student | طالب` **gateway role** (the key that unlocks channels)
3. sets their CEFR level
4. assigns the level role (+ strips any stale one)

Admin-gated (`manage_guild`) and confined to `#admin-commands` like your other admin commands. Re-running just updates the level — no duplicates.

## New flag: `manual_onboarding` (default ON)
When on:
- the ✅-react gate and `!agree` **no-op** — students can't self-grant the role (silent; nothing prompts them)
- the automated **Nour journey DMs stop**
- `grant_student_role` gained a `start_journey` arg; `!onboard` passes `False`

## 🔒 Channel security is unchanged
`hissar_role_gate` stays ON. The channel overwrites (deny `@everyone`, allow the gateway + level roles; admin channels locked per #469) are **independent** of these flags. The gateway role still unlocks channels exactly as before — only the *self-grant* path is off, and the team grants it via `!onboard`. Un-onboarded members still see only `#rules`/`#welcome`; admin channels stay hidden.

## Tests
`tests/test_manual_onboarding.py` (6): grant with/without journey, react + `!agree` no-op under `manual_onboarding`, journey bails, and self-serve still works when the flag is off (no regression). **193 tests across the related suite pass.**

## Deploy notes
- `manual_onboarding` defaults ON in code — after deploy, confirm the live DB flag is on (or `!flag enable manual_onboarding`).
- Existing students already hold their roles — **no migration needed.**
- Team workflow from now on: **`!onboard @student <A1-C2>`** (or `/onboard`).

author: umerimran-10xe
body:
Four defects the 10xEngineers CHI VIP found, plus the sleep/wake restructure the last of them needs.

- **[#17](https://github.com/10x-Engineers/CHI-OpenNoC/issues/17)** `hnf_mshr_ctl.v` — an L3 hit released a coherent read's `CompData` on the pipeline result alone, so a `ReadUnique` completed with its own snoops outstanding (§4.11.2 p.4-243, MUST). Held to the `(neednosnp | snp_getall)` gate `mshr_comp_rdy_set_s2` already applies to a Dataless completion. Also makes the `UD_PD` term at `:3284` reachable, which the old timing made dead (§4.4.1 p.4-194, MUST).
- **[#25](https://github.com/10x-Engineers/CHI-OpenNoC/issues/25) / [#29](https://github.com/10x-Engineers/CHI-OpenNoC/issues/29)** `snf_data_buffer.v` — the WriteDataCancel event, the data-phase completion and the entry it named were computed on three different clock phases, so a cancel never reached its own entry and instead named an unrelated one whenever two RXDAT flits arrived back to back. Recorded per entry now (§4.5.2 p.4-200, MUST).
- **[#15](https://github.com/10x-Engineers/CHI-OpenNoC/issues/15)** `hnf_mshr_addr_buffer.v` — an entry that turned into an internal evict left the allocation-time address CAM, so a later same-line request did not sleep behind the evict's own downstream write (§2.8.1 p.2-114, MUST; §4.11 p.4-242, MUST). Problem 2's before-the-evict half is **not** fixed.
- **[#95](https://github.com/10x-Engineers/CHI-OpenNoC/issues/95)** `hnf_mshr_ctl.v` — that widening puts a second writer on the sleep state, so the single successor slot per blocker becomes a per-blocker sleeper bit-vector and the four writers become a per-entry generate that ORs rather than overrides by program order. **This does not cure #95's hang**, which stays open.

## Test evidence

`testlists/opennoc.tl` against the VIP: **90/90 PASS**.

Each fix fails at `6eb4c83` and passes here, same knobs and seed:

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `opennoc_hnf/default.knobs` seed 1 | `CHI-04-112` (§4.11.2) | PASS |
| `opennoc_sn/pipeline_cancel.knobs` seed 1 | `CHI-04-114` — the cancelled write never completes | PASS |

[#14](https://github.com/10x-Engineers/CHI-OpenNoC/issues/14) was adjudicated **not a bug** and closed with a stimulus that demonstrates it; no RTL change. Two new defects found on the way are filed as [#94](https://github.com/10x-Engineers/CHI-OpenNoC/issues/94) and [#95](https://github.com/10x-Engineers/CHI-OpenNoC/issues/95).

author: gregberge
body:
Two corrections to the soft delete from #2574.

## The name is now genuinely free

`checkProjectName` skipped soft-deleted rows, so recreating a deleted project's name worked. But the deleted row *still held that name*, so every by-name lookup had two projects to choose from for one `{owner}/{project}` path.

Deleting a project now parks it as `deleted-<id>-<name>`. The id leads, so two parked names can never collide — the same name can be deleted, recreated and deleted again — and it survives truncation to `PROJECT_NAME_MAX_LENGTH`. The original trails it because a deleted project is still listed in the usage charts (below), and that's the name they label it with.

With the name released for real, `checkProjectName` goes back to spanning every row — one mechanism instead of two.

The prefix is **reserved** on the create/rename/transfer path: a name a user picks must not be able to land where a delete will park one, which is the only way two projects of an account could share a name. It's checked in `resolveAvailableProjectName` rather than `checkProjectName`, because `resolveProjectName` retries the latter by appending `-1`, `-2`, … — a rejection no suffix can lift would make that recursion unbounded. Git-imported repo names go through that retry path and so aren't covered; a repo would have to be named `deleted-<another project's exact id>-…` to collide.

## Consumption stays accurate

The account metrics excluded deleted projects while every meter behind them — `Account.$getScreenshotCountBetween`, `period-usage.ts`, `checkIsOutOfCapacity` — has always counted them. So the usage chart and the invoice disagreed *on the same page*: a customer could delete a project, watch the chart drop, and stay billed and blocked.

The screenshots were consumed and are still billed, so the charts count them too, labelled by the parked name. Reverted: `resolveProjectIds`, both `projectsQuery` builders, and both raw-SQL `AND p."deletedAt" IS NULL` predicates.

The staff activation loader keeps the split it actually wants:

```sql
count(distinct projects.id) filter (where projects."deletedAt" is null) as "projectsCount"
```

`projectsCount` counts what the account *has*; `buildsCount` / `screenshotsCount` / `firstComparisonAt` are history a deletion doesn't take back.

## Two things caught on the way

**The stamp is now the gate.** The write carries its own `deletedAt IS NULL` and its row count decides whether to notify, replacing a read-then-write where two concurrent deletes both got through and both emailed every owner. This is the case CLAUDE.md's "never gate an insert on a prior existence check — two concurrent requests can both pass it" covers, and #2574's comment claimed a guard the code didn't have.

**Two assertions could not fail.** `expect(stored?.deletedAt).not.toBeNull()` passes when `stored` is `undefined` — i.e. when the row was hard-deleted, which is exactly the regression the test existed to catch. Now `invariant(stored, …)` first.

## Tests

Five new guards, each verified to fail without its fix: the parked name and the name being reusable; the parked name staying inside `PROJECT_NAME_MAX_LENGTH`; the reserved prefix being refused; one notification when two deletes race; and a deleted project's screenshots still counted in `Account.metrics`.

`pnpm run static-checks` clean; 814 unit and 1282 integration tests pass.

## Not in scope

A review of #2574 surfaced a larger gap neither PR touches: the id- and slug-addressed **child** routes (`api/auth/build.ts`, `api/auth/test.ts`, `graphql/buildAccess.ts`, `mediaAccess.ts`, `testAccess.ts`, `getAutomationRuleForAdmin`, the PR-comment renderer, the GitHub Actions OIDC exchange) reach a project through its build/test/media rather than through a project lookup, so they still serve — and accept writes on — a deleted project. Worth its own change.

author: bjmeetsfo
body:
Every write serialized the per-key maps for the keys it touched into
JSON, to record the membership it left behind. For a key holding a
series that is the **whole series**: appending to a node holding 850
events serialized all 850 -- 8,647 of the 8,838 allocations a message
write cost, and the reason filling a node cost the square of its length.

Allocations per message written, by how many events its node already
holds:

| events on the node | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 50 | 963 | **189** |
| 200 | 2,490 | **189** |
| 800 | 8,592 | **189** |

Flat, and 126x lower than the 23,822 it was two changes ago.

### The rule

The capture exists so a reload does not resurrect an entry a write
evicted or tombstoned: reconstruction from physical pages would find it
again, so the write records what it left behind. A write that only
**added** leaves nothing to resurrect -- replay rebuilds the same
membership from the same pages.

So the capture now runs only when a touched key's membership shrank.
Deciding that is thirteen `len()` calls and no allocation.

### What I could not prove

**The whole suite -- 1,603 tests -- passes with the capture disabled on
every write**, not just on appends. The mechanism has no coverage at all.

This change is strictly more conservative than that mutant, and keeps
the capture for exactly the case the mechanism describes. But a test
that fails when it is wrongly skipped does not exist to be satisfied,
and I would rather say so than imply the green suite means more than it
does.

I wrote such a test and **threw it away**: it asserted a deleted message
stays deleted across unload/load, and it passed with the capture removed
entirely. `apply_key_states` runs during index-log delta folding on a
cold reload, which that path does not reach. Shipping it would have
looked like coverage without being any.

Two things worth a second opinion from someone closer to the durability
design:

- whether the capture is still load-bearing at all, given nothing tests
  it;
- and if it is, a test through the delta-fold path would be worth more
  than this change.

An `#[ignore]`d test, `what_capturing_a_writes_key_states_costs`,
already measured this exact cost -- "JSON on a write path is worth a
number rather than a suspicion" -- and stopped there.

Full lib suite: 1,592 passed, 0 failed.

---

### It is also a disk-space fix, by more than it is an allocation one

Measured after the fact, writing 8,000 messages of 64-byte text across
20 nodes, and reading the files off disk:

| index log | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| total | **86.3 MB** | **1.47 MB** |
| per message | 10,787 B | **183 B** |

The captured membership was written into every delta record, so each
record carried its node's whole series. That is 59x less index-log on
disk.

Per message, everything under `indexes/` together:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| index log | 10,787 B | 183 B |
| WAL | 98 B | 98 B |
| base index | 16 B | 16 B |
| **total** | **10,901 B** | **297 B** |

For a 64-byte payload that is amplification of 170x before and **4.6x**
after.

Two notes on method, since both nearly misled me:

- At 200 messages the WAL looked like 1,311 B/message. It is a 256 KB
  preallocated file; the number was an artifact of dividing it by too
  few messages. At 8,000 it settles at 98 B.
- The base index is **16 B per message**, which is where this wants to
  be and is worth stating alongside the rest.

author: alegzandr
body:
This PR adds several professional editing features to the cut room:

## Summary
Implements gap closing, paste-insert editing, track solo functionality, footage-driven timeline frame rates, marker colors, track renaming, and preview guide overlays. These features enable more efficient editing workflows and better timeline management.

## Key Changes

**Gap Closing & Paste-Insert**
- Added `gapAt()` model function to detect gaps between clips on a track
- Implemented `closeGap()` and `closeGapsAtPlayhead()` to remove gaps by sliding subsequent clips left
- Added `pasteInsertAtPlayhead()` to paste clips while pushing existing content right, with automatic clip razoring at the playhead if needed
- Extracted razor logic into `src/store/razor.ts` for reuse across split and paste-insert operations

**Track Solo & Visibility**
- Added `isTrackSoloedOut()`, `isTrackAudible()`, and `isTrackVisible()` model functions to determine track state based on solo/mute/hidden flags
- Implemented `toggleTrackSolo()` action to solo/unsolo tracks
- Updated playback engine and audio mix to respect solo state
- Added solo state indicator in track headers

**Timeline Frame Rate**
- Implemented `timelineFps()` function that snaps measured source frame rates to a ladder (24, 25, 30, 50, 60, 100, 120 fps)
- Uses fastest video clip frame rate on timeline, falling back to project rate (60 fps)
- Memoized for performance during playback
- Updated ruler to display frame-based ticks when zoomed in, using timeline fps instead of fixed tenths of seconds

**Track Management**
- Added `renameTrack()` action and inline rename UI in track headers
- Added `trackDisplayName()` utility to show user-given names or fallback to "V1"/"A2" positional names
- Added `selectClipsAfterPlayhead()` to select all clips ending after the playhead
- Added `moveSelectionToTrack()` to move selected clips to adjacent tracks

**Marker Colors & Guides**
- Added `MarkerColor` type with six colors (cyan, red, amber, green, violet, pink)
- Implemented marker color selection in UI with color swatches
- Added `PreviewGuides` overlay modes: safe margins, rule-of-thirds grid, and social platform chrome
- Implemented `PreviewGuidesOverlay` component and guide menu in preview toolbar

**Selection & Trimming**
- Updated `splitAtPlayhead()` to support multi-clip stacked selections
- Updated trim hotkeys to trim all selected clips the playhead is inside, as one undo step
- Added frame-based stepping using timeline fps for arrow keys and nudge operations

**Context Menu**
- Added "Close gap" option to timeline context menu (only shown where gaps exist)
- Added marker color selection menu
- Added track rename option

## Implementation Details

- Razor logic centralized in `src/store/razor.ts` with `razorClip()` and `insertRoom()` functions
- Gap closing and paste-insert operations use `withHistory()` to group multiple clip moves as single undo steps
- Timeline fps memoized per project identity to avoid recalculation during playback
- Ruler tick steps now distinguish between frame-based (sub-second) and second-based steps
- Track solo state cascades through playback and export logic
- All new features include i18n strings across 8 locales (en, de, es, fr, ja, ko, pt-BR, zh-CN)

## Tests

author: lucasvital
body:
## 🔴 Urgente — corrige a corrupção do JSON do Google

Erro que apareceu:
```
Invalid GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON (length=28): SyntaxError ... at position 4
```

`length=28` é exatamente o **valor mascarado** (`4 + 20 "*" + 4`). Ou seja, o **JSON real foi sobrescrito pela máscara** e o worker do Sheets parou.

### Causa raiz
O `mask()` embute 20 `*`, mas a checagem de "está mascarado" usava `/^\w{4}\*+\w{4}$/` — e `\w` **não casa com `{` nem espaço/quebra de linha**. Como o JSON começa com `{`, a máscara dele não era reconhecida → num save seguinte era gravada como valor real → corrompeu.

### Correção
- `global-config`: `mask()` sempre embute um run de 12+ `*`; novo `looksMasked()` detecta **pelo run de estrelas** (independe do conteúdo); `upsertMany()` **recusa gravar** um valor mascarado sobre uma chave secreta (blindagem no banco).
- `settings` (rota) e `Settings.tsx`: passam a usar a checagem baseada no run.
- Testes: `looksMasked` (JSON/token/curto/real), `listMasked`, guard do `upsertMany`.

Agora, mesmo que um valor mascarado chegue por qualquer caminho, ele **nunca** sobrescreve o segredo real.

## Verificação
- `vitest run` — 179 testes passando (6 novos)
- `tsc` backend + painel, `eslint` — ok

## ⚠️ Ação necessária depois do deploy
O JSON real **já foi perdido** (foi sobrescrito). Depois de subir este fix, vá em **Configurações → Service Account JSON**, clique **TROCAR** e **cole o JSON da service account de novo**. A partir daí ele não corrompe mais.
