author: h0mele55
body:
## What

Removes `PROPOSE` from the identity write ladder. It is now `DISABLED → DRY_RUN → AUTOMATIC`.

Closes #2241.

## Why removal, and not building the approval queue

**PROPOSE was not a safety step — it was the safety bypass.**

The widen-one-rung rule means a tenant *must* pass through PROPOSE to reach `AUTOMATIC`. And
`PROPOSE → AUTOMATIC` was the **only ungated transition in the ladder**: the 7-day dwell at
`identity-write-policy.ts` is conditioned on `current.mode === 'DRY_RUN'`, and `dryRunSince` is
nulled on arrival at PROPOSE. So the real shape was:

> 7 days at DRY_RUN → one PUT → PROPOSE → one PUT → **AUTOMATIC**

Two consecutive requests from "observed" to unattended writes against a customer's directory. The
rung's *existence* is what made that possible. Deleting it makes `DRY_RUN → AUTOMATIC` a single rung
gated by the dwell that already exists — **the hole closes as a side effect of a deletion**, with no
new gate to write and get wrong.

Meanwhile the rung produced nothing: `identity-disable-account.ts` refused every candidate in
PROPOSE (the approval queue was deliberately never built), while the pass still wrote an
`IntegrationExecution` with `status: PASSED` and a green "Ran — complete" badge. It did not look
broken; it looked healthy while deciding nothing.

It forecloses nothing. When an approval queue is built, PROPOSE returns — with a dwell, and with
something behind it.

## What this makes true, stated plainly

After this lands, **one PUT after `2026-09-05T15:07:17Z`** takes the one production tenant with a
settings row from observation to unattended directory disables. The remaining protection is
DISABLED-by-default plus the 7-day DRY_RUN dwell.

That same first pass is also the **first ever exercise** of `checkDisableBlastRadius` and of
`IdentityWriteJournal` (0 rows, verified against production). Both read as sound; neither has run.

## The hazard this change creates, and how it is closed

`isAboveClamp` sorts an unknown mode to `-1`, which reads as **not above the clamp — i.e. permitted**.
So the moment PROPOSE leaves `LADDER`, a row still stored at PROPOSE becomes an unknown mode and
would be *allowed to run*. The failure direction is permissive.

Closed three ways:

1. **`IdentityWriteMode` is now derived from the `LADDER` tuple**, so a retired rung is a compile
   error at every site naming it — that alone surfaced all 9 remaining call sites.
2. **`coerceStoredMode` at the single read boundary.** `getIdentityWritePolicy` is the *only* reader
   of `identityLeaverMode` / `identityJoinerMode` in `src/`, `scripts/` and `prisma/` — verified by
   enumerating every caller — so there is no second seam.
3. **Two allowlists replacing conditions previously reached by exhaustion** (the shape retiring a
   rung makes wrong): the writer factory builds a live writer only at `AUTOMATIC`, and the disable
   usecase writes only at `AUTOMATIC`.

**The hazard was reproduced, not assumed.** With the coercion removed *and* the disable allowlist
neutered, a stored-PROPOSE row produced outcome `DISABLED` — an actual directory write. That is the
predicted failure, observed.

## No migration

The `PROPOSE` enum value is deliberately **retained** in `IdentityWriteMode`. Postgres cannot drop an
enum value in place, and CLAUDE.md's Task-enum lesson is explicit that an `ALTER TYPE` in a rolling
deploy fails still-running containers with SQLSTATE 42704. An unreachable enum value costs nothing.
`git diff -- prisma/migrations` is empty; `npx prisma validate` passes.

## The safety test is a property, not a transition

A transition-shaped test is exactly what the 4-rung ladder **passed** — each step looked gated or
harmless and the hole was in the *composition* of two. So the headline test filters every rung for
one that reaches `AUTOMATIC` with no banked window and asserts the result is `[]`, paired with a
positive asserting exactly `['DRY_RUN']` reaches it after the dwell. It is ladder-length independent:
the reviewer inserted a brand-new ungated rung `REVIEW` and it went red.

## Also corrected

- The API **rejects** PROPOSE (400) rather than coercing it. Coercing a *write* would store a rung
  the caller never asked for **and silently restart the 7-day dwell** as a side effect.
- The **third** copy of the ladder at `admin/identity-write-policy/route.ts:46` — the duplication
  `write-ladder.ts`'s own docstring says it was created to eliminate, having named two others and
  missed this one. Now `z.enum(LADDER)`.
- **A false promise shown at the moment of decision.** `messages/en.json` + `bg.json` rendered *"The
  product will raise each action for a person to approve before anything is written to your
  directory"* as the confirmation body an owner reads immediately before widening. Nothing raised
  anything, and no test pinned the string.
- **CLAIM CORRECTED:** CLAUDE.md said `IdentityWriteJournal` "has no reachable caller today". True
  under the old clamp; **false since #2187** raised it to `AUTOMATIC`. The advice is unchanged (0
  rows) but the reason is now "nobody has reached AUTOMATIC", not "no caller exists" — a distinction
  this PR makes load-bearing.
- **Why Entra has no self-lockout rail**, written down because it reads like a bug and nearly was
  filed as one. `entra-id/writer.ts` never sets `selfAccountIds` and `matchesSelf` returns false on
  `undefined` — but the writer is app-only (`client_credentials` against `.default`), so the
  authenticating identity is a service principal and cannot appear in a candidate set drawn from
  `ConnectedIdentityAccount` rows. The comment names the condition that would make it real: any
  `authorization_code` / `refresh_token` grant on an entra-id connection. None exists in `src/`.

## Change class

**SIGNIFICANT** under `docs/change-management-policy.md` — it changes a documented safety control.

**Rollback:** revert the commits. No migration, no schema change, and the enum value is retained, so
a revert restores the four-rung ladder with no data step. A tenant that reached `AUTOMATIC` under
this change stays at `AUTOMATIC` after a revert — narrowing is always allowed, so the operator path
back is a single PUT to `DISABLED`.

**Verification:** 661 suites / 9295 tests (the CI Ratchets set) green, run twice. 176 identity unit
tests green post-rebase. The DB-backed integration suites were verified in isolation (9/9) — an
earlier run showed failures caused by a concurrent workflow's jest `globalSetup` terminating
connections on the shared base database, not by this change.

author: waldaara
body:
Closes #138

## What changed

Rich text rendered as bare `p`, `h2`, `ul` and `blockquote` tags, styled by a wall of arbitrary variants on the article container. A heading written in the editor and a heading written in a component were two different things that happened to look similar — and would drift the moment either changed.

They now convert through the site's own components with the `converters` prop: a paragraph in a post is the same `Text` as a paragraph anywhere else, a heading the same `Heading`. The arbitrary-variant wall is gone.

## How to verify

Open a post and inspect a paragraph inside the article body: it carries the same classes as a `Text` elsewhere on the site.

I checked exactly that — the body paragraphs render as `font-sans text-[0.95rem] leading-[1.75] font-normal text-foreground/80`, the shared component's output, rather than an unstyled `p`.

## On the `randomUUID` error

**I could not reproduce it.** I edited a post through the admin API with the dev server running and reloaded the page: it returned 200, showed the edited content, and the server log had no prerender error.

So I do not know whether these converters fixed it or whether it needs different conditions than I managed to create. If it comes back, the next thing to try is `await connection()` on that route — the same remedy as `/apply` and the admin — at the cost of the post pages no longer prerendering. **Worth reopening rather than assuming this closed it.**

## Risk and rollout

Presentational. If a post uses a node type without a custom converter — tables, uploads, horizontal rules — it falls through to Payload's default, so nothing renders blank.

- [x] Title follows Conventional Commits and matches the work

author: terraincognita07
body:
## What
Migration 039 adds two nullable, unbackfilled columns and the single writer of each.
`webhook_last_delivered_at` is stamped only after `Deliver` returns nil, through
`MarkWebhookDelivered`, CAS-pinned to the `webhook_config_version` the pass claimed
under and monotonic. `calendar_feed_key_epoch` is stamped inside the existing
`SaveCalendarFeedToken`, in the same UPDATE as the token triple.

## Why
The ledger (item 23) must not render a watermark as a delivery time: a watermark is
claimed before the POST, holds a cycle anchor, and stands for a send that was never
accepted. No column could say "a delivery was accepted" until now — hence NO BACKFILL,
stated in the prose of both dialects.

## Risk
High: schema, forward-only, no `down.sql`. Newly reachable: one DB write inside the
notify pass's success branch, per accepted delivery per owner, in the scheduler
process — where previously only a pre-POST CAS ran. A failing stamp is logged and
leaves `report.Sent` alone.

`MarkWebhookDelivered` deliberately does **not** advance `webhook_config_version`;
038's prose said a fourth writer owes the advance, and is corrected in both dialects.

## How verified
Full suite green (`-timeout 20m`, TESTING.md package set); `gofmt`, `go vet`, archcheck
clean; patch-coverage gate OK. Red before the fix:
`TestWebhookDeliveryRecordsAcceptedTimestampOnlyAfterSuccess` (the symbols do not exist
on main). `git grep` for both fields in `internal/templates` and `internal/api` is empty.

## Rollback
Reverting this commit restores HEAD behaviour exactly; both columns become unread and
always NULL. The migration is forward-only and both columns are nullable without a
default, so an older binary ignores them. A true schema rollback is a restore from the
pre-upgrade backup.

author: drewrisinger
body:
## Overview

Using verilator within cmake could fail for certain inputs, which was traced to the CMake ``verilate()`` function using ``verilator_bin`` (result of make) vs ``bin/verilate`` (perl script). ``bin/verilate`` sets the stack size to unlimited by default, while ``verilator_bin`` does not, which can then cause certain RTL conversions using ``verilator_bin`` to fail if they create very large stacks.

This should standardize CMake to use ``bin/verilator`` by default.

Fixes #8269

author: andresstbn
body:
## Contexto

El visor de `/docs` estaba fijado a `main`, así que los RF y SPEC que viven en una rama en curso eran invisibles, y producto no tenía dónde reaccionar a ellos.

No hay sincronización de repo ni base de datos de por medio: el visor es un proxy de lectura contra la API GraphQL de GitHub con caché en memoria de Nitro. "Sincronizar" no escribe nada, solo refresca la caché.

## Navegación por ramas

- La rama viaja como parámetro por los endpoints, servicios y estado del cliente, y queda en el query de la ruta: `/docs?branch=feat/x&tipo=rf&doc=RF-012.md` es un link compartible.
- Nuevo `GET /api/docs/branches`: lista **solo** las refs cuyo árbol `docs/rf` o `docs/specs` difiere de `main`, comparando `oid`. Sin esto el selector se llenaría de ramas con docs idénticos.
- La ref se pasa como variable GraphQL real en vez de interpolarse en el string de la query, y se valida en el handler.

## Comentarios por documento

- Nuevos `GET`/`POST /api/docs/comments`, respaldados por el PR abierto de la rama.
- Un ancla oculta `<!-- horizon:doc=... -->` acota cada hilo a un RF o SPEC concreto, así un PR que toca varios documentos mantiene los hilos separados. GitHub no renderiza los comentarios HTML, así que es invisible también allá.
- El autor sale de la sesión de Firebase verificada, nunca del body; el PAT de servicio publica en su nombre.

## Bugs de caché corregidos

Dos defectos que la selección de ramas habría vuelto graves:

1. `getKey` ignoraba la rama → se servían los documentos de una rama bajo otra.
2. `force` salteaba la caché sin invalidarla → al sincronizar veías datos frescos, pero la siguiente navegación dentro del TTL devolvía los viejos. Reemplazado por `shouldInvalidateCache`.

## De paso

El cliente GraphQL de GitHub se movió a `server/utils/`, lo que elimina el import de `h3` en la capa de servicios que RULES.md §7 prohíbe.

## Requiere acción antes de que funcionen los comentarios

El PAT de `NUXT_GITHUB_TOKEN` hoy tiene `Contents: Read-only`. Publicar comentarios exige agregarle **`Pull requests: Read and write`**, y en `Datak-SAS` puede requerir aprobación de un administrador de la organización. Sin ese permiso la navegación por ramas funciona igual; los comentarios devuelven 403 con mensaje en español.

## Verificación

- `pnpm run typecheck` limpio.
- `pnpm run lint` limpio.
- `pnpm run test:unit`: 77 tests en 9 archivos, todos pasan. Incluye `test/unit/docs-branches.test.ts`, nuevo, cubriendo `pickBranchesWithDocChanges` (rama idéntica a main se descarta, difiere en rf o en specs se incluye, sin árboles no explota, main nunca duplicada) y el ancla de comentarios (un comentario de un RF no aparece bajo una SPEC; el marcador se remueve del cuerpo mostrado).
- Las rutas GraphQL contra GitHub no están ejercitadas por tests: se validan en producción.

author: danich
body:
`IsCalled` returned `true` the moment a message replied to the bot or mentioned it, before the dice were rolled. The two branches below it that add `reply_weight` and `call_weight` fire on exactly those conditions — so control never reached them. Both weights were dead code, and the panel offered two controls that changed nothing.

The early return is gone. A direct address now adds its weight to the roll, which is what the weights were for.

## This changes when the bot speaks

The guarantee is not lost, it became configurable: a weight at or above `answer_level` answers every time, because the lowest roll is zero.

At the values deployed today — `answer_level` 990, `call_weight` 700, `reply_weight` 400 — the new behaviour is:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| mention | always | ~71% |
| reply to the bot | always | ~41% |

Those numbers were tuned while the weights did nothing, so they are arbitrary rather than chosen. **Set `call_weight` to 990 or above to get the old always-answer behaviour back** — per channel in the panel, or as the default in `calarbot2_call_weight`.

`aiAnswer` is switched off in every channel right now, so nothing changes the moment this merges.

## Kept

`isDirectAddress` stays. Its other caller decides *how* to answer — through the router or as plain chat — which is a separate question from whether to.

## Tests

`TestModuleIsCalledDirectReplyAlwaysTrue` and `TestModuleIsCalledDirectMentionAlwaysTrue` asserted the rule being removed. They are replaced, not deleted, by a test that pins both halves of the new contract: a zero weight stays silent against an unreachable threshold, and a weight at the threshold answers on 100 consecutive rolls. Thresholds sit outside 0..1000 on purpose so the outcome does not depend on luck.

`go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` green.

author: reachjalil
body:
Stacked on #4327 (`feature/excel-workbook-tools`), which introduces `@openwork/workbook`. This PR carries only its own commit (`eca825be9`); review the diff against that branch. Once #4327 merges this will be retargeted to `dev`, rebased, and its evidence re-run.

## Problem

`xlsx` (SheetJS) was the only dependency in the repository not resolved from the npm registry — it was fetched as a tarball from `cdn.sheetjs.com`, which is why `supply-chain-lockfile.test.ts` existed: some pnpm versions silently drop that entry's `integrity` hash on a lockfile rewrite, leaving the tarball trusted on faith. The package is also the one flagged in the Dependabot backlog as abandoned on npm.

Its only consumer was the artifact spreadsheet preview (`artifact-spreadsheet-model.ts`), which used it to show the first sheet of a `.xlsx` and to write edits back. That path had its own problems: it read cells as *formatted text* and wrote every edited cell back as text (a `1742.42` cell became the string `"1742.42"` on save), and it started the grid at the first used cell, so a sheet with data at `B2` was rewritten with that data at `A1`.

## Change

- **`artifact-spreadsheet-model.ts`** keeps its public API (`parseSpreadsheet`, `serializeSpreadsheet`, `SpreadsheetRows`) and swaps the engine for `@openwork/workbook`:
  - `parseSpreadsheet` returns the first sheet as a dense grid anchored at A1 (`sheetGridRows`), so positions survive a save. Values are the stored values: numbers as written, `TRUE`/`FALSE`, ISO dates for date-formatted serials, a formula's last calculated result.
  - `serializeSpreadsheet` writes typed cells via `cellInputFromText`: canonical numbers become numbers, `TRUE`/`FALSE` booleans, `=`-prefixed text formulas; anything else (including `02134` and `1,000`) stays text.
  - `.xls` and `.ods` throw a one-line explanation instead of a parse error.
- **`open-target.ts` / `artifacts.ts`** — `.xls` and `.ods` are no longer classified as in-app `sheet` previews; they open externally like other unsupported files. `.xlsx`, `.csv`, `.tsv` are unchanged.
- **`apps/app/package.json` / `pnpm-lock.yaml`** — `xlsx` removed, `@openwork/workbook` added. The lockfile diff is the two importer lines plus the removal of the tarball entries; nothing else was re-resolved.

What is below is what merged.

Codex's P1 on [CLIPITFRONTEND#82](https://github.com/aubincorinaldiecooper-bit/CLIPITFRONTEND/pull/82), the backend half. The owner asked for the sign-in foundation that keeps a guest's video and moments across sign-in; this is the piece that makes it hold outside the one tab.

## What changes for the person using it

- **Sign in from your phone, or from a new tab, and your video is still yours.** Until now the video and moments a guest made followed them through sign-in only when the magic link was opened in the very tab that uploaded the video. Opened anywhere else — which is how email links are opened — the account came up empty and the work stayed behind on a guest session nobody would return to.
- **Nothing changes about what a guest tab is.** The guest token still dies with its tab, by the standing decision in the frontend's `lib/api.ts`. What travels is a separate, single-use claim that only lets the person signing in take over unowned work.

## How (as merged)

- **Migration 040** `session_handoffs`: a single-use token (digest only, like sessions), the guest session it names, an hour to live, `redeemed_at`. Rows go with their session.
- `POST /api/sessions/handoff` (session required, rate-limited with session creation): a guest gets `{handoff, expiresAt}`; a signed-in session gets `{handoff: null}` — nothing to hand over.
- The exchange accepts `handoff` beside `guestToken`. `adoptOnSignIn` honours whichever claims arrived: each once; the same session named twice adopted once; an owned session never taken however it was named; the hand-over spent whether or not it was needed; a failure logged by name only and never failing the sign-in.
- `redeemHandoff` marks the row in the statement that finds it.

author: mircea-c
body:
#### Problem

The expected `Cargo.lock` was rebuilt from every workspace member in the repository, so
one workspace's lock answered for another's crates. A registry package sharing a name
with a sibling workspace's member at the same version read as `missing package x 1.2.4`,
even though that lock was right to leave it alone.

#### Change

`lock_member_names` asks cargo which crates the workspace rooted at that lock owns.
Workspace dependency matching keeps the union: a pin crossing workspaces by path still
has to move. A `Cargo.lock` with no sibling `Cargo.toml` is now an error.

author: muhammadasif2017
body:
Follow-up to the earlier pass on this branch. A review of the jobs feature found the tracking side (CRUD, kanban, timeline, parsing, enrichment, attention) holding up, with four correctness bugs sitting in the layer that *measures* it, plus two structural costs the code comments described accurately without naming the cheaper fix.

Full reasoning and rejected alternatives in ADR-033.

## Correctness

**`appliedAt` was the date a job was saved, not applied to.** `@default(now())` at row creation, and nothing moved it when a job left `WISHLIST`. `SENT_APPLICATION_FILTER` already excluded wishlist rows from "applications sent" metrics — but said nothing about what happens once a row leaves that status and re-enters them carrying its save date. Applying today to a job wishlisted in June was reported as a June application: absent from `thisMonth`, on June's trend bar, outside a 30d filter, wrong in the CSV, sorted to the bottom of the list. Now re-stamped when the job leaves `WISHLIST` in any direction (the board allows a drag straight to INTERVIEWING); an explicit `appliedAt` in the same request still wins.

**STALE_APPLIED tested the application date, not movement.** The comment said "no movement for 7 days"; the query said `appliedAt < 7 days ago`. The sibling STALE_INTERVIEWING rule six lines above already used the correct event-recency test. A job followed up on yesterday still nagged as stalled — and with the fix above, a long-wishlisted job would have been flagged "stalled for 90 days" the instant it was applied to.

**`avgTimeInStageDays` averaged inter-event gaps, not stage occupancy.** `logRoundEvent` writes `INTERVIEW_ROUND_ADDED` with `toStatus` set to the job's *current* status, so scheduling three rounds chopped one stay in INTERVIEWING into three short intervals, each counted as its own sample — the more rounds a job really had, the faster the stage looked. Only `CREATED`/`STATUS_CHANGE` bound an interval now.

**Stats used the server's calendar; emails used the user's.** `User.timezone` already drives the digest and reminder schedulers, but `getStats` and `computeTrendBuckets` used server-local date math. On a UTC server, a UTC+5 user's evening application landed on the previous day's bar, and at a month boundary the "this month" card disagreed with their calendar. New `common/timezone.util.ts` (Intl, no new dependency — same approach `NotificationsScheduler` uses) encodes wall-clock days as UTC midnight so bucket arithmetic has no DST discontinuity, and converts back when a true instant is needed.

## Structure

**Company uniqueness moved into the database.** `resolveCompanyId` ran in a `Serializable` transaction with 8 jittered retries. Its own comment explained why: the case-insensitive `findFirst` had no matching index, so Serializable predicate-locked the user's whole `(userId, name)` range and two creates for *unrelated* company names aborted each other — a standing tax on the bulk paths (extension, CSV import). A functional unique index on `(userId, lower(name))` makes a case-variant race an ordinary unique violation, so the method is now `findFirst` + `create` + one `P2002` re-fetch. Transaction, retry loop and backoff all deleted.

**Search can use an index.** Four `pg_trgm` GIN indexes back `buildJobWhere`'s unanchored `ILIKE` — previously a sequential scan per keystroke of the debounced search box. Verified against the plan: `Bitmap Index Scan on "Job_company_trgm_idx"`. `buildJobWhere` also NFKC-normalized the search *term* while stored rows kept whatever form they were written in; `CreateJobDto` now folds on write and the migration folds existing rows with Postgres `normalize()`.

**Kanban board ignored the page's filters** — it sent only `limit` + `statusIn`, so filtering the list and switching to the board silently showed the whole pipeline again. Board and list now share one filter builder and one cache key shape. A status with no board column (Rejected/Ghosted) fetches nothing and explains itself rather than rendering an empty board.

**Date-range filter UI** — the backend has supported `dateFrom`/`dateTo` all along (and the README advertised it) with no way to reach it. From/to inputs on the jobs page, threaded into the list, the board and the CSV export.

## Migration

`20260903090000_company_ci_unique_and_job_search_trgm` — applied to local Postgres, **not yet to prod.** It fails loudly if a user already holds two companies whose names differ only by case; merge them in the Companies UI first.

⚠️ Both indexes are raw SQL and invisible to Prisma (no schema syntax for expression or operator-class indexes). **The next `prisma migrate dev` will propose DROPping all five — delete those lines from the generated migration.** Noted in `schema.prisma` beside both models and in `backend/CLAUDE.md`.

## Verification

- backend: 562 unit tests, 82 e2e, `tsc --noEmit` clean
- frontend: 436 tests, lint clean, `next build` clean
- case-insensitive uniqueness confirmed live (`23505 companies_userId_lower_name_key`)

Also fixed, separately (`dda0dcb`): a stale e2e assertion still expecting oldest-first timeline ordering after `7c07df5` flipped `getEvents` to newest-first — merge-blocking under `e2e-pr.yml`.

Known pre-existing, untouched: the e2e `afterAll` intermittently exceeds Jest's 5s hook timeout on `app.close()` (BullMQ/Redis teardown while an enrichment job retries against Groq). Reproduced on unmodified HEAD. Tests always pass 82/82; only teardown flakes.

## E1 + G5 (v1.0.60 SCOPE): read the source-status artefact, don't re-derive it

The G1c/G3 artefact (`/api/v1/sources`) landed in #1346. This makes the walk and the install READ it, closing E4's "three stores agreeing on zero" gap — a store point count has no per-source identity and no "recorder exists but has not fired"; the artefact does.

### G5 — the box-walk probe
`scripts/box_walk_probes/probes/source_status_artefact_is_served.sh` curls `/api/v1/sources` on the box and adjudicates whether the RECORD is served and usable (≥13 rows, each with a status), not whether everything landed (at T+0 `not_run` is honest). Refuses a 404 error body as the artefact (the `freshness_panel_has_dates` trap). `self_test` drives the adjudicator against 5 synthetic bodies and exits 1 as `run_box_walk` requires; auto-discovered by the runner.

### E1 — the install-log readout (#599)
install.sh, above `gui_done ok`, logs a T+0 per-source summary read from the same artefact. Fail-soft, log-only, set-u-suppressed recap block (braced-and-defaulted). `bash -n` clean.

### Proofs
- G5 self_test: valid 13-row passes; 404 body / transport error / dropped-source / status-less row all refuse. rc=1 (healthy).
- E1 summariser: `status=ok item_count=0` not counted as landed; 404 body → the not-reachable note.
- Both **box-gated for the end-to-end** (a running Doctor at install/walk time); the source-side logic is proven here.

### Next in the chunk
G4 (panel renders it), E2/E3 (Doctor surfaces it; per-surface T+0 and T+1h), C8 (T+1h keeps-updating) — all read this same artefact.

author: mabruzzo
body:
## Overview

This PR aims to factor out some of the data members used for tracking internal state variables:
- I created the `SimRuntimeState`[^1] class for this purpose
- I transferred the `Output_Initial`, `Output_Now`, `Output_Complete_Data`, and `TRANSFER_HYDRO_BOUNDARIES` data members from the `Header` class into the `SimRuntimeState` class.

## About Integration Counters

At the moment, I have left the integration counters (e.g. current simulation time, current timestep, elapsed wall-clock time, number of of complete cycles) in place in `Header`. A case could be made for transferring these quantities into the this new class, my instinct is that they are a different category of quantities (i.e. unlike the quantities inside `SimRuntimeState`, these quantities are **ONLY** modified by the top-level loop).

I suspect I'm being a bit of a perfectionist here (part of it may be laziness -- I would need to make some adjustments for recording these quantities to the HDF5 file) and could be convinced to transfer these quantities. It probably makes a sense to do this (but perhaps in a separate PR -- that change will touch a LOT of code).

## Motivation

The purpose of this PR is to move us closer to having the `Header` class just track immutable values that don't change once the are initialized. I think this is desirable from a code-organization perspective in three (semi-related) respects:

1. In my experience, its easier to reason about large programs (without without needing to be familiar with every aspect of the codebase) when mutable state is clearly denoted as such.

2. In general, we want to minimize the number of these variables to the greatest extent possible. Introducing a new variable is often the easiest way to implement certain kinds of logic, because they make the control-flow much harder to follow (e.g. figuring out how the various `Output_` variables worked was a bit of a chore and I've never been a fan of `TRANSFER_HYDRO_BOUNDARIES`). By giving these variables a dedicated home, it will make it easier for reviewers to see when a new one of these variables is introduced. Often times, it may not be necessary to introduce one of these variables at all (and instead pass the information they denote as explicit function arguments):  
   - for example, I'm pretty sure it would be straight-forward to eliminate `Output_Initial` and it would take a little more effort to eliminate `Output_Complete_Data`
   - I'm also pretty sure we convert `TRANSFER_HYDRO_BOUNDARIES` into a dedicated argument, but this would take quite a bit more work.[^2]

3. (Less importantly) this is a step in the direction towards streamlining the initialization process of `Grid3D`. Let me explain:
   - I've never been a fan of of the way that initialization of `Grid3D` is so spread out. As a rule of thumb, a constructor should leave an object in a valid state, whereas we create a partially initialized `Grid3D` and initialize things piece-by-piece. In more (don't get me wrong, I understand why we do this)
   - For unrelated reasons, I plan to introduce a constructor for `Header` that fully constructs a fully initialized object directly from a `ParameterMap` (i.e. this will help us remove stuff from the `Parameters` object and it will help us pass a fully initialized `Headers` object onto `Rad3D`)
   - If the `Headers` object is fully initialized by the constructor (its all self-contained  -- and we don't immediately start overwriting intermediate state), I think this could make it easier to follow the initialization of `Grid3D`.

[^1]: I could be convinced to change the name
[^2]: I fleshed out what this might take in the data-member's docstring

author: keeganthomp
body:
Cleans up the embedded-yield (B2B2C) API surface and adds partner fee sponsorship, from the earn API audit. One mono PR by request. Full rationale lives in the repo: ADR 0002's 2026-09-02 addendum, `routes/earn/CLAUDE.md`, and the new docs guide.

## Endpoint changes

| Endpoint | Was | Now |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `GET /v1/earn/external-wallet/positions/:ownerAddress` | owner as path segment | **`GET …/positions?ownerAddress=`** (old shape 404s, pinned) |
| `GET /v1/earn/external-wallet/earnings/:ownerAddress` | owner as path segment | **`GET …/earnings?ownerAddress=`** (old shape 404s, pinned) |
| `GET /v1/earn/external-wallet/movements/:movementId` | DB-only; settled by the ~1-min sweep | same path, now the fail-soft **chain read-through** #1583 gave the treasury reads |
| `POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/deposit-transactions` | owner is fee payer, only signer | same, plus optional **`feePayer`** (partner pays fee + share-ATA rent, co-signs) |
| `POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-transactions` | owner pays | same `feePayer` option |
| `POST …/deposits`, `POST …/withdrawals` (submits) | verified the owner signature only | verify **every** signature (owner + fee payer), per-slot errors |
| `GET /v1/earn/strategies[/:strategyId]` | live but absent from the public OpenAPI/docs | published in both OpenAPI documents + reference/docs |

**Canonical embedded-yield flow now** (public OpenAPI + new guide `docs/guides/embedded-yield`): `GET /strategies` → `POST /external-wallet/deposit-transactions` → customer signs (partner co-signs when sponsoring) → `POST /external-wallet/deposits` → poll `GET /external-wallet/movements/:movementId` → read `earnings|positions|movements?ownerAddress=` → exit via `withdrawal-transactions` + `withdrawals`.

## Why this is simpler/better

- **One addressing style.** Every per-owner read takes `?ownerAddress=`; the path-vs-query split and the `positions/summary` literal-vs-param hazard are gone. Breaking, but pre-GA with no external consumers; the dashboard BFF is translated in this PR.
- **The poll tells the truth in seconds** on the partner surface, not just treasury: each detail read observes the exact recorded signature on chain and advances the guarded ledger row; the sweep stays the recovery path; a 404 is decided before any RPC (no timing oracle).
- **A stablecoin-only customer can now deposit.** `feePayer` lets the implementor pay from its own wallet with its own signature: no Kora, no SDP co-signing, no policy-gate change (the partner authorizes its own wallet). PRO-1744 (SDP-pays) is untouched.
- **Partners can self-serve.** They need `strategyId` and live APY, and `/strategies` was undocumented; the who-pays-fees story existed nowhere. Both are now first-class in the public spec and guide.

**before** — a sponsored-fee deposit was impossible:

1. build compiles the owner as fee payer, one signature slot
2. a zero-SOL owner fails simulation at build (fee + ~0.002 SOL first-deposit rent)
3. submit verifies the owner signature only

**after** — with `feePayer`:

1. build simulates AND compiles with the partner in the fee-payer seat, and passes it as the provider `rentPayer` (Kamino forwards it; Veda payer-swaps since #1611)
2. compile asserts the signer set ordered and exact, `[feePayer, owner]`: refuses a plan smuggling an extra signer, and refuses one that never names the owner as signer (money can't move on the partner's signature alone)
3. customer signs, partner co-signs outside SDP, submit ed25519-verifies both and records `share_ata_rent_funder = feePayer`
4. the exit refunds rent to the recorded funder, never the fee mode of the day; split-swap `followUp` carries `feePayer` so a rebuild can't silently bill the customer

## Reviewer notes

- **The compile signer assertion is the security seam** (`vault-execution.service.ts`): keep it ordered-exact; loosening it to a set check reopens the smuggled-signer hole.
- **`VaultFeeMode` gained `caller-provided`** and every consumer is now exhaustive; the custody signing path throws on it (unreachable by construction, asserted anyway).
- **Fingerprints unchanged**: both external-wallet fingerprints already include the build id, so a different-feePayer rebuild conflicts; pre-deploy fingerprints stay byte-identical.
- **`feePayer === owner` normalizes to absent** at route, service, and compile, so the invariant never depends on one layer.

## Schema before/after (migration 0078)

Real `psql \d earn_external_wallet_transactions` diff on a fresh DB via the repo migration runner, through 0077 vs with 0078:

```text
+ fee_payer               | text
+ share_ata_rent_funder   | text
+ "…_fee_payer_format_check"   CHECK (fee_payer IS NULL OR length(fee_payer) BETWEEN 32 AND 44)
+ "…_rent_funder_shape_check"  CHECK (share_ata_rent_funder IS NULL OR creates_share_account AND share_ata_rent_funder = fee_payer)
```

Nullable, no backfill: every existing row was owner-paid, which NULL already means.

**Verification**

- `vitest run` (22 API files: earn routes, services, repos, value-moving conformance, OpenAPI, retired-route pins): **474 passed**; endpoint behavior exercised through `app.request` against real testcontainers Postgres, including two-signer submit with real keypairs, forged/missing fee-payer signature 400s, rent-funder projection, and 404 pins for the retired path shapes
- `vitest run` sdp-web (earn module + BFF proxies): **189 passed**
- `tsc --noEmit` (sdp-api, sdp-web, sdp-types) + `biome check`: clean
- `pnpm --filter sdp-docs build` + `check:links` (55 pages): green — the build caught a YAML-frontmatter bug in the new tag description, fixed here
- `pnpm check:module-boundaries`, `pnpm check:api-playground`: clean; Postman/llms artifacts regenerated and committed
- Local-stack browser e2e is running as the immediate follow-up; results land as a PR comment

Known gaps

- Treasury's `GET /vault-deposits*` still speaks the legacy status vocabulary (`LEGACY_VAULT_DEPOSIT_STATUS`); migrating it is the agreed follow-up ticket under PRO-1519, deliberately out of this PR

author: mastersingh24
body:
Closes #799.

The closing criterion the 2026-09-02 run set for itself was *"core-tui#302 is fixed and §8's two failing boxes are re-driven"*. Both are done — #302 shipped in core-tui v0.24.1, the pin landed in #900, and both boxes now pass against a live runaway on the demo-3 GKE cluster.

## F4 is fixed

| Box | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Esc during a turn cancels **and** holds | fail | pass |
| Banner distinguishes cancelled from gate-shut | fail | pass |

A read-only observer polled `GET /status` at 1 Hz on a second port-forward, so the pause state is recorded rather than recalled:

```
19:41:28 {"state":"paused","paused_since":"2026-09-02T19:41:27.821382832Z",
          "pause_reason":"operator-interrupt","interrupted":true}
```

Both fields are load-bearing, and each rules out a different false pass. `operator-interrupt` with a **hyphen** is the daemon's own constant from `AttachInterruptHold("")`; the plain-hold path mints `operator interrupt` with a space, so the interrupt arm demonstrably ran rather than the downgrade. `interrupted: true` comes from `a.cancelInFlight != nil`, so there was a real turn to cancel — the one thing a bare pause landing on a quiet agent cannot fake. The TUI printed `canceled · CANCELED / turn canceled` alongside.

The window was **not** the delegate-and-wait shape the previous verdict recommended — two attempts at that were absorbed (F7). What produced it was better: the agent went into a `mark_task_done` loop on its own, and a runaway emitting tool calls and no content is a more faithful instance of the condition the old `turnInFlight()` render gate misread than any scripted prompt.

Also cleared, the two boxes #900 added to §8 after the first run: `/usage` pins the tail (core-tui#303's fix confirmed, on the command it was reported against), and slashes-dispatch-while-held — which passes for `/mouse` and fails for `/usage`, recorded as F8.

## Two new findings, neither gating

**F7 — a follow-up prompt is absorbed as "already handled."** Twice, a new instruction typed into a session whose incident was closed came back as a summary of the closed work. The inbox preamble's own last line is the guard against exactly this (*"Summarizing work you already reported is not a response to a new question"*) and it did not hold. Recipe content rather than core-agent, so not filed here, but it is the second time this UAT has been slowed by the agent answering a question other than the one asked, and it is adjacent to #639.

**F8 — a held agent treats host-registered slash commands as prose.** Filed as [core-tui#311](https://github.com/go-steer/core-tui/issues/311). `/mouse` dispatches and stays parked; `/usage` opens the gate and arrives at the model as steer text. Both of the held-input gate's recognisers are static maps, and the host catalog is fetched only for the palette — `slashCommandsMsg` drops the specs when it closes, so the Enter handler has nothing to consult. That reads as deliberate: for a remote host `SlashCommands()` is an HTTP call, and making one inside a keypress is the event-loop block behind core-tui#69 / #630. Four of core-agent's 13 host commands fall through, and the ones that matter are `/new` and `/attach` — how an operator *leaves* a misbehaving agent. Same inversion `/quit` had in core-tui#299.

## #896 got a live trace, and it is worse than the issue reads

Across seven minutes the 1 Hz poller logged exactly two lines: the initial `idle`, and the `paused` that Esc caused. Between them were two complete turns and the runaway. The endpoint reported none of it.

So `AttachStatus()` does not merely fail to seed a mid-turn attach — it never reports a running turn at all, and an operator polling `GET /status` to ask "is it doing anything?" is told no, right through a runaway. That is why `interrupted` rather than `state` is the oracle used throughout the new section.

## What is still un-run

Two boxes across the whole document, both for want of a provisioned viewer identity rather than a defect: read-only attachment (§8) and the old-daemon handshake box (§1), which needs a pre-hold binary. Unchanged from the previous run and called out as such.

## Adversarial review

- **Is the pass real, or did Esc land on an already-finished turn?** This is the failure mode that makes a green §8 worthless, so it is ruled out three independent ways: `interrupted: true` is daemon-side liveness from `cancelInFlight`, not a client guess; the hyphen in `operator-interrupt` proves the interrupt arm rather than the hold arm; and the daemon logged `auto-continue: a turn is already running; standing down` for this session immediately beforehand. Any one alone would be weak — the runaway was silent, so absence of printed output proves nothing either way.
- **Does the pass depend on the new client?** Yes, and that is checked rather than assumed: same daemon image (`2.9.0-dev.4`), same watcher, same content, same model as the failing run. The only variable is `core-agent-tui` rebuilt against v0.24.1.
- **Am I claiming the fix works for the scripted window?** No. The recorded window is the `mark_task_done` runaway, and the doc says so plainly rather than implying delegate-and-wait was used. The previous verdict's recommended method is recorded as having failed, with the reason (F7).
- **Watchdog.** I nearly recorded "`watchdog: enforce` failed to halt the runaway" as a finding. Dropped — the operator interrupted within seconds, so the pattern threshold may simply never have been reached, and I have no evidence either way. Absent a watchdog line in the daemon logs it stays an open question, not a claim.
- **F8's blast radius is computed, not estimated.** The four fall-throughs come from taking the union of `builtinSlashNames`, `midTurnSafeSlashes` and `midTurnRefusedSlashes` against the adapter's 13-entry `SlashCommands()`, with `canonicalSlashName` applied — which is what catches that `/perms` is fine and `/usage` is not.
- **F8 isolated before filing.** `/usage` works at idle including pinning the tail, which rules out the command, the host's `InvokeSlash` path and #303, and puts the defect squarely in the held-input recogniser.
- **Docs-only.** No code, no CHANGELOG entry — this is an internal UAT record, not user-visible behaviour. `verify-docs-lint` clean.

author: mmamedel
body:
`<objc/objc-runtime.h>` is a macOS-SDK-only umbrella header — it does not exist in the iOS or iOS Simulator SDKs — so the six headers that include it cannot compile for any non-macOS Apple target.

This matters even without a mobile backend, because the affected headers are guarded by `WEBVIEW_PLATFORM_DARWIN`, which `macros.h` defines for *any* `__APPLE__` target:

```c
#if defined(__APPLE__)
#define WEBVIEW_PLATFORM_DARWIN
```

So they are already reachable on iOS and fail on the include alone.

### Why the replacement is equivalent

On macOS the umbrella header contains nothing else (`MacOSX26.5.sdk/usr/include/objc/objc-runtime.h`, 52 bytes, in full):

```c
#include <objc/runtime.h>
#include <objc/message.h>
```

Both of those exist in the macOS, iPhoneOS and iPhoneSimulator SDKs.

### Before / after

```console
$ xcrun clang++ -x c++ -std=c++17 -target arm64-apple-ios15.0-simulator \
    -isysroot $(xcrun --sdk iphonesimulator --show-sdk-path) \
    -Icore/include -c probe.cc
```

where `probe.cc` is just `#include <webview/detail/platform/darwin/objc/objc.hh>`.

Before:

```
In file included from webview/core/include/webview/detail/platform/darwin/objc/objc.hh:36:
In file included from webview/core/include/webview/detail/platform/darwin/objc/Class.hh:35:
webview/core/include/webview/detail/platform/darwin/objc/invoke.hh:35:10: fatal error: 'objc/objc-runtime.h' file not found
   35 | #include <objc/objc-runtime.h>
      |          ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1 error generated.
```

After: compiles for both `arm64-apple-ios15.0-simulator` and `arm64-apple-ios15.0` (device).

### macOS unaffected

```console
$ cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build build
[100%] Built target webview_example_bind_cc

$ ctest --output-on-failure
100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 14
```

`clang-format --style=file` reports no changes on all six touched files (`SortIncludes: true` puts `message.h` before `runtime.h`).

### Scope

Header spelling only — six one-line includes, no guard changes, no new files, no behaviour change. Your CI covers `macos-14` and `ubuntu-22.04`, so it will confirm the macOS half but cannot exercise the iOS half.

Found while writing an iOS backend against this library's API, described in #1170 — but this fix stands on its own and is independent of whether a mobile backend is ever wanted here.

author: jjvm19
body:
vision-clipping.com moved onto Cloudflare today, in front of the same GitHub Pages origin. Three Dynamic Redirect rules now answer at the edge:

| request | 301 to |
|---|---|
| `/cases/andrew-tate.html` | `/breakdowns/andrew-tate-clipping/` (retired page, kept its old traffic) |
| `/foo/index.html` | `/foo/` |
| `/foo.html` | `/foo/` (query string preserved) |

`404.html` is excluded and still serves normally.

That is a real 301 instead of a meta refresh, and it fires before the request reaches the origin, so the bridge files are now dead weight. Verified all 54 against the edge before deleting: every one 301s to exactly the canonical target its own bridge named.

Deleting them also closes the last of the duplicate-URL problem from PR #10. GitHub Pages serves `foo.html` at the extensionless `/foo` with a **200**, so every remaining bridge was still keeping a third indexable URL alive as a redirect stub. With the file gone, `/foo` falls back to GitHub Pages' own 301 to `/foo/`.

`tools/redirect-bridges.mjs` is kept as the rollback path only — if Cloudflare is ever taken out from in front of the site, run it to put the bridges back, otherwise every old `.html` URL 404s.

author: michalkalis
body:
Session E (167.9–167.12) ran end to end on founder GO and reached its terminal state: a rating batch of **21 post-filter rows** is live on the prod rating web, waiting for the founder's rating (167.13). Nothing was imported into the corpus — that is Session F.

**Rating URL:** https://quiz-pack-api.fly.dev/web/rate/1eb9a19d-f64a-4de7-9005-100b235a6003?rater=michal (curl → 200)

## Funnel

| Stage | Round 1 | Round 2 |
|---|---|---|
| sourcing | 160 facts / 36 topics | 203 facts / 48 topics |
| generating | 30 | 29 |
| dedup | 30 | 29 |
| verifying | 28 verified, 0 withheld | 29 verified, 0 withheld |
| composition | 16 | 16 |
| topup | 27, `fact_pool_exhausted: False` | 27, `fact_pool_exhausted: False` |
| post-cutoff filter | **19** accepted / 8 rejected | **2** accepted / 25 rejected |
| **merged union** | | **21** ≥ 20 → A13 ✅ |

Rejects: round 1 — 8× `no_2026_token`. Round 2 — 12× `no_2026_token`, 13× `duplicate_round1` (first live exercise of the 167.7 cross-round guard). `freshness_current`: 0×.

`freshness_tag` on the published 21: 19 NULL (evergreen), 2 semi-stable, **0 current** — exactly the D1 expectation, no drift into the news class.

**D6 false-negative measurement (never measured before): ~0 of 8.** Every round-1 reject is a genuinely evergreen question with no post-cutoff content (Rick Rubin / Def Jam, Nigel Godrich / Radiohead, Ted Lasso 2021, Rango 2011, Van Halen 1978, Glenn Close). The filter is not cutting good post-cutoff questions.

## Cost

**API spend $0** against the authorised $1–2 — but for a bad reason, not a saving: ⚠️ **the OpenAI account is out of credits** (`429 credit_balance_exhausted` on every `web_search` call, confirmed with a raw `POST /v1/responses` probe). The paid sourcing leg contributed 0 facts; the whole pool is Wikipedia. Generation and fact-check ran on the subscription via the #169 session gateway (`cost_cents: 0`), judges hard OFF.

No threshold was lowered: JUDGE_QUORUM, the 40-fact gate, the ≥20-accepted bar and the 80% floor are all untouched.

## The one code change

`LLM_SESSION_TIMEOUT` (`packages/shared/quiz_shared/llm/factory.py`) — session branch only, unset = today's behaviour exactly.

`claude -p` is a materially slower transport than the HTTP API the call sites sized their timeout for. Measured here: one fact-first batch (30 questions, 36.7k in / 38.7k out) takes **412 s** on `session:fable` and so died on the 300 s `GENERATION_TIMEOUT` every single time — at 160 facts *and* at 46 facts, so it was never a fact-pool-size problem. The #169 smoke only ever ran `--target-count 3`, which is why this never surfaced. It is a transport belt, not a quality gate; `STAGE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` still caps the stage and every fail-closed gate is untouched.

Two tests: the default is unchanged when the env var is unset, and the override wins when it is set.

## Notes for the next session-mode run

1. `LLM_SESSION_TIMEOUT` is mandatory at full batch size.
2. Mac sleep kills the `claude -p` child and leaves the parent hanging on a dead pipe — run long jobs detached under `caffeinate -ims`.
3. Wikipedia caps at 4 facts per topic, so a bigger pool means **more sub-phrasings**, not narrower ones.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/ -q` → 1159 passed, 1 skipped
- A11 both rounds: fact file older than its pilot ✅
- A12: 0 rows with a null `source_url` outside the `logical_puzzle` exemption ✅
- A13: 21 ≥ 20 ✅ · A14: publish exit 0 + batch_id, mapping non-empty, curl 200 ✅ · A15: reasons + samples + freshness recorded ✅

## Why

The day view was missing two actions that exist on the week view, and "add to calendar" was still offered on sessions that were already over.

`pnpm test -- resources/js/components/legacy/DayView.spec.ts resources/js/components/legacy/GrowthSessionCard.spec.ts`

Covers: copy emits for the owner and is absent for everyone else, the calendar link points at Google Calendar, and both the link and the day-view footer disappear on a finished session.

author: ahmedtmm
body:
> Stacked on #40. Merge that first; this retargets automatically.

## Summary

**Eleven directories have an `index.ts`, and each does the assembling** rather than pointing at where it happens.

**Five build layers** — `thread`, `interactions`, `message-stream`, `state`, `client` — in the shape of the daemon's own layer module: options schema and type, a config service where there are options, the implementation layer that acquires its dependencies, `makeXLayer(options)` with an explicit requirement list, a default instance.

**Six build handlers** — `turn` owns `makeTurnRoutes`, `turn/routes` owns `makeTurnRouteHandlers` over the seven route factories, `surface` owns the Bolt boot, `dashboard` and `message-reply` own their factories.

The composition **moved into** each index. Nothing is re-exported: `src/index.test.ts` fails on an index that uses `export *` or does not export a `make*`.

## Two needed the source module split first

An index that only forwards a name means the composition has not been found yet, and twice that was literally true:

- **`reply-live.ts`** returned one object with six operations inline, so there was nothing to compose. They became named factories — `replyText`, `replyBlocks`, `updateText`, `updateBlocks`, `attachFile`, `removeMessage` — each keeping its original `Effect.withSpan` name, so the trace tree is unchanged.
- **`turn/routes`** had seven `make*Route` factories and no assembly at all. The new deps type is narrowed to the six fields they actually use, rather than the full `TurnRouteDeps`.

## The detail worth reviewing

`surface/index.ts` takes the turn wiring as a **thunk**, not a `startTurn` handler. Turn routing is currently built *between* `makeBoltApp` and the first listener registration, and `SlackReceiver`'s constructor starts its dedup prune timer — so taking the handler directly would have forced routes to be built first and moved Bolt app construction later. The generic hands the caller's own value back out, and boot order is unchanged.

`bolt-lifecycle.ts` loses `goLive` entirely, which also drops its dependency on `interactions`.

## What has no index

`helpers/*`, `turn/attachments`, `turn/context`, `turn/listening` — pure functions with no services and no assembly step. An index there would be a barrel or an invented wrapper. Callers import the module that owns the name.

## How I verified

- `bun test` — **1063 pass, 0 fail**.
- `bun run typecheck` — **0 errors**.
- oxlint with the monorepo config — **0 violations**, `no-cycle` included.
- **Confirmed the lint run was not vacuous**: planted a two-file import cycle under `src/__probe/`, watched `no-cycle` fire twice, deleted it. A silent run is otherwise indistinguishable from the linter not running.

Supersedes #43 and #44.

author: jperelli
body:
## Summary

Periodic tasks can now define **subtasks** (child issues created under each generated issue) and **related issues** (relations from each generated issue to existing issues). Both apply to cron/rake runs and "Run now". **Requires migration.**

Storage: two new JSON columns, mirroring the existing `watcher_user_ids` / `custom_field_values` approach:

```ruby
Periodictask::SUBTASK_KEYS  = %w[tracker_id subject assigned_to_id estimated_hours]
Periodictask::RELATION_KEYS = %w[relation_type issue_id delay]
# subtasks:  [{ 'subject' => 'Step **MONTH**', 'tracker_id' => '2', 'assigned_to_id' => nil, 'estimated_hours' => 1.5 }]
# relations: [{ 'relation_type' => 'precedes', 'issue_id' => '42', 'delay' => '2' }]
```

Setters normalise Rails indexed-hash params (`{'0' => {...}}`), strip strings, drop fully blank rows and parse `estimated_hours` via `String#to_hours`. `assign_periodictask_params` defaults both to `[]` so removing every row in the form actually clears stored config.

Post-save generation is centralised so run-now and the scheduler share one path:

```ruby
# Periodictask
def complete_generated_issue(issue, now)   # replaces fill_watchers + record_generated_issue call sites
  fill_watchers(issue); record_generated_issue(issue)
  create_subtasks(issue, now) + create_relations(issue)   # => array of error strings
end
```

- Subtasks: `Issue.new(parent_issue_id: issue.id, ...)`; blank tracker/assignee fall back to the parent's, subject supports the same `**MACROS**`. Children are also recorded in `created_issues` history.
- Relations: `IssueRelation.new(issue_from: issue, issue_to: Issue.visible.find_by(id:), relation_type:, delay:)`. Note Redmine reorders `from/to` itself for symmetric types (e.g. `relates`), so tests check `parent.relations` rather than `relations_from`.
- Failures of a subtask/relation don't block the parent issue: errors are aggregated into `task.last_error` (and `flash[:error]` for run-now, `Rails.logger.error` for the checker).

Validation: subtask `subject` required; relation `relation_type` must be in `IssueRelation::TYPES` and `issue_id` numeric.

UI: new `_subtasks_relations` partial in the form with add/remove rows (jQuery, `__INDEX__` template rows), issue autocomplete via `auto_complete_issues_path`, delay field shown only for `precedes`/`follows`; the detail page lists configured subtasks and relations. New locale keys added to all 12 locales.

Tests pass on Redmine 5.1, 6.1 and 7.0 images (`Dockerfile.test`), rubocop clean.

body:
> "그 업무보고의 **이달의 반응**쪽에 있는 **전체 기간 엑셀**은 이제 없어도 되는거 아냐?"
>
> (차이를 설명한 뒤) "**전체기간 엑셀은 상단에 엑셀 리포트가 있으니까 삭제해도 될거 같은 기능**
> 이라는 생각.."

업무 보고 한 화면에 엑셀 단추가 둘이었다. 위쪽 `엑셀 리포트` 와 `이 달의 반응` 머리의
`전체 기간 엑셀` — 이름으로 갈라 놓기는 했지만, 받을 때마다 어느 것인지 따져야 하는 자리였다.
실제로 쓰는 쪽은 리포트였다.

## 무엇을 잃는지 알고 지운다

둘은 같은 것이 아니었다. 지우기 전에 짚어 드렸고, **알고도 지우기로 한 것**이다.

| | `엑셀 리포트` (남음) | `전체 기간 엑셀` (지움) |
|---|---|---|
| 주소 | `/api/export/report.xlsx?month=…` | `/api/export/reactions.xlsx` |
| 기간 | **한 달치** (달을 받는다) | **전체 기간** (달을 안 받는다) |
| 모양 | 화면 한 장을 옮긴 문서 — 갈래별로 장을 나눔 | 표 한 장 — `구분` 칸으로 갈래 구분 |
| 쓰임 | 그 달 보고를 그대로 넘김 | `구분` 칸이 있어 **피벗**에 좋았음 |

**여러 달을 한 파일로 받는 길은 이번에 같이 없어진다.** 여러 달을 견주려면 달마다 `엑셀 리포트`
를 받아 붙여야 한다.

## 되살리는 법

지운 것을 한 커밋에 모아 두었고, 찾아가는 길을 코드에도 남겼다(`app/routers/data_io.py`
그 자리의 주석).

```
git log -S "reactions.xlsx" -- app/routers/data_io.py
git show <그 커밋>^:app/routers/data_io.py
```

## 지운 것

- **화면 단추** — `templates/report.html` 의 `전체 기간 엑셀` 과 그 위 설명 주석.
  `이 달의 반응` 칸과 갈래 넷은 그대로다.
- **길** — `GET /api/export/reactions.xlsx` (`routers/data_io.py` 의 `export_reactions`).
- **딸린 것** — 상수 `REACTION_HEADERS`, 그리고 그 함수 하나만 쓰던 모듈 최상단의
  `from ..services.pipeline import REQUEST_STATUS`. 함수 안 지역 import
  (`IrRequest`·`Meeting`·`MEETING_KINDS`·`OUTCOMES`)는 함수와 함께 사라진다.
  최상단 `VcContact` 는 **남긴다** — 아래 `export_job` 이 쓴다.
- **검사** — `tests/test_dashboard.py` 의 `test_reactions_export_carries_dates`.

## 남은 링크가 없는지

`reactions.xlsx` · `export_reactions` · `REACTION_HEADERS` · `전체 기간 엑셀` ·
`반응 현황` 을 저장소 전체(템플릿·JS·검사·`docs/`·`deploy/`·`scripts/`·워크플로)에서 훑었다.
남은 것은 되살리기 안내 주석뿐이다.

**권한 목록은 손댈 것이 없었다.** `deps.CONSULTANT_PATHS` 와
`tests/test_consultant_access.py` 의 `EXPECTED_OPEN` 에 이 주소는 애초에 없었다
(컨설턴트에게 열려 있던 엑셀은 `consulting.xlsx` 뿐이다).

**스윕 검사도 손댈 것이 없다.** 훑는 검사들이 전부 `app.routes` 를 그때그때 읽어서, 라우트가
사라지면 대상에서 저절로 빠진다(`test_consultant_access.py` · `test_admin_guard.py` ·
`test_startup_tab.py` · `test_llm_brief.py`).

## 확인

화면을 실제로 열었다(`/report`, Playwright).

- `이 달의 반응` 머리에 `전체 기간 엑셀` **없음** · `reactions.xlsx` 링크 **없음**
- `이 달의 반응` 칸과 갈래 넷은 **그대로**
- 위 `엑셀 리포트` 는 **눌러서 받아 열었다** — `업무보고_2026-09.xlsx`, 정상 xlsx
- 로그인한 채로 `GET /api/export/reactions.xlsx` → **404**

`pytest` **1425 passed · 20 skipped**. JS 는 건드리지 않았지만 `node tests/js/*_test.js`
20개도 확인.

---

**딸린 발견(이 PR 밖).** 빈 볼륨으로 컨테이너를 새로 띄우면 `alembic upgrade head` 가
`0018_send_item_parts` 에서 `duplicate column name: parts_json` 으로 죽는다.
`0001_initial` 이 `Base.metadata.create_all()` 로 **지금 모델의 스키마**를 통째로 만들기
때문에, 뒤따르는 `ADD COLUMN` 들이 전부 중복이 된다. `main` 에도 그대로 있는 문제라 여기서는
건드리지 않았다(확인용 DB 는 `0001` 까지만 올리고 `alembic stamp head` 로 띄웠다).

author: igortodorovskiibm
body:
Batched decode aborts outright whenever the zDNN backend is enabled.

## The failure

`llama-batched-bench` dies at every batch size:

```
ERROR: verify_transformed_dimensions() (tensor_desc.c:317):
  ZDNN_INVALID_SHAPE: Invalid shape for dim2. (reason: dimension is 0)
ggml/src/ggml-zdnn/utils.cpp:138: GGML_ASSERT(status == ZDNN_OK ||
  (status & 0xFFFF0000u) == ZDNN_WARNING) failed
 2: ggml_zdnn_init_tensor
 3: ggml_backend_zdnn_buffer_init_tensor
 5: ggml_gallocr_alloc_graph
```

`ggml_backend_zdnn_buffer_init_tensor()` builds a ztensor descriptor for every tensor placed in a zDNN buffer. When a dimension is zero, `zdnn_generate_transformed_desc()` rejects it and `ZDNN_CHECK` escalates that to a `GGML_ASSERT` abort. Batched decode produces zero-sized tensors routinely.

`dim2` is `ne[1]`, but the guard uses `ggml_is_empty()`, which tests all four dimensions — so it covers the general case rather than only the shape that happened to be observed.

## The fix

An empty tensor holds no data for the accelerator to read. Register the buffer with its ztensor left zeroed, and skip both stickification and the `MUL_MAT` bias allocation. `buffer_size` stays 0, which is exactly what `ggml_backend_zdnn_buffer_free_buffer()` already tests before releasing a ztensor, so the free path needs no change.

## Why this is worth prioritising

Concurrent sequences are the largest inference win available on this platform by a wide margin — far larger than any kernel work in this repo. Measured on z17 with SmolLM2-135M-f16, 8 threads:

| batch | generation t/s | vs batch 1 |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 28.17 | — |
| 4 | 209.99 | 7.5x |
| **8** | **245.85** | **8.7x** |
| 16 | 225.81 | 8.0x |
| 32 | 14.38 | 0.5x |

Generation is bandwidth-bound and sits at roughly 84% of the memory ceiling, so reading weights once per step instead of once per token is the whole win. Those numbers could only be collected with `GGML_DISABLE_ZDNN=1` — this abort makes the biggest available speedup unreachable on the accelerator path.

## Verification, and its limits

Type-checked against the real `ggml` and `zdnn` headers. **Not built or run on z hardware** — that needs the CI build, and the runtime fix should be confirmed by running `llama-batched-bench` with zDNN enabled before this is relied on.

This is the second crash of this family, after `-dev zDNN` failing with `pre-allocated tensor (cache_k_l0 (view)) in a buffer (zDNN) that cannot run the operation (SET_ROWS)`, which is still open.

Note: needs a DCO sign-off before merge.

author: yongjohnlee80
body:
`admitSegmentFrame` never checked whether the segment was **already discarding**, and admission runs *before* the loop's discard branch — `waitHeader`, peek, admit, and only then the discard check. So every frame a client pipelined behind a refusal re-entered admission, re-charged a segment that had already been refused, and drew **another** `ErrorResponse`.

PostgreSQL answers an error mid-segment by discarding until Sync and **saying nothing further**.

## Measured

Four over-cap frames behind one breach drew **four refusals** through the real loop; at the unit, a second admission call on a discarding segment re-counted `msgs 1→2` and wrote a second `ErrorResponse`.

The session survives and the counters reset at Sync, so this is **not** a stability defect — it is protocol-sequence breakage a driver sees, because each `ErrorResponse` is one the client must account for where the protocol promises silence. Severity is lector's to rule; I am not pre-judging it, having been wrong to lean benign once already.

## Why no cell caught it

The existing cap cell reads to the **first** `ErrorResponse` and breaks, then drains to readiness — the duplicates land in the gap it does not look at. Same one-step-short shape as the four rounds on #67, in a cell I wrote.

## The discriminator is ultron-prime's

When his delivery boundary landed on #72 the existing discard cell went green, and he warned that **a green integration cell is not evidence that re-admission is impossible**: a boundary that keeps frames out of reach hides the defect rather than fixing it, and *fixed* and *unreachable* are different facts about a component. Counting `ErrorResponse`s before readiness is the property only re-admission changes, and no reader-side change can alter that count.

jarvis's audit named the component; Ultron's discriminator proved the defect was live in it.

## Two cells, because one cannot be trusted alone

| cell | what it drives |
|---|---|
| `TestAdmission_ADiscardingSegmentIsNotReAdmittedFrameByFrame` | the wire shape through the real loop: four over-cap frames + Sync → exactly one `ErrorResponse`, then one `ReadyForQuery` |
| `TestAdmission_AnAlreadyDiscardingSegmentIsNotAdmittedAgain` | the same property driven **directly** at `admitSegmentFrame` — the unit an integration test cannot reach once a delivery boundary exists upstream |

Reverting the short-circuit reddens both. Baseline asserted green first, per `code-review` §15.

## For whoever merges second

On **#72's** branch this short-circuit also calls `fr.skipFrame(h)`, so a discarded frame's body is never decoded — which matters once the post-auth cap is the documented 64 MiB. That half depends on #72's loop draining a refused frame instead of handing it to `Receive`, and **cannot land here**: `admitSegmentFrame` takes no reader on this base. The note is in the code beside the fix, so the obligation travels with it rather than living only in this description.

## Gates

VM43 (`autodb-r3-pg`, `golang:1.25`) at `71e548c` on base `acaf7a5`:
- `go test ./...` — green
- `go test -race ./frontdoor ./core/exec` — green

author: ichirokuxvi
body:
Implements `apps/velista/plans/0059-the-screen-that-picks-the-shops.md`.

A page at **`account/profiles/:profileId/supermarkets`**, reached by a button on the
profiles page, listing the shops in that profile's postal codes and letting somebody
switch each one off. It is the first place in velista where a user sees an actual shop.

The backend halves it depends on are already on `dev`: `GET /v1/catalog/shops/summary`
and `GET /v1/catalog/shops` (backend plan 0068), and
`PUT /v1/account/shopping-profiles/:id/locations` (backend plan 0064).

## What is here

- **A page, and a sibling of `account/profiles` rather than a child**, declared before
  it. The router would backtrack to it anyway; stating the order makes it a decision
  rather than a piece of luck about how backtracking works. `routes.spec.ts` asserts it.
- **A search bar, always**, before a franchise is picked and after. It searches across
  every franchise, and a result names its chain, because "Ronda de los Tejares" does not
  identify a shop on its own. One spec per matched field: shop name, chain name, address,
  city, postal code.
- **Franchise buttons with three states.** "Chain excluded" and "some shops excluded" are
  different promises (the first covers shops the brand has not opened yet), so they are
  drawn differently and both are named in words, never by colour alone.
- **OTHER**, the client side bucket of chains with no `externalBrandKey`, which is what an
  independent shop becomes when it is imported. Its read goes out unfiltered and is
  bucketed here, because the server has never heard the word.
- **Shops grouped by postal code**, headed by `ProfilePostalCode.label` and falling back to
  the code. A profile holding Córdoba and Madrid has no single centre, so distance is not
  the axis.
- **Toggling is optimistic** and reverts the row if the write fails. The brand control
  writes the **chain** exclusion, so it reads as excluding the brand rather than pretending
  to tick every row; a row under an excluded brand is inert.
- **Three empty states**, and only the first (no postal code) offers an action.
- **`OSM_ATTRIBUTION` rendered from the constant** wherever the shops are, with GeoNames'
  CC BY credit beside it once a derived postal code is on screen. Both come through a
  single re-export in `velista/models` that says why reaching into those two framework free
  libraries is safe.

## Notes

- `ShopStore` is provided by the **page component**, not the route: a route's providers are
  never destroyed, so its `DestroyRef` would never fire.
- Nothing in the feature imports `@angular/core/rxjs-interop`, asserted by a scope scan
  spec in the shape of the live basket's.
- `ShoppingProfileStore.setChainsExcluded` is new, and the profiles page's own chain toggle
  now delegates to it, so the rule about what an included chain looks like is written once
  where both writers reach it.

## Checks

- `nx affected -t lint test build` against `origin/dev`: 19 projects, all green.
- `velista-e2e` against a dev slot with all five apps served: 40 passed. (The first run had
  8 Mobile Chrome failures across every spec, including ones untouched here; they were cold
  start contention on the dev servers and did not reproduce.)
- Not exercised by hand against a live backend: that needs a Luna slot with harvested shop
  data in a profile's postal codes.

author: shockwav3
body:
# Rework test setup: separate unit/integration, per-package scoping

## Summary

Restructures how tests are organized and run, without touching what any test actually verifies. Motivated by two things: the combined test-run output was hard to read once RabbitMQ tests joined the suite, and there was no way to run just one package's tests without booting infrastructure for packages you're not touching.

* Unit vs. integration split by filename convention (`*.unit.test.ts` / `*.integration.test.ts`) — self-classifying, no config edits needed when new test files are added later. 26 existing test files renamed accordingly (pure renames, no content changes).
* Container startup parallelized: `packages/core/test/globalSetup.ts` now starts Postgres and RabbitMQ concurrently (`Promise.all`) instead of sequentially, and the container-start logic itself is extracted into two standalone, reusable files — `setupTestcontainersPostgres.ts` and `setupTestcontainersRabbitmq.ts` — so it's defined once and reused rather than duplicated.
* Per-package test scoping: `packages/core` and `apps/api` each now own their own `vitest.config.ts`, runnable independently via `pnpm --filter <package> test`. `packages/core` further splits into unit/integration sub-projects (`--project unit` / `--project integration`) using a single-file projects array, so a unit-only run pays zero infrastructure cost, and an integration run only boots what that package's tests actually need.
* The root `vitest.config.ts` / `pnpm test` path is unchanged — still the full, shared-container run used for CI.
* Fixed a real bug surfaced by this work: `testDatabase.ts`'s changelog-directory lookup was anchored to `process.cwd()`, which only worked because nothing had ever invoked it from outside the repo root before. Now resolved relative to the file's own location, correct regardless of which package's script invokes it.

## Verification

`pnpm test` (root, full suite), `pnpm --filter @workflow-engine/core test:unit`, `pnpm --filter @workflow-engine/core test:integration`, and `pnpm --filter @workflow-engine/api test` all confirmed green independently.

**Not in scope:** no test behavior changed, no new tests added — purely organizational/infrastructure.

author: alexandertroyscott
body:
## Problem

Loki crashes on startup with:
```
init compactor: failed to init delete store: mkdir /loki/compactor/deletion: permission denied
```

The `loki/loki:3.1.0` image runs as user `loki` (UID 10001), but the `loki-compactor` Docker volume is owned by root. The container can't create the `deletion` subdirectory.

## Fix

Added `user: "0:0"` to the Loki service so it runs as root. This is standard for Loki in Docker since it needs write access to its data and compactor volumes.

author: tomnewport
body:
## Summary

Sweep of the open "Issue with word / phrase" reports.

Word-bank answers are graded as a **bag of words** with articles folded out (`phraseCorrectBagOfWords`), so a rendering that says the same thing with one word fewer is rejected outright — there is no partial credit and no "you left a tile unused" nudge. Four of the reports were exactly that shape, and one contrast item was genuinely unanswerable.

| Phrase | Change |
| --- | --- |
| «Я была́ в гостя́х у ба́бушки.» | accept `I was visiting Grandma's.` alongside the "at Grandma's" primary |
| «Де́ти бы́стро оде́лись и пошли́ в шко́лу.» | accept `The children dressed quickly and went to school.` |
| «На у́лице мно́го автомоби́лей.» | accept `Many cars are in the street.` |
| «В магази́не мно́го кроссо́вок.» | accept `Many trainers are in the shop.` |
| «Вчера́ мы чита́ли интере́сный расска́з.» | reglossed `Yesterday we were reading an interesting story.`, old rendering kept as an alternate |

Notes on two of them:

- **The two «мно́го» sentences.** Russian has no dummy "there", so learners assemble the existential without it ("in the street are many cars"). The new alternates are ordinary English whose word bags match those answers, so they land on the existing right-words-wrong-order self-confirm path rather than being graded wrong.
- **читать / прочитать (#611).** The verb-contrast drill shows the English alone and asks which verb the sentence needs, but English past simple "read" is aspect-neutral — the item had two right answers, which is the failure `contrastDrillPools` guards against for *literally identical* English but cannot see here. "were reading" makes the imperfective readable. Same shape of fix as #612/#556.

The alternate that was already on «Де́ти бы́стро оде́лись…» (`children quickly got dressed and went to school`) differed from the primary only by the article `The`, which grading already ignores, so it accepted nothing — it is replaced rather than added to.

### Reports not fixed here

- **#582** (услы́шать conditional) was already fixed by #612 — the gloss it complains about no longer exists. Closed separately.
- **#610** («Окно́ на́шего до́ма выхо́дит в сад.», answer `the window of house looks onto the garden`) is graded correctly: the answer drops «на́шего»/"our", which is the very word the exercise drills, and "of house" is not a rendering to accept. Left open with an explanation.

### Also noticed (not changed here)

99 of the corpus's 3,346 `en_alt` entries differ from their primary only in articles, so grading — which strips `a`/`an`/`the` — already accepted them and they widen nothing. Dead weight rather than a bug, and adjacent to #599; happy to sweep them separately.

## Issue

Closes #593
Closes #594
Closes #595
Closes #609
Closes #611

## Checklist

- [x] `npm run lint` and `npm test` pass (100 files, 34,010 tests)
- [x] Updated the AGENTS.md "Project map" if a route, store, or `src/lib/` module changed — n/a, vocabulary only
