author: lalitmaganti
body:
`trace_processor bundle` now also writes sources.pb and disassembly.pb
members so the UI can show annotated source and assembly without the
binaries or source tree at hand.

Source files are the ones referenced by symbolized frames, both from
symbols already in the trace and those just produced. Only absolute
paths are tried, files over 1 MB are skipped and at most 16 MB is
bundled; --source-prefix-map FROM=TO reads files under a different root
while keeping the debug info path as the key, and --no-sources skips
the step.

Disassembly covers the functions containing sampled addresses of every
mapping the local symbolizer resolved against a binary on disk. The
symbolizer now reports that binary and the mapping-to-link-time address
correction; the bundler finds the containing functions with llvm-nm and
disassembles each with llvm-objdump, keeping bytes, text, statically
known branch targets and source lines. When the symbols came from a
split debug file (a .dSYM bundle or an ELF holding only debug info) the
code is taken from the mapping's own path, verified to have the same
build id, with objdump pointed at the debug file for lines. The last
symbol of a section extends to the section's end. --no-disassembly
skips the step. Both steps report what they bundled and, with
--verbose, what they could not.

author: eenndan
body:
Closes QA **W7-02** (HIGH) and **W7-03** (MEDIUM, U12) — one gesture, two symptoms.

`File ▸ Save as track…` promotes the current start/finish + sector lines into a named track. A named
track **is** a trusted start line, so the session flips Provisional → Verified — but with **no
re-segmentation behind it**, so nothing rebuilt itself and the gesture reached only the trust strip
over the map. Both findings are that one omission, seen from two sides.

## Before / after, from the findings' own repros

Run unedited against this branch and against `main`
(`PACER_REPO=<worktree> pixi run python /tmp/claude/pacer-qa-2026-09-01/W7-library/repro/QA-W7-0{2,3}.py`).

### W7-02 — `QA-W7-02.py`

`BEFORE` = pre-save, `AFTER` = post-save, `REOPENED` = the finding's inverse control (one re-open of
the identical file, nothing else changed).

**on `main`** — `AFTER` is byte-identical to `BEFORE`:

```
BEFORE:   row = 'unknown track  · provisional' '0:23.231'
BEFORE:   entry track=None verified=False trust_label='provisional' trustworthy=False
BEFORE:   prior_best('Sandown Park')=None pb_series=[]
BEFORE:   pb title = 'PB progression'  summary = ''
STATUS BAR: "saved track 'Sandown Park' — future recordings here auto-detect it"
session.timing_verified = True  track_name = Sandown Park  provisional_banner visible = False
tracks.json = ['Sandown Park']
AFTER:    row = 'unknown track  · provisional' '0:23.231'
AFTER:    entry track=None verified=False trust_label='provisional' trustworthy=False
AFTER:    prior_best('Sandown Park')=None pb_series=[]
AFTER:    pb title = 'PB progression'  summary = ''
REOPENED: row = 'Sandown Park' '0:23.231'
REOPENED: entry track='Sandown Park' verified=True trust_label=None trustworthy=True
REOPENED: prior_best('Sandown Park')=23.231227918796566 pb_series=[('2026-05-09', 23.23122791879...)]
REOPENED: pb title = 'PB progression — Sandown Park  (1 session: 0:23.231)'
```

**on this branch** — `AFTER` now equals the re-open control, with no re-open:

```
BEFORE:   row = 'unknown track  · provisional' '0:23.231'
BEFORE:   entry track=None verified=False trust_label='provisional' trustworthy=False
BEFORE:   prior_best('Sandown Park')=None pb_series=[]
AFTER:    row = 'Sandown Park' '0:23.231'
AFTER:    entry track='Sandown Park' verified=True trust_label=None trustworthy=True
AFTER:    prior_best('Sandown Park')=23.231227933627977 pb_series=[('2026-05-09', 23.2312279336...)]
AFTER:    pb title = 'PB progression — Sandown Park  (1 session: 0:23.231)'
          summary   = 'Sandown Park  ·  1 session  ·  best 0:23.231 (2026-05-09)'
REOPENED: row = 'Sandown Park' '0:23.231'  (identical — the re-open is now a no-op)
```

`prior_best` `None` → `23.231`; `pb_series` `[]` → one dated point; `is_trustworthy` `False` → `True`;
the PB-progression header and the progress summary line, both empty on `main`, now name the track.

### W7-03 — `QA-W7-03.py`, rendered

Both runs report `provisional_banner visible = False` in the same frame — the strip has cleared. What
the pixels say (crops are view-local, dark theme, `PACER_NO_MEDIA=1`):

| | map canvas | Laps table |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **`main`** | amber `drag to set start/finish` / `lap timing provisional` beside the start marker | `▶ 1  0:23.231  319  76.6` — every cell italic, **no ★** |
| **this branch** | no caption — clean canvas | `▶ ★ 1  0:23.231  319  76.6` — upright, **★ restored** |
| control (re-open) | no caption | `▶ ★ 1` upright |

The branch crops are pixel-equivalent to the finding's own inverse control.

## The three judgement calls

**1. Re-upsert vs rebuild — I did both, at the seam rather than the call site.**

They are not alternatives; they fix different halves. W7-02 is *index* staleness (nothing in the view
layer writes `library.json`), W7-03 is *view* staleness. Patching only `_save_as_track` would have
rotted at the next path that flips `timing_verified`, so:

* `CentralView.refresh_timing_trust()` is now the complete trust seam — it drives the strip, the map's
  on-canvas cue, the Laps table's muting/★ and the Stats page. Flip a trust flag, call this, and the
  frame agrees. The banner-only body moved to `_refresh_trust_banners()`, which the **rebuild seam**
  calls instead: `rebuild_derived_views` has just rebuilt those other three, so it must not redo them.
  That keeps the cost of a re-segmentation exactly where it was.
* Two private refreshers became public seams for it: `MapView.refresh_provisional_cue()` (was
  `_refresh_provisional_cue`; renamed rather than wrapped — one name per thing) and the new
  `LapTable.refresh_timing_trust()`, which calls `_apply_highlights()` rather than `refresh()`: the
  rows cannot have moved, the trust flags say how authoritative the existing times are, not what they
  are. `_apply_highlights` rewrites every cell's foreground/font/tooltip and, via `_apply_current_lap`,
  every Lap cell's text — so the ★ comes back with it.
* `StudioWindow._refresh_library_entry()` re-upserts the entry from the session as it now stands.
  Deliberately **not** a PB moment: the celebration is decided once, on load, against the index as it
  stood *before* this session entered it — re-deciding it here would re-fire the toast on every drag,
  against an index that already contains the session.

**2. The start/finish drag — the reporter was right, and it has the library half only.** Measured on
the real app (`_on_lines` driven with the map's own payload, sidecar cleared so the recording opens
Provisional):

```
before drag: timing_verified = False
BEFORE: entry track=None verified=False best=23.231227933627977 trust_label='provisional' trustworthy=False
after drag : timing_verified = True   provisional_banner visible = False
AFTER (main)  : entry track=None verified=False  trust_label='provisional' trustworthy=False   <-- stale
AFTER (branch): entry track=None verified=True   trust_label=None         trustworthy=True
```

Its **UI** half does *not* apply — `_on_lines` runs `rebuild_derived_views`, and the crops after a drag
on `main` are already clean (upright `▶ ★ 1`, no map caption). So the drag needed the library fix and
nothing else. Worse than the flag alone: a drag re-times **every lap**, so the entry's `best` was also
frozen at the pre-drag value and the PB history quoted lap times the app no longer shows anywhere.
Fixed in the same shape — `_refresh_library_entry` is connected to `timingEdited`, which covers the
drag, Add/Reset sector and ⌘Z alike.

**3. Guarding — matched to the load path exactly.** `_refresh_library_entry` wraps the whole body in
the same `except Exception → print` the load path uses (`# noqa: BLE001`, the index is additive), so a
library-write failure can never turn saving a track into a crash. The load path's two skip rules moved
into a shared `_library_excludes()` — the bundled `DEFAULT_SAMPLE` and a 0-lap session — so a later
refresh can never index what the load-time upsert refused. `pixi run smoke` exercises that live: it
edits timing lines on the 0-lap bundled sample and still reports `library entries: 0 (sample correctly
not indexed)`.

One extra, in the same spirit: `_save_as_track` now also retracts the stale untimed status notice
(`"unknown track — start/finish line was auto-fitted; drag it into place to fix lap timing"`) before
posting its own confirmation, so the bar does not fall back to a sentence the save just answered.

## Gates

**1. `pixi run lint`**
```
✨ Pixi task (lint): ruff check .
All checks passed!
```

**2. `pixi run test`**
```
100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 71
Total Test time (real) = 108.60 sec
```

**3. `pixi run smoke`**
```
studio: 175 points, 1 laps, 1 chapter(s).
points: 175 laps: 1 valid: 0 best: None
marker/cursor OK, current lap: None
after add-sector: laps 1 valid 0
library entries: 0 (sample correctly not indexed)
SMOKE OK (no-video)
```

**4. `pixi run golden`**
```
ok determinism: two builds match (616 leaves, max |Δ|=0)
ok revert: ref_cleared == base (max |Δ|=0)
ok baseline: 616 leav

author: screwyprof
body:
`Ratio` was a derived field **written in four places and read in one** — and three of those writes were immediately overwritten by the next stage.

```
WRITE  parser.go     parse()
WRITE  prettycov.go  mergeFiles()      <- overwrites parse's
WRITE  prettycov.go  mergePackages()   <- overwrites that
WRITE  prettycov.go  rollUp()          <- overwrites that
READ   printer.go
```

Two problems follow from storing it.

**A stored percentage can disagree with the counts beside it.** That is exactly how the roll-up bug worked in #3: it summed `Covered` and `Uncovered` correctly and computed `Ratio` from the wrong operands. As a method that is unrepresentable.

**It put a NaN in the struct.** A package with no statements gave `0/0` = NaN, and NaN does not equal itself, so two identical parses compared unequal — breaking any caller that compares stats, not just the display. That is the RED test in the first commit.

## API

```go
func (c CoverageStats) Ratio() (pct float64, ok bool)
```

`ok` is false when there is nothing to cover, which is **not 0%**. That keeps "no statements" representable without a sentinel value or an enum — the counts already say it.

Breaking: `stats.Ratio` becomes `stats.Ratio()`.

## Knock-on

- `printer.go` is the only reader and now decides how that renders: `n/a` instead of the literal `NaN` it used to print.
- The package-level `ratio()` helper is gone.
- The oracle's assertion that a node's ratio describes its counts is deleted — with a derived value it is a tautology.

## Verified

```
before:  empty - NaN          after:  empty - n/a
```

Real profile unchanged: `delegator 94.01 / pkg 96.41 / scraper 90.00 / web 95.15`. Full suite, `golangci-lint` 0 issues, fmt clean, `make build`.

body:
The last five from the scan (after #1939, #1943, #1945, #1947, #1950, #1951,
#1953, #1954).

**The inbox reduces a delivery's content before its 202, and the regex doing it
was unbounded.** Measured, not estimated: 720 KB of unclosed `<script>` cost
**232 s** — one request holding a process for four minutes, inside a 300/hour
per-IP budget. Bounding the run and clamping what reaches it brings the worst
case to ~530 ms; an ordinary status is unchanged at ~450 µs. The numbers are in
the code beside the rule they justify.

**Four smaller ways out.** Chromium applies implicit proxy-bypass rules for
loopback, so a captured page could navigate to `http://127.0.0.1:4000/`, reach
this server past the vetting proxy, and have the result stored as the member's
own screenshot. Both "Run the check" buttons let the server fetch a
member-chosen URL without limit while *saving* the same data paid a budget
(measured: 40 fetches for 40 presses). The rel=me proof — which decides whether
someone owns a domain — was read over cleartext. And an inbound signature had to
cover neither the destination's name nor its value, so the same bytes verified
at a second installation.

author: hobbyiq
body:
The published accuracy number — **"HobbyIQ's projected price landed within X% of the actual next sale, on N held-out sales"** — validating the whole ladder including #1647's `player-index-projection` rung.

## What this is

For each held-out sale, the engine is asked to price that identity **as of that sale's own timestamp**, using only data that existed before it, and the projection is scored against what the card actually sold for. Sliced by rung, sport, price band and pool freshness.

Extends the existing CF-BACKTEST-ACCURACY math (2026-07-17) rather than forking it. The 2026-07-17 orchestrator scored *recorded* valuation snapshots, which exist only for a user's holdings and carry no rung attribution; this **re-computes** the engine as of a past instant, so any identity with a sale can be an evaluation point and every point knows which rung priced it.

## No lookahead is structural

`valueIdentity({ asOfMs })` is the one entry the evaluator can call, so it cannot forget to pass a cutoff. From there the instant is both the **clock** the rungs reason with and the **ceiling** on what they may read, enforced *in the query* at every read:

| read | path |
|---|---|
| exact pool | `unifiedPricing.asOfMs` → `exactPoolReader` |
| player basket | `playerTrendRung` → `playerIndex` → `playerIndexRead` |
| fallback ladder | `computeHobbyIqFmv.asOfMs` → `queryPool` (all 11 rungs) |

The ladder is bounded too, deliberately: it is the **baseline the #1647 improvement claim is measured against**, and a baseline that could see the future would silently flatter the new rung.

A leak here does not produce an obviously wrong number — it produces a *better-looking* one. The engine "predicts" a sale it can already see, the error goes to zero, and the report becomes a lie that validates itself. So it is pinned differentially: `asOfLookaheadIsolation.test.ts` splices future-dated rows into the fixture and requires every rung's answer to be byte-identical. Both load-bearing claims were mutation-checked red (drop `asOfMs` at a call site; drop it from the memo key).

The player-index memo is keyed by cutoff. Without that, a backtest pricing many points for one player milliseconds apart would serve the first point's basket to the rest — a leak whose presence depends on the order the sample is walked in, which is the worst property a correctness guarantee can have.

## Two defects the live run found, that green fixtures did not

**1. The cutoff was admitting the sale it was predicting.** `c.soldAt` is compared as a *string*, and the pool holds one instant three ways (measured: 3,062 `+00:00`, 878 `.000Z`, 60 `Z` per 4,000 rows). Those sort by ordinal, not by time — `"+"` < `"."` — so a `.000Z` ceiling admitted the `+00:00` spelling of its own instant. Observed live: a card priced off a pool of **one comp — the sale being predicted** — and "predicted" to the cent.

`asOfCutoff.ts` cuts at the start of the instant's second, in the form that sorts below every serialization, with a parsed-time guard behind it. Both layers are pinned *independently*: the end-to-end case alone could not see the string bug, because the parsed guard masked it.

That leak was worth **19.9% → 37.1% median error** on the same sample. The honest number is the worse one.

**2. The sample was 100% baseball.** An unstratified cross-partition walk is not a random sample — partition order correlates with sport, and the first 6,400-point run was entirely baseball against a population that is 51% baseball / 16.6% basketball / 16.5% pokemon / 13.4% football. Every per-sport slice was an empty claim and the headline was a baseball number wearing a global label. The sampler now walks one stratum per sport on measured shares.

## Metrics

Error divides by the **actual sale**, not the prediction: with the prediction on the bottom an engine improves its score by predicting high, and "within 10%" stops meaning within 10% of the sale. Bias is reported beside the spread, because being 20% high on everything is a correctable defect and being randomly 20% off is not.

The #1647 comparison is speculation-rung vs the family/sibling cohort it was inserted above — not vs the whole population, and not vs the exact-pool rungs that never competed for those cards. It is a **cohort** comparison, not an A/B, and the report says so in those words. It can also return "regresses", and there is a test that proves it can.

## Ops

**READ ONLY** — the script has no write path at all and ignores `apply`. Both runner gates: sharded on `sha1(row id)`, stops at its own `RUN_MINUTES` budget and prints the marker (#1361). **No new dispatch input** — `SAMPLE_LIMIT` reads the existing generic `limit` (the surface is at 24 of GitHub's 25).

```
MODE=sample  SLOT=0 SLOTS=16 LIMIT=1600   # score this shard
MODE=combine                              # merge shards -> REPORT.md
```

## Gates

- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- New suites **28/28** (13 lookahead isolation + 15 metrics)
- Full backend on CI (run [33697243433](https://github.com/HobbyIQ/HobbyIQ-V1/actions/runs/33697243433), head `dc02b068`): **9,929 passed / 49 failed in 17 files**. All 17 fail identically on clean `origin/main` and all 17 are the same class — `Cannot find module .../backend/dist/...`, suites that import built output the unit-test job does not build. **None is one of this PR's suites**; `asOfLookaheadIsolation` and `engineBacktestMetrics` both pass on CI.

  <details><summary>the 17</summary>

  `allCanonicalVerticals`, `auditFlagMarkerIsOnlyImprove`, `bcpCardLineIsNotARung`, `bcpLadderScopeIsAProduct`, `collisionTriage.destinationBasis`, `conformLookupRepairs`, `conformNeverAdoptsAVendorRow`, `consolidateDuplicates.preflightCorroborated`, `consolidateDuplicates.preflightSkipsFlagged`, `crossSourceDedup.behaviour`, `explodeWritesToTheContract`, `freshnessCanaryRowFloor`, `gradedIdentityIsEvidenceBacked`, `pricingInvariantAuditor`, `slugGuardResolverParity`, `triageContentHashCollisions.endToEnd`, `triageContentHashCollisions.twoPopulations`

  </details>

  *(An earlier revision of this section claimed "10,082 passed / 6 failed in 7 files" and then listed eight names. That count was never measured on this head — the numbers above are read off the CI run linked.)*

### The parsed guard is pinned on its own (post-review)

`isBeforeAsOf` was the only defense against a serialization the 19-character string bound cannot order — and a mutation weakening it to `t < asOfMs` survived all 26 original tests. Two cases now cover its two jobs, each mutation-checked against its own mutation:

- **a zoned spelling of the held-out instant.** `"2026-06-04T19:09:00-04:00"` is the same instant as the as-of, but its first 19 characters read four hours earlier, so `c.soldAt < @asOf` **admits** it. The three measured pool spellings are all UTC, which is exactly why the prefix bound works on them and why no existing case could see this. The parsed guard is the only rejection.
- **the strict-vs-inclusive boundary at a mid-second as-of.** The query cutoff is second-truncated, so it drops the whole second including the milliseconds *before* the as-of; the guard floors to the same second to match. `t < asOfMs` admits a row Cosmos never returns — the header's "the two filters can never disagree" invariant, violated. Invisible at a second-aligned as-of, which is what every other case uses.

No `backend/src` behavior change on any production path: every as-of field is optional and null-defaulted, and with it absent the queries are the ones that always ran. No deploy needed for the backtest itself.

author: taylorservice-spec
body:
Read-only census answering the one question that has blocked R-32 production deployment since DECISIONS #153.

**Writes: 0. Deploys: 0. Nothing repaired.**

## Result

    technician + PARTS_MANAGER        0
    technician + WAREHOUSE_MANAGER    0
    technician + BOTH                 0
    UNIQUE EXPOSED PRINCIPALS         0

No production principal holds the `technician` compatibility Role at all. Exactly one holds any active RoleAssignment — `admin@global` — and the `admin` Role declares no `scopesByPermission`, so R-32 does not restrict it.

## The framing that matters

The two production managers carry their operational role and **no RoleAssignment whatsoever** — not the governed manager Role, not the carrier. They are unexposed because they have **no governed reorder authority to lose**, which is a different statement from the deployment preserving their access.

Production is safe for R-32 because production is **barely using the governed access model**: 2 role assignments, 1 principal, no manager Roles, no location scopes. That answers the exposure question conclusively; it is not evidence production is ready to *use* R-32. Granting the managers their governed Role at `location` scope stays a separate Owner-gated step, and this census performed none.

## Read-only is enforced, not asserted

`functions/scripts/r32ProductionExposureCensus.js` imports no writer, seeder, migration or backfill module; reaches no Firestore write verb; is inert on import; and refuses any project id other than the production one resolved from `config/environments.json` — never `.firebaserc`, which defaults to production. There is deliberately **no `--apply`**: a census that can also mutate is a migration tool with a modest default.

`functions/test/r32ProductionExposureCensus.test.mjs` (8/8) fails if any of that changes, and covers the classification logic on fixtures — exposure requires both halves, a disabled carrier is not live authority, a terminated employee is not live authority, unresolvable joins are named rather than guessed.

Both guards were exercised for real: the script refused `--projectId eos-platform-sandbox`, and refused to run without `--read-only`.

## Anomaly recorded, not fixed

`PRINCIPAL_HAS_NO_EMPLOYEE_LINK` — the `admin@global` principal has no `users/{uid}.employeeId`. Not an unresolved join and not a blocker: a principal with no employee link cannot carry an operational role, so it cannot satisfy the exposure definition. Recorded because an admin outside the employee model is worth attention on its own terms.

## Data minimization

Artifacts carry `principalUid` and `employeeId` only. No emails, names, tokens or credentials — verified; the only `@` in the JSON is the `admin@global` role/scope label.

## Verification

- `test:governance` **634/634**, artifact drift gate **exit 0 on the committed tree**
- census fixtures **8/8**
- no deployable file changed; **deployment required: NO**

## Recommendation

`R32_PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT_READY_FOR_SEPARATE_AUTHORIZATION` — **not** deployment authorization.

body:
## Why

Argo CD (argo.namastex.io) will keep the HML instance on the `dev` branch. It needs one image per dev version cut that it can pin by digest from the private GitOps repo. The public repo currently builds images only for candidate tags.

## What

- `.github/workflows/image-dev.yml`: reusable (`workflow_call` with `ref`) plus manual `workflow_dispatch`. Builds `ghcr.io/automagik-dev/omni-api` for amd64+arm64 from a commit that must be on `dev`, pushes `dev-<sha12>` and floating `dev`, attests provenance. Job-local `packages/id-token/attestations: write`, no environment, no tags, no dispatches, no secrets beyond `github.token`. No push trigger: direct commits to `dev` never build.
- `.github/workflows/version.yml`: after a merged PR bumps `dev`, a `dev-image` job calls `image-dev.yml` with the bump commit. Skipped for `candidate=true` cuts (those mint via `image-build.yml`). A local call resolves from the calling ref, so it works before the file reaches `main`.
- `scripts/release/verify-oci-alias.sh --tag` to read back a dev alias (`--version` unchanged, `v*` refused under `--tag`).
- Contract tests: full `image-dev.yml` and `version.yml` blocks (triggers, on-dev ancestry guard, exact permissions, only version.yml may call it, no dispatch path); 19 born-red mutations across the two rounds.
- Docs: dev image channel section; HML/prod rows in the deploy README pointing at the private GitOps repo.

## Merge order

Merge #940 (dev → main) first: merging any PR into `dev` creates a version bump, which changes a protected build input and would invalidate candidate v2.260902.5. This PR itself touches no build input.

## Not in scope

The Argo AppProject/Applications and the digest pin lanes live in `git.namastex.io/khal/deploy` (PR #282 there). No AWS or cluster access is added here.

## Summary

Raises the pin `0.4.0 → 0.5.0` so the template and the fleet land on **one** doctor version, rather than the fleet trailing the template by one right as it rolls out.

Also raises the `2026-09-02-date-only-field-annotation` note's doctor requirement to `>= 0.5.0` to match, keeping the sentence that explains 0.4.0 is where the `date-only` check itself landed.

The upgrade-note gate widening from nestled#146 — `scripts/` and root `AGENTS.md` now require an upgrade note. That's the gap that let the db-update pipeline rewrite land noteless.

author: nicolaidolmer
body:
## Hvad
Måler de to påstande i #3966 mod kode på `origin/main` (3/9), og konkluderer at begge er bekræftede, ejer-godkendte balance-valg — ikke fejl. Ingen kodeændring. Tilføjer én forklarende sætning i `help.json` (EN+DA).

Refs #3966

## Hvorfor
Issuet blev rejst 19/8 (to spillere, samme morgen) og er allerede grundigt undersøgt af ejeren selv i issue-tråden (kommentarer 20/8-25/8). Denne PR verificerer at konklusionerne stadig holder mod kode på `main` efter rebase (3/9), og lukker dokumentations-halen.

### Påstand 1: "Kan brosten kun trænes på let belastning?"

**JA, bekræftet mod kode, og det gælder ALLE færdighedssessioner — ikke kun brosten.**

`backend/lib/trainingDayTypes.js` (`SESSION_INTENSITY`):
```
technique: "easy", aero: "easy", loebslaere: "easy",
endurance: "easy", tempo: "normal",
vo2max: "hard", threshold: "hard", sprint: "hard",
```
Brosten trænes via fokusset `technique` (`backend/lib/training.js`: `technique: [descending, cobblestone]`), og `technique` er en af de tre `SKILL_SESSIONS` — intensiteten er ikke et frit valg, den er en fast egenskab ved sessionen. Modellen er indført bevidst i #3762 (ejer-besluttet 14/8, dagstype-før-session), citeret i `docs/TRAINING_RULES.md` §3: "Intensiteten er ikke et valg, den er en egenskab ved sessionen." Kun Intervaller/Tærskel/Sprint (`vo2max`/`threshold`/`sprint`) findes på "hård".

**Dokumentationen er allerede rettet** (PR #4062, merged): `help.json`s `dailytraining.dayTypes.text` beskriver nu eksplicit at en færdighedsdag har "en fast langsommere fart uanset hvad rytteren er bygget til, så den kan aldrig slå en hård dag på hans eget speciale."

### Påstand 2: "Er træningsudbyttet reelt faldet?"

**JA, to sekventielle, ejer-godkendte rebalancer ramte lige før/omkring spillernes rapporter — begge dokumenterede, ingen af dem uverificerede.**

- **#3709 trin 4/5** (live 14/8, FØR rapporterne): indførte `ROLE_CLASS_RATE` (`backend/lib/riderProgression.js`: signatur/sekundær/håndværk/anden-rolle/svaghed) og sænkede `offFocusMult` (`backend/lib/training.js`). Formentlig den reelle årsag til 19/8-rapporterne.
- **#3746 trin 7** (live 20/8, EFTER første rapport, samme dag som opfølgningen): rekalibrerede `rateByPotential` betydeligt ned.
- **#4063 (merged, samme issue-tråd)** løftede `rateByPotential` op igen 21/8 efter ejer-beslutning om at gøre unge high-potential-ryttere synligt fremadskridende — verificeret stadig live og uændret på `main` 3/9 (`backend/lib/riderProgression.js:142`).
- `ROLE_CLASS_RATE` og `offFocusMult` (den anden halvdel af kæden) er **ikke** rørt siden 14/8 — begge har eksplicitte anker/negativ-test-kommentarer i koden mod at ændre dem uden ejer-go (nævnt i #4063's egen PR-beskrivelse).

Brosten specifikt lægger to ekstra dæmpere oveni, begge bevidste (`docs/TRAINING_RULES.md` §2.1): intensiteten er låst til let, OG en færdighedsdag trænes ALTID til den laveste rolleklasse-rate (håndværk), også når evnen er rytterens signatur — eksplicit ejer-besluttet 14/8, for at en færdighedsdag aldrig skal kunne slå en hård dag på rytterens eget speciale. (Præcise rate-tal er bevidst udeladt her, hard rule 17 — se `backend/lib/riderProgression.js` for de faktiske værdier.)

**Konklusion: begge påstande er balance-valg, ikke bugs.** Ingen af de to kræver en kode-fix i denne PR. Det åbne spørgsmål om hvorvidt stakken (rolleklasse-rater + off-focus-mult) samlet set er hvor ejeren vil have den, er allerede noteret i issue-tråden som noget der afgøres i en kalibreringssession — ikke afgjort her.

## Test plan
- [x] `node scripts/i18n-check-keys.mjs` — grøn
- [x] `node scripts/i18n-check-leaks.mjs` — grøn (ingen nye leaks)
- [x] `npm run lint --prefix frontend` — grøn
- [x] `npm test --prefix frontend` (node --test) — 2770/2770 grøn
- [x] `npm run build --prefix frontend` — grøn
- [x] `pwsh -File scripts/preflight-pr.ps1` — "PREFLIGHT GRØN"
- [ ] Backend tests — ikke kørt (ingen backend-fil ændret, kun to locale-filer)
- [ ] `npm run test:e2e` — IKKE kørt her (orkestratoren ejer e2e-slottet)

## Brugerverifikation (KRÆVET)
- [x] Ikke testet end-to-end i browser: PR'en er en **verifikations- og dokumentations-PR** (kun `help.json`-tekst ændret), ingen visuel eller funktionel adfærd ændrer sig. Konklusionen er verificeret ved at læse produktionskoden på `origin/main`, ikke ved simulering.

## Risk / auto-merge
- [ ] `auto-merge` ikke sat — bør have ejerens øje på konklusionen før merge, selvom risikoen er lav (kun copy-ændring)
- [x] Ingen package/workflow/auth/DB/upload-ændringer

## Filer rørt
- `frontend/public/locales/da/help.json` — én sætning tilføjet i `dailytraining.typeGating.text`
- `frontend/public/locales/en/help.json` — samme, engelsk

## SSOT
`docs/TRAINING_RULES.md` §2.1 ("En færdighedsdag trænes ALTID til håndværks-raten...") og §3 ("Intensiteten er ikke et valg, den er en egenskab ved sessionen") citeret ovenfor — ingen af de to påstande modsiger SSOT'en, begge er allerede beskrevet der. Ingen SSOT-opdatering nødvendig, da konklusionen matcher det dokumentet allerede siger.

## Patch note
Ingen brugerrettet adfærdsændring (kun én hjælpe-sætning tilføjet). Patch note udeladt jf. close-out-reglen ("eller skriv hvorfor ikke").

EN (til `help.json`, allerede indsat i denne PR): "The pace is adjusted from time to time as part of ongoing game balancing, so a rider's daily progress can feel different from one update to the next even though nothing about him personally has changed."
DA: "Tempoet justeres løbende som en del af den fortsatte balancering af spillet, så en rytters daglige fremgang kan føles anderledes fra én opdatering til den næste, uden at noget ved rytteren selv er ændret."

## Ud af scope
Issue-trådens sidste to kommentarer (22/8, 25/8) rejser et TREDJE, separat signal: en GC-rytters punch stod fuldstændig stille (0 fremgang over flere hårde VO2max-pas) EFTER rate-løftet i #4063, mens climbing/tempo på samme rytter voksede normalt i samme periode. Det peger på noget punch-/rolle-specifikt, ikke den generelle rate-stak denne PR dækker. Overlapper #4128 (samme rytter-klasse, "evne står stille") og er allerede sporet af ejeren under princip A i `docs/TRAINING_RULES.md` §12.1 (issue #4634, "GC-rytterens punch-loft hæves"). Ikke rørt her.

author: amissori-coder
body:
Chi riceve le richieste del modulo si impostava solo da una finestra a parte, raggiungibile da un pulsante in cima all'elenco. Il difetto non era la finestra: era il momento. Quella domanda ci si pone quando si sta per spedire, e chi non ci era passato apposta scopriva settimane dopo che le richieste erano arrivate a nessuno.

## Nella finestra dell'invio

Sotto il testo del messaggio ci sono adesso i due campi, **A** e **Cc**, con dentro gli indirizzi di adesso. Si salvano premendo Invia, insieme al resto, e **prima** che parta il primo messaggio: se il salvataggio non riesce si fa in tempo ad accorgersene, mentre una richiesta arrivata a nessuno non si recupera. Non blocca l'invio — il messaggio è comunque buono — ma lo dice.

Il blocco compare se il **testo** contiene il collegamento al modulo, non se la campagna si chiama sponsor: il pulsante si può togliere dalla sponsorizzazione e si può incollare in un invito, e in tutti e due i casi la domanda "a chi arrivano le risposte" segue il pulsante.

E compare solo se i destinatari di adesso sono **già stati letti**. Mostrarlo vuoto perché la lettura non è ancora tornata vorrebbe dire che premendo Invia si salvano due caselle vuote e si cancellano gli indirizzi che c'erano: un danno silenzioso, fatto da chi non stava nemmeno cercando di cambiarli.

## Dagli Aderenti Revilaw

Accanto a ogni campo c'è la tendina dei nominativi in anagrafica, con nome e indirizzo. **Aggiunge** invece di sostituire e torna subito su "scegli", così se ne mettono tre di fila; lo stesso indirizzo due volte non si ripete.

Si legge da `Persone` e non dagli utenti dell'area riservata: in anagrafica c'è anche chi l'area riservata non la usa, ed è gente a cui una richiesta commerciale va comunque. Fuori restano i non attivi, gli eliminati, gli indirizzi storti e i doppioni.

## Accanto alla tabella

Una riga in chiaro dice a chi arrivano le risposte, con il pulsante per cambiarle. Non è un doppione della finestra dell'invio: lì lo si decide una volta e poi la finestra si chiude, qui resta scritto, e chi apre l'elenco tre settimane dopo vede subito se le richieste stanno andando a qualcuno o si stanno fermando in archivio. Quando non c'è nessuno la riga è rossa e lo dice.

Il pulsante in cima cambia nome in **"Richieste ricevute"**, che è quello che apre: due pulsanti chiamati uguale, uno sopra l'altro, erano il modo più rapido per non capire quale premere.

## Una volta sola

Il blocco dei due campi è scritto una volta e usato in tre posti (invio, finestra delle richieste, e in lettura accanto alla tabella): tre copie divergono, e basta che una dimentichi lo scarto degli indirizzi storti perché le richieste smettano di arrivare senza che si veda.

L'azione `contatti` accetta `soloDestinatari`, così le due schermate che mostrano solo "a chi" non si portano dietro anche l'elenco delle richieste ricevute.

## Verifiche

465 controlli automatici, tutti verdi, di cui 24 nuovi sul blocco condiviso: chi entra e chi non entra fra gli aderenti, la tendina che aggiunge senza sostituire e senza ripetere, il Cc che non scrive nel campo A, la casella vuota che non prende una riga bianca davanti, la frase di riepilogo.

Finestra dell'invio ed elenco guardati in Chromium. Alzata la `v=` di `app.js` e `styles.css`.

body:
## Descrição da Mudança

Configuração de padronização e qualidade de código do projeto, garantindo que toda a equipe desenvolva no mesmo padrão e prevenindo bugs básicos antes mesmo do commit.

## Tipo de Mudança

- [ ] Bugfix - Correção de bug
- [ ] Feature - Adição de nova funcionalidade
- [ ] Refactoring - Refatoração de código
- [ ] Documentation - Atualização de documentação
- [X] Chore - Tarefas de manutenção
- [ ] Deploy - Deploy de nova versão
- [ ] Infrastructure - Atualização de infraestrutura

## Como Testar:

1. Atualize seu ambiente:

`npm install`

**Teste a Formatação Automática (Prettier):**

2. Abra `app/login/page.tsx` e desalinhe o código de propósito (dê vários espaços ou quebre linhas no meio de uma tag).

3. Aperte Ctrl + S (ou Cmd + S). O arquivo deve se reformatar sozinho.

**Teste o Bloqueio do Commit (ESLint + Husky):**

4. No mesmo arquivo, crie uma variável. Ex: `const variavelTeste = "teste";`

5. Tente fazer um commit no terminal: `git add .` e `git commit -m "teste"`. O terminal deve ficar vermelho, abortar o commit e acusar o erro na variável variavelTeste.

**Teste a Exceção do Underline:**

6. Volte no arquivo e mude o nome da variável para `const _variavelTeste = "teste";`

7. Tente commitar novamente. O Husky vai rodar, processar o arquivo, aplicar o Prettier e permitir a criação do commit.

author: valdislaul-dot
body:
## Summary

**Phase 1: Service Skeleton + /health Liveness**
**Goal:** The gogo API service exists as a resident FastAPI process on the Windows machine — it boots, auto-starts after reboot, answers liveness probes without ever touching state files, and refuses to start if it would be exposed without a token.
**Status:** Verified ✓

gogo 主升浪交易系统新增第三个入口:仓库内 FastAPI 服务(`api/` 包)。GET /health 为纯内存探活(always-200 + monotonic uptime,永不 401/503、不受数据新旧影响);启动时序 fail-closed(非回环无 token 拒绝启动且不生成 token 文件);token at rest(`data/api_token.txt`,secrets 生成、同 commit gitignore);`run_api.bat` + `install_api_task.ps1` 注册 `gogo-api` 计划任务(AtStartup + 5 分钟延迟,Interactive/Limited,重启 3 次/10 分钟,ExecutionTimeLimit 无限)。仓库首套自动化测试落地:pytest 18 passed + 1 skipped,零网络。验证 13/14 truths 实机确认,重启自启经人工确认通过;安全审计 14/14 威胁 CLOSED;UI 审计 23/24。

## Changes

### Plan 01-01: Service Skeleton + /health Liveness
Repo's first package (`api/`) with a pure in-memory always-200 GET /health, SEC-03 fail-closed boot (refusal evaluated before any token generation), D-03/D-05 token-at-rest handling, D-06 same-commit gitignore, dependency floors, and the repo's first offline pytest suite (18 passed, 1 skipped, zero network).

**Key files:**
- `api/main.py` — FastAPI app, /health handler, boot sequence with SEC-03/D-03 ordering
- `api/boot.py` — pure boot helpers (is_loopback, read_token, has_token, ensure_token)
- `pytest.ini`, `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/test_health.py`, `tests/test_boot.py` — offline suite with autouse network-block
- `.gitignore` — `data/api_token.txt` entry (same commit as generator), `requirements.txt` — floors fastapi>=0.115.14 / uvicorn>=0.51.0 / pytest>=8.3 / httpx>=0.25.2

### Plan 01-02: Windows Autostart
Repo-root `run_api.bat` (5 ASCII lines, `%~dp0`-derived) and `scripts/daily/install_api_task.ps1` registering the idempotent, convention-shaped `gogo-api` Task Scheduler task — live-started and probed 200 on 127.0.0.1:8000; real-reboot confirmation recorded as a passed human check.

**Key files:**
- `run_api.bat` — launcher, path derived from its own location, output appended to logs/api/console.log
- `scripts/daily/install_api_task.ps1` — idempotent registration (Interactive/Limited, AtStartup+Delay PT5M, RestartCount 3/10-min, IgnoreNew, ExecutionTimeLimit PT0S)

## Requirements Addressed

- **HLT-01** — GET /health 探活:纯内存返回 `{"status":"ok","uptime_seconds":N}`,永远 200,不受鉴权拦截,数据过期绝不 503
- **SEC-03** — 默认绑 127.0.0.1,非回环无 token 拒绝启动(fail-closed)
- **OPS-01** — Windows 任务计划程序开机自启(run_api.bat,沿用 install_scheduled_task.ps1 惯例)
- **OPS-02** — pytest+TestClient 种子测试(仓库首套自动化测试)

## Verification

- [x] Automated verification: 13/14 must-haves machine-verified, 1 present-behavior-unverified resolved via human check (18 passed + 1 skipped pytest; live /health 200; SEC-03 refusal live-proven; git check-ignore exit 0; task config machine-probed)
- [x] Human verification: post-reboot auto-start — passed (reboot + ~6 min wait + unassisted probe → 200)
- [x] Human verification: MVP user-story format decision — accepted prose-goal goal-backward verification (mode-agnostic)
- [x] Security: 14/14 threats CLOSED (ASVS L1), threats_open: 0
- [x] Nyquist: 4/4 requirements with automated or completed-manual verification

## Key Decisions

- SEC-03 boot check runs BEFORE any token generation (Pitfall-2 ordering) — refusal branch never creates the token file; generation only on the loopback/default branch
- Token at rest: `data/api_token.txt`, `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`, env-first-file-second; gitignored in the same commit as the generator (D-06)
- Boot-trigger delay delivered as fixed `Delay=PT5M` (not RandomDelay): PowerShell 5.1 cannot express RandomDelay on AtStartup triggers — CIM class lacks the property, XML schema rejects it; the legacy convention task never carried one either
- Task registration requires elevation on this machine (0x80070005 non-elevated) — RESEARCH assumption A1 disproven; installer documents the elevated run
- `-ExecutionTimeLimit` unlimited (PT0S): Task Scheduler's default 3-day limit would silently terminate the resident service mid-week

## User Stories & Acceptance Criteria

- Acceptance criteria are covered by the linked requirements and verification evidence.

## Risks & Dependencies

- No known high-risk rollout dependencies.

## Success Metrics & Release Criteria

- Release when automated verification and required manual checks pass.

## Stakeholder Review & Approval

- Product owner approval pending for service-skeleton-health-liveness.

author: otenim
body:
## Problem

`bagwiz movify --pcd ...` failed at frame 0 on a rosbag whose `/sensing/lidar/concatenated/pointcloud` messages carry a **stale `row_step`**:

```
[ERROR] [bagwiz.cmd.movify]: frame 0: topic '/sensing/lidar/concatenated/pointcloud': point cloud data is smaller than height * width * point_step
```

Inspecting the actual messages shows the data blob is fine — `data.size() == height * width * point_step` (e.g. `height=1, width=120754, point_step=16`, `data=1932064`) — but `row_step=451120` is smaller than `width * point_step`, a leftover from a source cloud that the concatenation pipeline that produced the bag did not update when it grew the width. `check_layout()` in `cloud_view.cpp` treated `width * point_step > row_step` as a hard error, so the point-cloud panel rendered nothing, while the camera-overlay path (`project_pointcloud` in `projector.cpp`, which walks the blob flat and ignores `row_step`) rendered the same clouds without complaint.

## Solution

Per the PointCloud2 semantics, a `row_step` smaller than `width * point_step` cannot describe the blob (a row would not fit in it), so the only consistent interpretation is dense packing. The layout handling is relaxed accordingly:

- `bagwiz_pointcloud/src/core/pointcloud/cloud_view.cpp`: `check_layout()` is replaced by `resolve_layout()`, which
  - treats a too-small `row_step` as dense packing (`width * point_step`),
  - trims every per-point walk (`project_cloud_to_view`, `bev_auto_range`) to the blob's complete points — the full rows plus the partial trailing row — instead of rejecting a short blob,
  - fails only when not even one complete point fits ("point cloud data is too short to hold one complete point").
- `bagwiz_pointcloud/src/core/pointcloud/projector.cpp`: `project_pointcloud` (the camera-overlay path) clamps its flat walk to the points the blob actually holds, closing an out-of-bounds read for clouds whose data is shorter than the declared `height * width * point_step`.
- The doc comments of both headers are updated to describe the tolerant behavior.

Stricter paths that rewrite data (`pcd concat`, `calib cam-lidar`, SLAM deskew) keep their own validation and are untouched.

## Test plan

- [x] New/updated unit tests in `cloud_view_test.cpp` (stale small `row_step`, truncated unorganized blob, organized blob with a partial trailing row, blob too short for one point) and `projector_test.cpp` (clamp to the points the blob holds) — all confirmed to fail before the fix
- [x] `colcon test` for `bagwiz_pointcloud` and `bagwiz`: 1380 tests, 0 failures (1 pre-existing skip)
- [x] End-to-end on the original 20 GB rosbag with the exact reported command line (`movify -i output_0.db3 --pcd /sensing/lidar/concatenated/pointcloud --pose /localization/kinematic_state --width 2880`): previously errored at frame 0, now renders all 539 frames to a 2880x1620 H.264 video; extracted frames visually confirmed (point cloud + pose trajectory render correctly)
- [x] pre-commit hooks (clang-format, cpplint, cppcheck, ...) pass

## Linked issue

Closes #343

## Exact behavioral claim

A printed enumerated Multiattack composition ("The bear makes one Bite attack and one
Claw attack") is now modelled as an exact per-name composition, not a free choice: the
21 affected creatures (corrected census, not the issue's original estimate of 19 — see
below) can no longer substitute one named attack for another. `MultiattackEffect`
gains an optional `Composition` (`IReadOnlyList<MultiattackComponent>`, `Name` +
`Count`), populated only for a multi-name enumerated composition. `Encounter.Attack`
refuses a swing that would exceed a name's printed count with a new code,
`attack.composition_exhausted`, before anything is spent. `SimpleTacticsPolicy`'s
per-swing executor is now cap-aware, so the tactics policy completes the printed
composition (one Bite, one Claw) instead of picking the higher-value attack twice and
then aborting the turn on a refusal — the stall/short-swing hazard named in the
designer's spec (§3.7) is closed by landing the engine guard and the policy filter
together, in the same PR.

## Tests and evidence

**Regeneration** (`regenerate-content` skill): `dotnet run --project tools/SrdExtract
-- --out data/srd` reports unchanged totals — 330 monsters, 339 spells, 38 weapons, 13
armor, 258 magic items, 0 errors, 15 warnings (all expected: Archmage XP, twelve
truncated spell-component lines, two "Rarity Varies" items). Residue: **0 vanished, 0
appeared** — every `unmodelledClauses` array is byte-identical to pre-change (verified
programmatically, monster-by-monster, against `git show HEAD:data/srd/monsters.json`).

all 21 (diffed the full monster objects programmatically against the pre-change JSON —
no other monster's multiattack object moved):

| Brown Bear | Bite×1, Claw×1 | Wyvern | Bite×1, Sting×1 |
| Ettercap | Bite×1, Claw×1 | Cloaker | Attach×1, Tail×2 |
| Grick | Beak×1, Tentacles×1 | Tyrannosaurus Rex | Bite×1, Tail×1 |

author: indigo423
body:
Closes #689.

`LegacyConverter` validated the polling profile it emits against **hardcoded** defaults rather than the cadence the legacy file carries. `SnmpPollConfig` bounds neither `refresh-interval-ms` nor `snapshot-expiry-ms`, so a 0.8 file with a zero or multi-day interval ran fine, converted cleanly, and then failed the next startup — in a message naming a polling profile the converter had **invented**, which appears nowhere in the operator's file.

That is verbatim the failure mode `outOfRangeNumbersFailDuringConversion` exists to prevent. It varies only the node body, and the cadence lives in `riptide.snmp.poll`, so neither key was reachable from it.

The check delegates to the real `PollingProfile` rather than re-stating its bounds — the reason the node checks beside it give: *a copy would drift from the rules that run at startup*. Its message is then re-stated in terms of the key the operator wrote, with the value they wrote.

## Two ways the first version was wrong

Both found by review, both demonstrated by running the CLI rather than reading it.

**It refused files whose output carries no cadence at all.** A label-only file emits no `polling:` block, and neither does one whose every polled node is an FR-9 carve-out — cleartext v2c on a multi-address range, which this file's own comment calls *"the commonest legacy shape"*. Both were blocked, with a message claiming the conversion "would produce a file that fails at startup" — false for exactly those inputs. The check is now gated on a profile actually being emitted.

**Worse, it wrote a log line into the generated configuration.** `validate()` warns when expiry is shorter than refresh; `ConvertCommand` runs with no Spring context, so Logback falls back to stdout; and stdout is where the generated document goes:

```
$ riptide convert legacy.yaml > new.yaml
$ head -2 new.yaml
01:22:36.416 [main] WARN org.riptide.inventory.PollingProfile -- … expires snapshots (PT5M) faster …
# Generated by 'riptide convert'. …
```

It **parses** — the message contains a colon, so SnakeYAML reads it as a second root key — so it would have been committed rather than noticed. Each key is now paired with a partner chosen so that branch cannot be reached. Verified against the real CLI: the generated file starts with its own comment again.

The underlying stream collision is filed as **#727**. Nothing reaches a logger from this path today, but any future log call reopens it, and the failure mode is a corrupted output file rather than an error.

## Also corrected from review

- **The test pinned nothing about the guard.** It asserted only on `riptide.snmp.poll`, which `LegacyConfigReader` also emits for an unmappable key and a non-integer value. It now asserts on text only this check produces, plus the offending key.
- **The two inlined defaults are gone.** `PollingProfile.builtInDefault()` is public and already imported, and `PollingDefaultsGuardTest` pins those values across the three classes that declare them. A fourth copy here would have drifted silently the next time they changed — the same class of bug being fixed.

## Verification

`make jar` green, **1702 tests** (was 1699).

Mutation-tested: neutering the guard fails `outOfRangeCadenceFailsDuringConversion` and only that test. A first attempt that deleted the call was **inconclusive rather than a kill** — Error Prone's `UnusedMethod` failed compilation, so surefire never ran and there was no `Tests run:` line to read — and was redone in-body.

author: youknowone
body:
The portal metatrace walk stopped reporting `Continue` on a back edge. The
cause was not in the portal: **a payload enum's variant fields were packed from
byte 0, on top of the discriminant the variant inherits from its base.**

## The defect

`majit-translate` models a Rust payload enum the way `rclass.py:499-518` does —
a base carrying only `__discriminant`, and one subclass per variant carrying
that variant's fields and inheriting the base's byte 0. Seating the payload
after the tag was gated on a two-name allowlist (`Result`, `Option`). Every
other payload enum fell through to default packing, which puts field `i` at
`i*8` — field 0 on the tag's byte.

`StepResult`, what every opcode handler returns, is one of them. Measured descrs
before the fix:

| descr | kind | size | fields |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `StepResult.__discriminant` | base | 8 | `__discriminant` @0 |
| `StepResult::CloseLoop` | variant | 16 | `jump_args` **@0**, `loop_header_pc` @8 |
| `StepResult::Return` | variant | 8 | `__pos_0` **@0** |

So `close_loop` wrote tag `2` to byte 0 and the next op overwrote it with
`jump_args` (a `None`, i.e. null). The reader saw tag `0` — `Continue`. Backend
independent; it is in the jitcode, not in any assembler.

## The fix

Replace the allowlist with the question it was standing in for: does the base
register a `__discriminant` row that this variant inherits, and does any
variant's field land inside the tag's byte range?

`tag_recorded_but_unspellable` registers no base row at all, so a payload at 0
there aliases nothing — that is the `base_has_discriminant` term. An unrecorded
tag width reads as a machine word, and an enum for which Charon recorded **no**
layout answers "yes, seats on the tag" outright: that is precisely the case
that hid this bug, because the variant offsets then come from default packing.

An earlier attempt spelled the overlap test as
`enum_layout.is_some_and(...)`, which did nothing — `StepResult` has no Charon
layout, so the guarded case and the broken case were disjoint.

## After

`MAJIT_PCSEQ` on the portal walk, with the same script:

```
execute_opcode_step    pc=3    value=75  -> 1160
execute_jump_backward  pc=38   value=2   -> 75     (was 0)
eval_loop_jit_portal   pc=436  value=2   -> 791    (was 0 — the CloseLoop arm, first time)
```

and the run answers correctly instead of aborting.

`pyre/check.py --backend dynasm`: **ALL PASSED 536/536**. The predicate moves
every payload enum in the LLBC set that Charon recorded no layout for, not just
`StepResult`, so that is the number that matters here.

## The instrument that found it, and one for wasm

`pcseq_branch` returned early unless `frames.len() == 1`, so only the root
jitcode's branches printed. The line that settled this — `execute_jump_backward`'s
own `switch` on the `StepResult` discriminant — is three frames down. It now
prints at every depth with `d=<depth>` and the owning jitcode's name.

Every other portal instrument is a `std::env::var` read (`PYRE_PORTAL_METATRACE`,
`..._ENTRY`, `..._SKIP`, `MAJIT_PCSEQ`), and **the wasm guest has no
environment**, so none of them can fire there. `PORTAL_DIAG` is two counters
read through one `pyre_jit::eval::portal_diag(slot)` by both consumers: the
native `[jit-stats] portal_diag` line, and the `pyre_jit_portal_diag` /
`pyre_jit_portal_diag_len` exports the wasm runner prints as the same line.
Exported rather than imported, as `pyre_jit_bridge_diag` already is — an import
shifts the JIT's function-index space.

Both bumps sit inside `can_enter_jit`'s body, which `jtransform` rewrites into
the `loop_header` operation and so never traces. That placement is the whole
design: `pyre-jit` is one of the four LLBC crates, so a counter in
`eval_loop_jit`'s `CloseLoop` arm gets lowered into the portal jitcode, and
`AtomicU64::fetch_add` is outside the LLBC set — it would become a symbolic
residual sitting between the arm and its `loop_header`, which no `pyre-jit`
path can bind. The instrument would have blocked the thing it was measuring.

The runner reports a slot the guest exports but its own legend does not name as
`slot<N>`, rather than dropping it the way the `bridge_diag` positional mirror
would. Neither counter is in `JITSTATS_SNAPSHOT_FIELDS`, so no recorded
baseline carries them.

## The reading it buys

First portal measurement ever taken from inside the wasm guest, `hot.py`
(a 200k-iteration `while`), against the native dynasm binary on the same
script:

| | `can_enter_jit` | `can_enter_jit_taken` | `loops_compiled` | `guard_failures` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| dynasm | 1930 | 2 | 1 | 1 |
| wasm | 1041 | 2 | 1 | 1 |

Both compile the one loop and take it twice — once on the initial trace, once
after the guard failure. The counts differ in the *untaken* polls, i.e. the
interpreted warm-up before the loop goes hot, which is a threshold-accounting
difference and not a portal one. `back_edge_polls` reads 0 in both runs while
`can_enter_jit` reads four figures, which is worth knowing before anyone uses
`back_edge_polls` as the portal-entry count.

The runner also prints, unprompted, the reason this line had to exist at all:

```
[pyre-wasm-runner] ignoring PYRE_JIT_TRACE_CACHE_DIR, PYRE_JIT_TRACE_CACHE_ENTRIES:
the wasm guest has no environment, so guest-side knobs and probes do nothing here
```

## Also here

Three comments that named the wrong thing. `pcseq_branch`'s doc still described
the depth gate this branch removes. `get_jitcode_calldescr` reads as if the
`(fnaddr, calldescr)` it stamps on every CodeObject jitcode were how pyre calls
a Python function — it is never dispatched (`bhimpl_recursive_call_*` goes
through `get_portal_runner`; pyre's `inline_call` handlers read a build-time
descr pool a runtime jitcode is never in), and the descr beside it describes
`bh_portal_runner_c`, not the slice-taking `bh_portal_runner` whose address it
takes. `executor.rs`'s Float arm named the same wrong function as
`portal_runner_adr`'s value.

### What does this PR do?

Ports the React Read Data category to Angular Recipes (8 recipes) — UIAPI GraphQL queries end to end:

- Single Record, List of Records — fetch-on-mount via ngOnInit, Relay edges[].node unwrapping, { value } scalar wrappers.

Repo/GitHub hygiene pass. The repo had no `.github` templates, so bug reports arrived without Godot version or repro steps, feature requests without an affected subsystem, and PRs without the local check results `CONTRIBUTING.md` already asks for.

author: jamesmaina263-debug
body:
Closes the OS-10 gap in the GTM tracker (Launch Blocker): device-data encryption for offline storage, previously untouched.

**Key management (founder decision):** non-extractable AES-GCM 256 device key, generated once per device, stored as a CryptoKey object directly in IndexedDB (new device_key store, schema v3). Raw key bytes can never be exported via JS.

**Scope:** the two fields that actually carry PII across the two generic offline stores -- pending_mutations.payload (attendance marks, health notes, admissions identity fields) and cached_reads.value (kiosk roster names). Routing metadata (id, module, type, status, cache key) stays plaintext so indexes keep working.

**Deliberately not cleared on logout** -- pending_mutations is deliberately preserved across sign-out already (see clear-on-logout.ts), so destroying the key at logout would silently lose queued-but-unsynced work instead of protecting anything extra. Documented in docs/OFFLINE_ROLLOUT.md.

**Backward compatible:** a pre-OS-10 plaintext record is detected and returned as-is, not force-decrypted.

Verified: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean repo-wide, vitest 113/113 green (6 new tests for the crypto layer itself, including one that reads the raw IndexedDB record directly to prove the plaintext isn't on disk, not just that round-tripping happens to work).

author: lalitmaganti
body:
Add a details tab showing a function's source and disassembly, each
line and instruction annotated with the number of samples taken on it
(self) and including its callees (total), shaded by share of the
hottest row. The data comes from the source_file and disassembly tables
populated by `trace_processor bundle` and the callstacks.annotate
stdlib module; when neither source nor disassembly was bundled the tab
explains how to bundle them.

Source is syntax highlighted for C, C++ and Rust and instructions for
their mnemonics, registers and numbers, with a small dependency-free
tokenizer. The assembly view draws branches to targets within the
function as arrows in a gutter, packed into lanes with loops coloured
distinctly, each row rendering its own slice so the listing stays
virtualized.

The tab opens from a "View source & assembly" action on flamegraph
nodes of the stack sample flamegraphs, both for area selections and for
single samples. To locate the function, the stack sample metrics carry
the source file, sampled address and mapping id of each node as hidden
properties.

## Summary

- [#454](https://github.com/Bicpema/bicpema/issues/454)（[#328](https://github.com/Bicpema/bicpema/issues/328)のsub-issue）に対応。
- `new_simulation.py` 実行時にコピーされるひな形 `templates/` をBootstrapからTailwindCSSへ移行した。以降、新規作成されるシミュレーションはTailwindCSSベースになる。

### 導入方法

- `tailwindcss` / `@tailwindcss/vite`（v4系）をdevDependencyとして導入し、`vite.config.js` にプラグインを追加した。
- Tailwind v4 + `@tailwindcss/vite` はVite側の解決したモジュールグラフを自動スキャンして利用クラスを判定するため、シミュレーションごとに個別のcontentパス設定が不要（ページ単位でCSSが最適化される）。
- 共有のTailwindエントリーCSS `vite/css/tailwind.css`（`@import "tailwindcss";` のみ）を新設し、各シミュレーションはこれをimportする形にした（`import "bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css"` の置き換え）。

### Bootstrap JSコンポーネントの代替

- 設定モーダルの開閉（`data-bs-toggle="modal"` 等）の代替として、素のJSでモーダルを開閉する共有モジュール `vite/js/bicpema-modal-controller.js`（`initModal()`）を新設した。新規ライブラリは追加していない。
- `templates/js/init.js` の `elementSelectInit()` から呼び出すようにし、`index.html` のモーダルブロックを（コメントアウトを外すだけで）そのまま利用できる。

### 既存シミュレーションへの影響

- `vite/simulations/*` の45件は引き続きBootstrapを個別にimportしており、`vite.config.js` へのプラグイン追加だけでは影響を受けない（各シミュレーションは独立したHTMLエントリーのため）。`npm run verify:runtime` で全45件が問題ないことを確認済み。
- `vite/js/bicpema-canvas-controller.js` が付与する `rounded border border-1` クラスは変更していない。Tailwindの `rounded` / `border` は同名ユーティリティとして生成されるため、Bootstrap版・Tailwind版どちらの共存期間中も見た目が大きく崩れない（`border-1` はTailwindには存在しないクラスだが無害）。

## Test plan

- `python new_simulation.py` でテスト用シミュレーションを生成し、以下を確認（作業後に削除済み）:
  - [x] `npm run build` でエラー・警告なくビルドされ、TailwindのCSSが生成されている
  - [x] `npm run verify:runtime` が成功する
  - [x] 実ブラウザで表示確認: ナビバー、左下再生停止ボタン、右上設定ボタンのレイアウトが正しい
  - [x] 設定モーダルの開閉を4パターンで確認: 設定ボタンで開く／オーバーレイクリックで閉じる／×ボタンで閉じる／閉じるボタンで閉じる
- [x] 既存45件のシミュレーションに対する `npm run verify:runtime`（全件成功、影響なし）

body:
### What changes were proposed in this PR?

Two frames agree when they hold the same rows in the same order with the same
values, and the comparison says which of those failed rather than that they
differ. A float is compared within a tolerance, since the two paths reach the
same number by different arithmetic.

A visualization has no frame to compare. What it emits is a figure, and the
meaning of a figure is in the numbers behind it, so the figures are compared
number by number; a plot that renders as an image is compared as the HTML it
emits instead.

### Any related issues, documentation, discussions?

Part of #8325, 5 of 20; that issue lists the set in order.

### How was this PR tested?

The tests in this change cover it. The whole set is exercised together once the last piece lands: every operator run through the engine and through its generated script, and the two answers compared.

author: cadam11
body:
## What changed

`QuerySettings.autoExecuteOnOpen` is deleted — from the interface and from `DEFAULT_SETTINGS`.

Nothing has ever read it. Auto-execute is decided per tab (`tabStore.openQueryTab(…, autoExecute)`), and the only meaning a *global* flag could have had is "also run a `.sql` file the moment it opens" — a new and dangerous behaviour nobody asked for. Task 15 shipped no control for it deliberately (absence over an inert toggle), so removing the field takes away no user-visible surface.

Six files:

- `packages/shared/src/types/settings.types.ts` — the interface member and the default are gone.
- `packages/renderer/src/state/settings.spec.tsx` — **new tests** (see below).
- `packages/renderer/src/features/settings/settings-groups.tsx` — the header comment's paragraph explaining why the Query group has no auto-execute row now says the field was deleted rather than "the decision is a follow-up ticket".
- `packages/renderer/src/features/settings/settings-dialog.spec.tsx` — deleted `offers no control at all for a setting nothing could consume`. It asserted that the `settings-query-auto-execute` testid was absent; with no field behind it, the guard guards nothing.

## Why the persisted data is safe

`validateSettings` (`persistence/renderer-state.ts`) keeps stray keys on purpose — "dropping a stray field would discard data the merge is capable of ignoring" — and `mergePersistedSettings` spreads the persisted group over the defaults. So a `autoExecuteOnOpen` written to `AppState` by an older build is **not** dropped at runtime; it rides through as an inert passenger with no reader and nothing it can shadow. That is the honest behaviour, and the second new test pins it exactly rather than claiming a scrub that does not happen.

## How verified (TDD, red → green)

Failing test first, in `packages/renderer/src/state/settings.spec.tsx`:

- `mergePersistedSettings — the deleted autoExecuteOnOpen field > is gone from the query defaults` — **red** before the deletion (`expected { … } to deeply equal { … }`, received had `"autoExecuteOnOpen": false`), green after. Exact `toEqual` rather than `toMatchObject`, for the same reason `settings.types.spec.ts` pins the editor defaults exactly: a query preference must not be able to arrive, or linger, without a consumer.
- `… > carries one left on disk through harmlessly, without disturbing the surviving fields` — the persisted-value half.

Gates, all green in the worktree:

- `pnpm run typecheck` — 6/6 tasks successful.
- `pnpm run lint` — 4/4 packages, `--max-warnings 0`.
- `pnpm run test` — **218 files, 3715 tests passed**.

No hand-rolled doubles were added; the new tests call the real `mergePersistedSettings` and the real `DEFAULT_SETTINGS`. Docker was healthy (`docker info` OK) but no Docker tier was run — this change cannot reach a database.

## Docs-site

**No behaviour is documented differently, because none changed** — three citations were re-anchored. The setting itself has no page: `docs-site/src/content/docs/reference/settings.md` documents five query rows (maximum rows, execute scope, show execution time, confirm before execute, query timeout) and never mentions auto-execute; the four docs-site hits for "auto-execute" (`features/schema-diff.md`, `features/ai-assistant.md`, `features/object-explorer.md`, `features/query-editor.md`) are all about the *per-tab* behaviour, which is untouched.

The three docs edits are all citation re-anchors, not claims: `reference/settings.md:128` (`:52` → `:51`), `reference/settings.md:138` (`:80` → `:79`) and `features/results-grid.md:173` (`:27-42` → `:26-41`) — every line each one points at was moved by this deletion. `pnpm run check` (0 errors/warnings/hints, 16 files) and `pnpm run build` (42 pages) both pass.

## Unrelated changes

None. The diff is six files (four source, two docs-site pages carrying three citation re-anchors) and touches nothing outside this field.

## What a reviewer should specifically check

1. **The passenger, not a scrub.** Confirm you agree the inert leftover key is acceptable rather than worth a pick-list in `mergePersistedSettings`. A pick-list would be new code and would fight the deliberate "keep stray fields" rule in `validateSettings`.
2. **Deleting the dialog spec's guard.** The alternative was to keep it as a permanent "never add this control" tripwire. I judged a guard for a field that no longer exists to be noise, and the reasoning now lives in `settings-groups.tsx`'s header comment instead.
3. **Line-number citations.** Docs-site cites `settings.types.ts` by line in several places, and this deletion shifts everything below it up by one or two (the interface member, then the default). **Three citations were exactly correct on `main` and are re-anchored here**: `reference/settings.md:128` (`:52` → `:51`, the theme default), `reference/settings.md:138` (`:80` → `:79`, the query timeout) and `features/results-grid.md:173` (`:27-42` → `:26-41`, `CopyFormat` and `GridSettings`). Thanks to the reviewer for catching the first and third — my initial pass claimed only one citation was accurate, which was wrong.

    The **eleven** other `settings.types.ts` line citations across these pages were *already* stale before this PR — they predate the J-44 comment block (e.g. `reference/settings.md:135` cites `:66` for `maxRowsToDisplay`, now line 80; `features/query-editor.md:179` cites `:70` for `executeScope`, now line 83). I deliberately did **not** touch them: a sweep across four pages is a mechanical change outside this ticket and would collide with the sibling branches in flight. Flagged as a follow-up.

body:
user 裁定 2026-09-02(#666、**A**)の実装です。

> 「読んでいたノートの本文に入る」
> (読んでいたノートは開いたまま。本文のいちばん下に写真の行が 1 行増える ── 録音・画面録画とまったく同じ)

## 画面で何が変わるか

| | これまで | これから |
|---|---|---|
| ノートを読んでいて「添付」を押し、写真を選ぶ | 画面が「IMG_0421.jpg」に変わり、**読んでいたノートが消える**。本文には 1 文字も入らない | 読んでいたノートは**開いたまま**。本文のいちばん下に **1 行**入る |
| 画像かどうか | ── | 画像は**本文に絵が出る形**(先頭に感嘆符が付く画像記法)、それ以外は**リンクの形** |
| 追記できない種類(添付など)を開いていた | ── | 添付にはなるが本文には入らない。**画面は開いていたほうのまま**で、下に理由が 1 行出る |
| いま本文を書けない(編集中など) | ── | 捨てずに**預かり**、書けるようになったら入る |

⚠ 録音・画面録画は前からこの形でした ── 同じ帯の隣どうしなのに**結果が逆**だった、というのが #666 です。

## どう作ったか

`src/adapter/ui/actions/asset-into-note.ts` を作り、**「入れ先を先に控える / 選択を返す / 参照を 1 行入れる / 書けないなら預かる」を 1 か所**へ寄せました。`capture.ts`(録音・画面録画)と `attach.ts`(添付)の**両方**がこの口を通ります ── 写して 2 つにすると、断り方も預かり方も**片方だけ直る日**が来ます(CLAUDE.md §7)。

字も実装に合わせて戻しました:断り文「(入れ先のノートが決まりません)」/ マニュアル §2 / お知らせ / `⋯` の説明欄。PR #665 では実装がそうしないので**下げて**いたものです。

---

# 着地前レビュー 2 本が見つけたもの

⚠ **どちらも本物の欠陥を掘り当てました。** とくに 1 件は「**私が直したつもりで直っていなかった**」ものです。

## 🔴 1. 貼り付けの断り文が、user に一度も届いていなかった

`OP_FAILED` に載せた「編集欄が閉じたため…」は、**添付を作った瞬間に消えます** ── `attachFiles` は非同期なので、その行が出た**あと**に `CREATE_ENTRY` が走り、reducer が `error: null` を書きます。実測:

```
error(before)            = "編集欄が閉じたため、…差せませんでした"
error(after attachFiles) = null
```

⚠ `capture.ts` の同じ注記が**既にこれを戒めていました**(そこを踏み直しました)。事情は `attachFiles(…, why)` として渡し、取込の知らせと**同じ 1 行**に出す形にしました。
⚠ 直す前の検査は fake の `attachFiles` に当てていたので、**成り立たない条件**を見ていました(本物は `CREATE_ENTRY` を撃つ)。

## 🔴 2. 預かった追記が、2 本目から黙って捨てられていた

`APPEND_TO_ENTRY` は **`writeLock` が立っている間の要求を黙って捨てます**。その錠が解けるのは **worker の ack が返ったとき**なので、**microtask 1 つでは絶対に解けません**。ところが `writable-queue` は預かりを `splice` して**まとめて**流していたので、**2 本目以降は必ず捨てられ**、しかも呼び側は「本文に入れました」と言っていました。

⚠ #666 でこれが**主経路**になります ── **写真を 3 枚まとめて落とすと 3 枚目が消えます**。

🔑 `pump()` で **1 本ずつ**流し、走らせる直前に `canWriteBody` を見直す形にしました。
🔴 さらに **`pump()` が 2 本飛ぶと同じ預かりを 2 回走らせる**(`pending[0]` を microtask の外で読み、`shift()` を中でしていた)── 実物の器に当てて `A,B,B` を再現し、掴みと取り出しを 1 手にして塞ぎました。

## 🔴 3. 私が書いた理由が、事実と違っていました

「入れ先を輪の外で採らないと **20 枚落として 19 枚が迷子**になる」── **起きません**。`putAssetIntoNote` が選択を**同期に返す**ので、ノートを開いていれば次の周回でも同じノートが読めます(5 枚落として知らせの列まで完全に一致)。

🔑 **本当に差が出るのは「何も開いていないとき」だけ**で、そこでは断り文が「ノートを開いていないので」から「追記できない種類なので」へ**化けます**(user は開いてもいないノートの種類を理由に断られる)。その 1 点を pin しました。
⚠ CLAUDE.md §1「**『これが無いと壊れる』と書く前に、外して壊れるのを見る**」の **3 度目**です。doc の字も直しました。

## ⚠ 4. 空振りしていた検査(どれも全 7413 件を素通りする変異が在った)

| 変異 | 直す前 | いま |
|---|---|---|
| `into` を輪の中で採る | SURVIVED | ⑨ が KILLED |
| 預かりの器を偽物へ差し替え | SURVIVED | ⑦ が KILLED |
| `mime` を `file.type` へ(OS が MIME を付けない経路で**絵が出なくなる**) | SURVIVED | ⑧ が KILLED |
| 断り文から理由を落とす(マニュアルが逐語で引いているのに) | SURVIVED | note-tools-guard が KILLED |

## ⚠ 5. 実ブラウザで「本文に入った」を 1 度も見ていなかった

unit は `REQUEST_APPEND` という **event** までしか見ておらず、「disk へ書く → 読み直す → **絵として描く**」の 3 段は誰も通していませんでした。裁定 A そのものを見る smoke を 1 本足し、**配線を外すと落ちる**ことを確かめています。

## ⚠ 6. 実ブラウザ smoke 3 件の観測点(手元のフル smoke が教えた)

`#412` / `office-entry` / `launcher` は**どれも「取り込んだものが勝手に開く」に寄りかかって**いました。とくに `#412` は **1 枚目の大きさを 2 枚目のものとして読んで**おり、`office-entry` は**対照群が対照群でなくなって**いました(画像の添付を見ているつもりで、開いたままの docx の入口を数える)。
⚠ 緩めていないことは変異試験 S2 で確かめています ── 縮める処理を壊すと、直した後の spec も **KILLED** します。

## ⚠ 7. 字の食い違い 3 件

- 左の列の「添付」ボタンの `title` が古いまま(`⋯` 側だけ直っていた)── **digest で対に pin** しました。⚠ 字が違うのには理由が在るので**1 本には寄せません**(左の列は特定のノートを指していないので「いま開いているノート」、`⋯` はその行を開いたメニューなので「このノート」)
- `docs/manual.md` 4 か所が「添付は独立したノートになる」のまま。とくに §記法の「**参照をコピーして貼ってください**」は、自動で入る物を **user にもう一度貼らせる手順**
- 貼り付けの落ち先が取込側と**同じことを 2 回**言っていた(`main.ts` は知らせとエラーを ` — ` で 1 行に並べる)

---

# ⚠ この PR と無関係な CI の赤を 1 件直しています

`verify` が落ちた 2 件は、`WebAssembly.Suspending` が**手元(Node 22)には無く、CI(Node 24)には在る**ことだけで決まっていました(前の commit では緑だったので、CI 側の node が上がった時点で赤くなったことになります)。

🔑 **手元で再現してから直しました** ── `--require` で `Suspending` を生やすと、手元でも同じ 2 件が同じ字で落ちます。直し方は「走らせる node の性質」ではなく**主張の形**へ:`Suspending` を付け外しして**答えが付いてくる**ことを見る / JSPI を無い側へ**固定してから**測る。⚠ **対照群**も足しました(JSPI が在る環境では JSPI を足りないものに数えない)。

⚠ 本来この種の赤は別の PR に剥がすところですが、**このセッションは指定された 1 本の branch にしか push できない**ので、独立した commit として分けたうえで同じ PR に載せています。

---

## ⚠ 残りは #668 へ

取り込んだ添付が画面のどこにも出てこない(9 種のうち 7 種)/ 編集中は**ファイルを選ばせてから**断る / 3 枚入れても戻せるのは 1 行 / 添付するたび「探す」の絞りが消える / 順番待ちの 1 行の言い方 / お知らせの上限。**どれも見え方が変わる**ので、画面の言葉で選択肢にして user の裁定を待ちます。

## 検証

| | 結果 |
|---|---|
| unit | **7420 件緑**(425 file)。新規 13 件 |
| 変異試験 | **12 件すべて KILLED**(配線 / 入れ先 / 選択の戻し / 画像判定 / 黙らない / 追記できない回 / 縮め / 預かりの旧実装 / `pump` の競合 / 輪の中で採る / 偽の器 / `file.type`) |
| typecheck / lint | 緑(unit は **JSPI 有り / 無しの両方**で回した) |
| 手元のフル smoke(390) | 全数緑(落ちた 2 件は観測点を直して解消) |
| CI(run `33699488365`) | **verify / smoke (1) / smoke (2) すべて success** |

Closes #666
Refs #632, #668

author: zhewenl
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #55027 for `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`. Hybrid models with a non-prefix-cacheable scratch group (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's QSA key ring, `CircularBufferSpec` with `prefix_cacheable=False`) were still counted by `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler`:

- `_estimate_lazy_target_blocks` added `cdiv(max_num_batched_tokens, ring_block_size)` for the ring group. The ring block size is the compression ratio (8 on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) versus 800 for the cacheable groups, so the lazy-mode free-block target was inflated several-fold. With `max_num_batched_tokens=8192` the ring alone contributes ~1024 blocks (x2 watermark) to a target that should be ~15 blocks, so lazy mode keeps far too many GPU blocks free and aggressively offloads.
- The load and eager-store loops iterated the ring group and relied on its block size dividing the scheduler block size (true today only because `QSAKeyStateCache` asserts it).

The store/load round-trip itself already worked: the scheduler reuses the core `KVCacheCoordinator`, which returns no hit blocks for non-cacheable groups, and ring blocks are never hashed so they were skipped by accident. This PR makes that explicit.

## Fix

- Skip non-prefix-cacheable groups in `_estimate_lazy_target_blocks`.
- Gate the load and eager-store loops on `KVCacheConfig.prefix_cacheable_transfer_group_ids`, the same projection `MooncakeStore` uses in #55027. Group ids are core ids (the CPU config mirrors the GPU groups), so no remap is needed.
- Add a QSA-shaped scheduler test: full attention + `CircularBufferSpec` ring, asserting the ring block never appears in store/load pairs, the cacheable group round-trips, and the lazy target matches the config without the ring.

**Depends on #55027.** This PR uses `KVCacheConfig.prefix_cacheable_transfer_group_ids`, which #55027 introduces. The branch is based on `main` and contains only this change, so `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler` construction (and its tests) will fail with `AttributeError` until #55027 merges. Do not merge before it.

## Duplicate-work check

- `OffloadingConnector` has the same class of bug (its config builder asserts divisibility for every group). #54743 already fixes it, so it is deliberately **not** included here.
- #54735 / #54736 touch `simple_kv_offload/manager.py` (hybrid DCP geometry) but do not address non-cacheable scratch groups. Expect a trivial merge conflict in the load loop if they land first.
- Searches: `gh pr list --search "SimpleCPUOffloadConnector"`, `"simple_kv_offload"`, `"simple offload prefix_cacheable"`, `"CircularBufferSpec connector"`: no open PR covers this.

## Test plan

```
pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py -q                # 38 passed (2 new)
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_simple_cpu_offload.py -q  # 4 passed
pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py -q                   # 1 skipped (needs GPU)
ruff check / ruff format on changed files                            # clean
```

The new `test_lazy_target_blocks_ignore_non_prefix_cacheable_groups` fails on main (`40 != 8` in the test config). `test_qsa_ring_group_is_never_stored_or_loaded` passes on main too and pins the current behavior.

Not run: end-to-end lazy-mode serving on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`. Worker side is unchanged (it dedups registrations by storage pointer and the ring shares the HMA allocation).

## AI assistance

This PR was authored with AI assistance (Claude). The human submitter has reviewed every changed line and run the tests above.
